texto: Pues después de esto me hago un Vladimir y a tomar por culo no? El meme este de los pensamientos más profundos de un hombre heterosexual los tuve yo con 13 años? Pos lo mismo. Lo de que se grabe todo en la misma sala es como curioso??? Pero se cargan esa sensación de aislamiento cuando abren la puerta del jurado para que les manden la prueba y con la escena del baño entonces no sé por que lo han hecho. Con los personajes no me meto mucho por que entiendo que están escritos para que la mayoría no te caiga bien y te toquen los cojones, pero para que los dos mejores personajes sean un señor petulante que no muestra emoción alguna en toda la película y un abuelete que parece que le va a dar un ictus en cualquier momento, los otros os los podéis imaginar. Ya ni hablamos del olor a esmegma que despide esta película con ABSOLUTAMENTE TODO TIOS y la gracia que me ha hecho al final con un plano amplio de la calle desde unas escaleras super altas, ver a una mujer diminuta con un abrigo de piel. En plan para decir que había una mujer en la película. Mi conclusión es que esto no tiene ni pies ni cabeza y que los abogados de ese juicio verdaderamente eran malísimos por que para que los papanatas estos desmontaran el caso, QUE SE PODIA RESOLVER SOLO, EN 20 MINUTOS A LA MÍNIMA QUE LE DIERAS 2 VUELTAS EN LA CABEZA, tenían que haberles regalado el título en la tómbola de la feria; que a lo mejor es por que llevo desde los 9 años viendo CSI y derivados, pero yo desde un primer momento he dicho: todas estas pruebas son circunstanciales y el caso solo tiene sentido si lo miras con estas conjeturas, pero vamos, seré yo que soy muy listo o algo. Y entiendo que me quieren filosofar sobre quienes somos nosotros para decidir quién vive y quien muere, y que en un crimen como este nunca se puede llegar a estar 100% seguro de la verdad al mismo tiempo que me abrían melones de diferencias de clases, prejuicios infundidos injustamente, masculinidades fragiles y de más mariconadas; pero es que no me ha importado tres cojones por que yo desde un principio ya sabía lo que iba a pasar por que era ultra predecible. Mira que no sé, que voy a ver si para compensar mañana me veo Bottoms. Edit: ni 20 minutos después de hacer esta pedazo de review me estoy viendo un broski report y no me avergüenza decir, pensar o confirmar que cualquier cosa que diga esta mujer tiene mayor peso lógico y sociocultural que toda esta película. Además de que es literalmente el mejor ejemplo del stream of consciousness, Virginia Woolf, eres cenizas al lado de Brittany Broski.

texto: É um bom filme. mas sinceramente achei um pouco superestimado.a ideia é excelente e é impressionante como conseguem sustentar praticamente o filme inteiro em uma única sala, dependendo quase que unicamente dos diálogos e das discussões entre os personagens. A tensão funciona e a forma como os argumentos são construídos é satisfatória. Mas talvez eu tenha assistido com expectativas que não foram atendidas. Dado a reputação que o filme carrega, frequentemente aparecendo em rankings de melhores filmes de todos os tempos, eu esperava uma experiência mais marcante e impactante talvez. Reconheço completamente sua relevância para a história do cinema em si pois acredito que o contexto histórico e o fato do filme inteiro se passar dentro de uma única locação e sendo sustentado por 12 homens conversando era uma demonstração impressionante de inovação na escrita e direção. Ainda assim, é fácil entender por que virou um clássico. Só não entrou pra mim nesse nível de “obra-prima intocável” que tanta gente coloca.

texto: Can you imagine if people actually changed their minds when presented with rational arguments? God, what a lovely world that would be. I would’ve preferred if Jack Klugman had been the one trying to convince everyone instead of Henry Fonda. It would’ve been more impactful for someone who came from an impoverished background to make the case rather than an architect. I also thought the scene when everybody turns their backs on the racist guy was pretty corny and too stagey for a movie. It felt like a bit of a cop out in a movie as dialogue heavy as this to just stonewall the guy. While I can’t get mad at the movie for only casting dudes, I can get mad that women didn’t used to be allowed on juries, because what the fuck was that? Our opinions counted for nothing? Fuck all the way off. As angry as I am now, I can’t even imagine how infuriated I would’ve been back then. Lee J Cobb gives the best performance here. I think I’ve only ever seen him in The Exorcist before, and he’s such a sweetie in that it was a bit sad to see him play such a jerk in this. I had fun telling Kay what they might know each actor from, but I’m sure they had less fun with it than I did. Two I couldn’t get - the oldest guy is the voice of Piglet and a bunch of Disney characters, and the guy who doesn’t sweat is the father-in-law from Christmas Vacation. Anybody else notice how dirty the floor is in the jury room? People in the 50s really just dropped their trash wherever.

texto: Makes sense why this is regarded as one of the best films of all time, so good! Pacing is so good and you jump into the plot right away. For better and worse this movie created a whole legal drama genre that has real life impacts on the justice system. This movie was made 30 years before DNA and I think it’s a stronger movie for the reason that there is no DNA to think about. Juries actually over rely on the presence of DNA (and other iffy Law and Order type science like bullet casing marks) when deliberating a verdict. Get into the nitty gritty! Think about how could one witness hear a scream if the other witness said the train was passing at the exact same moment. This movie is a liberal fantasy that relies on one person insisting on considering the opposing view point, in this case a verdict of not guilty. But, I actually that’s a strength of this movie rather than a weakness. We have to suspend disbelief all the time for a films to be impactful, so why not choose to believe that despite known social and peer pressure someone can voice their disagreement. Devils advocate is usually a negative instigator but it’s fun to watch someone play out that line of argument in a way that is actually worth considering. The justice system is racist. The people making arrests, prosecuting, and deciding criminal cases are racist. The backbone of “justice” should not depend on one good man doing the right thing. Nothing is ever truly objective, which is especially true of the law despite all the language that hopes to make you think it is. I think I’m probably the prime audience for this movie and loved it! Put me on a jury!! I’d be so ethical!!

texto: Por vezes, alguns dos considerados "cânones" do cinema são ainda mais fascinantes do que sua fama tende a sugerir. Assisti 12 Angry Men (1957) com uma noção abstrata prévia, mas realmente não estava esperando que o filme fosse ser tão intrigante e instigante. Não atoa é um filme tão aclamado, é uma obra tão meticulosa em cada um de seus aspectos — sobretudo sua blocagem e encenação — que chega a ser gratificante um filme que se preocupa tanto em trabalhar o cinema numa premissa tão teatral. Ele exemplifica bem, inclusive, a relação que estas duas artes tem. Desde a criação do cinematógrafo, o cinema extraiu muito de sua base no teatro como também em outras artes. Conceitos como mise-en-scène, por exemplo, são emprestados. Mas justamente dessa raiz que a sétima arte se ramificou. No teatro, o olhar vem de amplas perspectivas. Organizar atores, cenários e objetos é um trabalho cuidadoso que oferece um guia em comum a cada pessoa em cada acento. No cinema, essa organização é voltada a um único olhar: o olhar da câmera. Ela permite um close-up em qualquer detalhe que tanto a pessoa da primeira fileira como a última irão observar com perfeita nitidez. Mas também, quando o diretor confia no uso da profundidade de campo em seu filme, ele ganha uma liberdade e oferece um direito ao espectador para olhar o que lhe chama mais atenção no plano — seja no primeiro quanto no segundo plano — .  Num filme de ambiente pequeno e fechado como este, o uso desta ferramenta pode não parecer em primeiro momento, mas é tão relevante quanto o close-up. Quando se há uma visão dos jurados na mesa, o espectador tende a prestar mais atenção naquele que mais lhe gera interesse ou intriga. Conferir por conta própria um pequeno detalhe na interpretação de cada ator na mesa (independente dele ser ou não o principal foco naquele instante). Quando um dos jurados começa a ser abertamente racista e cada um sutilmente se retira da mesa/desvia o olhar/vira as costas, o plano aberto junto a profundidade do campo montam diante de nossos olhos quase que uma pintura. Quando um dos jurados tira a faca do bolso e crava na mesa, a forma como o choque de todos gera desorganização ainda é organizada pela maneira como cada um está presente na imagem de acordo com sua própria expressividade. São inúmeras cenas marcantes. O filme se declara humanista, independente dos fatos. Neste sentido ele é metalinguístico: Independente da verdade, as perspectivas subjetivas são inevitavelmente manipuladas. Votar pela inocência do réu é algo que fere egos, pisa em tabus e preconceitos, indaga convicções, nenhum deles nem o espectador estava na cena do crime. Eles encenam, simulam, deduzem, o cinema é a verdade simulada do mesmo modo. E a indagação que a obra faz segue sendo fundamental sobretudo numa geração tão insensível e  apática quanto a nossa. Cinco minutos é tempo para decidir por uma vida sem pensar em sua realidade, seu contexto, sem se por no lugar? Mais do que a verdade, é isto o que importa para o filme, e para a arte, a única verdade é a de quem reflete a obra.

texto: I had read some of the notoriously negative German reviews of this when it released with a few calling it war kitsch and one review even saying it's retroactively a right wing film in how it leans into the stab in the back theory that was so popular amongst post WW1 right wingers. Needless to say my expectations where low and in the intervening time I'd read the book which I had enjoyed. I was utterly shocked with how dull and flatly shite this film is. It's main fault is a vague timbre of genericism that pervades every part of it, non descript music, flat acting, dull pacing and many war tropes combine to create a totally banal experience. The only point I really liked was the opening sequence where a dead soldiers tunic is scavenged, repaired and handed to Paul, our protagonist. The film however goes downhill from here, it removes the crucial section from the 1930 film and book where Paul returns home and meets his ever jingoistic teacher and adds in a truly useless subplot following a German politician negotiating the armistice and a grim general desperate to fight to the bitter end. Both storylines take up crucial time from Paul and his comrades, time which in the wonderful 1930 film added levity and camaraderie, a thing that barely exists here. In fact in some ways this film is orgisatically obsessed with grimness and violence,.it does so with the same shlocky gore that Hacksaw Ridge revelled in, another shite war film. It would be forgivable I'd the battle sequences where well done but they have rigid and unrealistic quality to them that detracts from their effect, the French use flamethrowers at point blank range whereas in reality they would have been used at a further distance, tanks fight without infantry support. This is coupled with the disjointed nature of the film due to the added storylines and the setting around the last week for the war the film tries to add a Dunkirk/Nolanesque countdown clockwork mechanism that is just daft and a far cry from the leviathan feeling of the book and original film where time moves over the course of years as Paul grows rougher, more weary. Here we have a rushed opening sequence after which most of the movie takes place around the last week with Paul being stabbed by a Frenchman at 11 o'clock as the war ends. It's so crazy and dumb in fact that after the soldier pulls the bayonet from Paul's body and the blood pours out we hear another Frenchman outside say, "It's 11, stop fighting!" FUCK OFF LIKE. That is something a child writes and this movie won four Oscars. The book and original film rather end with Paul being banally shot by a rogue sniper with the backdrop of an otherwise quiet frontline. I think it is obvious which is more effective. The real sadness of this film is all the people that will watch it and revel in it and enjoy it and will never watch the original and actually experience just how good that film is and how superior it is. A totally dull affair and not worth any time

tema: Fidelidade ao livro e à adaptação de 1930
exemplo: Este grupo critica o filme por se afastar do romance original e da versão de 1930, omitindo passagens importantes e alterando o final, o que descaracteriza a obra.
texto: Impressive movie, but they absolutely miss the key themes of the book and turn the plot into what it wasn’t meant to be, a showing of the epic huge loud battles and brutality. The clue is in the name here, this movie misses the mark. The biggest betrayal is the omission of the key scenes of Paul returning home, and how he is treated by those around him versus who he has become and how he feels. The focus is put on parts of the war that, although essential, are not the focus of the book, which is what makes the book so special in the first place! I’m sure if I’d seen the movie first I’m sure I would have enjoyed it much more. My first dislike is the focus on the idea of them being young boys and inexperienced. In the book, there is no confusion that the boys are young, but by this point they were the older group, and this is again so important to the book. To make them young and inexperienced is to take away the fact that they are young and yet they have so much experience and are numb to everything now. My other problem is the omission entirely of the Catholic hospital recovery scenes. I understand that you must omit things, and so normally I wouldn’t have a problem with the omission of such a scene for times sake. But they omitted these scenes so they could focus on the war and battle aspect of the movies, which again IS NOT MEANT TO BE THE FOCUS. The changing of the scene with the French soldier makes no sense to me, while of course still emotionally devastating, to begin the scene with Paul moving across the crater to stab the man I feel removes the desperation element of the act, and makes the remorse feel less genuine. Furthermore, they change not only Paul’s ending, instead of dying on a normal day he dies minutes before the armistice in an epic battle. I can’t understand why they did this (well I can, blockbuster drama) but I really hate it, the way he dies is meaningful and integral to the feeling you get after finishing the book. Finally, they include armistice discussions which are not at all mentioned in the book. This is just a mind boggling decision, as again I might remind you, the name suggests the book is about the everyday life on the front NOT ABOUT THE WAR ITSELF. There are enough movies about the politicians who ended the war, but the reason, again, that this book is so important is that this is emitted. Those on the front had no idea these talks were going on, had no idea what tomorrow would bring let alone and were forgotten and abandoned by those in power, purely cannon fodder to continue and unnecessary and futile war. Basically, if you want a good movie about life as a German soldier in World War I watch this movie, but you like the book, do not watch this movie. It cuts out important parts of the book that make it a masterpiece  in favour of nothing special. There are so many movies out there that do exactly what this movie does, most do it better, but there are no books that do what All Quiet on the Western Front does. I could go on and on.

texto: this film fails on every single level. it immediately begins with its corny, over the top message right in your face dialogue. i accept it. maybe it's because it's translated from German. seriously, it's very obvious this was written for people who are not very smart. i don't care about a single character sincerely. they all seem like empty dolls to die. why should i care if they do, honestly. i hated paul so much when he died i started clapping, because i was going to be actually mad if they didn't kill him. not because war is hell or whatever but because he's so unlikeable and dumb and boring. he's the placeholder for a human but this isn't a video game. why do i care about anything this stupid, boring, annoying man goes through. i don't. all of the cinematography was a blatant ripoff of 1917. not a single element of the original (1930) film is to be seen here. the most memorable parts of that movie aren't even Frankenstein'd into this mess they're just forgotten. the hands on the barbed wire. them in the trenches for days at a time, shaking in the overwhelming noise of the constant bombing and shelling. the crosses going over the young boys who we learned to know and watched march to their deaths. nothing here is memorable or even likeable. there are stupid horns that sound like dubstep sometimes and it honestly feels disrespectful to the actual victims. I've never once hated a soundtrack so much to feel like it was disrespectful to real life, but this feels like it is. all of the characters lack basic common sense and don't even act like human beings. i don't think any of them are even trying to survive (understandable). daniel bruhl pisses on his shoe at one point. a dude stabs himself to death with a fork. there is no humanity to be found here. the ending marches the soldiers to their deaths post cease fire just in case you didn't understand war is meaningless. the main character stands up and dies awkwardly in what is supposed to be a cinematic shot or whatever and then a boy takes his dog tags like he did at the start. subtlety is dead. i guess they thought perhaps we were too stupid to understand basic metaphors, human dialogue or anything that isn't shoved down our throats. the scene that left the biggest mark on me from the first film was when a soldier steals his dead friend's boots, simply because he needs them to continue on. it made me weep. the scene which is arguably the climax of the film were the main character kills a French soldier in a trench and then regrets it is so overdone and bland here that i didn't even cry (i easily cry at any and all films). this film tortures you so much all i felt was tired, but it still didn't convince me war is hell. i can see it now, a little boy who was swayed by internet opinions and happens to idolize the Germans actions watching this and still thinking it was worth it, and that the main character died fighting with honor. it fails at every single possible thing. the beginning is supposed to be school boys naively joining the army and then showing us the reality of the brutality of war but this film is so eager to start it even butchers that by giving us a beginning sequence which screams the messaging in your face before the actual film has even started. they could've just left that as a short film and left me alone. this was a completely useless jerkoff fest made by people who can't understand the themes of a very simple book. there is a complete lack of empathy for any of the soldiers in this film which is hilarious because that's seemingly the entire point of it (for you to empathize with the German soldiers who died for an evil and wrong cause). i do have plenty of empathy for the fact that these were just people but somehow the film is simultaneously too nice to them and too uncaring at the same time. it doesn't understand its own message and neither do i. the only part of this film i enjoyed is the trench sequence right next to when the French's tanks showed up and a little after that, i enjoyed around 30 minutes of this film. the rest of it is a complete mess.

texto: From a cinematographic perspective, it is offensively clean (like commercial worthy) while relishing the very thing it's "critiquing." The soundtrack is unbelievably bland also. Narrative-wise, the disillusionment and loss of innocence is handled so shoddily compared to the 30s original that this just sits in the camp of a standard war movie. This will not be remembered the same way. It's sad that all it takes for people to praise a movie as a masterpiece is technical competence.

tema: Espectacularização da violência e estética publicitária
exemplo: Algumas reviews apontam que o filme transforma a guerra em espetáculo visual, com fotografia bela mas que glamouriza o sofrimento, contradizendo sua mensagem antiguerra.
texto: Nouvelle adaptation du roman d’Erich Maria Remarque, le film d’Edward Berger entend faire éprouver physiquement l’horreur de 14-18. Tranchées, boue, mutilations, agonies, rats, chevaux morts : rien n’est épargné au spectateur, tandis que le contraste avec le confort des états-majors souligne l’inhumanité du massacre. La démonstration est techniquement impressionnante, mais son insistance finit par en révéler la limite. À force de mouvements de caméra étudiés, de raccords spectaculaires et de compositions soigneusement travaillées, Berger esthétise précisément la violence qu’il prétend dénoncer. Cette fascination formelle introduit une certaine complaisance dans un propos antimilitariste par ailleurs fort peu neuf : un siècle après les faits, fallait-il encore deux heures trente pour nous apprendre que la Grande Guerre fut une boucherie ? L’ampleur de la production impressionne davantage que son regard. Un film de guerre puissant dans sa fabrication, mais dont le spectaculaire finit paradoxalement par affaiblir la dénonciation.

tema: Espectacularização da violência e estética publicitária
exemplo: Algumas reviews apontam que o filme transforma a guerra em espetáculo visual, com fotografia bela mas que glamouriza o sofrimento, contradizendo sua mensagem antiguerra.
texto: I appreciated what the film was trying to do more than I appreciated watching it. War movies usually have one of two failure modes. The first is accidentally making war look exciting. The second is spending three hours insisting that war is bad, as though the audience arrived expecting a TED Talk titled “Actually, trench warfare seems underrated.” All Quiet on the Western Front mostly avoids the first trap, then walks straight into the second. Every scene is calibrated toward the same conclusion: young men are chewed up by institutions that barely notice their existence. This is true. It is also established about thirty minutes in. The remaining two hours mostly increase the fidelity of the suffering rather than the depth of the argument. The craftsmanship is undeniable. The cinematography is gorgeous in a way that feels almost inappropriate. The sound design is relentless. The performances are excellent. But I kept waiting for the movie to tell me something about the psychology of war, nationalism, courage, fear, or even ordinary survival that I didn’t already know. Instead, it kept turning the volume up on a point it had already made. Maybe that’s the point. Maybe war really is just endless repetition punctuated by arbitrary death. But a movie isn’t obligated to reproduce the experience of its subject. Sometimes it should interpret it. Beautifully made, emotionally exhausting, and ultimately less interesting than the history that inspired it.

texto: I appreciated what the film was trying to do more than I appreciated watching it. War movies usually have one of two failure modes. The first is accidentally making war look exciting. The second is spending three hours insisting that war is bad, as though the audience arrived expecting a TED Talk titled “Actually, trench warfare seems underrated.” All Quiet on the Western Front mostly avoids the first trap, then walks straight into the second. Every scene is calibrated toward the same conclusion: young men are chewed up by institutions that barely notice their existence. This is true. It is also established about thirty minutes in. The remaining two hours mostly increase the fidelity of the suffering rather than the depth of the argument. The craftsmanship is undeniable. The cinematography is gorgeous in a way that feels almost inappropriate. The sound design is relentless. The performances are excellent. But I kept waiting for the movie to tell me something about the psychology of war, nationalism, courage, fear, or even ordinary survival that I didn’t already know. Instead, it kept turning the volume up on a point it had already made. Maybe that’s the point. Maybe war really is just endless repetition punctuated by arbitrary death. But a movie isn’t obligated to reproduce the experience of its subject. Sometimes it should interpret it. Beautifully made, emotionally exhausting, and ultimately less interesting than the history that inspired it.

texto: This just wasn’t very good. It feels like a mess of various scenes that make no sense together. I was honestly pretty confused about what was going on at times and it lacked a certain flow to the plot. The movie also completely misses the mark in terms of the book. Rather than portraying an emotional struggle, the movie portrayed a sort of physical brutality present in war, but lacked any philosophical thought the book offers. Additionally, the plot was very different from the book’s and they made many very unnecessary changes. I also think it also fell short in the task to portray a friendship between the soldiers and the main character, which was a guiding and reoccurring theme in the book. I simply wasn’t very impressed with the movie and while it did invoke sympathy (as it should when one sees many 18 yr olds stabbed and blown to shreds), it didn’t offer anything past that. I wasn’t eager to continue watching or even to finish the movie. The only good thing it offered was its cinematography, which alone cannot make up for anything that it lacks. The book was far better and I don’t understand why everyone is so impressed with this shitshow of a movie.

texto: this film fails on every single level. it immediately begins with its corny, over the top message right in your face dialogue. i accept it. maybe it's because it's translated from German. seriously, it's very obvious this was written for people who are not very smart. i don't care about a single character sincerely. they all seem like empty dolls to die. why should i care if they do, honestly. i hated paul so much when he died i started clapping, because i was going to be actually mad if they didn't kill him. not because war is hell or whatever but because he's so unlikeable and dumb and boring. he's the placeholder for a human but this isn't a video game. why do i care about anything this stupid, boring, annoying man goes through. i don't. all of the cinematography was a blatant ripoff of 1917. not a single element of the original (1930) film is to be seen here. the most memorable parts of that movie aren't even Frankenstein'd into this mess they're just forgotten. the hands on the barbed wire. them in the trenches for days at a time, shaking in the overwhelming noise of the constant bombing and shelling. the crosses going over the young boys who we learned to know and watched march to their deaths. nothing here is memorable or even likeable. there are stupid horns that sound like dubstep sometimes and it honestly feels disrespectful to the actual victims. I've never once hated a soundtrack so much to feel like it was disrespectful to real life, but this feels like it is. all of the characters lack basic common sense and don't even act like human beings. i don't think any of them are even trying to survive (understandable). daniel bruhl pisses on his shoe at one point. a dude stabs himself to death with a fork. there is no humanity to be found here. the ending marches the soldiers to their deaths post cease fire just in case you didn't understand war is meaningless. the main character stands up and dies awkwardly in what is supposed to be a cinematic shot or whatever and then a boy takes his dog tags like he did at the start. subtlety is dead. i guess they thought perhaps we were too stupid to understand basic metaphors, human dialogue or anything that isn't shoved down our throats. the scene that left the biggest mark on me from the first film was when a soldier steals his dead friend's boots, simply because he needs them to continue on. it made me weep. the scene which is arguably the climax of the film were the main character kills a French soldier in a trench and then regrets it is so overdone and bland here that i didn't even cry (i easily cry at any and all films). this film tortures you so much all i felt was tired, but it still didn't convince me war is hell. i can see it now, a little boy who was swayed by internet opinions and happens to idolize the Germans actions watching this and still thinking it was worth it, and that the main character died fighting with honor. it fails at every single possible thing. the beginning is supposed to be school boys naively joining the army and then showing us the reality of the brutality of war but this film is so eager to start it even butchers that by giving us a beginning sequence which screams the messaging in your face before the actual film has even started. they could've just left that as a short film and left me alone. this was a completely useless jerkoff fest made by people who can't understand the themes of a very simple book. there is a complete lack of empathy for any of the soldiers in this film which is hilarious because that's seemingly the entire point of it (for you to empathize with the German soldiers who died for an evil and wrong cause). i do have plenty of empathy for the fact that these were just people but somehow the film is simultaneously too nice to them and too uncaring at the same time. it doesn't understand its own message and neither do i. the only part of this film i enjoyed is the trench sequence right next to when the French's tanks showed up and a little after that, i enjoyed around 30 minutes of this film. the rest of it is a complete mess.

texto: Première fois depuis les Hunger Games que je vois un film juste après avoir lu le livre donc je vais me faire plaisir. Les images, les décors et les grandes scènes d’action sont vraiment très bonnes. Le plan d'ouverture, puis de fin, est peut-être l’une des plus belles manières d’exposer la futilité de la guerre dans un seul dialogue, juste un simple plan fixe sur une forêt. Néanmoins, le film prend le parti de suivre les négociations de l’armistice en parallèle de l’histoire des protagonistes. Or, dans le livre, c’est justement l’absence totale de point de vue autre que celui de Paul qui rend le récit si tragique. À chaque instant, la guerre pourrait s’arrêter dans 2 minutes ou dans 10 ans, ça ne fait aucune différence pour les soldats engagés. Pire, le film introduit à la moitié cet espèce de compte à rebours avant l’armistice pour rajouter de la tension, décision qui dessert totalement son propos. Autre parti pris décevant, l’incarnation d’un grand méchant par le général allemand. “Regardez comme c’est dommage, tout les gens aux autres postes de commandement étaient bien intentionnés, c’est juste un seul méchant monsieur qui cause la mort de tout ces jeunes”. Encore une fois, dans le livre, personne n’est nommé comme responsable de la souffrance des soldats. Toute l’horreur repose là-dedans : des gamins de 20 ans, pris dans un engrenage bien au-delà de leur échelle, et aussi inutile qu’implacable. Une réalité beaucoup plus nuancée et dure que le sosie de Dr Eggman qu’on retrouve. En bref, un film qui incarne visuellement très bien les horreurs de la guerre, mais qui omet totalement les éléments narratifs les plus essentiels du matériel de base. Un film de guerre qui fait coquille vide ?? Chokbar (non)

tema: Elogio à fotografia e aspectos técnicos
exemplo: As reviews medianas frequentemente elogiam a fotografia, a trilha sonora e a recriação visual da guerra, descrevendo-as como impressionantes e imersivas, mesmo quando a narrativa não convence.
texto: O cineasta François Truffaut possui uma frase popular: “não existe filme antiguerra”. Em sua tese ele conceitua e discorre sobre a linguagem sensual e entretida do cinema, isso leva a conclusão que não importa o quanto você faça um filme sobre guerra, mostrando inúmeros lados horríveis deste acontecimento horrível, o cinema sempre vai romantizar isso, não por que os criadores quiserem muito das vezes, mas por que é assim que a sétima arte se depõe em nossos olhos e signos. Dito isso, a obra de Edward Berger anda em um liminar tão amedrontador, com um visual tão profundo e melancólico, criticaram as esferas de mais privilégios as bases mais sofridas de uma guerra que por um momento parece que a súmula de Truffaut se equivoca aqui, mas tudo isso para demonstrar que às vezes a maior busca por um sentimento antiguerra traz o amor a guerra. O diretor resolve adicionar a essa obra de trilhagem tão interessante e obscura, com retoques de profundidade de símbolos inclusos como é o exemplo da raposa e das florestas, para no fim adaptar de certa forma uma espécie de jornada do herói. O começo do filme é didático em mostrar um dos melhores acertos do filme, a guerra aqui é trabalhada como produto, como venda. Os soldados morrendo, as costureiras refazendo uniformes, as substituições… tudo aqui mostra um tom legível de repetição e precificação da vida de cidadãos, atitudes essas que realmente acontecem em tempos de guerra. E quando o filme volta para essa leitura é quando ele mais acerta na minha opinião. Todavia, o filme ainda não se desprende totalmente de uma leitura protagonista, jornada e inclusive tem ate mentor. Esse ponto não necessariamente é ruim, tendo em vista que muitas vezes são esses laços que passam a mensagem de humanidade em um cenário de morte, porém é perceptível que na maioria dos filmes grandes de guerra, aqui não diferente, neste posso de sujeira, sangue e morte há um quê de realismo, sempre tem, “o meu filme de guerra tem mais tons de real e de verdade” e quando se tenta sair na contramão da citação que falei no começo deste texto é quando se dá conta do tom persuasivo e nada antiguerra de um filme. O protagonista aqui possui laços, possui dor e temos medo de perder os amigos dele, e isso é um romance de guerra no final das contas! é ruim? É bom? É o cinema persuadindo nós mais uma vez. __dantas

exemplo: Diversas reviews medianas apontam que a adaptação deixa de fora cenas e críticas essenciais do romance original, como o retorno do protagonista à vida civil, e que outras versões transmitiram melhor a mensagem antiguerra.
texto: This an effective anti-war film, showing the callous disregard governments had for the people who were willing to die for them, as well as some of the physical and psychological impacts aspects war had on the soldiers (though I do feel the film plays it a little safe when showing the horrifying ways soldiers could be injured, maimed, or killed). However, I find it extremely frustrating that this film chose to cut out what I consider to be the most important scenes of Erich Maria Remarque's original novel - in which the protagonist briefly returns to his home and discovers that he is no longer able to appreciate or connect to any aspect of it, alongside comparing his lived experience of the war to the romanticised and glorified idea the people around him have of war. These scenes were crucial to the points Erich was trying to make about blind nationalism and getting swept up in populist and patriotic rhetoric.

Yes it obviously portrayed war as horrible and had the contrast between solidiers and higher ranking members not fighting on the battlefield but it was all too clinical, polished and perfected. There wasn’t really any challenge to the system which kind of still left a sense of glorification. Finally there wasn’t really any connection to the key soldiers, it took until the attack half way through to actually have a stark reaction to the atrocities. The cinematography was great but just didn’t suit what the film should have been, needed much more authentic grit.

texto: This an effective anti-war film, showing the callous disregard governments had for the people who were willing to die for them, as well as some of the physical and psychological impacts aspects war had on the soldiers (though I do feel the film plays it a little safe when showing the horrifying ways soldiers could be injured, maimed, or killed). However, I find it extremely frustrating that this film chose to cut out what I consider to be the most important scenes of Erich Maria Remarque's original novel - in which the protagonist briefly returns to his home and discovers that he is no longer able to appreciate or connect to any aspect of it, alongside comparing his lived experience of the war to the romanticised and glorified idea the people around him have of war. These scenes were crucial to the points Erich was trying to make about blind nationalism and getting swept up in populist and patriotic rhetoric.

texto: Right it’s good don’t get me wrong I don’t love this one as much as I did on first watch. Sure it’s pretty good at showing you the brutality of war and the loss and trauma soldier experience while fighting but I also find it contradicts itself with Hollywoodisms that we see like constantly cutting to the political melodrama parts where we get a generic almost cartoonish general. I think when the film focuses on combat I can see how some may say it trays to much like a spectacle but I do think that’s a strength of the film as I think it uses these Hollywoodisms not as entertainment but more to horrify its audience. The constant cutting back to the elites really was jarring for me and killed the pacing at times for me. A grand spectacle that stumbles on it’s themes.

texto: After watching both iterations I come to find out there is a 3rd one that is the original made in the 1930s. Added it to my list but will not be getting to that anytime soon, this movies are long. However 1930s is not to far away from the actual war… This is what I expected from this film, I watched in German and read the subtitles and i recommend to do that because it makes the actor’s performances more realistic. The way they did each character is accurate except for Kat which I was kinda of pissed about and the plot is set to finish the last day of the war. I didn’t enjoy that part of the remake. That’s the whole reason Paul lives for his friends and he eventually is supposed to become the new verterán on the front lines protecting the new recruits. The action scenes are 1000 percent better than the 1970s version which makes the film more entertaining. Shows again the same POV of the German side during WW1 and does it the same as the original so i appreciate that aspect. This is a rare case where I prefer the old version, the relationship between the boys seemed more genuine, here it’s almost as if they rushed it and they don’t flush out each character. Does its job though solid take. Wonder what the 1930s version has in store for me.

texto: O cineasta François Truffaut possui uma frase popular: “não existe filme antiguerra”. Em sua tese ele conceitua e discorre sobre a linguagem sensual e entretida do cinema, isso leva a conclusão que não importa o quanto você faça um filme sobre guerra, mostrando inúmeros lados horríveis deste acontecimento horrível, o cinema sempre vai romantizar isso, não por que os criadores quiserem muito das vezes, mas por que é assim que a sétima arte se depõe em nossos olhos e signos. Dito isso, a obra de Edward Berger anda em um liminar tão amedrontador, com um visual tão profundo e melancólico, criticaram as esferas de mais privilégios as bases mais sofridas de uma guerra que por um momento parece que a súmula de Truffaut se equivoca aqui, mas tudo isso para demonstrar que às vezes a maior busca por um sentimento antiguerra traz o amor a guerra. O diretor resolve adicionar a essa obra de trilhagem tão interessante e obscura, com retoques de profundidade de símbolos inclusos como é o exemplo da raposa e das florestas, para no fim adaptar de certa forma uma espécie de jornada do herói. O começo do filme é didático em mostrar um dos melhores acertos do filme, a guerra aqui é trabalhada como produto, como venda. Os soldados morrendo, as costureiras refazendo uniformes, as substituições… tudo aqui mostra um tom legível de repetição e precificação da vida de cidadãos, atitudes essas que realmente acontecem em tempos de guerra. E quando o filme volta para essa leitura é quando ele mais acerta na minha opinião. Todavia, o filme ainda não se desprende totalmente de uma leitura protagonista, jornada e inclusive tem ate mentor. Esse ponto não necessariamente é ruim, tendo em vista que muitas vezes são esses laços que passam a mensagem de humanidade em um cenário de morte, porém é perceptível que na maioria dos filmes grandes de guerra, aqui não diferente, neste posso de sujeira, sangue e morte há um quê de realismo, sempre tem, “o meu filme de guerra tem mais tons de real e de verdade” e quando se tenta sair na contramão da citação que falei no começo deste texto é quando se dá conta do tom persuasivo e nada antiguerra de um filme. O protagonista aqui possui laços, possui dor e temos medo de perder os amigos dele, e isso é um romance de guerra no final das contas! é ruim? É bom? É o cinema persuadindo nós mais uma vez. __dantas

texto: I’m gonna be that book reader for a second here. The movie was good and layed out its message fairly well, but of course the book was better… They did unfortunately leave out one of the most impactful parts of the book for me, which was Paul’s temporary leave home where he laments about how estranged he feels from his family now due to his time as a soldier. The film just didn’t have a deeply human and personal scene that randomly hit me with tears like Paul’s comment about his favourite food being the potato pancakes from his mother. The film is shot and acted beautifully I will say! I do like the shots of the government figures and politicians with their teacups and fancy attire, but I will still (repeating myself here) argue that I preferred the novel’s inner monologue about the world leaders’ decisions to keep at war for profit and gain for their countries, sitting back at home making these decisions while the young soldiers do the fighting for them. Very impactful. I recommend the film! But I’d read the book first for greater impact. (I also recommend reading up on the author. His life was very interesting to read about.)

texto: Forging your parent's signature for a field trip is good.  Forging your parent's signature to join an ongoing war is bad. The 2022 adaptation of Erich Maria Remarque's seminal anti-war novel isn't what I'd call a remake of Lewis Milestone's Best Picture-winning film from 1930 (or the Delbert Mann version which was made for television in 1979) but rather another interpretation of the story.  It's the same sentiment I have regarding the new Sense and Sensibility coming out.  Rather than remaking the Ang Lee one, it appears to just be the next go-around of filming Jane Austen's book. Director Edward Berger goes all in on the "war is hell" imagery here.  His tasteful eye, combined with the astonishingly great cinematography by James Friend, allows All Quiet on the Western Front a certain visceral heft that may not have been possible given the constraints of its earlier predecessors.  Nothing in the film is particularly new if you've seen its contemporaries but it still manages to achieve its purpose emotionally, thematically and cinematically. Just to get my negative out of the way, I don't get why Volker Bertelmann snagged the Oscar here.  Those three notes sound too much like dubstep for my taste.  Anachronistic scores can work but it took me out.  That said, Bertelmann's other compositions in the film are quite effective but maybe I'm bitter that Justin Hurwitz's Babylon score, easily one of the decade's most memorable film soundtracks, lost to this.  Then again, considering the same branch didn't even nominate Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross for Challengers, I can't say I'm surprised. Felix Kammerer gives a remarkable debut performance.  His face screams someone whose pure innocence will be decimated by the brutality of war, not unlike the young boy from Come and See.  Albrecht Schuch is great too as Kat.  He was a highlight from that Berlin Alexanderplatz in 2020.  Daniel Brühl is easily the most recognizable actor here, lending credibility as Matthias Erzberger, a German politician instrumental in the armistice that ended the war. I was mesmerized by Berger's command of the camera.  He puts you down and dirty in those trenches.  It's a harmonious mixture of some phenomenal production design by Christian M. Goldbeck, seamless integration of visual effects and some awesome makeup that cakes our actors in mud to resemble the horrifically obscuring conditions that it takes to engage in this level of combat.  There's a reason Paul goes from smiling and chipper at the start to absolutely stone-faced by the end. The assembly line nature of the youth as they enter their regiments is frightening.  A batch of young soldiers dies only to be replaced by younger soldiers whose eyes can't fathom the terrifying things they're about to inflict and be inflicted upon.  The scene of Paul engaging in a one-on-one with the French soldier is devastating because it's a fight or flight scenario while also an acknowledgement of how war encourages the loss of our humanity little by little until we can't even comprehend the actions we commit. Paul is one of many millions of people who were indoctrinated into thinking that what they were doing was a good thing and that the future tales of heroics will far exceed anything on the battlefield.  Meanwhile, the people with the power to the end the war only did so when it mathematically didn't make sense to continue and even still there were those who pridefully refused to concede, thus dragging on the war.  You just become numb to it all, senseless to the feeling that you're a pawn, an eventual casualty in a long list of obituaries. If the Germans pulled a Reynolds Woodcock and simply sewed the names into the fabric it'd make the whole recycling uniforms thing easier.

texto: If you think Interstellar 's plot is silly and just a vessel for visuals, then let me present Arrival . The "linguistics" is so lazy that I wrote it off pretty quick, and decided to just appreciate the spectacle. Best way to watch it I reckon, given no characters are worth your time. The only one they even pretend to bother to flesh out is Amy Adams', but the plot is so silly, and everything just seems to fall into place. She never really seems to fail or struggle with anything. Just tries again. Oh, now she's done it. Yay. The reveal of her big dilemma may have hit had the film not showed it at the beginning, to set up for a worse twist. But I genuinely care so little about the plot, it's not really worth going into what it's about. Film is grey. Big. Pretty cool sometimes. Just don't think about anything that happens for more than 4 seconds and you are golden.

texto: ~ 2.75/5 ~ To think people compare this with interstellar is blasphemous if you ask me. Was it okay? Sure.  But it was just that. Okay. At best. The actors did a pretty good job and the visuals were nice along with the music that was on the background - the song that was basically the intro to the film is one of my favourites actually. But the story was lacking. It was confusing, but not in the way that interstellar was. It wasn’t because things were so complicated but because it made little to almost no sense. The main idea had potential, don’t get me wrong, but I feel like the execution undermined the story a lot. At some point, the only thing that made me want to reach the end of the movie - aside from it being over - was the fact that I needed to see how they would wrap it up. texto: As vezes pra ver um filme estadunidense você tem que ignorar a "estadunidensice" por trás dele, mas dessa vez ficou difícil afetando a experiência. Arrival dirigido por Denis Villenueve é uma obra de ficção científica, que trata da chegada de uma especime alienígena que tenta contatar a humanidade em diferentes regiões do mundo, o filme visualmente falando, é lindo, sua fotografia é selo Denis Villenueve, lindíssima. Queria dar ênfase também no desing dos aliens desse filme que são um dos mais criativos que vi Agora sobre o enredo, pessoalmente imaginei que focaria no estudo de uma língua alienígena, com eles tentado decifrar cada gota da linguagem dos Heptadotes, coisa que foi resolvida em 50 minutos, e talvez essa ideia tenha me decepcionado um pouco ao passar da obra, o problema inicial começa no que disse anteriormente: "diferentes regiões do mundo", logo tem geopolítica, e como é um filme do E.U.A, a China é estereotipada como o mais extremista em relação aos aliens, a Rússia como uma ditadura que mata seus pesquisadores por revelar informações, e cara, isso só dá a impressão de ser pura propaganda(e pasmem, é), com a "américa" sendo a mais racional e calma dos 3(sim, mesmo que eles tenham sido também relativamente agressivos, isso não foi tão demonstrado no filme, tanto que não nomearam nenhum superior estadunidense, só general Shang Shang e Shang). O motivo do general chinês mudar de ideia é idiota, e isso se encaixa no segundo ponto, que é mais pessoal O filme começa uma coisa e termina uma completamente diferente, isso não é ruim na maioria dos casos, mas aqui em específico só me frustrou, sair de um filme de tentativa e erro de comunicação para o plot principal envolvendo uma visão não linear da história não me agradou ou me envolveu, com esse sendo um dos pontos para o general chinês largar sua postura agressiva, parece uma solução extremamente vaga pra um problema que foi mostrado durante o longa inteiro. No fim o filme é bom, só me desagradou

texto: Louise: What is your purpose on Earth? Abbot: Offer Weapon Everyone's reaction to that is such a good example of people's interpretation of things can lead to problems that aren't even there. My first thought was, they're offering humanity a weapon to protect themselves. But somehow they thought it meant, a weapon to use against each other. How would anyone even get to that conclusion? What the weapon or gift turned out to be, is the last thing I was expecting. I'm still not fully sure I understand. Obviously Louise was brought in to translate the aliens language, so she had the most time to study them and their gift. But wouldn't others around the world also be studying it? So she shouldn't be the only person who gets to "use" the gift. Like the other films I've seen from Dennis Villeneuve, there's not much excitement to Arrival. But I'm glad I finally found a movie of his I like. Because the whole thing is definitely interesting. I'm curious from the start what is happening, and once it was over I still had a lot to think about. As soon as Louise mentioned how Kangaroos got their name, I paused the movie to find out if that was true. Turns out it's considered a myth, which if I'd waited at least another 30 seconds I would have found out. But it sounded believable, and apparently hasn't completely been disproved.

texto: Arrival: Villeneuve's (failed) Space Odyssey Look, I'm not going to come out and say that this is a bad film, because it clearly isn't, but I would hesitate to say that it's a good film as well. Day by day, my feelings that we as a species should have retired the sci-fi drama genre after Solaris (1972) grow. To be perfectly frank, I felt nothing from this film, one that definitely earned the description of, "a mile wide, and an inch deep." It attempts to tackle so many things at once that it eventually lacks any true identity and fails to separate itself from similar pictures of the 2010's. Even starting the film, I was immediately hit with a rushed, melodramatic sequence of our protagonist and her daughter all throughout her life, which ended before I could even form a thought. Why even include it? Does it serve any purpose besides telling me, "You are going to watch a drama. This will be sad. Feel sad for this person." I will give credit where it's due. The cinematography is obviously gorgeous and is by far my favorite aspect of the film. The sound design and score are both ominous and melancholy. However, I don't love the production value as a whole, because the incredibly dull color palette is a bore to look at. The set design of the military base was also quite bland. The alien itself was without a doubt beautifully surreal, and the scenes of Banks/Donelly attempting to communicate with them are easily my favorites in the film. Even the concepts alone are quite fascinating and even well-executed at times, but I can't help but get the feeling that I've seen this film before. There are so many aspects that are completely run-of-the-mill, such as Banks' "tragic backstory," which we learn later in the film is actually after the main events. Yes, I thought the "recalling the future" concept was quite cool, but it ultimately accomplishes nothing but feel emotionally manipulative yet cold at the same time. Seriously though, how many characters are there in the sci-fi genre that are nearly identical to Banks? A lonely, alienated melancholic genius that gets brought in to "solve the mystery," while everyone else distrusts her and treat her with hostility. She really fits right in with the crowd. I just can't stand the execution of so much of this film. The exposition was actually quite intriguing, but I got to the second act of the film and was fighting the urge to fall asleep. Was it trying to bore me on purpose? I enjoyed the third act much more than the second, as that's when the stakes really raise and we get a bit of well-done suspense. It sucks, because that's when I really felt how much potential this film had! The ending montage didn't do it for me though. Every science fiction film nowadays does this to make it seem "emotional," but it ends up just feeling extremely forced. Without a doubt my least favorite from Villeneuve at the moment, but you never know... perhaps a rewatch could boost it all the way to the top, and I realize how it's secretly a masterpiece. But then again, perhaps not. Not a bad film, but not an especially good one either.

texto: As vezes pra ver um filme estadunidense você tem que ignorar a "estadunidensice" por trás dele, mas dessa vez ficou difícil afetando a experiência. Arrival dirigido por Denis Villenueve é uma obra de ficção científica, que trata da chegada de uma especime alienígena que tenta contatar a humanidade em diferentes regiões do mundo, o filme visualmente falando, é lindo, sua fotografia é selo Denis Villenueve, lindíssima. Queria dar ênfase também no desing dos aliens desse filme que são um dos mais criativos que vi Agora sobre o enredo, pessoalmente imaginei que focaria no estudo de uma língua alienígena, com eles tentado decifrar cada gota da linguagem dos Heptadotes, coisa que foi resolvida em 50 minutos, e talvez essa ideia tenha me decepcionado um pouco ao passar da obra, o problema inicial começa no que disse anteriormente: "diferentes regiões do mundo", logo tem geopolítica, e como é um filme do E.U.A, a China é estereotipada como o mais extremista em relação aos aliens, a Rússia como uma ditadura que mata seus pesquisadores por revelar informações, e cara, isso só dá a impressão de ser pura propaganda(e pasmem, é), com a "américa" sendo a mais racional e calma dos 3(sim, mesmo que eles tenham sido também relativamente agressivos, isso não foi tão demonstrado no filme, tanto que não nomearam nenhum superior estadunidense, só general Shang Shang e Shang). O motivo do general chinês mudar de ideia é idiota, e isso se encaixa no segundo ponto, que é mais pessoal O filme começa uma coisa e termina uma completamente diferente, isso não é ruim na maioria dos casos, mas aqui em específico só me frustrou, sair de um filme de tentativa e erro de comunicação para o plot principal envolvendo uma visão não linear da história não me agradou ou me envolveu, com esse sendo um dos pontos para o general chinês largar sua postura agressiva, parece uma solução extremamente vaga pra um problema que foi mostrado durante o longa inteiro. No fim o filme é bom, só me desagradou

texto: Louise: What is your purpose on Earth? Abbot: Offer Weapon Everyone's reaction to that is such a good example of people's interpretation of things can lead to problems that aren't even there. My first thought was, they're offering humanity a weapon to protect themselves. But somehow they thought it meant, a weapon to use against each other. How would anyone even get to that conclusion? What the weapon or gift turned out to be, is the last thing I was expecting. I'm still not fully sure I understand. Obviously Louise was brought in to translate the aliens language, so she had the most time to study them and their gift. But wouldn't others around the world also be studying it? So she shouldn't be the only person who gets to "use" the gift. Like the other films I've seen from Dennis Villeneuve, there's not much excitement to Arrival. But I'm glad I finally found a movie of his I like. Because the whole thing is definitely interesting. I'm curious from the start what is happening, and once it was over I still had a lot to think about. As soon as Louise mentioned how Kangaroos got their name, I paused the movie to find out if that was true. Turns out it's considered a myth, which if I'd waited at least another 30 seconds I would have found out. But it sounded believable, and apparently hasn't completely been disproved.

texto: Human Kind of Sci-Fi. Arrival moves through these calm currents of emotion throughout. There’s anxiety, sadness, curiosity and this constant sense of unease, yet somehow it remains incredibly peaceful at the same time. It’s strange to feel so emotionally engaged while also feeling completely at ease. Amy Adams gives such a quiet performance, but underneath that stillness are these huge waves of emotion. Like watching an ocean that looks completely calm from the surface, while everything underneath is constantly moving. She was perfect for this role. The score adds so much to that feeling, giving the film this almost meditative quality that carries from beginning to end. I genuinely felt at peace watching this. Everything about Arrival comes together so naturally. The direction, Amy Adams’ performance, the score, the writing. Nothing feels out of place, and everything adds to the same feeling. This might even be a perfect movie.

texto: What a beautiful and devastating film this is. Because memory and association are strange and mysterious things, acting as both teachers and deceivers, Max Richter’s iconic composition “On the Nature of Daylight” has a profound effect on me whenever I hear it. I connect it to certain difficult experiences of loss and grief. Maybe that is why the piece has been used in so many films exploring those very themes. If someone asked me the question Louise puts to Ian, my answer would be different. If I knew my future contained love, but also the devastating loss of that love, and I had the power to change it, I would. Accepting future pain for oneself may be brave. Choosing it on behalf of others is a different moral question.

texto: Eu adoro filmes que conseguem pegar uma ideia de ficção científica e, em vez de usá-la apenas como espetáculo, transformar essa ideia em uma discussão sobre algo profundamente humano. A Chegada faz exatamente isso. É um filme sobre alienígenas, linguagem, comunicação e uma possível ameaça à humanidade, mas, no fundo, é muito mais sobre tempo, escolhas e a maneira como lidamos com aquilo que sabemos que vai acontecer. A linguagem é o verdadeiro coração do filme. Conforme Louise aprende a se comunicar com os heptápodes , percebemos que não estamos simplesmente acompanhando alguém traduzindo palavras. Ela está tentando compreender uma forma completamente diferente de enxergar o mundo. A ideia de que a língua que falamos pode influenciar a maneira como percebemos a realidade é fascinante, e o filme leva isso até uma consequência muito maior: e se aprender uma nova linguagem significasse aprender uma nova maneira de experimentar o próprio tempo? É aí que A Chegada deixa de ser apenas um filme de primeiro contato e se transforma em algo muito mais emocional. A maneira como o filme apresenta as lembranças de Louise é genial porque, durante boa parte da história, acreditamos estar vendo o passado dela. Aos poucos, percebemos que aquelas imagens não são exatamente memórias. E quando a verdade finalmente se revela, várias cenas anteriores mudam completamente de significado. O mais doloroso é perceber que Louise passa a conhecer o futuro e, mesmo sabendo que determinadas coisas vão acontecer, decide vivê-las. Ela sabe que haverá amor, felicidade, mas também sabe que haverá uma dor enorme. E mesmo assim escolhe seguir em frente. Isso transforma a pergunta do filme. Não é mais “se você pudesse conhecer o futuro, tentaria mudá-lo?” , mas “se você soubesse que algo maravilhoso terminaria em sofrimento, ainda escolheria vivê-lo?” E acho essa uma das ideias mais bonitas e tristes que um filme poderia explorar. Louise não escolhe porque não entende o que vai acontecer. Ela escolhe justamente porque entende. O sofrimento não apaga o valor de tudo aquilo que veio antes. Também gosto muito de como o filme utiliza a própria estrutura narrativa para fazer o espectador experimentar, de certa forma, aquilo que Louise está experimentando. O tempo deixa de ser uma linha simples de começo, meio e fim. Informações que pareciam pertencer ao passado ganham outro significado quando descobrimos que pertencem ao futuro. É um daqueles filmes em que a segunda metade não apenas explica a primeira: ela transforma a primeira. E visualmente A Chegada acompanha perfeitamente essa proposta. Os ambientes são enormes, silenciosos e quase contemplativos. A presença dos alienígenas causa estranheza sem precisar transformar tudo em espetáculo. A trilha de J óhann Jóhannsson também contribui muito para essa atmosfera de mistério e melancolia. No fim, A Chegada me pega porque utiliza a ficção científica para fazer uma pergunta extremamente humana: se pudéssemos conhecer toda a nossa história antes de vivê-la, escolheríamos vivê-la mesmo assim? E a resposta de Louise é ao mesmo tempo devastadora e bonita.

exemplo: As reviews destacam a reflexão sobre tempo não linear, a aceitação do sofrimento e a decisão de viver plenamente mesmo conhecendo as dores futuras.
texto: One of the most human sci-fi’s i’ve ever seen. my fascination with linguistics actually made this movie so much more of an interesting watch. I learned about the sapir-whorf hypothesis which essentially is the idea that language can fundamentally alter the structure of thought and even your perception of reality. the movie then takes this incredibly intellectual concept and turns it into something so human. Louise knows the beginning, the middle and the end simultaneously. she knows she will have a daughter she loves beyond comprehension, she knows she will lose her, she knows her marriage will fall apart partly because of the choice she makes but she still chooses that life. Her choice wasn’t solely because “love is worth the pain.” But does something ending tragically make the happiness that precedes it any less real? if you knew exactly when and how you would lose someone, would loving them become meaningless? or would knowing how temporary it is make every moment with them infinitely more precious? The ultimate choice was choosing to live the entire experience, regardless of its ending. there’s something so beautiful yet terrifying about accepting your life as a whole rather than judging it solely by where it leads. Can’t stop thinking about this movie. Would I  willingly walk into the greatest grief of my life just to experience the love that comes before it? Thank you for the existential crisis villeneuve incredible.

exemplo: As reviews destacam a reflexão sobre tempo não linear, a aceitação do sofrimento e a decisão de viver plenamente mesmo conhecendo as dores futuras.
texto: Derrière son apparence de science-fiction, Premier Contact est avant tout une réflexion sur le temps, l’amour et le deuil. Denis Villeneuve pose une question d’une profondeur rare : si nous connaissions à l’avance les joies et les épreuves qui jalonneront notre existence, choisirions-nous malgré tout de la vivre ? Sans jamais chercher l’émotion facile, il apporte une réponse d’une grande délicatesse. Un film intelligent, profondément humain, qui continue à résonner bien après le générique.

texto: What a beautiful and devastating film this is. Because memory and association are strange and mysterious things, acting as both teachers and deceivers, Max Richter’s iconic composition “On the Nature of Daylight” has a profound effect on me whenever I hear it. I connect it to certain difficult experiences of loss and grief. Maybe that is why the piece has been used in so many films exploring those very themes. If someone asked me the question Louise puts to Ian, my answer would be different. If I knew my future contained love, but also the devastating loss of that love, and I had the power to change it, I would. Accepting future pain for oneself may be brave. Choosing it on behalf of others is a different moral question.

exemplo: O filme apela descaradamente à nostalgia, relembrando cenas e personagens do passado em vez de criar algo novo.
texto: As the end marker for a long running generation of marvel movies, Endgame unfortunately drops the ball in all ways that matter. A lame attempt at reconciling irreversible character and wider plot choices, this film not only disrupts long established character growth and progression, but it also abruptly cuts off any opportunity for what many would call a “happy ending.” Multiple beloved characters are given the “tortured male existence trope,” wherein their wider personality and moral identity are swept to the wayside in order to justify a new generation of characters to swoop in following their exit. For example, by both butchering Peggy Carter and Steve Rogers emotional maturation and individuality in order to manufacture a “romantic reunification” following Steve’s travel back in time, Marvel has essentially removed both Peggy’s autonomy outside of being “Captain Americas love interest,” as well as Steve’s long established faithfulness to Bucky Barnes and his dedication to serving the weak. In no world would Steve rogers abandon a freshly reintroduced to society Bucky, nor a disrupted world reeling with the sudden re-appearance of 50% of the world’s population. In his decision to abandon his shield and interrupt Peggy’s progression towards an accomplished life as a shield founder and agent, as well as her pursuit of future love and motherhood as expressed in the original timeline, Steve is making an exceptionally selfish decision—which as any Marvel fan is aware—is the antithesis of his character. This is just one of the irreconcilable changes made to a central character that insults years of character establishment and development, which is then followed by yet again a female character being fridged for the greater plot. First starting with Gamora in Infinity war and now Natasha in Endgame, it is clear to see that the writers find no use for these strong female characters in these last plot stages other than as a motivation for male suffering and lament. Gamora, both present and past iterations of herself (as featured in this film), have much more worth as a character representing long building abusive deprogramming and female strength and endurance in the face of tragedy, than as a “sad she’s different than my girlfriend” trope—as presented by Peter Quills reaction to her appearance. Prior to this, viewers are slapped in the face with the sacrifice of Natasha for the soul stone, where her death is framed as a noble sacrifice in order to allow Clint Barton to return to his family once the snap is reversed. While faithful to Natasha’s character, one can only reconcile so much with the fact that it had to be only female character of the original Avengers to lose her life first. This is especially exasperated by the emphasized female power scene in the final battle, where every female hero on scene band together to fight, almost as an attempt by the writers to apologize for killing off the woman who pioneered female superhero-dom in modern media not 40 minutes earlier. All in all, these are just some of the many faults within this movie—which in its essence is a blatant attempt to slap a crooked bandaid on Marvels obvious (and clumsy) transition to a newer generation of actors and characters. As entertaining as a battle packed, time travel action movie can be, Avengers Endgame is a lazy attempt at hopefully pushing viewers towards future projects as they kill off their favorite characters one by one. We can only hope that these new superhero’s will be given the opportunity to grow into characters of their own and establish a storyline outside of the shadow of their predecessors.

texto: Siguiente paso en la maratón Marvelita para estar un poco al día pre-Spiderman. Bastante sorprendido con que así sea el clímax final de 22 películas, porque realmente Infinity War sí se siente como tal y Endgame solo cumple la última hora y quizá en su planteamiento inicial. El histórico final de la anterior continua con un mundo casi post apocalíptico que me hubiera encantado que se explotara un pelín más. Tras ese inicio, la película claramente tiene el objetivo de llegar a una batalla final épica y falla clamorosamente en la manera de lograrlo. El planteamiento argumental es hacer viajes en el tiempo para robar las gemas del infinito, usarlas para revivir a todo el mundo y devolverlas a su lugar correspondiente para no generar líneas temporales caóticas. A las paradojas propias de las pelis de viajes en el tiempo no se le presta excesiva atención porque tampoco es el sitio, y así se permiten darle alguna patadita a la lógica. Eso funciona como excusa para hacer una especie de repaso a algunas pelis y personajes que se siente un poco liosa, anti climática y de una autorreferencialidad  que juega en contra de la épica de la peli. Esa vuelta a espacios de pelis anteriores sirve como excusa para traer a Thanos (el de la línea temporal actual está muerto) de vuelta, mucho menos desarrollado e interesante que la anterior. Además, lo más grave, es poco consistente con lo ocurrido ya que el personaje parece reaccionar a cosas que él no ha vivido. Por ejemplo, critica a los humanos por no haber sabido aprovechar su plan y por ello los condena a desaparecer para crear un nuevo mundo de cero. No queda natural y parece mucho más villano básico que en la anterior. texto: Infierno en el espectáculo más grande sobre la Tierra Una de las películas más taquilleras de 1974 fue The Towering Inferno : un drama de cine catástrofe (y un poco catastrófico) cuyo título resume todo el argumento. En la tradición de The Greatest Show On Earth , The Towering Inferno es un desfile de cameos de actores famosos y dinero: todo es un aparato que fue acompañado por récords en ventas de entradas y hasta nominaciones al Oscar. Pero, pese a tantas entradas vendidas y noninaciones, ambas son películas que parecen haber sido relegadas al olvido hoy en día. El espectáculo (que se traduce en un juego de identificar los segundos de caras famosas cuando aparecen) se opone a la narración: hoy puede resultar más épico sobrevivir a las 3 horas de duración de cada uno de estos títulos que los desafíos que sus respectivos personajes enfrentan. El problema no es el "qué": es el "cómo" se muestra lo que se cuenta. Avengers: Endgame sufre un problema similar. No se trata de cuestionar decisiones argumentales. Hay una idea vertebral dando vueltas que recorre los laberintos del tiempo: ahí es cuando la película se vuelve más interesante. Cuando se aleja de los guiños para fanáticos que establecieron un contrato de lectura previo y de los planos generales de ejércitos incomprensibles sobre un fondo gris, cuando se centra más en los conflictos de los personajes que en las piruetas de héroes, sin peso ni alma, hechos por computadora. El pasado no se olvida pero tampoco puede repetirse: el Capitán América dice "we move forward". Hay una contradicción ontológica dentro de esa misma propuesta que funciona como espejo de las teorías de la imagen tiempo. Pero todo amenaza con diluirse en cameos y malabares logísticos (que tienen que ver más con los nombres que aparecen en pantalla que en innovaciones visuales o estéticas) para cerrar una historia que, con más torpezas que aciertos narrativos, lleva más de una década. La primera unión de los Avengers en la película de Joss Whedon conserva su energía: era la primera vez y estaba claro. Cada vez que se intentó replicar ese "momento" parecía perder más fuerza en la pantalla, aunque el leitmotiv sonara más alto y se amontonaran más y más personajes. A veces menos es más. La cacofonía visual no es sinónimo de emoción y lo que alguna vez fue novedoso ya se convirtió en rutinario. A esta altura uno puede identificar una estructura narrativa definida que incluye referencias pop (en especial, de la década del '80) y algún chiste inocente que contrasta con añadidos serios y dramáticos subrayados por música y encuadres solemnes que desentonan con el espíritu que los precedía. Más triste es que algunos personajes queden relegados a ser un Deus ex machina y que parezcan la representación simbólica no irónica del famoso "debo irme, mi planeta me necesita" de Los Simpson . ¿Por qué forzar personajes interesantes a estar solo para la foto cuando podían ocupar roles más interesantes? Son decisiones artísticas, y algunos no tendrán problema con ellas, pero Endgame no tiene la cohesión narrativa de historias corales tipo Nashville , City Of Angels o Magnolia , aunque lo intenta y eso no es un detalle menor. Infinity War funcionaba porque entendía que los héroes se definen en acciones antes que en palabras. A las piñas: como también sucedía en The Avengers . Tenía un personaje con un arco dramático definido y dividía el tercer acto en tres espacios distintos para darle lugar a cada línea dramática. El montaje en paralelo estaba justificado y adquiría sentido de urgencia. Ni el villano quedaba diluido en el medio del caos ni los héroes se amontonaban. Si todo es épico, nada es épico. Pasaron apenas diez años pero el cine de superhéroes se convirtió en algo tan despersonalizado y homogeneo que, en contraste, películas de estudio como Iron Man , The Dark Knight , Watchmen o Hellboy II muchos las reconocen ahora como productos artesanales que tenían algo para decir sobre el estado del arte y del mundo. Quizás todo se vuelva tan prefabricado y difícil de diferenciar que digamos lo mismo de Endgame en 10 años.

texto: Siguiente paso en la maratón Marvelita para estar un poco al día pre-Spiderman. Bastante sorprendido con que así sea el clímax final de 22 películas, porque realmente Infinity War sí se siente como tal y Endgame solo cumple la última hora y quizá en su planteamiento inicial. El histórico final de la anterior continua con un mundo casi post apocalíptico que me hubiera encantado que se explotara un pelín más. Tras ese inicio, la película claramente tiene el objetivo de llegar a una batalla final épica y falla clamorosamente en la manera de lograrlo. El planteamiento argumental es hacer viajes en el tiempo para robar las gemas del infinito, usarlas para revivir a todo el mundo y devolverlas a su lugar correspondiente para no generar líneas temporales caóticas. A las paradojas propias de las pelis de viajes en el tiempo no se le presta excesiva atención porque tampoco es el sitio, y así se permiten darle alguna patadita a la lógica. Eso funciona como excusa para hacer una especie de repaso a algunas pelis y personajes que se siente un poco liosa, anti climática y de una autorreferencialidad  que juega en contra de la épica de la peli. Esa vuelta a espacios de pelis anteriores sirve como excusa para traer a Thanos (el de la línea temporal actual está muerto) de vuelta, mucho menos desarrollado e interesante que la anterior. Además, lo más grave, es poco consistente con lo ocurrido ya que el personaje parece reaccionar a cosas que él no ha vivido. Por ejemplo, critica a los humanos por no haber sabido aprovechar su plan y por ello los condena a desaparecer para crear un nuevo mundo de cero. No queda natural y parece mucho más villano básico que en la anterior. La última hora vuelve a ser increíble, la batalla final es espectacular y el final con el sacrificio de Iron Man (que inició el MCU y acabó con él hasta ese momento) es muy emotivo.

texto: Mit ‚Avengers: Endgame‘ findet Phase 3 des MCUs nun ihr vorläufiges Ende. Zeigt man sich zu Beginn noch ungewohnt ernst und erwachsen, so nimmt der Humor und der typische Marvel-Charme spätestens im zweiten Drittel komplett überhand und an Dramaturgie ist bis zum großen Finale kaum mehr zu denken. Bei dem knallt es dann aber wieder richtig. Also doch irgendwie wieder die typische Marvel-Blaupause ohne großartige emotionale Fallhöhe, nur diesmal ruhig, ausgedehnt und in XXL-Länge. Fans werden vor lauter Fanservice fast den Verstand verlieren und das Kino mit Freudentränen in den Augen verlassen. Aber nüchtern betrachtet gegenüber ‚Infinity War‘ oder gegenüber Sternstunden wie ‚Captain America: The Winter Soldier‘ ist ‚Avengers: Endgame‘ eher schwach.
