texto: Honestly, upon rewatching these movies, as decade-defining as it was to see the Avengers movies in theaters, they just don't hit the same on home release. Like they're plenty entertaining, and Infinity War is genuinely a great movie, but the payoff and subsequent downward trend of the MCU movies that directly followed this one (which has recently gotten better with additions like the last 2 Spider-Man movies and Thunderbolts) just feels a bit exhausting rewatching this one. I think this more negative approach I'm having with this rewatch stems from the anxiety of the upcoming Avengers movie being centered around my favorite comic book character of all time, Dr Doom, who is miles more powerful and methodical than a character like Thanos. As well as the MCU's portrayal of the character was, Thanos could and should never hold a candle. Before the MCU was celebrated for giving a new life and dedicated following to all the B-list characters Marvel had to settle with due to the big 3 (Spider-Man, F4, and the X-Men) being owned by Fox and Sony, there was a legacy of iconic comic heroes and villains that spanned over half a decade. And within the culture of comics, if you asked someone to name a comic book villain from Marvel Comics, 9/10 you're not going to hear Thanos, Ultron, or even Venom. They will say Dr. Doom. To the comic fan, Thanos is a nice can of RC Cola, but Doom... Doom is Coke from a glass. Despite this level of hype this character is known for, his film adaptations have been genuinely terrible, to the point of being disrespectful (I'm looking at you F4 2016). I guess the point I'm trying to make is that the luster is being lost for me in this film, along with the decisions of the past and present, which make me enjoy this film a little less and make me especially nervous for the film that, as a Doom fan, should leave me feeling excited but is instead making me feel the complete opposite way. All I ask for is a faithful adaptation of Dr. Doom in some facet, and I can die happy.

texto: I was never the biggest fan of time travel movies. Sometimes they work really well (Back to the Future, Terminator 1 and 2, etc.). Sometimes they feel like a get-out-jail-free card when a story paints itself into a corner. The first half of ENDGAME feels a lot like the latter, playing as a greatest hits clip show just to remind us of the MCU's awesomeness. The back half works better in terms of emotion, especially as a close to both Steve Rogers and Tony Stark's storylines. It's the culmination of a decade's worth of buildup that we will likely never see again regardless of how DOOMSDAY or SECRET WARS turn out. I'm not sure which I like least: Jolly Green Hulk or Fat Thor. Is this the most superhero movie that a superhero movie ever superheroed?

texto: " I love you 3000 ".                      "It's Been a Long, Long Time". El cierre definitivo de una era que cambió la historia del cine comercial para siempre. Después de 11 años, 22 películas y docenas de arcos argumentales entrelazados, Avengers: Endgame no solo logra estar a la altura de las colosales expectativas, sino que entrega una experiencia cinematográfica épica, nostálgica y profundamente emotiva. La película equilibra magistralmente la melancolía del duelo tras las pérdidas de Infinity War con la esperanza, la acción a escala monumental y el humor característico del UCM . El viaje en el tiempo no es solo un recurso narrativo, sino una hermosa carta de amor a toda la franquicia, permitiéndonos revivir momentos icónicos desde una nueva perspectiva antes del enfrentamiento final. El clímax y la batalla final es puro espectáculo visual y fan service ejecutado con brillantez, pero su verdadero corazón reside en las despedidas. Darle un cierre tan digno, humano y perfecto a personajes con los que crecimos — en especial a Tony Stark y Steve Rogers — es el mayor logro de los hermanos Russo. Un hito generacional que difícilmente se volverá a repetir. "Avengers... assemble." — Steve Rogers "I'm gonna need a dance raincheck."

tema: Discurso feminista forçado e sem sutileza
exemplo: As críticas apontam que o filme martela sua mensagem feminista de forma exagerada, sem deixar espaço para interpretação, tratando o público como se não fosse capaz de entender subtextos.
texto: Barbie wants to empower women while apparently believing women can’t understand subtext. I’m still trying to figure out who this movie is for. Kids are too young to understand most of what it’s trying to say about womanhood, sexism, beauty standards, motherhood, careers and social expectations. And adult women absolutely do not need a two-hour movie explaining to them that being a woman can be difficult. I’m apparently old enough to understand patriarchy but not old enough to recognize a metaphor without Margot Robbie explaining it to me. It wants to tell women they’re intelligent, strong and capable while simultaneously refusing to trust them to understand a theme unless someone delivers a monologue explaining exactly what it means. That irony might be the most interesting thing in the entire movie.

tema: Discurso feminista forçado e sem sutileza

texto: Enfin vu le film le plus populaire de Greta Gerwig (et mon premier film d’elle par ailleurs). Malheureusement j’ai pas été emballé par la proposition. Je trouve que ça faisait trop mélange entre un long clip musical et une publicité/vitrine géante de « luxe » quasiment. On en fait trop d’ailleurs avec la musique durant tout le film c’est tellement fatiguant qu’un moment, il y a deux pistes musicales l’une sur l’autre c’est juste insupportable. C’est dommage parce que la propagande féministe est louable mais le message est entaché de dialogues un peu trop enfantins ou un peu trop débiles à mon goût même si je pense que c’est l’univers qui veut ça. Le fond est pas si mal mais la forme délivrée est pas subtile et trop gratuite. L’humour en général dans le film est lourd et certains tacles pas très biens sentis. Margot Robbie est vraiment top après Ryan Gosling et Will Ferrell m’ont saoulé un peu je vais pas mentir. America Ferrera et Ariana Greenblatt sont sans plus pour ma part. Il y avait tout dans le film pour en faire quelque chose de réellement iconique et en faire un très bon blockbuster. Le côté monde alternatif, les côtés positifs et négatifs de Barbie avec ses stéréotypes sur le corps et l’esprit féminin, montrer qu’elle était, est et sera une figure de proue des jeunes filles mais surtout à l’avenir, une figure d’émancipation féminine dans une société patriarcale. Seulement, ça manque de justesse dans la forme du propos pour que ce soit apprécié de tous, à n’importe quel âge.

texto: Barbie wants to empower women while apparently believing women can’t understand subtext. I’m still trying to figure out who this movie is for. Kids are too young to understand most of what it’s trying to say about womanhood, sexism, beauty standards, motherhood, careers and social expectations. And adult women absolutely do not need a two-hour movie explaining to them that being a woman can be difficult. I’m apparently old enough to understand patriarchy but not old enough to recognize a metaphor without Margot Robbie explaining it to me. It wants to tell women they’re intelligent, strong and capable while simultaneously refusing to trust them to understand a theme unless someone delivers a monologue explaining exactly what it means. That irony might be the most interesting thing in the entire movie.

texto: The film is just as plastic and artificial as the source material it’s based on. I was severely disappointed after I finished the film. It has no nuance, no depth and for me, it’s just a vapid, virtue signaling mess. The problem isn’t the moral core of the film, which I do agree with, but how it’s dealt with. In my opinion it feels surface level and strangely disingenuous. This isn’t helped by the story, which has no twists and no particularly strong plot, it’s just filled with a bunch of underdeveloped characters that flash their fake smile at you as they wave the films message in your face like a great pink neon sign. That being said, the film has its moments, but most of these come from the more silly joke driven bits and are quickly overshadowed by the “I’m fourteen and this is deep” level existentialism. It’s like Gerwig was torn between making a film for young girls and a serious feminist film, and then from that inner battle rose this compromise, which fails to deliver on either. Still, thanks for all the silly goofs it’s not unbearable watch, at times it’s almost entertaining. Though, it’s a crime that the song Barbie Girl was not once played. Shame.

texto: Enfin vu le film le plus populaire de Greta Gerwig (et mon premier film d’elle par ailleurs). Malheureusement j’ai pas été emballé par la proposition. Je trouve que ça faisait trop mélange entre un long clip musical et une publicité/vitrine géante de « luxe » quasiment. On en fait trop d’ailleurs avec la musique durant tout le film c’est tellement fatiguant qu’un moment, il y a deux pistes musicales l’une sur l’autre c’est juste insupportable. C’est dommage parce que la propagande féministe est louable mais le message est entaché de dialogues un peu trop enfantins ou un peu trop débiles à mon goût même si je pense que c’est l’univers qui veut ça. Le fond est pas si mal mais la forme délivrée est pas subtile et trop gratuite. L’humour en général dans le film est lourd et certains tacles pas très biens sentis. Margot Robbie est vraiment top après Ryan Gosling et Will Ferrell m’ont saoulé un peu je vais pas mentir. America Ferrera et Ariana Greenblatt sont sans plus pour ma part. Il y avait tout dans le film pour en faire quelque chose de réellement iconique et en faire un très bon blockbuster. Le côté monde alternatif, les côtés positifs et négatifs de Barbie avec ses stéréotypes sur le corps et l’esprit féminin, montrer qu’elle était, est et sera une figure de proue des jeunes filles mais surtout à l’avenir, une figure d’émancipation féminine dans une société patriarcale. Seulement, ça manque de justesse dans la forme du propos pour que ce soit apprécié de tous, à n’importe quel âge.

texto: Costumes and production design are 10/10 and I found the visual language of the climax to be really effective. It ends up working best as a screwball comedy with some genuinely hysterical moments littered throughout the film. Gosling is pretty much as great as you hoped he’d be. On the other hand, some of the bits don’t land at all and when the movie leaves the Barbie world, it really loses steam. Most of the real world stuff is oversimplified and unfunny. Lots of ink will be spilled about how this movie is either the future of feminist filmmaking or some kind of woke fever-dream that’s going to destroy cinema. It’s neither. And whichever side of the aisle you end up on, you’re giving Mattel the cultural conversation they wanted, which sucks because it feels unearned.

texto: Un film qui m’a plutôt surpris par ce qu’il cherche à raconter derrière son apparence de comédie colorée et légère. Barbie est évidemment très drôle et possède une identité visuelle vraiment réussie. Les décors, les costumes et la direction artistique donnent au film une personnalité qu’on reconnaît immédiatement. Margot Robbie et Ryan Gosling sont également excellents, avec un Ryan Gosling qui vole presque la vedette à chacune de ses apparitions. J’ai surtout apprécié le fait que le film ne se contente pas de faire une simple adaptation de la poupée Barbie. Il aborde des sujets plus sérieux sur les attentes liées aux hommes et aux femmes, l’identité et la place qu’on cherche à trouver dans la société. Cependant, malgré toutes ses qualités, je n’ai pas été aussi touché que je l’aurais voulu. Certains messages sont parfois un peu trop appuyés et le film m’a semblé perdre un peu de son charme lorsqu’il devient plus sérieux. Une comédie originale, drôle et très bien réalisée, avec de bonnes idées et d’excellentes performances, mais qui ne m’aura pas totalement convaincu.

texto: Costumes and production design are 10/10 and I found the visual language of the climax to be really effective. It ends up working best as a screwball comedy with some genuinely hysterical moments littered throughout the film. Gosling is pretty much as great as you hoped he’d be. On the other hand, some of the bits don’t land at all and when the movie leaves the Barbie world, it really loses steam. Most of the real world stuff is oversimplified and unfunny. Lots of ink will be spilled about how this movie is either the future of feminist filmmaking or some kind of woke fever-dream that’s going to destroy cinema. It’s neither. And whichever side of the aisle you end up on, you’re giving Mattel the cultural conversation they wanted, which sucks because it feels unearned.

tema: Crítica ao patriarcado e às expectativas femininas
exemplo: A review destaca o monólogo de America Ferrera como um retrato poderoso das contradições e cobranças enfrentadas pelas mulheres na sociedade, como a exigência de ser bonita, mas não exibida, e bem-sucedida sem parecer ambiciosa.
texto: “ É literalmente impossível ser mulher . Você é tão bonita, tão inteligente e me dói muito você pensar que não é boa o suficiente. Nós sempre temos que ser extraordinárias. Mas, de algum modo, estamos sempre fazendo errado. Devemos ser magras, mas não demais, e nunca dizer que queremos ser magras. Devemos dizer que queremos ser saudáveis, mas também temos que ser magras. Devemos ter dinheiro, mas não podemos pedir dinheiro, porque é grosseria. Devemos ser chefes, mas não más. Devemos liderar, mas não detonar as ideias dos outros. Devemos adorar ser mãe, mas não falar dos filhos o tempo todo. Devemos ter uma carreira, mas também cuidar sempre de outras pessoas. E responder pelos maus atos dos homens, o que é loucura, e ainda caladas, pra não nos chamarem de reclamonas. Devemos ficar bonitas pra eles, mas não tanto a ponto de tentá-los ou ameaçar outras mulheres, porque devemos ser parte da sororidade, mas nos destacando . E devemos sempre ser gratas. Mas lembrar que o sistema é fraudado. Devemos reconhecer isso, mas ser sempre gratas. Jamais devemos envelhecer , jamais ser rudes, jamais nos exibir, jamais ser egoístas, jamais vacilar, jamais fracassar, demonstrar medo, jamais passar do limite. É difícil demais, é contraditório demais, e ninguém te dá uma medalha ou te agradece . Acontece que, não só você está fazendo tudo errado, mas também tudo é culpa sua. Estou tão cansada de ver a mim mesma e todas as outras mulheres nos desdobrando pra que as pessoas gostem de nós…” Esse monólogo da America Ferrera diz tudo. Pra esse filme ser *perfeito só faltou a parte de que a Barbie pode ser empoderada e também apaixonada pelo Ken. Namoral eu queria o romance :|

texto: It is the most consoling thing as a young woman to see a film that completely verifies the experiences I have had. The unattainable goals of a ‘modern’ woman that have left us in spirals that allow the patriarchy to thrive. I watched the film late after release, so I had already read a lot of opinions about the film and honestly I came in expecting something else. From the reviews of men I was expecting a man hating movie that ultimately said women are the better sex. Which was so far from the point, and quite ironic that so many men have concluded that this was the message of the film. Kens struggle to become more than just an accessory to Barbie is the embodiment of what women have fought against for generations. And even though we preach about the empowerment we try to give women, we still find ourselves searching for that male validation.

texto: We have to take note that the society in Barbie's world is a horrible system. It is beneficial to women therefore it oppresses the men.. for example, the kens are treated the same way women are treated in our real world. Unequal and unfair treatment, in simplier words; Barbie's world are only a reverse gender society where instead of having the women oppressed, it's the men being oppressed. I could totally agree that it works as a feminist film, a representation for women therefore it's not a perfect film for feminism. It works well with portraying women's daily struggles, but if it were to be a feminist film, it wouldn't be a perfect fit. Our patriarchal society has engraved in our minds that women are simply lower than men as the default—but in a Matriarchal society, we believe the women can serve as better leaders than men does because of women's regulation of emotions. We can never truly achieve the total equality in our society when the case is arguing wether which gender performs better than the other.

texto: Barbie was surprisingly great and funny. My best friend and one of my Regal coworkers, Ezekiel enjoyed the movie too. Barbie is directed by Greta Gerwig, who previously directed Lady Bird and the 2019 Little Women. This movie stars Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling, Will Ferrell, Michael Cera, Kate McKinnon, Rhea Perlman, etc. Barbie and Ken are having the time of their lives in the colorful and seemingly perfect world of Barbie Land. However, when they get a chance to go to the real world, they soon discover the joys and perils of living among humans. This movie was actually great. It really surprised me and the movie was so freaking funny! The scenery was really cool, Barbieland looked like an actual Barbie play set. The humor was hilarious, especially Will Ferrell as the CEO of Mattel. Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling were really good as Barbie and Ken. My Barbenheimer experience is now complete! Between this and Oppenheimer, I enjoyed Oppenheimer a lot more. But this was still a fun movie. I’m actually glad that I saw this movie with my Regal coworkers. It was fun going to an employee screening for the movie. So overall, Barbie was a great movie and I’m gonna give Barbie 4 stars out of 5. I recommend it. Thanks for reading my Barbie review! 💅🏻💄

texto: La película es bastante chula, y tiene bastante carga emocional, que es contrarrestada por el personaje de Ken para no hacerla tan pesada. La actuación de Margor y Ryan es simplemente increíble. Tiene un gran mensaje y muy importante que mucha gente no entendió o no quiso escuchar. Además el marketing para esta película fue increíble, porque con la tontería de ir todo el mundo de rosa al cine a verla, logró que me vistiera de rosa y fuera al cine con mi grupo de amigas. La peli si que se me hizo pesada en algunas partes, pero también me emociono mucho el bonito mensaje por la lucha por la igualdad y como reflejaron como nos sentimos a veces las mujeres. Y ya para rematar, había puros temazos en la pelicula. "I'm just Ken" es una canción súper divertida y pegadiza. En resumen. Amo a Margot. Amo a Ryan. Amo el personaje de Barbie. Amo el personaje de Ken porque al final acaba entendiendo todo. Y esta película, aunque se me haría pesada de volver a ver, se ha guardado un lugar en mi corazón.

texto: I think Barbie is one of those movies I wish every little girl could watch before the world gets the chance to tell her who she is supposed to be. Because underneath all the pink and glitter, it is a story about becoming a woman. About growing up and slowly realizing that there is no version of yourself that will ever be enough for everyone. Be beautiful, but not vain. Be smart, but not intimidating. Be strong, but still soft. Have ambition, but don't make anyone feel small. Be independent, but still be desirable. How exhausting it is to be a woman and constantly feel like you're failing at a set of rules that were never meant to be followed. And then Barbie asks you to let all of that go. To exist without having to be perfect. To be messy, uncertain, angry, joyful, ordinary. To grow older without believing you've become less valuable. To understand that your worth was never supposed to depend on how well you fit into someone else's idea of a woman. Maybe that's why this movie means so much to me. I wish little girls could see it before they learn to shrink themselves. Before they learn to apologize for taking up space. Before they learn that being loved sometimes means becoming smaller. I want them to grow up knowing that they don't have to be the prettiest, the smartest, the kindest, or the most accomplished person in the room. They just have to know that their life belongs to them. And maybe that's what Barbie really changed for me: Being a woman isn't about becoming the perfect version of yourself. It's about finally realizing you were never meant to be a version of anyone else.

texto: We have to take note that the society in Barbie's world is a horrible system. It is beneficial to women therefore it oppresses the men.. for example, the kens are treated the same way women are treated in our real world. Unequal and unfair treatment, in simplier words; Barbie's world are only a reverse gender society where instead of having the women oppressed, it's the men being oppressed. I could totally agree that it works as a feminist film, a representation for women therefore it's not a perfect film for feminism. It works well with portraying women's daily struggles, but if it were to be a feminist film, it wouldn't be a perfect fit. Our patriarchal society has engraved in our minds that women are simply lower than men as the default—but in a Matriarchal society, we believe the women can serve as better leaders than men does because of women's regulation of emotions. We can never truly achieve the total equality in our society when the case is arguing wether which gender performs better than the other.

texto: Μπορεί να φαντάζει στην επιφάνεια ως ένα σκοτεινό, κανιβαλιστικό love story που μπλέκει το κόκκινο του έρωτα με το κόκκινο του αίματος, στην βάση του όμως το "Bones and All" του Λούκα Γκουαντανίνο δεν είναι τίποτα παραπάνω από ένα άτυπο companion piece του Call me by your name, μία χαμηλότονη δηλαδή ερωτική ιστορία που φαντάζει στους ήρωές της κοσμοϊστορικών διαστάσεων, όσο οι ίδιοι ανακαλύπτουν τον εαυτό τους και ψάχνουν να βρουν την θέση τους σε έναν επιθετικό και επικίνδυνο κόσμο. Με έναν φανταστικό Timothée Chalamet και μια αποστομωτική Taylor Russell στους πρωταγωνιστικούς ρόλους αλλά και έναν εντυπωσιακό θίασο περιφερειακών χαρακτήρων που αποτελεί το καλύτερο guest ensemble των τελευταίων χρόνων (από Mark Rylance μέχρι Chloë Sevigny κι από David Gordon Green μέχρι Jessica Harper!), ο Γκουαντανίνο αποδεικνύει πόσο καλά μπορεί να αφουγκραστεί την σιωπή μετατρέποντάς της σε θόρυβο, πόσο καλή γνώση του genre κινηματογράφου έχει τελικά, μετατρέποντάς τον σε κάτι απλό, καθημερινό, οικουμενικό και πόσο καλά μπορεί να μετατρέπει μικρές στιγμές σε τεράστιες, πατώντας παύση σε όλα όσα συμβαίνουν τριγύρω. Θα μπορούσα να αρκεστώ και μόνο σε αυτές τις στιγμές, είναι με διαφορά οι καλύτερες σκηνές ολόκληρου του φιλμ.

texto: Μπορεί να φαντάζει στην επιφάνεια ως ένα σκοτεινό, κανιβαλιστικό love story που μπλέκει το κόκκινο του έρωτα με το κόκκινο του αίματος, στην βάση του όμως το "Bones and All" του Λούκα Γκουαντανίνο δεν είναι τίποτα παραπάνω από ένα άτυπο companion piece του Call me by your name, μία χαμηλότονη δηλαδή ερωτική ιστορία που φαντάζει στους ήρωές της κοσμοϊστορικών διαστάσεων, όσο οι ίδιοι ανακαλύπτουν τον εαυτό τους και ψάχνουν να βρουν την θέση τους σε έναν επιθετικό και επικίνδυνο κόσμο. Με έναν φανταστικό Timothée Chalamet και μια αποστομωτική Taylor Russell στους πρωταγωνιστικούς ρόλους αλλά και έναν εντυπωσιακό θίασο περιφερειακών χαρακτήρων που αποτελεί το καλύτερο guest ensemble των τελευταίων χρόνων (από Mark Rylance μέχρι Chloë Sevigny κι από David Gordon Green μέχρι Jessica Harper!), ο Γκουαντανίνο αποδεικνύει πόσο καλά μπορεί να αφουγκραστεί την σιωπή μετατρέποντάς της σε θόρυβο, πόσο καλή γνώση του genre κινηματογράφου έχει τελικά, μετατρέποντάς τον σε κάτι απλό, καθημερινό, οικουμενικό και πόσο καλά μπορεί να μετατρέπει μικρές στιγμές σε τεράστιες, πατώντας παύση σε όλα όσα συμβαίνουν τριγύρω. Θα μπορούσα να αρκεστώ και μόνο σε αυτές τις στιγμές, είναι με διαφορά οι καλύτερες σκηνές ολόκληρου του φιλμ.

texto: “The world of love wants no monsters in it.” Até os Ossos é um filme que eu gostei bastante, mas com um nó atravessado que demorei pra nomear. Ele é lindo de ver, tem duas atuações que me seguraram, tem uma metáfora potente, e ainda assim eu saí dele sentindo que faltou alguma coisa pra ele virar a obra que claramente queria ser. Eu gostei mas com ressalvas. A história acompanha a Maren e o Lee, dois jovens que compartilham a mesma condição, são canibais por natureza. Luca Guadagnino transforma isso em um road movie pelos Estados Unidos dos anos 80, os dois cruzando estradas vazias, cidades pequenas, motéis, tentando existir num mundo que jamais aceitaria o que eles são. É um romance sobre dois outsiders se encontrando, se reconhecendo, e descobrindo que talvez não estejam tão sozinhos quanto pensavam. E é aqui que mora o que eu mais gostei. O canibalismo, no filme, é metáfora de ser diferente, de carregar dentro de si uma coisa que a sociedade lê como monstruosa, de amar e desejar de um jeito que o mundo insiste em condenar. A fala de Janelle diz tudo, o mundo do amor não quer monstros dentro dele. É sobre não caber, sobre ser empurrado pra margem por uma natureza que você não escolheu, sobre procurar outra pessoa que carregue a mesma fome pra não ter que carregar sozinho. Essa leitura é o que sustenta o filme. Mas é também na metáfora que mora parte do meu incômodo, e é um incômodo dividido. Porque o filme nunca decide de tudo o que o canibalismo é. Ora é símbolo do outsider, ora é vício, ora é o amor absoluto de se entregar por inteiro a alguém, e ao mesmo tempo é uma coisa literal. Essa indefinição é meio faca de dois gumes pra mim, parte dela é exatamente o que me agrada, essa abertura pra ler o filme de vários ângulos, mas parte dela me deixa incomoda, com a sensação de que o filme não sabe direito o que quer dizer com a própria imagem central. Senti que Até os Ossos quer ser coisas demais ao mesmo tempo. Ele é road movie, é romance, é terror, é coming-of-age, e nem todas essas peças encaixam com folga. Tem horas em que ele parece uma sucessão de cenas belíssimas que não terminam de formar um quadro só. Cada pedaço isolado funciona, a fotografia é deslumbrante, os momentos de terror são bons, o romance convence, mas o conjunto fica disperso, sem a coesão que faria tudo isso virar uma coisa inteira. Até os Ossos é um filme que eu gostei de verdade, que me deu imagens interessantes, com atuações de Timothée Chalamet e Taylor Russell que merecem o crédito. Só não me pegou por completo, porque ele se espalha demais.

texto: Träumer Kino der schönsten und seltsamsten Sorte, das vielleicht gar nicht so das großartige Werk mit Metaphern aufgeladen ist, sondern eher eine kleine sympatische Kuriosität. Bones and All würde ist ein wenig bizarr und voller Gegensätze, aber im Kern würde ich sagen, es ist eine Außenseiter-Story, wie man ein Leben lebt mit einem let's call it "Lebensstil", der als problematisch angesehen wird. Dazu gehört sowas wie, dass sobald das Leben unerträglich wird, man Gleichgesinnte findet, die einem Halt geben, das Konzept fatalistischer Liebe und natürlich ganz viele Bilder, die ein Midwest-Roadtrip so gemütlich machen, wie man ihn sich nur vorstellt. Der krasse Gegensatz ist dann natürlich der Part, wo Maren und ihre vielen Bekanntschaften Menschen essen, aber auch das wird weirdly eklig faszinierend eingefangen und wirkt gegen Ende fast schon karthatisch. So ganz konnte ich mir keinen Reim auf diesen Aspekt der Geschichte machen, aber wie gesagt ist der Film sehr laid back und hat mir eher etwas Komfort mit dem Gefühl gegeben, wenn man im Leben einsam ist und sich anders und missverstanden fühlt. In gewisser Weise ist es auch ein Coming of Age Film. Aus Marens Perspektive beginnt ihr Leben erst so richtig, als ihr Vater sie zurücklässt und sie die Welt auf eigene Faust, ohne einen Vormund, entdeckt. Sie lernt noch viele andere Menschen wie sie kennen und irgendwann wird klar, dass im ganzen Land eine Art Community existiert, die ihre Dränge unterschiedlich ausleben, aber alle versteckt vor der allgemeinen Gesellschaft leben. An der Stelle geht der Lebensstil von Maren und Lee auch perfekt mit der im Midwest geprägten Armut einher. Man kann sich nirgends niederlassen, entwickeln, ist generell misstrauisch und kann morden und rauben wie es einem beliebt, weils eh kaum jemand nachverfolgt. Am Ende ist Bones and All für mich weniger Horror oder große Metapher als einfach ein stimmungsvoller Roadtrip über Einsamkeit, das Heranwachsen und das Bedürfnis, irgendwo dazuzugehören. Nicht jede Idee geht für mich komplett auf, aber Luca Guadagnino erschafft daraus so eine eigenartige Wohlfühlmelancholie, dass ich mich in der seltsamen Perspektive von Maren und Lee total verloren habe.

texto: Could this movie not get Goodyear to sponsor the tires? I can't imagine Goodyear would have turned down the opportunity to be in a Pixar movie. (Movie description in bold at the bottom) By the time The Incredibles (2004) came out, I was beginning to get too old for Pixar movies. I was a teenager and wanting to start enjoying more older fare. With this being said, I stopped watching a lot of Pixar films after Incredibles . Cars was the first one I didn't see, and now, on the 20 year anniversary of the films release, I feel like I really didn't miss much. Cars feels like Pixar's first real cynical movie; making a movie that feels like it was done as a vehicle (pun unintended) to sell toys first and a good movie second. This is odd considering this is the company that made the Toy Story franchise. Between world mechanics that get too confusing, and a story that just isn't interesting, Cars feels like the first real wiff in Pixar's history of great quality films. While the car mechanics can get confusing, there are aspects of the world design that are kind of nice. Examples include Sally Carrera's (Bonnie Hunt) hotel which are shaped like traffic cones (you just have to forget that this is influenced by Native American teepees) and a doctor's office being just a car mechanic shop. There are also some really nice landscapes of the American desert, which look really good. Cars are meant to take us from point A to point B. Cars asks if this go go lifestyle is really that good. It pines for the old days when experiencing life was part of living. This is done through Route 66, which traveled in a maundering way that worked with the land, instead of through it. When the interstate was built, it bypassed Radiator Springs, and car travel became simply about the destination. Cars is bringing up points that were explored in media like Fahrenheit 411 , where people travel so fast they can't see the world around them. The message of the film does work overall, and is a saving grace for the movie. The problem with the movie is the world of the Cars. As I watched the film, I got more frustrated as to what is considered a car thing and what is a take on human things. Why does Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson) have a human-like tongue? What is Mack (voiced by John Ratzenberger) being bullied by a bunch of punk cars a parallel to in human form? Do all these cars have the life expectancy of people? By the time the movie got to the halfway point, I settled into just going with the fact that sometimes the cars are just car stuff, and the human stuff is just human stuff that the movie is doing. However, the fact that my mind was consumed with these questions as I was watching the movie is a bad sign for the movie. The cast is overall good in this movie, and it was nice to hear Paul Newman, in his last appearance in a non-documentary, but this movie does one thing that is unforgivable. It establishes a forever legacy for Larry the Cable Guy. Larry as Tow Mater is by far one of the most annoying characters ever put to screen. His southern twang and just overall annoyance was something I just never got used to. Cars 2 has the reputation of being the worst Pixar film, or at least the first truly bad Pixar film, and since it features Tow in a bigger role, I can see why. A little of Larry goes a long way, but for me I wish Larry would go far away and never come back. This movie is just boring. I really didn't care about Lightning, or any of the characters. They are all so boring and add so little. This was a movie solely meant to sell toys. I guess it worked, since this was the first non Toy Story movie to get a sequel, but for Pixar I think we all expect better than a concept that seems more fit for a Saturday morning cartoon show than a feature length film. Then again, Transformers (2007) would come out the very next year and be one of the most profitable films of that year, so what do I know? In a world populated by anthropomorphic race cars, Lightning McQueen (voiced by Owen Wilson) is one of the best race cars in the world. After finishing in a three way tie with Chick Hicks (voiced by Michael Keaton) and Strip "The King" Weathers (voiced by Richard Petty), the three cars must go to California to race in a tiebreaker. On the way west, Lightening gets lost and finds himself in the decrepit town of Radiator Springs. After damaging the towns main road, Lightening must begrudgingly repair the road as he complains and gets more annoyed with this failing town. Seen at Landmark Guildford, Surrey, BC, Canada, 11:25AM, Aud 6.

texto: Carros é, com folga, o trabalho mais preguiçoso, conceitualmente bizarro e cheio de fórmulas batidas de toda a história da Pixar. Em vez de entregar a genialidade emocional ou a ousadia dos grandes trabalhos do estúdio, a animação parece uma propaganda gigante para vender brinquedo de plástico, embrulhada em uma Jornada do Herói tão burocrática, previsível e sem graça que beira o insuportável. O grande erro da narrativa está na tentativa de aplicar a clássica jornada do Joseph Campbell a um protagonista raso e mimado como o Relâmpago McQueen. Ele começa como o típico babaca egocêntrico e arrogante que precisa passar por provações para se transformar, mas o roteiro conduz essa redenção de forma tão robótica que nada ali convence. Ao se perder a caminho da Califórnia e destruir a rua da esquecida Radiator Springs, McQueen é forçado a ficar preso no interior, onde encontra o batido arquétipo do mestre recluso no Doc Hudson e o alívio cômico caipira na figura do Mate — que mais irrita do que diverte. A dita "transformação espiritual" dele ao descobrir o valor da vida simples não parece fruto de uma tomada de consciência orgânica, mas sim de uma imposição das circunstâncias, fazendo com que a lição de moral no clímax da corrida final soar puramente piegas, forçando a barra para transformar um esportivo vaidoso em santo de uma hora para outra. Além dessa estrutura dramática capenga, a própria lógica do universo é um buraco negro de absurdos. É impossível se importar de verdade com um mundo feito puramente de lataria, onde a existência de portas, janelas e calçadas não faz o menor sentido pela ausência total de seres humanos. Para piorar, a direção se perde em um segundo ato extremamente arrastado, parando a história para mostrar piadas infantis de carros assustando tratores e romances sem química nenhuma entre dois automóveis. Carros pegou a estrutura mais nobre da narrativa universal e a reduziu a uma história rasa de cidade grande encontra o interior, trocando a profundidade poética da Pixar por um amontoado de clichês comerciais.

texto: I have this recurring dream. It’s the dead of night. I’m walking down a street on the way from the station towards my old house. There’s a field to one side of me and the road to the other. The only light I see is the flickering orange light of the dim street lamps. The only sound is my feet touching the worm and dashed concrete. Suddenly I hear the distant noise of tires on tarmac. I am not nervous, not really, but I can hear that it’s going to drive passed me. I can hear it coming closer until I know it’s on the same street as me. I turn as the car passes me and I glance at it. It is a car and it isn’t. It’s a live car. There’s no driver and the car has a face. The face stares back at me. I hope to never see that face outside of a dream. The thing slows down and smirks at me. It is matching my pace as I try to turn away from it. The last thing I feel is its tire feet mount the curb and the last thing I hear is the car whispering something that sounded like the noise of lightning. Then I wake up.

exemplo: A trama segue uma fórmula batida de jornada do herói, com uma redenção pouco convincente e reviravoltas previsíveis, resultando em uma história sem originalidade.
texto: Carros é, com folga, o trabalho mais preguiçoso, conceitualmente bizarro e cheio de fórmulas batidas de toda a história da Pixar. Em vez de entregar a genialidade emocional ou a ousadia dos grandes trabalhos do estúdio, a animação parece uma propaganda gigante para vender brinquedo de plástico, embrulhada em uma Jornada do Herói tão burocrática, previsível e sem graça que beira o insuportável. O grande erro da narrativa está na tentativa de aplicar a clássica jornada do Joseph Campbell a um protagonista raso e mimado como o Relâmpago McQueen. Ele começa como o típico babaca egocêntrico e arrogante que precisa passar por provações para se transformar, mas o roteiro conduz essa redenção de forma tão robótica que nada ali convence. Ao se perder a caminho da Califórnia e destruir a rua da esquecida Radiator Springs, McQueen é forçado a ficar preso no interior, onde encontra o batido arquétipo do mestre recluso no Doc Hudson e o alívio cômico caipira na figura do Mate — que mais irrita do que diverte. A dita "transformação espiritual" dele ao descobrir o valor da vida simples não parece fruto de uma tomada de consciência orgânica, mas sim de uma imposição das circunstâncias, fazendo com que a lição de moral no clímax da corrida final soar puramente piegas, forçando a barra para transformar um esportivo vaidoso em santo de uma hora para outra. Além dessa estrutura dramática capenga, a própria lógica do universo é um buraco negro de absurdos. É impossível se importar de verdade com um mundo feito puramente de lataria, onde a existência de portas, janelas e calçadas não faz o menor sentido pela ausência total de seres humanos. Para piorar, a direção se perde em um segundo ato extremamente arrastado, parando a história para mostrar piadas infantis de carros assustando tratores e romances sem química nenhuma entre dois automóveis. Carros pegou a estrutura mais nobre da narrativa universal e a reduziu a uma história rasa de cidade grande encontra o interior, trocando a profundidade poética da Pixar por um amontoado de clichês comerciais.

texto: I have this recurring dream. It’s the dead of night. I’m walking down a street on the way from the station towards my old house. There’s a field to one side of me and the road to the other. The only light I see is the flickering orange light of the dim street lamps. The only sound is my feet touching the worm and dashed concrete. Suddenly I hear the distant noise of tires on tarmac. I am not nervous, not really, but I can hear that it’s going to drive passed me. I can hear it coming closer until I know it’s on the same street as me. I turn as the car passes me and I glance at it. It is a car and it isn’t. It’s a live car. There’s no driver and the car has a face. The face stares back at me. I hope to never see that face outside of a dream. The thing slows down and smirks at me. It is matching my pace as I try to turn away from it. The last thing I feel is its tire feet mount the curb and the last thing I hear is the car whispering something that sounded like the noise of lightning. Then I wake up.

texto: In theaters with Ethan Brooks (what a great day, what a great guy 🔥). We walked in on “Lightning! You ready?” The electricity that flowed through me from that statement could have caused a power outage. This was pure nostalgia, and a really neat experience because I remember seeing this in theaters in 2006. I’ve never had a 20 year gap between seeing something at the movies, and it made me feel quite old. Is this gonna start happening to me as movies are re-released through the years? And I noticed so much more this time, including the many innuendos. Fire soundtrack, a perfect and exhilarating opening 20 minutes, inventive mechanics, good morals, and hilarious Mater lines. “It’s the ghost light!!” totally got me. But I still fear that Pixar is just too basic in general. I want Ghibli. Give me Ghibli.

texto: There’s just something so fulfilling about getting to watch your childhood movie on the big screen for the first time ever, I mean damn, 6 year old me would be so happy. Cars was MY movie, the first movie I ever really loved, and it’s always gonna mean the world to me even though now I can say that every other Pixar movie from the 2000’s easily surpassed it. I can still find truly remarkable aspects of movies like Ratatouille, Monsters Incorporated, Up, and I can recognize these as truly landmark films in the history of animation. Cars isn’t that. It’s a simple, quaint little story that doesn’t do much to impress. What you see is what you get, but that isn’t really a bad thing? I mean sometimes it’s really nice to just sit down and watch something that’s just plain good, especially as a kid, I mean I could’ve been watching pure slop as a child and I absolutely did, but damn it, Cars isn’t slop. It has a ton of charm that even if it doesn’t wow me, I can absolutely respect the hell out of it.

texto: |EN| Cars John Lasseter , 2006 Cars is one of those movies that does exactly what it sets out to do, without ever managing to leave a particularly deep impression. Lightning McQueen's story is simple and fairly classic: an arrogant protagonist completely focused on success is forced to stop and experience a world completely different from his own, eventually learning to value the people and things he used to overlook. His redemption arc is predictable, but it works. Whenever the film wants to be emotional, it actually manages to get there, especially through the relationship Lightning builds with the people of Radiator Springs. It does not try to complicate its story, and that is probably one of its strengths. The screenplay is simple, straightforward, and well written, with plenty of humor and a pace that keeps the film enjoyable. The world of Cars is also a lot of fun to spend time in. Turning a universe entirely inhabited by cars into a kind of American road movie is a simple idea, but Pixar manages to build a coherent world around it, filled with memorable and likable characters. Still, the film never left me particularly impressed. Its themes are the familiar ones of growing up, humility, friendship, and rediscovering what really matters, but they are not explored in a way that feels especially original to me. It is a good animated film, entertaining, emotional when it wants to be, and perfectly suited to the audience it was made for. But, for me, that is pretty much where it ends. Nothing wrong with it, nothing extraordinary either: a solid film, but nothing more. |IT| Cars John Lasseter , 2006 Cars è uno di quei film che fanno esattamente quello che promettono, senza però riuscire a lasciare qualcosa di particolarmente profondo. La storia di Saetta McQueen è semplice e piuttosto classica: un protagonista arrogante e concentrato esclusivamente sul successo che, dopo essere costretto a fermarsi e a conoscere un mondo completamente diverso dal suo, impara a dare valore alle persone e alle cose che prima ignorava. Il percorso di redenzione è prevedibile, ma funziona. Quando vuole emozionare, il film riesce effettivamente a farlo, soprattutto nel rapporto che si costruisce tra Saetta e gli abitanti di Radiator Springs. Non cerca grandi complicazioni narrative e forse è proprio questo uno dei suoi punti di forza: la sceneggiatura è semplice, lineare e ben scritta, con una buona dose di umorismo e un ritmo che riesce a mantenere il film piacevole. Anche il mondo di Cars rimane molto divertente da vivere. Trasformare un universo interamente abitato da automobili in una sorta di piccolo road movie americano è un'idea semplice, ma Pixar riesce a costruirci intorno un mondo coerente e pieno di personaggi simpatici. Non è però un film che mi abbia lasciato particolarmente colpito. I suoi temi sono quelli classici della crescita, dell'umiltà, dell'amicizia e della riscoperta delle cose che contano davvero, ma non li tratta in un modo che mi sia sembrato particolarmente originale. È un buon film d'animazione, divertente, emozionante quando vuole esserlo e perfettamente adatto al pubblico a cui è destinato. Ma, per me, finisce sostanzialmente qui. Senza infamia e senza lode: un film riuscito, ma niente di più.

Radiator Springs has loads of personality, Doc Hudson is easily one of the strongest characters, and the racing scenes are still fun. texto: |EN| Cars John Lasseter , 2006 Cars is one of those movies that does exactly what it sets out to do, without ever managing to leave a particularly deep impression. Lightning McQueen's story is simple and fairly classic: an arrogant protagonist completely focused on success is forced to stop and experience a world completely different from his own, eventually learning to value the people and things he used to overlook. His redemption arc is predictable, but it works. Whenever the film wants to be emotional, it actually manages to get there, especially through the relationship Lightning builds with the people of Radiator Springs. It does not try to complicate its story, and that is probably one of its strengths. The screenplay is simple, straightforward, and well written, with plenty of humor and a pace that keeps the film enjoyable. The world of Cars is also a lot of fun to spend time in. Turning a universe entirely inhabited by cars into a kind of American road movie is a simple idea, but Pixar manages to build a coherent world around it, filled with memorable and likable characters. Still, the film never left me particularly impressed. Its themes are the familiar ones of growing up, humility, friendship, and rediscovering what really matters, but they are not explored in a way that feels especially original to me. It is a good animated film, entertaining, emotional when it wants to be, and perfectly suited to the audience it was made for. But, for me, that is pretty much where it ends. Nothing wrong with it, nothing extraordinary either: a solid film, but nothing more. |IT| Cars John Lasseter , 2006 Cars è uno di quei film che fanno esattamente quello che promettono, senza però riuscire a lasciare qualcosa di particolarmente profondo. La storia di Saetta McQueen è semplice e piuttosto classica: un protagonista arrogante e concentrato esclusivamente sul successo che, dopo essere costretto a fermarsi e a conoscere un mondo completamente diverso dal suo, impara a dare valore alle persone e alle cose che prima ignorava. Il percorso di redenzione è prevedibile, ma funziona. Quando vuole emozionare, il film riesce effettivamente a farlo, soprattutto nel rapporto che si costruisce tra Saetta e gli abitanti di Radiator Springs. Non cerca grandi complicazioni narrative e forse è proprio questo uno dei suoi punti di forza: la sceneggiatura è semplice, lineare e ben scritta, con una buona dose di umorismo e un ritmo che riesce a mantenere il film piacevole. Anche il mondo di Cars rimane molto divertente da vivere. Trasformare un universo interamente abitato da automobili in una sorta di piccolo road movie americano è un'idea semplice, ma Pixar riesce a costruirci intorno un mondo coerente e pieno di personaggi simpatici. Non è però un film che mi abbia lasciato particolarmente colpito. I suoi temi sono quelli classici della crescita, dell'umiltà, dell'amicizia e della riscoperta delle cose che contano davvero, ma non li tratta in un modo che mi sia sembrato particolarmente originale. È un buon film d'animazione, divertente, emozionante quando vuole esserlo e perfettamente adatto al pubblico a cui è destinato. Ma, per me, finisce sostanzialmente qui. Senza infamia e senza lode: un film riuscito, ma niente di più.

texto: Wow. I am not being hyperbolic when I say this: this is my favorite movie of all time. It has so much heart, so much depth, so many lessons, so many genuine laughs, and, yes, a couple of teary-eyed moments too. All in all, for me this really is the perfect movie. To anyone who looks down on this movie for having a fairly standard coming-of-age journey story or for it being 'just an animated kids movie,' from the bottom of my heart, fuck you. Doc and Sally are my favorite characters. Both of them have so much depth, and their voice actors both do amazingly. Paul Newman, of course, is the real star of the show. His voice just is Doc Hudson. RIP to the legend. Bonnie Hunt is a legend too. I'm just so grateful to my local theater for offering this 20th anniversary showing, because being 24 now and born just 4 years before this movie came out, I don't think I've ever gotten the opportunity to watch it on the big screen. And, what a beautiful theater experience it was. The entire time I was either smiling ear to ear, laughing out loud, or tearing up. I just love this movie. 5-year-old me did, too. Who could've guessed that that little kid would grow up to be such a film junkie, then would finally come back to Cars and feel like he's coming home. I'm so happy.

texto: Yes I do have quite a soft spot for this movie, I've seen it undoubtedly more times than any other movie over my entire life, and even still that doesn't make this a perfect or even great film for that matter. It carries echoes of John Lasseter's actual masterpiece, Toy Story 2 , yet stumbles through some weaker jokes and cheeky references, most of which I still have an affection for, but contrasted against 3 all-timer voice performances, this movie walks a tight line between generation-defining spectacle and reminders that this is still at its core an animated kid's movie from the 2000's. Hearing Paul Newman is the most obvious standout, bringing his classic charm to kids like me for the first time to drive home a simple yet timeless moral. Owen Wilson is a perfect other half to the main mentor/student dynamic, yet I can't shake the underlying discontent his character spends the first two acts reckoning with, especially with the context of his suicide attempt the following year. His career history of comedic roles aren't a crutch for this role, and instead the occasional vulnerability he shows makes this a surprisingly interesting undertaking for an otherwise straightforward narrative. Michael Keaton still consistently amazes me as the unforgettable asshole Chick Hicks, a role that proved to me how even Keaton's most random or commercial work has a special place in my heart existing long before I ever saw Birdman . As I get older I'll inevitably continue to love the dialogue of nostalgia and accepting change this movie presents even though the words themselves will never change, sometimes thats just what I want from cinema and this movie provides a window into my childhood like no other. Also why did Sally poop on McQueen when they were going for a drive that is just so strange.

texto: This movie is anti-capitalist but we're not ready f-oh who am I fucking kidding this is Letterboxd of course you're ready for that fucking conversation Watched the rerelease in theaters. It holds up in a lot of ways (especially atmosphere oh my GOD no one was doing 50s revivalism like Pixar), but I don't know if it holds up entirely compared to my childhood. The Doc Hudson storyline is in retrospect a little undeveloped until the sudden face turn at the end. However, at the same time, the film's central themes play into the structure of the story (in that the race itself is kind of unimportant) so it works in a strange way. For a movie titled " Cars " it's not really about racing, not even in the end like you'd think. It's honestly an anomaly when it comes to its structure and I admire it a lot for. It's not really an " adventure " film nor an " intense " one for the most part, which is pretty rare for a Disney film. I can't think of many other movies in their canon like it.

texto: Spielberg saisit l’occasion de ce scénario sans réalisateur pour faire son James Bond à lui après avoir été recalé plusieurs fois par les producteurs de la franchise. Le truc c’est que j’aime pas les James Bond… Je trouve que la mise en scène de la virilité ne fait généralement pas un film. Ici, c’est un peu pareil même si on ne suit pas un agent virile mais un duo policier/voleur glissant très vite vers le père/fils. Dans les deux cas, la bienveillance vis-à-vis de leur comportement désastreux agace. Et Brenda lâchement abandonnée ? Exclue du film comme une vieille chaussette. Et la mère ? Pourquoi ne mérite-t-elle pas le quart de la tolérance qu’on accorde au père ? J’entends que Spielberg veuille avant tout parler de difficultés économiques et de fin du rêve américain qui ne serait plus atteignable que par la triche et le vol mais non seulement ce n’est pas si original mais les vieilleries dans le regard m’ennuient. Spielberg s’identifie et ça donne un film désinvolte. Il y a de bons moments de pur genre avec des évasions rocambolesques qui sont pas mal mais ça ne sauve pas vraiment le film.

texto: It was a good time!! I felt that Leo DiCaprio really came through as more than 'pretty boy' here and that this was the beginning of the great movies to come by him. Leo DiCaprio plays the young Frank Abagnale Jr. who impersonates a PanAm pilot, a doctor, and a lawyer throughout his life to successfully con and pass millions of dollars in checks. Some surprise actors: Had no idea Christopher Walken, Ellen Pompeo, Jennifer Garner, or Amy Adams would be in this! Most notably, Amy Adams plays Brenda, the mousy, sensitive, nurse Frank works with. I thought her performance in this was heartbreaking and impactful. That said, I didn't think this was Tom Hanks' best movie. Tom Hanks plays Hanratty, the cop that is chasing Frank. I'm not sure if it was just from the script or seeing so many other Tom Hanks' movies, but it was difficult to place him here. I thought his standout moment was when he finds Frank in Montrichard, and this takes awhile to get to. Christopher Walken, on the other hand, is charismatic and intriguing throughout. I was almost waiting for him to surprise me and become a major villain somehow; but in this film, his character is filled with complexities and nuances.

texto: Una d'algunes de les que tenia pendents i ni m'ha impressionat ni m'ha decebut. No considero que sigui una obra aclaparadora perquè no té res que la faci sorprenent més enllà d'una història trepidant i excel·lentment narrada. Intueixo que això és el que provoca sensacions. Spielberg agafa la biografia de Frank Abagnale , un precoç estafador estatunidenc que causaria impacte a la societat nord-americana amb la seva habilitat per l'engany. Una cosa és tenir un bon material de fons i l'altra saber portar-lo a la pantalla gran d'una forma completament brillant. Em congratula veure que Spielberg ho aconsegueix i, aparentment, sense cap mena de dificultat. Com a espectador no necessites reflexionar en excés o estar atentíssim per no perdre't el mínim detall. És una pel·lícula que es gaudeix sola: té un ritme lleuger, molt viu i extremadament agradable. La crònica no és monòtona i presenta uns girs i ocurrències que traspassen el predictible. M'agrada pensar que tota història està precedida d'un missatge de fons, d'una intenció clara independentment de l'entreteniment. Aquí se'm complica més identificar-ho, no perquè no hi sigui, sinó perquè crec que se li dona menys importància. La inevitabilitat del protagonista per deixar de mentir és un tret que pot abordar certes reflexions, però per mi no arriba a una profunditat digna de menció. Frank Abagnale (un genial Leonardo DiCaprio ) fa de la mentida patològica el seu modus operandi, un comportament persistent i compulsiu que forma part de la seva identitat. Una característica visiblement present també en el seu pare (interpretat per un grandiós Christopher Walken ) que ens deixaria una metàfora molt il·lustrativa que després heretaria el seu fill: "Two little mice fell in a bucket of cream. The first mouse quickly gave up and drowned. The second mouse, he wouldn't quit. He struggled so hard that eventually he churned that cream into butter and crawled out." Frank Abagnale Sr. viu constantment en un món envoltat de fantasia, s'obliga ell mateix a viure en un ordre construït per les seves autocomplaences i vol sempre anar per un camí que no li correspon i no es pot permetre. Quan la realitat se li fa evident l'única cosa que sembla aprendre és traslladar les responsabilitats als seus perseguidors. La metàfora li serveix per arrossegar al seu fill amb el niu de l'adoctrinament. Projecta el seu ego i deixa de fer-li de pare per fer-li d'animador quan les seves decisions són notòriament reprovables. Aquest suport fa que Frank Abagnale Jr. sigui una versió "millorada" del que és el seu pare. Ell ja no menteix per benefici, menteix perquè li proporciona plaer i fa que la resta de mortals l'admirin. Utilitza constantment als qui l'envolten com a mers instruments a punt per ser manipulats. Tot això l'acaba convertint en un home exteriorment idíl·lic, però interiorment desert. Un narcisisme que, poc a poc i amb l'ajuda d'un agent de l'FBI (Tom Hanks), aconsegueix gestionar. Sí, és un relat de superació personal. No obstant l'anterior, la conclusió, amb tot el que comporta, és el postre en aquest menú de Spielberg .

texto: “Knock knock.” I've had many conversations with composers & friends about how much they were struck by John Williams’s opening credits music. The very first time at the cinema, I recall beaming at the screen – feeling the love for the Pink Panther movies & Henry Mancini. Instead of deploying his usual massive, brass-heavy orchestra, Williams curated a lean, intimate chamber ensemble focused on precise textures, including: - Solo Alto Saxophone: Played by renowned session musician Dan Higgins, the saxophone acts as the primary "voice". Its slinky, fluid lines mimic the nimble movements of Frank Abagnale Jr.. - Mallet Percussion (Vibraphone & Marimba): The vibraphone provides the characteristic mid-century jazz shimmer, while the woody timbre of the marimba anchors the lower rhythms. They frequently play interlocking triplet patterns together. - Tactile Sound Effects: The arrangement famously integrates finger snaps & human "shushes" directly into the percussion mix, instantly grounding the track in the jazz-club aesthetic of the era. Williams deliberately channelled the style of his own musical youth - when he was known as a jazz pianist named "Johnny Williams" - while paying homage to 1960s movie music masters like Mancini. And then this is my favourite Tom Hanks performance in a Spielberg movie. Hanratty is a straight man in a straight career, crunching numbers on criminals who have created new ways to crunch numbers. He is the perfect opposite of Frank. Hanks has physicality, but it’s a contained performance – all in the accent, stiff jaw & posture. “Next slide, please. Next slide, please.” Also have to give my respects to the twinkle in the eyes of Christopher Walken. The father/ son tale at the heart of this is pure Spielberg tragedy. Quite adjacent to the real-life tale, as is much of the movie – but those random restaurant meetings are just heart-breaking to watch. Thank goodness they never filmed his Central Station death as was planned. DiCaprio’s raw pain at learning about the death after-the-fact is pain enough. I haven’t loved anything by Spielberg as much in the quarter decade since. Part of my ‘Spielberg Phase’ of a LetterBoxd Review Catch-Up. Viewed courtesy of the Home Library

texto: Spielberg brilliantly sets the tone of Frank’s exploits as a game show, appropriating the very silly, very American craving for attention and flair for the spectacular(ly convoluted). I wonder how early on he knew it was all a ruse. A film about this self-fantasising myth-making as a craving, about the paradigm of greatness bringing out from deep beneath your soul a self-defeating, poisonous desire of making yourself seem larger than you really are - a mania quite indistinctive from America’s fascination with itself that naturally manifests in the entertainment industry. The film half-tries to argue itself as a tragedy about the power of will and talent recorrecting itself by the end, to project into the same Americanness with a much more blockbustery tone. A great director working the blockbuster formula for a critique of America’s spirit filled with plausible deniability. The long con of auteur blockbuster.

texto: I’m a huge fan of Leo Dicaprio and I recently started watching a lot of his earlier films. The story in this movie was captivating from the first scene. I loved the portrayal of the relationship between both Frank Abagnales. The cat and mouse chase all over the country between Frank and Carl, and their eventual mentor-mentor relationship was perfectly done. The cast is star studded and they all played their characters very well. The standout character is obviously Frank Jr - he is a complex character dealing with image issues as well as his need to be seen as what he’s incapable of being while being oblivious to his profound intellect and social capabilities.

texto: Kind of glazey to give a 5 star review but truly one of my favorite movies EVERRR. This movie was my introduction to Leonardo so maybe i’m completely biased but i love every aspect of it. I remember seeing it for the first time and falling completely in love with his acting…and looks too :,). The way Leo steals the screen everytime he acts; his charisma, aura, just everything he really did his big one. Leo has a way of really making you believe in his characters and get lost in every story he tells a KING in his prime. I love the relationship between Hanratty and Frank; the cat and mouse metaphor was really well portrayed, Tom and Jerry irl? It’s so sweet how he became almost a fatherly figure to Frank and so so sad the way Frank was basically raised to believe that forging checks was the way by his own, even if his father truly did love and care for him. I do love how no matter how wrong of a situation Frank had gotten himself into his father would still never give up his son, it truly shows the unconditional love between a parent and child and the way Frank did everything out of an almost pure innocence. He really was just a lost kid wanting nothing more than his family back, although he’s crazy for forging millions of dollars and multiple identities. (dramatized for the sake of a good movie.. but still) So sad Brenda gave him up, but valid lowkey. Crazy to think this was someone’s real life story they don’t make scandals like the 60s anymore….

texto: From the terrifying first trailer to the scathing reviews, I knew at some point in my life I was going to watch Cats. It was too much of an anomaly, too high-budget a disaster for me to ignore, I didn’t want to watch it, I HAD to see just how bad it was. And fuck me was this an absolutely terrifying fever dream filled with an uncomfortable amount of drugs, sex and music without having any drugs or sex and too much music. I’m genuinely scarred for having seen it all the way through. Let’s start with the plot. There isn’t any. And I’m not just saying that to be funny, this entire film is 90 minutes of introductions, 10 minutes of actual story and the other 10 minutes is weird panting and gyrating. Here I’ll give you a rundown of what happens; we open with our lead Victoria being abandoned by her owners, she’s introduced to the Jellicle Cats with their Jellicle Ball – and sidenote, they never explain what a Jellicle is and why it’s important to be one despite them saying Jellicle about 587 fucking times in the first five minutes – who take her to see the cats hoping to become the Jellicle choice and live a new life in the fucking sky or something. I swear to Christ, the little plot I can recognise as a story makes me think this is about a fucking suicide cult. From there Victoria meets Rebel Wilson’s hairy cooch, Jason Derulo’s CGI bulge, James Corden’s fat arse, a couple thieving twins who I couldn’t tell if they were related or not because of the fuck me eyes they were flashing at each other, Judi Dench’s old face and Ian McKellen making Meow noises before we actually get to the Jellicle Ball in which the contestants are STILL being introduced since the bad guy – Idris Elba and his unnervingly smooth fur body – has been stealing all the contestants with magic – oh by the way there’s fucking MAGIC in this film, they kinda dropped that on you without warning – so anyone who’s still taking part in the Ball we’ve never fucking seen before, making their musical numbers an exercise in futility because I don’t know them and I don’t want to fucking know them. Those two paragraphs cover around 80% of the story, all this film has is cats introducing themselves through song for an hour and a fucking half and then getting lucky if they have anything to say afterwards. It’s not a plot, it’s a fucking 2 hour montage of people we’ve never seen before and it doesn’t stop, new characters are still being introduced with their own numbers with over half the film already done. The only time it actually works is with Mr Mistoffelees who, despite a fairly low amount of screen-time, has been shown to be a cowardly magician and needs confidence to do Big Magic, that works but it comes so late into the game that it couldn’t save the rest of this train wreck. And before anyone dares defend this film, I know it’s based on a musical and I know it’s a different medium, but Hamilton managed to tell an entire historical story with only singing, this is just cats singing about themselves without a story to give them a reason to sing about themselves. The cast is absolutely stacked with big names who are given nothing to work with, and the ones that have something are the weakest actors in the film, I feel kinda bad for Francesca Hayward who plays Victoria because she’s suppose to be our lead, our surrogate into this bizarre, fucked up world of the Jellicle Cats and she’s given nothing, out of all the speaking parts she has probably the fewest amount of lines, every face she makes has this big wondrous smile about EVERYTHING, no matter how benign, and sure she dances well but in a film where everyone is dancing that doesn’t stand out. This is Hayward’s big theatrical break and she’s the most forgettable element in the film, which ironically might save her career. Out of everyone Victoria meets during the many MANY introductions she has to suffer through, not one of them make it worthwhile to sit through their number. Jason Derolo  - who I just hate in general anyway – sings about how Rum Tum Tugger  is a fussy little cunt then screams for milk, Mungojerrie and Rumpleteazer were the thieving twins who looked like they wanted to do a furry version of a Bratty Sis video, and I didn’t know they were twins until writing this review so that just knocks the film even lower for me. There was also a tap dancing train conductor who serves no fucking purpose, Ray WInstone hissing and wondering where the fuck his career has gone and Taylor Swift who even in a film filled with unnecessary sexual energy, gave off too much sexual energy. Seriously man, I got Lola Bunny flashbacks during her number. Worst of the lot was Rebel Wilson and James Corden as Jennyanyfots and Bustopher Jones respectively, I already dislike these two before going into the film and having them both talk the most out of almost any other character was a kick in the fucking dick. Wilson’s introduction was this disturbing piece where she did the most unsexy sexy poses while the camera focussed on her naked hairy body before bringing in singing mice and marching cockroaches with human faces which Jenny proceeds to eat several of when she’s not singing. Corden meanwhile sings for five minutes about being a fat fuck and eating a lot, that’s the entirety of his character, he’s fucking fat, and the fact that both of them are just allowed to skit and makes shitty jokes is simultaneously distracting from the actual plot while adding nothing to the plot either. Both of them were just playing themselves in fur suits and like I said I think both are fucking overdone anyway so I didn’t give a shit about them either way. The only people I see coming out of here unscathed are Ian McKellen and Judi Dench who both have strong enough careers to look past this blip, although Dench’s monologue at the end where she looks at the camera goes on WAY too long about how a cat is not a dog (the fuck?) and every pause makes you think that it’s finally over but no, she keeps fucking going. Jennifer Hudson as Grizabella should also be ok, despite being important to the film she only has three scenes but among those three is her version of the famous ‘Memories’ number which is unironically good, hell I’d say too good for this turd of a film. I’m also hoping that Idris Elba comes out of this unaffected, his villain Macavity is suitably villainous and his motivations generically evil enough – he wants to be the Jellicle Choice because Fuck You I guess – that Elba can work something out with the material but between nobody being able to recognise the most wanted cat in town and his own horrifying nude cat-body, I doubt he’s getting away from this thing clean. Director Tom Hooper has done a few things of note over the last few years, namely his last three films were all Oscar winners and he brought Les Mes to the big screen so I can see why he’s be chosen for this. But holy hell does he fuck this up, this has to go down as one of the biggest fuck-ups of direction of the 21st Century because while Hooper doesn’t do anything technically wrong, nothing he does is done right. Let’s get the big one out of the way; the cats look fucking weird, I knew the cats looked weird, I saw the trailer, I saw the memes, but nothing prepared me for the seeing them in full CGI horror, the first time I saw a Cat-Man clamber down a brick wall, looking like a human being contorting their body into some kind of fucking Cronenberg nightmare with a tail I realised that this was so much worse than I thought it was going to be. It’s the deepest level of the uncanny valley I’ve seen since The Rock in The Mummy Returns and that was 18 fucking years before this, nobody looks human but they don’t look like a cat either, they’re a disgusting hybrid of the two, these vaguely human looking faces pasted onto what looks like skin-tight cat-suits made with actual cat flesh, it NEVER sits right with you. What makes it even more uncomfortable is that there seems to be no rhyme of reason to the clothing, a few cats wear clothing but most of them are nude and some of them even take off their clothes making them nude and I’m left wondering if this is just a nudist colony with lax rules or if everyone is suppose to be naked and we’re just suppose to accept it. I know I shouldn’t be this focussed on naked cat people but I can’t help it, this movie has forces naked cat people into my fucking brain and given me no fucking logic about why they’re naked, hell I haven’t even touched upon the Rebel Wilson scene where she unzips her naked fur-body, as  in literally takes off her skin, to reveal a dance outfit underneath. It’s the tightness as well, I don’t know why they went out of their way to make the cats sexy but it just feels wrong, all the naked cat actors have all their curves pronounced so that every breast, every bulge, every butt covered in fur is on full display but without any form of genitals. Elba gets the worst of it because his fur colour is identical to his skin colour leaving him looking like a fucking Ken Doll with ears but not one person looks good like this. And that’s not even talking about how horny this film is, I heard the stories, I read the reviews that talked about how sexual the film was but it’s not until you’re seeing this cat people twist their bodies together, panting in unison and nuzzle into each other that you have to take a step back and realise that humans doing cat actions is trying way too hard to be sexy whilst not trying to be sexy. The Jellicle Ball is the most horrific example, it’s the hissing, the panting, the Judi Dench hairy leg spread, I honestly couldn’t tell you if the film was trying to be this sexual and went way too far or if it wasn’t trying at all and just came off that way by accident. I haven’t even touched upon the fucking music because I don’t know how to, the visual disaster overpowers the audio so much that I can’t tell if anyone actual sung during this film or not. Ok, over exaggeration, a few songs worked but only a few, the aforementioned Memories hit well and I was fine with the Mr Mistoffelees number but outside of them I really can’t remember any of the songs being any good. The opening introduction to the Jellicle Cats was upbeat I guess, I was too distracted by the CONSTANT use of Jellicle, Jennyanydots was too distracting with the human cockroaches and under-skin dress change for me to even remember what the song was. Tugger and Bustopher were both boring, end of discussion, McKellen’s small number as Gus felt like a lot of build-up for a limp-dick crescendo and Swift’s piece of Macavity trying to big him up almost worked as a villain song if I wasn’t distracted by the complete lack of Idris Elba penis. Before this film the only knowledge I had of Cats was hearing Memories here and there and the rape story from Team America, having now seen this film I know even less about Cats and I don’t want to know anything more about Cats. This is one of the strangest, most confusing, unsettling and fucked up pieces of cinema I’ve ever seen that wasn’t an intentional horror movie, I’ve never seen anything like Cats so 10/10 for uniqueness but just because nobody’s done it before doesn’t mean it’s a good idea and Cats the Movie was not a good idea. There’s no story, all we have is oversexed sexless Cat People introducing themselves for 2 hours before nothing happens and the film ends, nobody looks good, only a couple sound good, the CGI is a mess, the sexiness uncomfortable, the songs forgettable and the whole experience traumatising. I’d say you have to see it just to get the full picture yourself but honestly you’re safer avoiding this. 2/10

texto: Im slightly biased towards cats. It was the musical that made me fall in love with musical theatre and why have such an appreciation for it. Which may sound strange since it is so hated. In my defence i was young so i was easily impressed. So i don’t hate this film. It’s not amazing either. I think its biggest problem for me is the visuals. The whole cgi human/cats plus the cgi back grounds are severely distracting. I think if the set felt more real and they were in costume like the stage musical it may have looked better. Although cats is difficult since they are cats… I think the stage costumes could have such potential and the movie’s costumes could have been a strong point. Along with the costuming, the music and dancing are strong points for this musical. I wish it allowed more space for the dancing, less close up shots. The dancing cant be fully appreciated since the cgi cat/humans are distracting. I think the better visual would help highlight this, along with hiring strong dancers and ballerinas. The plot of cats is weak. I think the movie could have taken the opportunity to add a conflict to move the plot further. Maybe adding another song or two, along with beautiful ghost. A little more about victoria and how abandoned she is, her need to fit in with these cats she has met. Another point is the script/jokes which are also weak. If the writers/director were wanting to make a cats movie, i think expanding on it rather than a straight up adaptation would make more sense. The musical itself is weak in many areas. So the movie is weak and doesn’t exactly work because what works on stage does not guarantee it works on film. I think they should have made some serious changes. I also feel it lacks context, which leaves it confusing and boring at times. Maybe could have had Judy Dench narrate the film? The ending was of the film was underwhelming and the last song was boring. I enjoyed the film, i haven’t seen it since it came out. I just feel it is wasted potential. Maybe even a pro shot would have made more sense. Theres worse films out there. To be fair there is also better films out there.

texto: Yes, yes, it's absolutely awful! But the source material is already horrendous, and Tom Hooper had no business being given this big and blank a cheque at any point of his career. Plus, I do have a soft spot for the underdog (no pun intended), so given the scorn with which this is regarded, I've come round to finding it somewhat endearing. I've split the difference between 0 and 5 stars, though objectively I'd probably go with 1 and a half. The cast's output is thrillingly divergent. Some muddle through with their dignity essentially in tact (Dench, Swift, hey even Derulo!), while others invite pathos from the sheer degree of cringe inherent in their debasement (Corden, Wilson, dare I say McKellan?). Ultimately, though, it's a catastrophic failure of direction. But one I'm very glad exists! I need to screen record the bit where Judi Bench sadly responds "oh pussy!" lmaoooo me af

texto: I've seen this three times now, and every experience has just been more transcendent, more gloriously unhinged. I understand that, technically, theoretically, it's bad. But with a full crowd, it's a goddamn party.  The best, most riotously joyous time you'll have in a theatre this side of Gremlins 2. How can you honestly critique that? Other than to say, somehow, through all its flaws, ugly effects, and insane story decisions, Cats emerges as something that, in its own very specific way, is kind of a masterpiece. Alien and weird and awful and beautiful in a way no other film is. Never watch it alone. But never pass up the chance to see it with a packed house. It'll be one of the best theatrical experiences of your life. Long live Jellicle Cats. Long live Skimbleshanks.
