texto: Inception is a film made for the big screen. I remember it being exciting, new and so much fun on first viewing, so awe inspiring in theatres.  The movie falter a bit on repeat viewing, (there’s an emptiness that peaks its head out every once in a while), but it does hold up. I love that Christopher Nolan just decided to retro-fit this sci-fi story onto a heist narrative.  It works well! The team assembles, they all get their moments to shine, and they scatter with a knowing nod at the end of the robbery. This film has a LOT of things going on, it really walks a tightrope without managing to fall onto the hard pavement, although there are some close calls.  As is normal with a Nolan film, it’s too long. I think some of that could have been dealt with in the editing, but I’m not entirely sure what I would cut. It’s not really a detriment to the film, but why does Nolan insist on weird names like Ariatne? I get that there’s a literary reference there, but it’s a hard word for half the cast to say comfortably. But that ending is a corker! The spinning top.  The great musical swell by Hans Zimmer.

exemplo: A trilha sonora de Hans Zimmer é lembrada por criar uma atmosfera de mistério, urgência e grandeza, contribuindo para a imersão e o impacto emocional do filme.
texto: Desde el principio presenta una idea muy original: entrar en los sueños de otras personas para obtener o implantar información (como es el caso en esta película). Es un concepto complejo, pero la película logra desarrollarlo de una forma que se vuelve cada vez más interesante conforme avanza la historia. Lo que más me gustó fue precisamente el concepto de los sueños, las actuaciones y los giros de trama. La forma en que Nolan construye distintos niveles de sueños y hace que todos funcionen al mismo tiempo es algo que pocas películas han intentado hacer. Leonardo DiCaprio hace una gran actuación como Cobb. Además de liderar al equipo, consigue transmitir el peso emocional que carga durante toda la historia. También me gustó mucho la dinámica que tiene con los demás miembros del grupo, ya que hace que la misión se sienta más real y que te intereses por lo que les ocurre a todos. Mi escena favorita fue la batalla final. Es un momento lleno de tensión, acción y emoción donde todas las piezas de la historia comienzan a encajar. Además, la forma en que se conectan los diferentes niveles de sueños hace que la secuencia sea aún más emocionante. La música es otro de los puntos fuertes de la película. Ayuda a crear una sensación constante de misterio, urgencia y grandeza que encaja perfectamente con la historia. Algo que también me parece destacable es el uso de efectos prácticos. Nolan evitó depender completamente del CGI y utilizó escenarios reales, efectos físicos y cámaras IMAX para muchas secuencias importantes. Esto hace que escenas como los pasillos giratorios o los cambios de gravedad se sigan viendo espectaculares incluso años después de su estreno. Una película inteligente, emocionante y visualmente espectacular que demuestra por qué Christopher Nolan es uno de los directores más importantes.

texto: I’m LITERALLY obsessed with Inception. There’s something so immersive and almost unsettling about the way the film blurs the boundaries between dreams and reality. While watching it, I felt as though I was trapped inside a dream myself. I was constantly questioning what was real and what wasn’t. What I loved most is that it goes beyond being an incredible psychological thriller. It actually made me reflect on life, perception, memory, and the way we construct our own realities. It left me questioning how much of what we experience is shaped by our own minds, and whether reality is always as certain as we assume it is. It’s one of those films that doesn’t just entertain you, it stays with you and makes you think about it long after it’s over. It quite literally lingers - fav song reference lol.

exemplo: As reviews apontam que tratar o conflito como fantasia estilizada e vingança esvazia o peso histórico e soa desrespeitoso com o período retratado.
texto: BASTARDOS INGLÓRIOS Extremamente fraco, mal dirigido e, para mim, um filme ruim e até desrespeitoso. O maior problema é a maneira como Bastardos Inglórios trata a Segunda Guerra Mundial. A guerra e o horror nazista são transformados em uma espécie de fantasia estilizada, quase como se tudo tivesse sido construído para ser divertido e satisfatório. Para mim, isso tira muito do peso do período que está sendo retratado. E o humor também não funciona. É um filme para maiores de 18 anos, mas em vários momentos parece ter sido escrito para adolescentes que acham violência e palavrão automaticamente engraçados. Algumas cenas parecem existir apenas para virar uma edit no TikTok. A única coisa que realmente consigo elogiar é Christoph Waltz. Hans Landa é disparado a melhor parte do filme, e Waltz entende perfeitamente o personagem. Ele consegue fazer o sujeito ser carismático sem deixar de ser repulsivo, e sua atuação realmente merece todos os elogios que recebeu. Fora isso, não consegui encontrar muita coisa que me interessasse. Os personagens são pouco envolventes, o roteiro se apoia demais no estilo e eu pessoalmente não gosto da maneira como Tarantino dirige seus filmes. Violência estilizada e aquela necessidade constante de transformar tudo em uma cena “icônica” simplesmente não funcionam comigo. Talvez eu seja uma das poucas pessoas que realmente não entende todo esse amor pelo filme. Para mim, Bastardos Inglórios parece muito mais interessado em ser cool do que em dizer alguma coisa sobre a guerra que está retratando. -P.F. Prado

tema: Elogio isolado à atuação de Christoph Waltz
exemplo: Mesmo entre as críticas duras, muitas reviews reconhecem que a performance de Christoph Waltz é o ponto alto e o principal motivo para continuar assistindo.
texto: I was honestly surprised when I went back to Letterboxd and saw that this was a 4.4. It’s far off that for me. I know I started watching this when I was younger and stopped it. At the time, I think it was just for the gore, but maybe it was also me already knowing that I wasn’t going to like what the movie was. Also, clearly, my parents had absolutely no control over what I watched. But anyway. There were a few things I liked: Christoph Waltz’s performance, the colour choices, and… that’s pretty much it. I really didn’t like the pacing. There were so many scenes that felt unnecessarily prolonged and, to me, added very little to the story. And there are so many storylines that felt unfinished or underdeveloped. Honestly, I would have found the story of how the propaganda machine worked, how they turned Zoller into this heroic figure, made a movie about him, and used cinema as propaganda, so much more interesting. Or even Shosanna’s story: how she got the cinema, how she planned her revenge, and what she was actually trying to achieve. There was so much potential in both of these storylines. Instead, Zoller’s storyline becomes this weird thing where he seems almost harmless, even though he killed 300 enemies, randomly falls in love with Shosanna, and then, in the final moments, you actually see who he really is. I just kept thinking there was so much more that could have been done with these characters and their stories. And then, of course, the bane of my existence in movies: American soldiers coming to save the world. I’ve always hated that concept and I will always hate that concept. Apart from that, one of the things that annoyed me the most was how much time is spent building Hans Landa up as this terrifying and intelligent character, only for his story to end the way it does. He’s obviously a horrible character, but after all that build-up, I expected a much more ba-bam ending. Shout-out to Christoph Waltz, though. He was the main reason I kept watching, so naturally I was even more annoyed by how his character ended. And probably the biggest problem for me is that the movie felt childish at times, especially when it was trying to be funny. A situation like this is not funny to me, and some of the comedy completely took me out of it. The buongiorno scene that everyone seems to love, apparently peak comedy? I was just sitting there thinking, really? And cringing so much. Even the music, which I thought could have saved the movie a little bit for me, sometimes felt wasted. There were moments where I felt like it wasn’t being used at the right time, and some of the tension could have been so much better. Something about the pacing, the music, or simply the way the scenes were handled just didn’t get me there. The movie felt like it was lacking so much of its potential, and I think that was most obvious during those scenes. Maybe I’m missing something, but for a movie that is so highly rated and so highly praised, I spent a lot of it thinking: this is it?

texto: please don't let Quentin Tarantino ever write an Appalachian hillbilly character ever again and don't let Brad Pitt play one either. Christoph Waltz makes this movie. I particularly appreciated how this movie played with the various languages spoken by the characters and the impactful role it played within the plot; little language-specific idiosyncracies are used to add flourish to characters and build tension in a really creative way; it's nice seeing they took care to make Europe sound like Europe without cutting any corners. Overall the Characters (except Hans) were very weak as Tarantino standards go: feels like only Hans and Shoshanna are given enough fleshing out, whereas the rest of the cast is left out to dry; the cute little vignettes introducing the IB weren't enough to sell me on them, and then the movie failed to really do enough with them. Definitely one of Quentin's weaker films. 6.8/10

texto: Although i really enjoyed watching it, it hasn’t ruminated the best, especially in light of Quentin’s recent viral meltdowns and outbursts. The primary issue with the film is moreso in how the movie progresses, as a movie that starts strong and gets worse isn’t normal and this movie suffers from that second half slog. Extraordinary and iconic opening scene with masterclass acting transitions into a waiting game with an occasionally funny gag. Ending is decent, but that last fourth just makes the movie lesser. Excellent performances, especially from Christoph Waltz who is easily the highlight of this film, and awesome and memorable scenes like the bar scene are excellent but it just doesn’t alleviate the sluggish nature of the film.

texto: For how much people seem to enjoy this it felt somewhat lacking in substance, in terms of the humor, it was mildly funny and got some laughs out of me. Beyond the humor and some of the more tense scenes being well done, the film felt like a jingoistic overidealization of what the US actually contributed in WW2. Next to nothing about the film does much to display the nuances of WW2 and the sacrifices made by other countries such as the Soviet Union, China, or Poland beyond vague statements about other countries and treats the US like the primary operator within this war. In addition the alternate ending to WW2 as a whole just feels like a disservice to it's role as a war film and gains it nothing meaningful beyond swift justice to all the Nazi leaders under an ironic premise, the problem of it all is that no conflict is as clean-cut as Inglourious Basterds makes it seem. Overall if you're really itching to watch this whole film then knock yourself out, otherwise it wasn't much worth watching beyond a couple laughs.

texto: This is such a mixed bag of a movie. Every scene in which Hans Landa is in, is near perfect for me. He has such a gravitas to him that it feels like he is always in control and knows just a bit more than he should. For me that opening scene hits all of the points I wanted it to, perhaps as a standalone scene one of my favorites ever. The implications of being entirely powerless, not even having the bigger pipe, in your own home are so terrifying, especially since the one that had power over you can absolutely destroy your entire life. For me at least his menacing presence and the dark shadow that he casts over every scene he is in, is exactly what I want from a WWII movie. Landa shows how brutal and thorough the Nazis could be. But on the other side of that coin you have the Bastards. Most of their scenes are almost cartoonish, with slapstick gratuitous violence, and quippy remarks. All of the scenes with Hitler are no different. It's really hard to find him at all intimidating when he's portrayed as a whiny helpless child. It felt strange that every other Nazi on screen was more threatening than one of the most powerful, charismatic dictators of all time. Having seen a few other Tarantino movies, this feels like often the tone that he sets. But it's hard to overlook that first scene and the feeling that he could make a compelling story about the horrific and frightening aspects of the Holocaust, without the goofy nonsense. I feel like I could get behind this movie being a straight up comedy if it didn't have brilliant dramatic sequences that were just so much more compelling to me than the comedic ones. All that being said this was extremely well made. The set design, acting, cinematography, and direction, are all so well done. I especially enjoyed the shot composition. Every time that there was a close up of Landa while he's interrogating is so so good. And that shot in the opening looking out the doorway, is incredible. I just wish that all of the excellent technical aspects were backing up a more focused movie.

texto: For my first Tarantino movie, this was one hell of an introduction. What surprised me most was how much tension he can get out of people just sitting in a room talking. The opening scene alone had me completely locked in, and Christoph Waltz is terrifyingly good without ever needing to overplay anything. I also really loved how the movie balances all that slow-burn suspense with these sudden bursts of violence and dark comedy. By the time it fully turns into this insane revenge fantasy and starts rewriting history, I was completely on board. It’s bold, funny, brutal, ridiculously well acted, and somehow feels both incredibly controlled and completely unhinged. Definitely makes me want to work through the rest of Tarantino’s movies.

texto: Sering kali kita dijejali dengan petuah moral yang berbunyi, "Orang lemah membalas dendam, orang kuat memaafkan, orang cerdas mengabaikan." Di atas kertas, itu adalah konsep yang indah. Namun, di medan perang, ungkapan tersebut runtuh seketika dan kehilangan daya magisnya. Membunuh bukanlah sebuah urusan kecil. Tidak banyak keyakinan moral atau doktrin hukum yang mampu mengurus urusan cabut-mencabut nyawa ini secara jujur dan detail. Di sinilah Quentin Tarantino masuk dan menampar realitas tersebut. Ia mengajarkan satu taktik peperangan yang paling menakutkan yaitu bercerita. Lewat Inglourious Basterds, ia membuktikan bahwa cara menghancurkan lawan fasis tidak harus melulu dengan agresi militer terbuka. Terkadang, penghinaan paling brutal justru dilakukan dengan menciptakan panggung media di mana sang lawan justru terhibur saat narasi itu sedang membakar mereka hidup-hidup. Di dalam semesta fiksi historis ini, tata kelola kuasa dibagi ke dalam tiga yurisdiksi yang saling berbenturan. Pertama, mesin birokrasi Nazi yang diwakili oleh Kolonel Hans Landa sebagai sosok penegak sistem yang oportunis dan menjadikan kekejaman sebagai prosedur administrasi. Kedua, otoritas barbar dari unit gerilya pimpinan Letnan Aldo Raine yang beroperasi di luar konvensi perang demi menebar teror psikologis. Ketiga, keadilan senyap dari Shosanna Dreyfus, seorang penyintas yang menggunakan infrastruktur propaganda musuhnya sendiri (sebuah bioskop) sebagai ruang eksekusi. Ketiga faksi ini tidak sekadar bertarung memperebutkan wilayah, melainkan memperebutkan narasi tentang siapa yang berhak menulis akhir dari sejarah. Sebagai seorang arsitek emosi, Tarantino tidak pernah terburu-buru. Penceritaan dengan tiga sudut pandang ini berhasil dirajut dengan sangat rapi, ditopang oleh manajemen tempo (pacing) yang luar biasa kejam sekaligus elegan. Tarantino menguasai betul seni membangun ketegangan lewat percakapan di ruang tertutup, mulai dari peternakan susu LaPadite hingga kedai minum bawah tanah, sebelum akhirnya meledakkannya. Eksekusi ini dihidangkan tepat pada bagian akhir film dengan sangat megah. Penonton seolah diantarkan pada sebuah ujung cerita dengan cara yang sangat sopan. Kesopanannya menjadikan kita seolah disambut sebagai tamu kehormatan dengan ungkapan, "Anggap saja rumah sendiri," persis sedetik sebelum rumah tersebut dibakar habis. Jika kita membedah anatomi film ini menggunakan kacamata kebijakan, Inglourious Basterds adalah sebuah kritik telanjang terhadap bagaimana institusi mengelola propaganda. Joseph Goebbels menggunakan sinema (Nation's Pride) sebagai instrumen negara untuk melegitimasi pembunuhan massal dan mencuci otak massanya. Namun, logika sistem ini diaudit dan dibalik secara mematikan oleh Shosanna. Ia menyadari bahwa sistem fasisme yang begitu angkuh memiliki satu kelemahan fatal yaitu kecongkakan mereka sendiri. Dengan mengunci para petinggi Reich Ketiga di dalam bioskop yang memutar film mereka, Shosanna mengubah kebijakan propaganda menjadi ruang gas bagi para pembuat aturannya sendiri. Lebih jauh lagi, karakter Hans Landa adalah potret sempurna dari busuknya sebuah tata kelola kediktatoran. Kesetiaan pada ideologi hanyalah ilusi. Ketika kapal mulai tenggelam, sang birokrat tertinggi akan dengan mudah melacurkan seragamnya demi jaminan kekebalan hukum. Tarantino pada dasarnya tidak sedang membuat film sejarah, melainkan sedang menyusun sebuah peradilan alternatif. Inglourious Basterds adalah fantasi keadilan (poetic justice) ketika realitas hukum dan pengadilan perang (seperti Nuremberg) dirasa terlalu birokratis dan tidak pernah cukup untuk menebus dosa sejarah. Pada akhirnya, film ini meninggalkan satu peringatan struktural bagi kita. Senjata paling mematikan dari sebuah rezim bukanlah senapan, melainkan layar sinema. texto: My second Tarantino. Yeah, this is definitely as good as people say it is. Maybe not like A MASTERPIECE, it’s not even my favorite Tarantino so far because I liked Kill Bill a little bit more, but still an absolutely fantastic film. It does a very good job of blending like a serious war movie combined with a revenge story set in a historical drama. The concept is great, a ragtag group of soldiers going around slaughtering Nazis. Christoph Walz is AMAZING in this role. He just utterly disappears into Hans Landa. Another thing that I had high expectations for based on what I’d seen and was still satisfied was the opening sequence on the farm. As a huge “The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly” fan I could see the inspiration. It’s basically the same scene. He builds tension so well. Also this movie is so well written throughout with some fantastic dialogue. But that’s also its biggest weakness: this movie is.. a LOT of dialogue. I don’t have a problem with that, Oppenheimer is a 5 star movie in my book, but I feel like this was a little too long sometimes. Could’ve been a 130 minute film as opposed to a 150 minute one. Overall though, this doesn’t matter too much in the long run. That final act in the theater is PEAK and that final line is so meta I grinned so big.

exemplo: A violência estilizada e a fantasia de vingança são vistas como catárticas e satisfatórias, proporcionando um senso de justiça poética.
texto: Sering kali kita dijejali dengan petuah moral yang berbunyi, "Orang lemah membalas dendam, orang kuat memaafkan, orang cerdas mengabaikan." Di atas kertas, itu adalah konsep yang indah. Namun, di medan perang, ungkapan tersebut runtuh seketika dan kehilangan daya magisnya. Membunuh bukanlah sebuah urusan kecil. Tidak banyak keyakinan moral atau doktrin hukum yang mampu mengurus urusan cabut-mencabut nyawa ini secara jujur dan detail. Di sinilah Quentin Tarantino masuk dan menampar realitas tersebut. Ia mengajarkan satu taktik peperangan yang paling menakutkan yaitu bercerita. Lewat Inglourious Basterds, ia membuktikan bahwa cara menghancurkan lawan fasis tidak harus melulu dengan agresi militer terbuka. Terkadang, penghinaan paling brutal justru dilakukan dengan menciptakan panggung media di mana sang lawan justru terhibur saat narasi itu sedang membakar mereka hidup-hidup. Di dalam semesta fiksi historis ini, tata kelola kuasa dibagi ke dalam tiga yurisdiksi yang saling berbenturan. Pertama, mesin birokrasi Nazi yang diwakili oleh Kolonel Hans Landa sebagai sosok penegak sistem yang oportunis dan menjadikan kekejaman sebagai prosedur administrasi. Kedua, otoritas barbar dari unit gerilya pimpinan Letnan Aldo Raine yang beroperasi di luar konvensi perang demi menebar teror psikologis. Ketiga, keadilan senyap dari Shosanna Dreyfus, seorang penyintas yang menggunakan infrastruktur propaganda musuhnya sendiri (sebuah bioskop) sebagai ruang eksekusi. Ketiga faksi ini tidak sekadar bertarung memperebutkan wilayah, melainkan memperebutkan narasi tentang siapa yang berhak menulis akhir dari sejarah. Sebagai seorang arsitek emosi, Tarantino tidak pernah terburu-buru. Penceritaan dengan tiga sudut pandang ini berhasil dirajut dengan sangat rapi, ditopang oleh manajemen tempo (pacing) yang luar biasa kejam sekaligus elegan. Tarantino menguasai betul seni membangun ketegangan lewat percakapan di ruang tertutup, mulai dari peternakan susu LaPadite hingga kedai minum bawah tanah, sebelum akhirnya meledakkannya. Eksekusi ini dihidangkan tepat pada bagian akhir film dengan sangat megah. Penonton seolah diantarkan pada sebuah ujung cerita dengan cara yang sangat sopan. Kesopanannya menjadikan kita seolah disambut sebagai tamu kehormatan dengan ungkapan, "Anggap saja rumah sendiri," persis sedetik sebelum rumah tersebut dibakar habis. Jika kita membedah anatomi film ini menggunakan kacamata kebijakan, Inglourious Basterds adalah sebuah kritik telanjang terhadap bagaimana institusi mengelola propaganda. Joseph Goebbels menggunakan sinema (Nation's Pride) sebagai instrumen negara untuk melegitimasi pembunuhan massal dan mencuci otak massanya. Namun, logika sistem ini diaudit dan dibalik secara mematikan oleh Shosanna. Ia menyadari bahwa sistem fasisme yang begitu angkuh memiliki satu kelemahan fatal yaitu kecongkakan mereka sendiri. Dengan mengunci para petinggi Reich Ketiga di dalam bioskop yang memutar film mereka, Shosanna mengubah kebijakan propaganda menjadi ruang gas bagi para pembuat aturannya sendiri. Lebih jauh lagi, karakter Hans Landa adalah potret sempurna dari busuknya sebuah tata kelola kediktatoran. Kesetiaan pada ideologi hanyalah ilusi. Ketika kapal mulai tenggelam, sang birokrat tertinggi akan dengan mudah melacurkan seragamnya demi jaminan kekebalan hukum. Tarantino pada dasarnya tidak sedang membuat film sejarah, melainkan sedang menyusun sebuah peradilan alternatif. Inglourious Basterds adalah fantasi keadilan (poetic justice) ketika realitas hukum dan pengadilan perang (seperti Nuremberg) dirasa terlalu birokratis dan tidak pernah cukup untuk menebus dosa sejarah. Pada akhirnya, film ini meninggalkan satu peringatan struktural bagi kita. Senjata paling mematikan dari sebuah rezim bukanlah senapan, melainkan layar sinema. Dan ketika medium penipuan itu direbut kembali, api yang menyala tidak hanya membakar tubuh para tiran, tetapi juga meluluhlantakkan warisan sejarah mereka.

texto: This is positively, absolutely, without a doubt… a movie..Yep… Something inside of me kept going back and forth between the cruel irony of human vengeance and the reality of justice. “An eye for an eye right?” But now where’s the distinction of goodness and humanity from violence and cruelty..? The blurred line between human and humane. I can’t pretend to comprehend the horror of the true story of what this movie is trying to perhaps counteract? But why? Do we feel it’s a sort of atonement, or something to satisfy the deep disgust and hurt we feel towards such wicked atrocities ? Sure fair enough. This film is reaching for something so beyond its grasp though, something so heavy and dark and angry. But all it wants to do if touched is to glob more heavy, dark, and angry onto it. I can’t see it as helpful, we’re firing empty rounds at this point. It’s in quite the pretty package though! Christoph Waltz blows it out of the park (maybe that’s a tactless choice of words).. though I feel as though the script was even a bit clunky but that might just be because 80 freaking percent of it was in English subtitles. But also! 80 freaking percent of it was in English subtitles, so props to that. .

texto: I finally got around to watching every white dude's favorite film, and I really wanted to love it based on all the great things I had heard. However, I was bored the entire movie, and kept predicting what was going to happen next. The only two things I didn't predict were Dr. Mann turning on them & trying to kill Cooper, & the ending. Going into it, I literally said, "Let me guess, all the people on the mission are going to die except for Cooper & Brand." I was right. I didn't see the point of him leaving in the first place. I get that he wanted to save his family, but it ultimately seemed like a selfish decision to get to leave the planet you know is dying & your kids behind with it. He had no clue how many years it was going to be until he returned, or if he would even return at all. He left way too quickly in the beginning and left his daughter there sobbing (stupid). His son didn't even really seem to care that his dad left, and then at the end of the movie, Cooper doesn't even try to find his son?! What?? It's like he only cared about his daughter towards the end of the film. I wished that during the end they would show Murph at different ages trying to figure out what the gravity meant, but they clearly didn't want to hire another actor (lazy). I thought that the "gravity has the same properties as time" thing was dumb. If the wormhole was created by "them" in the future, how did they even get there in the first place to create the wormhole? I really didn't want to be a hater, but this film was just bad. The one thing I did like was the score; Hans always does a spectacular job. Overall, I have to give it a 2/5.

texto: I finally got around to watching every white dude's favorite film, and I really wanted to love it based on all the great things I had heard. However, I was bored the entire movie, and kept predicting what was going to happen next. The only two things I didn't predict were Dr. Mann turning on them & trying to kill Cooper, & the ending. Going into it, I literally said, "Let me guess, all the people on the mission are going to die except for Cooper & Brand." I was right. I didn't see the point of him leaving in the first place. I get that he wanted to save his family, but it ultimately seemed like a selfish decision to get to leave the planet you know is dying & your kids behind with it. He had no clue how many years it was going to be until he returned, or if he would even return at all. He left way too quickly in the beginning and left his daughter there sobbing (stupid). His son didn't even really seem to care that his dad left, and then at the end of the movie, Cooper doesn't even try to find his son?! What?? It's like he only cared about his daughter towards the end of the film. I wished that during the end they would show Murph at different ages trying to figure out what the gravity meant, but they clearly didn't want to hire another actor (lazy). I thought that the "gravity has the same properties as time" thing was dumb. If the wormhole was created by "them" in the future, how did they even get there in the first place to create the wormhole? I really didn't want to be a hater, but this film was just bad. The one thing I did like was the score; Hans always does a spectacular job. Overall, I have to give it a 2/5.

texto: Felt it necessary to rewatch since it’d been a decade. Despite its best efforts to conform to a more transcendent cinematic language, drawing from 2001 and other monuments of modernist cinema, the film is fundamentally incapable of embodying that language because of its ideological hostility to the very nature of art. Where 2001 embraces mystery, ambiguity, and the limits of human understanding, Interstellar cannot help but reduce everything to a problem awaiting calculation. The film reeks of the resurgent scientific arrogance that defined much of the 2010s, the kind embodied by Dawkins and his contemporaries. And Elon Musk now a testament of its logical conclusion. It carries the self-assured belief that scientific reasoning and human computation alone are sufficient to save humanity from the very crises those same forces helped create. Even the film’s apparent concession to the irrational, love, is ultimately folded back into the logic of quantification. And thus, even the very medium used to tell this story becomes a means to a self-defeating end. The older I get, the more deeply I believe that the arts are our greatest means of approaching transcendence. Art is how we encounter the sacred, how we gesture toward truths that words, logic, and reason can only circle. To use cinema in service of an ideology that insists every mystery must ultimately be rendered calculable is to undermine the very essence of the art form itself. A truly evil film.

texto: Boasts itself as both the most popular and most viewed film on this very platform as of this writing; I was likely going to stumble into it sooner or later, but of course since The Odyssey is the current hot (and somewhat contested despite what scores on here and IMDB would indicate otherwise) new thing, I just had to dive back into Christopher Nolan once more. Do I think this is any good? …Sort of? The production design is well crafted, colour grading is decent, the space stuff itself seems to have been thoroughly researched, and I can’t deny the score is well composed. However, like plenty of these Nolen directed flicks, it’s the story which I struggle to emotionally connect with. Not for lack of trying however, I just don’t feel that emotional spark others seem to with this guy’s works. Also, I think I just prefer 2002: A Space Odyseey as far as space travel films go, that one got weirder with it decades earlier and leaves further unanswered questions in its wake. Also, the World of Tomorrow shorts emotionally connect with me way more while also balancing a combination of weirdness and absurdity for that matter. I think I know what I’m looking for in Sci Fi at this point, and I don’t think this film is quite it with its attempts to be sentimental and tear jerking. This has its moments, don’t get me wrong, but they’re a bit too spread out for me across the almost three hour runtime for me to get into it fully. At least I can say I watched it and got something out of it.

texto: One of the greatest films ever made, periodt. Every single time Hans Zimmer’s organ music swells in Interstellar, I get chills. Christopher Nolan created a visual marvel that is one of the greatest I've ever seen, but what makes this movie an absolute masterpiece to me is how deeply emotional it is. A lot of sci-fi movies get so caught up in quantum mechanics and space travel that they feel cold and robotic. Interstellar does the exact opposite. It uses terrifying concepts like time dilation where a single hour on a water planet costs Cooper years of his daughter’s life back on Earth to create an unbearable sense of stakes and grief. No idea how he managed to fit wormholes, black holes, grief, promises, love, cold space, the bond of a father & child all at the same time. Nolan is undoubtedly goated. It’s ambitious, loud, visually flawless, and aggressively sentimental in the best way possible. A true Christopher Nolan classic. 🎬🚀

texto: Uff, qué puedo decir de esta película que no se haya dicho ya. La amo y me rompe el corazón cada vez que la veo. Es una obra maestra absoluta del cine de ciencia ficción y de la vida misma loco. Al principio confieso que me costó un poco enganchar por toda su avanzada filosofía, me parecía demasiado compleja para mi humilde cerebro pero a medida que avanzaba me fui metiendo en la historia y en los personajes. La parte que más me destrozó fue cuando Cooper se reencuentra con su hija, Murph, que ya es una viejita. No paré de llorar. Es desgarrador ver cómo el tiempo ha pasado y cómo él se ha perdido toda su vida. Es una escena tan potente y emotiva que es imposible no conmoverse. Y esa frase que dice: " El amor es la única cosa que trasciende el tiempo y el espacio ". Es tan real y tan doloroso a la vez. texto: One of my all time favorites. Doesn't hit the same way watching it on my TV at home as it does in the theater. Also probably cos there's no element of surprise left after multiple rewatches. Yet, after all these years, this is one of the best movies for me and definitely the best movie set in space. I did notice that while Nolan is quite visionary when it comes to production design and set pieces and the background score, he is quite conventional, sometimes even a bit simple in his writing of dialogues. Some dialogue seemed quite a bit cheesy if I'm being honest. Nonetheless, watching it tonight reminded me of the first time I watched it back in 2014 in the midst of my first semester of engineering. I was so enamored by this movie that I spend the next few days reading up about the movie, wormholes, blackholes and other fun stuff instead of studying for my exam for Mechanics, which caused me to fail the subject. In the 12 years since, I have no regrets about it. This is probably enough to describe how much I like this film.

texto: Okay, wait. I’m actually left speechless. I need time to process what I just watched. This was my first time ever watching Interstellar. I should’ve watched it years ago, but today was the day I finally decided to watch it. Now, I wasn’t ignoring it; I just been waiting for the right time, and honestly, I picked the best time to watch it because, oh my God, am I glad I got to experience this beautiful masterpiece, especially late at night. It just hit different. I need to see this like on an IMAX 70mm screen to experience it again. I know I’ll love it even ten times more than I already do. After finishing it, I started tripping for a sec because I started it at eleven-something PM, then all of a sudden, it’s two-something AM. That’s how locked in I was the entire time. Something I really want to mention, and I kept saying it to myself every scene, was “wowww,” because of how freaking incredible the cinematography was in this film. Like, I’m talking about peak max level. Man, I was literally obsessed seeing how gorgeous space looked. It felt like I was witnessing heaven itself, no lie. Definitely top 2 or 3 best cinematography I’ve seen of all time, no doubt about it. A few may disagree, but I don’t care. First of all, I can’t believe some people find Interstellar to be OVERRATED. Huh?! Like, how can you say that? I just think y’all are trying to be different so bad because they know it tops most of their favorite movies. Although, I still love Project Hail Mary more though. No shade at all. I’m just sharing my opinion, that’s all. But anyways, I’m here to talk about the best fucking performance I’ve seen of all time from the man himself, Matthew McConaughey. I just found out he wasn’t nominated at all whatsoever for his role. Some of the best acting I’ve seen in years, especially from him as well. The Academy Awards get a big L for that. Snubbing him is diabolical as fuck. He deserved an award for it. Everyone in that film should’ve got nominated. But that’s okay, because Interstellar is known for being one of the greatest films of all time, having the best visuals, the most empowering storytelling ever, and the majestic soundtrack to bless your ears, created from Hans Zimmer’s genius. Lastly, to be directed by the greatest to ever do it, aka Christopher freaking NOLAN, baby. He never misses, and I don’t think he ever will.

texto: Coringa: Delírio a Dois foi um filme de interpretação dúbia. Não é uma obra que odiei, muito pelo contrário, minhas expectativas eram extremamente altas por gostar muito do personagem Coringa, e talvez tenha sido justamente isso que tornou a decepção maior. Gosto da proposta do diretor de explorar o Arthur Fleck, aprofundando seus conflitos internos e mostrando o ser humano por trás do símbolo. As reflexões sobre identidade, solidão, julgamento e a forma como a sociedade constrói e destrói figuras públicas são interessantes e, em muitos momentos, muito bem executadas, o problema é que essa proposta entra em conflito com aquilo que o próprio filme promete, pois ao assistir a uma continuação de Coringa, é natural esperar o desenvolvimento do personagem que conhecemos, mas a narrativa permanece centrada quase exclusivamente em Arthur. Para outro filme, essa abordagem talvez funcionasse ainda melhor, mas, para uma sequência de Coringa, ela me pareceu uma escolha equivocada. Outro ponto que prejudicou bastante minha experiência foi o excesso de números musicais, que em diversos momentos tornaram o filme cansativo e quebraram completamente o ritmo da narrativa. Por fim, o desfecho também me dividiu, embora eu compreenda a intenção simbólica do diretor, a forma como Arthur morre me pareceu simples demais para um personagem tão marcante, portanto esperava um encerramento que desse mais grandeza à sua trajetória, e não um fim causado por alguém praticamente irrelevante para toda a construção da história. Ainda assim, reconheço que é um filme corajoso por fugir do convencional e propor discussões interessantes, minha decepção não veio da qualidade das reflexões, mas da sensação de que elas pertenciam a um filme sobre Arthur Fleck, e não à continuação do Coringa que eu esperava.

texto: Joker: Folie a Deux Review: Da Vinci pissing on the Mona Lisa ____________________________________________ "Arthur Fleck is dead.       Long live the Joker." ____________________________________________ 👍: Soundtrack/Sounds: 10/10 Plot/Concept: 6.2/10 Pacing: 7.1/10 Characters: 6.3/10 Emotion: 7.2/10 Cinematography: 10/10 Casting: 9/10 Acting: 9.5/10 Ending: 9.3/10 Overall: 🍿74/90🍿 Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot more good things than people give it credit for. Joaquin Phoenix gives another incredible performance and carries every scene with intensity. I also enjoyed all of the songs , and the soundtrack and sound design create a unique mood. The visuals are beautiful , with grey but yet bright colours that make Gotham look perfect. The scene where Two-Face is born was one of my favourites . And the overall court sequence is excellent. I also liked the ending . I know most people hate it, but I thought it fit the story well. In my opinion, this film is still very overhated. The Message: Joker: Folie à Deux shows how society can turn a broken person into a symbol they never wanted to become. Arthur is no longer seen as a human being with fears, but as the Joker , an idea that people project their own anger onto. The film questions whether people truly care about justice or if they simply enjoy watching chaos. Do we become who we really are or who everyone expects us to be. Arthur struggles between being himself and living up to the Joker . The ending suggests that ideas can survive even when the people cannot. symbols are often more powerful than people, and once society creates a legend , it becomes almost impossible to forget, no matter how much someone changes. ____________________________________________ 👎: Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot of problems. The biggest one is that almost nothing happens. The story barely moves forward , and around 70% of the film feels wasted because there is almost no real progress from beginning to end. The direction is bland, and the overall screenplay is weak. I enjoyed the songs themselves, but the musical numbers often don't fit the story and become exhausting after a while. Good music alone isn't enough to carry such a thin plot. Harley Quinn was also disappointing because she barely does anything important. She had a lot of potential , but the screenplay gives her very little to give , making her feel completely unnecessary. I know the film is overhated , but it's still a pretty mid film . To make things even worse, I watched it at 2 a.m. , so I even lost sleep for it. ____________________________________________ Overall: Joker: Folie à Deux is a weak ass film , but it's still massively overhated. It has some genuinely great aspects , especially the acting, visuals, and music, but they're overshadowed by an unfocused story, bland direction, and wasted potential. The flaws are simply much bigger than the strengths, making it an average experience. Rating by Greatness: ⭐✨ Rating: ⭐⭐ ```````````````

texto: Joker: Folie a Deux Review: Da Vinci pissing on the Mona Lisa ____________________________________________ "Arthur Fleck is dead.       Long live the Joker." ____________________________________________ 👍: Soundtrack/Sounds: 10/10 Plot/Concept: 6.2/10 Pacing: 7.1/10 Characters: 6.3/10 Emotion: 7.2/10 Cinematography: 10/10 Casting: 9/10 Acting: 9.5/10 Ending: 9.3/10 Overall: 🍿74/90🍿 Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot more good things than people give it credit for. Joaquin Phoenix gives another incredible performance and carries every scene with intensity. I also enjoyed all of the songs , and the soundtrack and sound design create a unique mood. The visuals are beautiful , with grey but yet bright colours that make Gotham look perfect. The scene where Two-Face is born was one of my favourites . And the overall court sequence is excellent. I also liked the ending . I know most people hate it, but I thought it fit the story well. In my opinion, this film is still very overhated. The Message: Joker: Folie à Deux shows how society can turn a broken person into a symbol they never wanted to become. Arthur is no longer seen as a human being with fears, but as the Joker , an idea that people project their own anger onto. The film questions whether people truly care about justice or if they simply enjoy watching chaos. Do we become who we really are or who everyone expects us to be. Arthur struggles between being himself and living up to the Joker . The ending suggests that ideas can survive even when the people cannot. symbols are often more powerful than people, and once society creates a legend , it becomes almost impossible to forget, no matter how much someone changes. ____________________________________________ 👎: Joker: Folie à Deux has a lot of problems. The biggest one is that almost nothing happens. The story barely moves forward , and around 70% of the film feels wasted because there is almost no real progress from beginning to end. The direction is bland, and the overall screenplay is weak. I enjoyed the songs themselves, but the musical numbers often don't fit the story and become exhausting after a while. Good music alone isn't enough to carry such a thin plot. Harley Quinn was also disappointing because she barely does anything important. She had a lot of potential , but the screenplay gives her very little to give , making her feel completely unnecessary. I know the film is overhated , but it's still a pretty mid film . To make things even worse, I watched it at 2 a.m. , so I even lost sleep for it. ____________________________________________ Overall: Joker: Folie à Deux is a weak ass film , but it's still massively overhated. It has some genuinely great aspects , especially the acting, visuals, and music, but they're overshadowed by an unfocused story, bland direction, and wasted potential. The flaws are simply much bigger than the strengths, making it an average experience. Rating by Greatness: ⭐✨ Rating: ⭐⭐ ```````````````

texto: Coringa: Delírio a Dois foi um filme de interpretação dúbia. Não é uma obra que odiei, muito pelo contrário, minhas expectativas eram extremamente altas por gostar muito do personagem Coringa, e talvez tenha sido justamente isso que tornou a decepção maior. Gosto da proposta do diretor de explorar o Arthur Fleck, aprofundando seus conflitos internos e mostrando o ser humano por trás do símbolo. As reflexões sobre identidade, solidão, julgamento e a forma como a sociedade constrói e destrói figuras públicas são interessantes e, em muitos momentos, muito bem executadas, o problema é que essa proposta entra em conflito com aquilo que o próprio filme promete, pois ao assistir a uma continuação de Coringa, é natural esperar o desenvolvimento do personagem que conhecemos, mas a narrativa permanece centrada quase exclusivamente em Arthur. Para outro filme, essa abordagem talvez funcionasse ainda melhor, mas, para uma sequência de Coringa, ela me pareceu uma escolha equivocada. Outro ponto que prejudicou bastante minha experiência foi o excesso de números musicais, que em diversos momentos tornaram o filme cansativo e quebraram completamente o ritmo da narrativa. Por fim, o desfecho também me dividiu, embora eu compreenda a intenção simbólica do diretor, a forma como Arthur morre me pareceu simples demais para um personagem tão marcante, portanto esperava um encerramento que desse mais grandeza à sua trajetória, e não um fim causado por alguém praticamente irrelevante para toda a construção da história. Ainda assim, reconheço que é um filme corajoso por fugir do convencional e propor discussões interessantes, minha decepção não veio da qualidade das reflexões, mas da sensação de que elas pertenciam a um filme sobre Arthur Fleck, e não à continuação do Coringa que eu esperava.

texto: Coringa 2 é um filme que não consegue se sustentar sozinho. Ele vive inteiramente à sombra do primeiro. A nova proposta de transformar a narrativa em um musical é, na teoria, interessante. Ela até combina com a leitura psicológica e frágil que esse universo fez do Coringa. O problema é que, na prática, a execução falha completamente. O longa não consegue decidir o que quer ser. Ele não funciona como musical, porque as músicas não impulsionam a história nem revelam nada novo sobre os personagens. E também não funciona como um drama de tribunal, porque o roteiro jurídico é fraco, arrastado e não constrói tensão real. No fim das contas, o que resta são dois pilares: as atuações, que continuam sendo impecáveis, especialmente de Joaquin Phoenix e Lady Gaga, e a fotografia, que segue linda e atmosférica. Mas tirando isso, o filme se esvazia. Não sobra substância, não sobra tema, não sobra impacto. Me parece que Todd Phillips gastou o filme inteiro tentando responder aos fãs que idolatraram o primeiro Coringa e transformaram aquele personagem em um ícone a ser seguido. Ele quis dizer: "olha, esse cara não é um símbolo, ele é só um doente". E tudo bem querer desconstruir isso. O problema é a forma. Ele mesmo criou essa versão do Coringa. Ele mesmo construiu um protagonista magnético, caótico e sedutor no primeiro filme. E agora parece arrependido disso. Em vez de aprofundar ou amadurecer essa ideia, ele optou pelo caminho mais raso e mais medíocre: desconstruir por desconstruir, chocar por chocar. O resultado é um filme que trai a própria proposta que o consagrou.

exemplo: Parte do grupo percebeu uma tentativa de desmistificar o protagonista, mostrando sua humanidade frágil e distanciando-se da imagem icônica do palhaço, o que gerou reações mistas.
texto: Sei que muita gente não gostou do segundo filme, mas eu tive uma interpretação diferente. Na minha visão, o diretor quis mostrar que Arthur Fleck não deve ser romantizado. Muitas pessoas passaram a enxergar o Coringa como um símbolo de revolta ou até admirar o personagem pelos motivos errados. Para mim, este filme desconstrói essa imagem e reforça que Arthur é uma pessoa profundamente perturbada, vivendo em um mundo que mistura fantasia e realidade. O musical, que foi a maior crítica do público, fez sentido para mim justamente por representar a mente do Coringa. Em muitos momentos, o filme parece não fazer sentido, mas essa confusão combina com a forma como Arthur enxerga o mundo. texto: Após o primeiro filme, o qual continua glorioso em contar uma ótima história com os personagens da DC. A continuação tinha um enorme desafio, como manter a qualidade? (o que fez muitos questionarem se era realmente necessário um segundo filme) Infelizmente, Coringa 2 falha e peca em criar uma narrativa interessante que nos faça torcer pelo protagonista (apesar de um vilão) A história parecia promissora: Após uma pessoa nunca antes vista assumir uma identidade sombria para finalmente ser vista, como essa mesma segue sendo sombra do próprio personagem? Se Coringa escalava do 0 a 100, seguindo a trajetória de ascensão de Arthur Fleck, a sequência mostra seu regresso para apenas o homem, apenas uma pessoa Não mais o símbolo ou seja lá o que o povo enxergava nele Tudo isso enquanto lidava com as expectativas daqueles que compraram sua loucura, seu personagem e mais um interesse romântico que parecia ser a única luz nesse túnel de solidão no qual vivia Na escrita isso parece incrível, mas na prática... O primeiro filme era magistral em poucas cenas sem diálogos falarem muito mais do que palavras, este tentou uma nova abordagem Diria que o musical não foi o que mais me incomodou (apesar de pouco ajudar na trama, pouco desenvolvia os personagens e mais parecia ocupar tempo de tela desnecessário A trama fracamente é confusa em alguns momentos, difícil de entender a motivação de alguns personagens e cenas que parecem sem sentido algum e nos tiram do ritmo A fotografia do filme continua perfeita, um dos meus pontos favoritos As músicas, não são de todo mal (apesar de sinceramente considerar elas desnecessárias) E a atuação continua um ponto positivo Mas em meio a um roteiro confuso, musicais deslocados e uma história que não alcança seu potencial, não me faz querer rever e sinceramente prefiro manter somente o original em minha memória A comparação é inevitável E Coringa 2 não chega aos pés de seu antecessor... E a tentativa de regredir a figura lendária do Palhaço do Crime de Gotham acaba por também regredir a história que Todd Phillips nos apresentou

texto: Shut up all of you. This movie, while definitely not as impactful as the first one, is straight genius 1. The idea of the Joker Arthur Fleck’s death at the end definitely shocked me, but its such a clever take on it. The Joker isnt one singular person, its an idea, a concept, a shared belief. So many people take roles playing the Joker because its not just one person theyre representing. They all have different takes on his quirks, his behaviour, his mental state because theyre taking this concept of the Joker and making it their own. And making this apart of the film’s themes had me gobsmacked 2. The lighting The lighting in both movies is incredible. Unfortunately, i began to conjure up this idea because of a tiktok, but it makes so much sense. Arthur is blue, Joker is yellow… together they make green. Lee is often dressed in yellow, pulling him into the fantasy of “the joker”. And when these different “sides” of him connect (or when he doesnt know which side to believe, the lighting is green. Its so cool and so clever. It’s subtle, but so intentional. 3. The singing Dancing has always been such a crucial idea attached to the Joker’s character—he loves music. Thus, it makes complete sense to make it part musical, especially when he’s in his delusional episodes where he’s imagining himself on a stage, being “the joker”. It can feel jarring at times, like it snaps you out of the plot sometimes, but I think thats the point. It’s supposed to shed some more insight into Arthur’s hurt and twisted mind. I can understand why some think it detracts from the film, but I personally don’t. I think it adds 4. Action movies Not all superhero/villian stories need to be straight up action. Now that is a waste of a film and such a incredibly complex character. Action and gore is straight up BORING if it doesn’t have proper reason or if it doesnt add anything to the movie. The Joker doesnt need action all the time in his origin story, and you think the movie does, you don’t understand the movie’s intention + the character AT ALL 5. CONNOR STORIE??! What are you doing here??

texto: i think joker: folie à deux is one of the most misunderstood movies in recent years. before anything, i am NOT justifying arthur fleck’s actions. this man literally killed 6 people. understanding a character’s psychology does not mean excusing what they did. that’s what makes this movie so interesting to me. it isn’t asking us to forgive arthur, it’s asking us to watch him completely lose himself. the musical aspect was definitely a choice, and i understand why it didn’t work for everyone, but i think people missed what it was trying to do. i don’t think most of the singing is actually happening. i think it’s all inside arthur’s head. the songs are his fantasies, his escape, and another sign that he can no longer separate reality from the world he created. the movie isn’t about the rise of the joker. it’s about the death of arthur fleck. after the first movie, everyone wanted arthur to become the joker we know from the comics. the mastermind, the villain, the legend. but todd phillips almost feels like he’s challenging the audience by refusing to give us that. we wanted the myth of joker, but he keeps showing us the broken man underneath the makeup. and honestly, i think that’s the point. gotham didn’t love arthur. they loved joker. harley didn’t fall in love with arthur fleck, she fell in love with the idea of joker. everyone was obsessed with the fantasy, including the audience. lady gaga was also incredible. i just wish we got more of her as harley quinn because she can genuinely act her ass off. but maybe the reason we don’t fully understand harley is because arthur doesn’t fully understand her either. we only see the version of her that exists in his mind. this movie is messy, and i understand why people don’t connect with it, but i think there is so much more going on underneath the surface. the musical numbers, the courtroom, the relationship with harley, and the ending all feel like a reflection of arthur’s collapsing mind. not a perfect movie, but definitely a much deeper one than people give it credit for.

texto: Todd Philips concebeu ao mundo uma sequência que muitos acreditavam que era desnecessária e um erro, mas ainda assim havia expectativa de que se no final do primeiro filme ele termina como algo maior, um símbolo de revolução em gotham, nesse segundo poderíamos ver o Coringa sendo esse líder revolucionário juntamente com a sua Arlequina, mas Todd pensou diferente e buscou trazer exatamente o contrário disso, e esse é um dos motivos de porquê esse filme foi tão odiado, por ser um filme totalmente Anti-Coringa, focado em descontruir tudo o que o primeiro fez, mostrar que Arthur não é um líder revolucionário, mas sim um homem deprimente, com disturbios mentais, que teve um dia ruim e transpareceu para Gotham o seu caos e sua violência reprimida, matando aqueles homens no metrô, inspirando que eles não deviam temer a elite e criar essa revolta, mas nesta sequência, isso é desconstruído à medida em que percebemos que os que idolatram o Coringa, não idolatram Arthur Fleck, idolatram aquilo que ele criou, aquela persona caótica que matou Murray Franklin na noite do dia 18 de novembro ao vivo na TV, e no momento chave do filme ele percebe, ele começa a enxergar que o Coringa traz morte por onde passa, atiça esse ódio nas pessoas, tanto de quem o apoia, tanto de quem não o apoia, e a partir dali, ele vai contra tudo aquilo que o Coringa representa, tudo aquilo que os fãs dele apoiam, desiste da imagem do Coringa, renuncia a identidade do Coringa, mas ali já era tarde demais, Arthur havia plantado a semente do caos em Gotham e não tinha como ser desfeito, Arthur é morto pela sua própria criação, por aquilo que ele criou para fugir da sua realidade, quando Arthur mostra quem realmente é ninguém liga, ninguém nunca se importou, as pessoas apenas queriam ter algo pra seguir, algo que as libertassem de si mesmas, ironicamente, o Coringa que nasceu dele mesmo o matou, não restando mais o homem por trás da máscara, apenas o Coringa.

Anyway, Hildur Guðnadóttir’s arrangements of all the songs are some of the most beautiful things I have ever heard. End of statement. See you next rewatch!

texto: Joker: Folie à Deux is a bold and unpredictable follow-up that refuses to simply repeat what made the first movie successful. It takes the story in a stranger, more experimental direction, mixing psychological drama with musical elements and exploring Arthur Fleck’s world from a different perspective. Joaquin Phoenix remains incredible, bringing the same intensity and complexity to the character, while the film’s atmosphere and style are still its biggest strengths. However, the pacing and some of the creative choices make it feel less focused than its predecessor. It doesn’t reach the same impact as the original, but it’s still an ambitious sequel that takes risks instead of playing it safe.

texto: It’s a little too experimental, but I have to respect the boldness of dropping this after the first one blew up. It’s still visually stunning, the performances are still great, and it still has a sharp social critique. The difference is this time the group of society getting dragged is the exact same crowd that parasocially worshipped the first movie, so of course it tanked at the box office. By refusing to glamorize the violence and making it obvious that the Joker should never have been idolized, the film held up a mirror and it hit way too close to home. The ending is bold, it delivers the point and it’s perfectly in line with Arthur’s arc from film one. He’s not the Joker. He just used the Joker persona to act on his impulses, and now he has to face the real consequences. Turning it into a musical was a wonderful move by Todd Phillips. It made sure anyone who used to larp as the Joker no longer wanted to be associated with it. Basically a full-on cleansing of its fanbase.

texto: Co written by Scott Silver (The Mod Squad, 8 Mile, The Fighter, Joker, The Finest Hours)  and Todd Phillips and directed by Todd Phillips (Joker, Road Trip, Starsky & Hutch (2004), The Hangover, The Hangover Part II, The Hangover Part III, War Dogs, A Star is Born, Due Date), 'Joker: Folie à Deux' explores the genesis of an ideology born from the violence of a world fuelled by disdain. Phillips continues painting a viscerally dark, painful picture of a man seemingly dismantled by the machinery of law, order and social justice, yet reassembled by the flickering embers of love for a woman captivated by his public enigma. Although 'Joker: File à Deux' weaves musicality into the narrative, this film loses nothing when leading viewers through the protagonists inner workings, and with some excellent performances producing a memorable experience, this is a sequel to be embraced, not disregarded. In closing, 'Joker: Folie à Deux' rests comfortably beside its predecessor, and while a sad, and at times, harrowing portrayal of a truly "tortured" soul, this title will endure multiple, impactful rewatches, which says far more than the critics and naysayer’s who rejected and reviled it's message upon release.

texto: Una hermosa película con un nombre incorrecto que la, hace ver mala. "Joker: Folie à Deux" Un nombre que usaron para vender la película como si fuera la secuela del Joker anterior y no fue así, fue más una historia aparte de Arthur viviendo su vida después de los sucesos anteriores y no, no es el Joker, es un hombre completamente enfermo, anoréxico y con un juicio por matar a 6 personas. El Joker era algo más raro, más irreal y no era un pobre señor enfermo con esa contextura de cuerpo. La película en su es muy hermosa, tiene canciones muy pero muy buenas, las escenas de los musicales son completamente arte, planos hermosos, colores hermosos, Joaquín Phoenix y Lady Gaga hacen un trabajo estupendo pero lo que arruina todo es el maldito título de la película ya que NO HABLA DEL JOKEEER. Le pongo 5 estrellas por como me gustó la película, por cómo lo ví, no lo ví cómo una secuela, lo ví cómo la continuación de ARTHUR después de todo lo que pasó, no lo ví como la continuación del Joker que se iba a convertir en el Joker que todo el mundo conoce. Esta es una película injustamente odiada por la gente. A mí parecer, Wander Bros. quiso vender su producto como " el Joker " pero terminaron sepultando su película.

texto: Entiendo las razones por la que la esta película es muy, MUY criticada. Pero, sinceramente, me gustó. Es IMPOSIBLE superar la primera película de el Joker, esa película es una obra maestra y su final complica mucho las puertas para la segunda, la idea de expresar las emociones confusas de Arthur en las canciones me parece excelente. A algunas personas no podrá gustarles el hecho de que esto sea un musical, pero considero que no es un mal implemento. Quizá aveces las canciones pueden entrar en momentos donde, coño, es algo raro que entren. Pero si, a mi me gustó. Entiendo porque es odiada, pero, me gusta. Arthur fue una víctima de las ideas que él mismo propagó con sus traumas y acciones bajo la mascara de el Joker. Y al darse cuenta que no es más que él mismo, rompe el corazón de aquellos que lo vieron como un símbolo, y bueno, acaba como acaba. No es la historia de el Guasón de Batman, es la historia de un símbolo que fue víctima de si mismo. 4/5 Sólido

texto: It’s a little too experimental, but I have to respect the boldness of dropping this after the first one blew up. It’s still visually stunning, the performances are still great, and it still has a sharp social critique. The difference is this time the group of society getting dragged is the exact same crowd that parasocially worshipped the first movie, so of course it tanked at the box office. By refusing to glamorize the violence and making it obvious that the Joker should never have been idolized, the film held up a mirror and it hit way too close to home. The ending is bold, it delivers the point and it’s perfectly in line with Arthur’s arc from film one. He’s not the Joker. He just used the Joker persona to act on his impulses, and now he has to face the real consequences. Turning it into a musical was a wonderful move by Todd Phillips. It made sure anyone who used to larp as the Joker no longer wanted to be associated with it. Basically a full-on cleansing of its fanbase.

texto: Una hermosa película con un nombre incorrecto que la, hace ver mala. "Joker: Folie à Deux" Un nombre que usaron para vender la película como si fuera la secuela del Joker anterior y no fue así, fue más una historia aparte de Arthur viviendo su vida después de los sucesos anteriores y no, no es el Joker, es un hombre completamente enfermo, anoréxico y con un juicio por matar a 6 personas. El Joker era algo más raro, más irreal y no era un pobre señor enfermo con esa contextura de cuerpo. La película en su es muy hermosa, tiene canciones muy pero muy buenas, las escenas de los musicales son completamente arte, planos hermosos, colores hermosos, Joaquín Phoenix y Lady Gaga hacen un trabajo estupendo pero lo que arruina todo es el maldito título de la película ya que NO HABLA DEL JOKEEER. Le pongo 5 estrellas por como me gustó la película, por cómo lo ví, no lo ví cómo una secuela, lo ví cómo la continuación de ARTHUR después de todo lo que pasó, no lo ví como la continuación del Joker que se iba a convertir en el Joker que todo el mundo conoce. Esta es una película injustamente odiada por la gente. A mí parecer, Wander Bros. quiso vender su producto como " el Joker " pero terminaron sepultando su película.

The pacing killed it for me, with so much of the movie feeling like characters walking around, talking and waiting for something to happen. I also couldn’t connect with the characters at all. I know it’s considered a classic, but this is one of those movies where I completely understand the praise and still absolutely hated watching it.

It may well be presenting a realistic view of life in the Paris projects in the 1990s but in spite of this, and the fact that it was really well acted in a particularly gritty documentary style, it didn't make up for the basic lack of story and character development. dialogues sont par moment bien écrits même si souvent ça fait tellement vieillot/pas naturel faut que je demande a des mecs plus vieux si on parlait comme ça dans les années 2000 Ça joue vraiment pas super bien sauf Cassel et j’ai un gros problème avec les intentions de Kassovitz ta3 khra et le film est tellement pessimiste genre il a lui même dit que son intention était pas de parler aux mecs de banlieue ou de représenter quelque chose qu’il connaissait/vecu, de son propre aveu, il a pris la banlieue pour parler aux bobos, et ça se sent parce qu’on romanise la hess constamment dans ce film, avec des dialogues qui viennent intellectualiser plus que nécessaire des trucs pour que les blancs se disent tiens ces singes savent réfléchir, genre quand Hubert dit qu’il veut quitter la cité et sa mère lui dit sur le chemin ramène de la salade, genre on peut pas quitter la cité C’est tellement sombre et empreint de fatalisme que ça en perd de son réalisme, je connais aucun mec de cité qui pense qu’il va avoir une vie de cafard mdrr tout le monde a de l’espoir Et aussi je trouve qu’en faisant de Vinz un mec pathétique et juste en le faisant passer pour un mec qui a de la haine en lui, malgré tout le contexte d’émeute et tout, on explique pas que cette haine chez les mecs de cité qui peut se traduire par la délinquance elle est due au fait qu’ils sont mis en marge de la société sur tous les aspects, pas que quand ils veulent s’incruster dans des soirées mondaines Et la scène dans la toilette (tellement moralisatrice au passage) est pas suffisante parce qu’on tout ce qu’on montre de négatif dans le film, à part les violences policières, bah c’est imputable aux émeutiers Et la scène de bavure est tellement faite pour qu’on ait de la pitié pour eux pas pour montrer les vices de la c’est les banlieues et leurs habitants le problème Et de ce que j’ai vu sur internet la vache que Vinz voit c’est un symbole de la police omniprésente dans son esprit bah ça vient pas expliquer en disant qu’il suit la même route que son frère en prison mais son frère on le responsabilise à fond, en plus de le dépeindre comme un ksos, Et je ne sais pas si hubert bricave mais bon je pense pas l’aimais bien parce que je l’ai vu petit, que visuellement c’était cool et que ça parlait de sujets qui m’évoquaient des trucs mais maintenant que je comprends les films bah ça pue le caca Sah comme texto: Acting exceptionnel, Vincent Cassel phénoménal. Noir et blanc, une seule journée : 30 ans après, aucune ride sûrement parce que ce qu'il raconte n'a pas changé. Très réaliste : tellement de temps morts comblés par des dialogues et autres que quand la violence arrive, tu la sens vraiment. Le trio est génial, ils s'engueulent mais restent ensemble jusqu'au bout car jusqu’ici tout va bien. Un blanc, un noir, un arabe c'est pensé : la galère n'est pas une question d'origine mais de quartier. « Jusqu'ici tout va bien »… tout le film tient dans cette phrase. Les plans de Cassel face caméra, forts. Les musiques (NTM) qui portent tout. La fin, je m'y attendais mais pas du tout : tu la prends en pleine face. Un des meilleurs films sur les quartiers en France, si ce n'est le meilleur le précurseur de plein d'autres, films comme séries.

texto: Admiro como muitos filmes da época conseguem tratar suas ideias com originalidade e coragem pra seguir seus ideais; La Haine muitas vezes foge da temática central (apesar de se manter sempre com a mesma ideia, mesmo que as vezes sendo secundária) e se propõe, voluntariamente, a desenvolver a relação e personalidade dos protagonistas mesmo que de maneira “avulsa” A atuação e cinematografia é outro fator a se destacar, e ambos andam muito lado a lado em várias cenas do filme, como se um não funcionasse tão bem sem o outro. Apesar de tudo isso, senti que a história quando focava em sua crítica principal batia sempre no mesmo ponto e, principalmente, da mesma forma, como se estivesse em um ciclo; pode ser proposital, mas te traz uma sensação de inércia no decorrer do filme e a mensagem satura um pouco essa mensagem. O final, inclusive, se torna esperado e até “previsivel” de certa forma em decorrência disso.

tema: Fotografia em preto e branco e estética
exemplo: A escolha do preto e branco é frequentemente elogiada por criar uma atmosfera única e realista, com enquadramentos marcantes que transformam cada cena em algo visualmente poderoso.
texto: Como descrever esse filme? La Haine é o tipo de filme que você não mudaria nada, absolutamente nada. O filme promete e entrega tudo que poderia ser: uma crítica à segregação, ao racismo institucional, exclusão social de imigrantes e seus descendentes na França e até questões filosóficas, como o existencialismo. O filme acompanha a relação de três jovens, um judeu (Vinz), um árabe (Said) e um negro (Hubert) que vivem numa França pós colonização e dentro de uma periferia, e que nutrem um ódio pelos preconceitos que sofrem na sociedade externa a esse banlieue , principalmente pela repressão policial . O seu estopim, de acordo com o filme, acontece pela morte de Abdel Ichaha, que era um amigo muito próximo do grupo, sendo uma referência direta ao caso de Makomé M'Bowole, um jovem de 17 anos que foi assassinado com um tiro à queima-roupa por um policial. A partir disso, Vinz, um dos membros desse grupo e o mais cabeça quente, num dos protestos que aconteceram após a morte de Abdel, encontra uma arma perdida de um policial. E então a trama gira em torno da sede que Vinz possui de matar um policial para "nivelar o jogo" e o desejo de ser respeitado pela sua periferia. Também somos apresentados com Hubert, a contraparte de Vinz. Se Vinz é o impulsivo, Hubert é o racional; se Vinz é briguento, Hubert, por mais que seja um lutador de boxe, prefere evitar brigas. o papel de Hubert nesse filme é essencial para o desenvolvimento de Vinz, agindo como um irmão mais velho, sempre aconselhando Vinz de que o objetivo de matar um policial nunca será a melhor escolha, porque isso não elimina o ódio, somente nutre. O terceiro membro, Said, age como o mais imaturo/inocente do grupo. Ele é um contraste entre os dois personagens, meio que o meio termo dos dois. Ao mesmo que tempo que Said muitas vezes fica do lado de Hubert nas suas decisões morais, ele também participa dos protestos que ocorrem no começo do filme. A estética muito estilosa do filme, para mim, é o que torna ele um dos filmes mais únicos e bonitos de se ver. Ao decorrer da trama você encontra diversas cenas incríveis, como a cena do Vinz no espelho, a dos três no banheiro com um enquadramento tão foda que fica até confuso, o uso do alto contraste entre preto e branco que aproxima o filme de um documentário real, as atuações, a transição da câmera da periferia para o centro de Paris, entre diversas outras qualidades. O final do filme é o ápice da trama, porque ele reforça a narrativa circular. O filme abre com Said abrindo os olho e termina com ele fechando. Isso acontece porque Vinz acaba entendendo o lado de Hubert e fazendo as pazes, mas na hora de ir embora, Vinz e Said acabam sendo pegos por policiais, e um deles acaba "sem querer" matando Vinz com um tiro na cabeça. Isso reflete na morte de Abdel, por mais que isso contradiga o que eu afirmei no começo, não era o estopim, era só mais um "até aqui, está tudo bem". Com Said fechando os olhos, o ciclo é repetido num loop de uma sociedade decadente. "É a história de uma sociedade que cai, e que repete, durante a queda, como para se reconfortar: Até aqui, está tudo bem, até aqui, está tudo bem, até aqui, está tudo bem. Mas o importante não é a queda, é a aterrissagem." Para mim, a sociedade já aterrissou. Para mim, a sociedade já aterrissou. 10/10

texto: La Haine sadəcə küçələrdə yaşayan üç gəncin hekayəsi deyil, cəmiyyətin yaratdığı qəzəb və ümidsizliyin portretidir. Film boyunca Vinz, Saïd və Hubert-in bir gününü izləsək də, onların yaşadığı problemlərin daha böyük bir sistemin parçası olduğunu hiss edirik. Qara-ağ görüntülər filmin atmosferinə inanılmaz dərəcədə uyğundur. Dialoqlar təbii, personajlar isə çox real hiss olunur. Ən çox xoşuma gələn tərəfi filmin heç kimi tamamilə “yaxşı” və ya “pis” göstərməməsidir — hər personajın öz baxışı və səbəbi var. Film sakit görünən anlarında belə gərginliyini qoruyur və sona doğru bu gərginlik getdikcə artır. Final isə bütün filmin mesajını bir anda daha aydın hiss etdirir.

texto: Meilleur cinématographie que j'ai vu de ma vie. Tu peux legit prendre n'importe seconde du film, mettre en pause, prendre un screenshot et tu possèdes une hard pic pour un IG post. Je n'arrêtais pas de dire "This shit is so fucking hard". Parfaite représentation des cités françaises des années 90. Ils sont tous pauvres, de plusieurs cultures différentes, mais la majorité vie tous du racisme. Les personnes qui ont grandit dans la haine, comme les 3 personnages du films, vont finir par partager cette haine partout où qu'ils vont.

texto: Rewatching this movie means to see  the contradiction that regulates the social war fed by inequality. La Haine ما يحتاج أحداث ضخمة حتى يشدك، لأن كل ثقله موجود بالشخصيات نفسها، بطريقة تفكيرهم، اختلافاتهم، غضبهم، ونظرتهم للحياة والواقع اللي عايشين بيه. كل واحد منهم يمثل جانب مختلف، ولهذا تفاعلهم ويا بعض هو اللي يخلي الفيلم ممتع فعلًا. أكثر شي عجبني إن الفيلم ما يحاول يخليك تشوف شخصية معينة كأنها الصح والباقي غلط، وإنما يخليك تعيش وياهم وتفهم شلون كل واحد وصل لهالمرحلة. الحوار، السكوت، النظرات، وحتى أبسط التصرفات تحس وراها تراكم كامل من الغضب والإحباط والصراع. والتصوير بالأبيض والأسود كان مناسب جدًا لجو الفيلم، وخلى كل مشهد يحسسك بثقل المكان والواقع اللي عايشين بيه. أكو لقطات بسيطة جدًا بس تظل عالقة بالبال، وهذا الشي يثبت شكد الإخراج كان مسيطر على التجربة. الفيلم بالنسبة إلي مو عن شنو راح يصير، وإنما عن شلون الشخصيات راح تتعامل ويا الشي اللي يصير، وهنا كانت المتعة الحقيقية. كل ما تتعمق بالشخصيات أكثر، تحس إن الفيلم يصير أثقل وأقوى

texto: Reminds me a lot of Star Wars Episode 1 in the way the film is focused on self-important lore and world-building above all else, turning its back on the fizzy melodramatic fun of the original works. None of the characters are engaging, little of the action is exciting, everything is so transparently in service of delivering lame jargon and iconography, which all has a smug 1960s hippie vibe to it that I find totally insufferable. The extent to which it is impossible to give a shit about Max or Furiosa is remarkable, they're not cool, charming, funny, self-reflective or in possession of any other potentially humanising traits, just relentless grim stoicism. Perhaps if the film were not saddled with one of Tom Hardy's most moronically misjudged performances and Max had some kind of charisma, like Mel Gibson achieved without sacrificing intensity, the viewer would have had some kind of way in to the film on an emotional level, shame no one reigned him in. Also remarkable is how unexpectedly slow it is, both dialogue and action scenes dragging terribly - take the scene where Max first holds Furiosa and the wives at gunpoint, it goes on so long with so little of any significance happening that it starts to become awkward, the characters just standing and looking at eachother. This absolutely feels like it was directed by a 70 year old and edited by someone with no prior action film experience. Of course there's a lot of spectacle, but you mainly consume it with a dispassionate appreciation of the scale and detail of the production design and the work that must have gone into realising it, rarely approaching the edge of your seat. Miller just isn't a good enough action director to cope with the scale he's aiming for here - within the huge road-fleets there's no real sense of where the active characters are in relation to eachother, of who is in which samey vehicle or where the danger will be coming from, so the feeling that the baddies are just popping into existence to fulfil a quota for action within an artificial entertainment becomes too nagging. Would also help if this hadn't aimed for a PG-13 rating, more graphic violence would at least provoke a visceral reaction to what's happening on screen that you don't get when the film is constantly shying away from the reality of people getting shot in the head or blown up or crushed by huge trucks. A lot of people seem to be very passionate fans of Fury Road and yet the follow-up was a huge financial flop, so why didn't they turn up for it in droves? I think the reality is that it's easy to make this film sound conceptually cool on paper, but on a more nuts-and-bolts level it is let down by weak direction - the idea of the film is better than the reality.

texto: Guns, explosions, and monster trucks. Is this what's considered "entertainment"? Thrown into a post-apocalyptic world, we are shown dynamics between governor and governed that are simply laughable, as if hoarding all the water from the population wouldn't cause an immediate uprising and lead to a proto-communist society. Scenes made purely to get a confused or indignant reaction from the spectator, making each ridiculous moment appear even more senseless than the prior. Despite having really gorgeous cinematography and color grading, everything else is as close to horrible as possible. Editing, VFX, and acting (by some charactes), are all lackluster, something that is amplified by the fact that the film has no real story to tell. I believe this is even more unengaging than Maze Runner 2 — my first one star review on Letterboxd— which at least had a malformed concept of a plot going on from the first movie of the saga, unlike what I've just watched. I don't enjoy these post-apocalyptic, survival action stories, with the sole exceptions being both The Last of Us games (so far), but I went into this film without any expectations whatsoever; so being met with with the most mindless, generic, action (sub)plot I've seen made me irritated from the start.
