tema: Mundo e lógica internos pouco convincentes
exemplo: A construção do mundo pós-apocalíptico e as regras que o regem são vistas como inconsistentes e pouco críveis, dificultando a imersão.
texto: A ver, primero que nada: no llegué a terminar la película. Pero si soy completamente sincera, los primeros 40 minutos fueron suficientes. Para muestra, basta un botón. Igual voy a ser buena y darle una oportunidad y terminarla, porque sé que tiene una cantidad absurda de críticas positivas y probablemente haya algo que todavía no estoy viendo. Pero si tengo que sacar una primera conclusión es que me está resultando muy difícil tomarme en serio lo que estoy viendo. No porque la propuesta sea exagerada (esa es parte de su identidad) sino porque muchas de las situaciones me resultan poco verosímiles incluso dentro de la lógica que plantea la propia historia. Lo que más me llama la atención es que se nota que tiene muchísimo presupuesto, pero pareciera que se olvidaron de ponerlo en el guion. Desde el principio me hice millones de preguntas sobre la lógica de esta peli: decisiones sin sentido, situaciones que parecen contradecir las propias reglas que plantea la película e inconsistencias de los personajes. Y creo que ese es mi principal problema: No logra hacerte entrar en su mundo. Es una distopía en la que casi no hay agua, el sol parece querer quemar a todo el mundo y solo lo mas importante para mostrar es como una sociedad decide resolver sus problemas manejando vehículos a toda velocidad por un desierto. Esta premisa puede ser completamente delirante, es justamente por eso q necesitás construir muy bien la trama y las reglas de ese universo para que el espectador diga “okay, esto está loco pero tiene sentido dentro de este mundo” y pueda empatizarrr. Además todo ocurre a una velocidad tan frenética y fría que lo hace todavía más difícil de procesar y así de apoco deja de impresionarte lo que ves. Todo está puesto al servicio de la acción, mientras que la trama y los personajes principales quedan bastante relegados. Y hablando de personajes, tampoco están tan buenos. El protagonista: tipo sensillo, fuerte, misterioso, sarcástico, antihéroe, con pasado trágico y prácticamente todas las características clásicas para que un hombre conecte. El villano es una cosa cochina no se que más decir. Y después están los personajes femeninos. Acá me costó mucho comprar el supuesto mensaje de empoderamiento. Tenemos un grupo de mujeres que son literalmente modelos, todas extremadamente atractivas, vestidas con muy poca ropa, ingenuas e indefensas. Incluso mantienen una actitud cariñosa con una persona que les hizo daño. Hay un personaje femenino que sí se presenta como fuerte y capaz, pero incluso no termina de despegarse de ciertos clichés. Visualmente la película es espectacular. Probablemente sea lo que más puedo rescatar hasta ahora. Tiene una estética muy original y extremadamente reconocible. Todo es exagerado y artificial, pero creo que justamente esa artificialidad es parte de su identidad. El mundo se siente quemado por el sol, los colores son súper contrastantes, los vehículos y personajes tienen diseños increíbles y cada plano parece pensado para ser visualmente muy impactante y llamativo. La música también acompaña muy bien toda esta locura. Si querés una película superficial, no tenés ganas de analizar demasiado la lógica de lo que estás viendo, querés acción prácticamente constante, paisajes increíbles, personajes visualmente muy llamativos y poco interés por el lore o la construcción del mundo, probablemente esta sea tu película. Pero bueno, en cuanto a la trama, se podría haber hecho y aprovechado muchísimo más (y sin hacer falta sacrificar acción) Hacer una película de 2 horas que básicamente trata sobre vehículos peleando en un desierto es una idea muy arriesgada. Para que funcione, hay que saber atrapar al espectador y hacer que le importe lo que está pasando no solo entretenerlo con explosiones y colores. Igual, voy a terminarla. Capaz dentro de una hora vuelvo acá a borrar absolutamente todo esto. Ojalá...

texto: Mad Max Fury Road (2015) von George Miller, erzählt von einer Verfolgungsjagd durch eine postapokalyptische Welt. Der Film hat in erster Linie sehr starke Actionszenen zu bieten, welche gehäuft auftreten und atemberaubend sind. Die inszenierte Welt weckt aber kaum mein Interesse. Sie wirkt auf mich überinszeniert und wenig kohärent. Diese Überinszenierung erzeugt bei mir eher Distanz als Faszination. Zudem finde ich abgesehen von Furiosa und Nux kaum einen Charakter interessant. Besonders die Antagonisten wirken eher wie groteske Symbole, die sehr einprägsam sind, aber für mich keine interessanten Figuren darstellen. Auch Max weckt kein besonderes Interesse bei mir. Oft sieht man Rückblicke, welche bei mir eher unbeantwortete Fragen aufwerfen als Interesse am Charakter. Dass die Charakterentwicklung auch über die Action geschieht, ist mir bewusst, dennoch kann ich mich damit nicht anfreunden. Der Film hat eine sehr simple Handlung, die aus einer Verfolgung besteht, was ich auch als eine der Stärken sehe. Es wird nicht versucht krampfhaft etwas Komplexes erzählen. Dass Start und Endpunkt derselbe sind, ist nett inszeniert gibt dem Film meiner Meinung nach aber auch keine besondere Tiefe.

texto: A film with a detailed world and impressive sets but just another standard non stop action movie. This is my first Mad Max film simply because I haven't been very interested in the series. I do however play games in my free time and after playing Mad Max on the Xbox I thought maybe I should give some of the films a go. Considering Fury road had some extremely positive reviews and starred Tom Hardy I had high hopes. I would have probably been better to assume the worst and be pleasantly surprised though. While it has some things going for it, overall I found it just another average action movie. The set design, world building, costume and sets are impressively immersive and the creators have done an impressive job creating a genuinely unique and believable world. The desert landscapes look incredible and are paired with some excellent cinematography that really brings the world to life. The costume design really brings the characters to life and when paired within the immersive environment it genuinely feels like the world has its own culture and history. Another great element is that it does actually feel like a non stop action film. I personally found the endless action a bit monotonous but if you are a fan of action films this is certainly something you will enjoy. Once the characters hit the fury road, the violence and intensity just keeps hammering away right until the bitter end. I wouldn't say I didn't enjoy the film at all, but for me the endless action didn't allow for any character or story development at all and at times it felt completely exhausting personally. It's just not enough for me to consider it a great film, it is however action paced, immersive and fun. It's also visually stunning and has some incredible stunts and vehicle sequences that offer a unique experience. Mad max is a simple and streamlined action film that's genuinely fun and is complete non stop action. While it has an excellent and immersive world I did find the action became a bit exhausting and did at times wish they spent more time offering viewers any sort of depth or character development. A genuine action film but nothing you haven't seen before from the genre. 6 / 10 Dave Kaye (Bilbo Bagsy) 13/09/2026

texto: A film with a detailed world and impressive sets but just another standard non stop action movie. This is my first Mad Max film simply because I haven't been very interested in the series. I do however play games in my free time and after playing Mad Max on the Xbox I thought maybe I should give some of the films a go. Considering Fury road had some extremely positive reviews and starred Tom Hardy I had high hopes. I would have probably been better to assume the worst and be pleasantly surprised though. While it has some things going for it, overall I found it just another average action movie. The set design, world building, costume and sets are impressively immersive and the creators have done an impressive job creating a genuinely unique and believable world. The desert landscapes look incredible and are paired with some excellent cinematography that really brings the world to life. The costume design really brings the characters to life and when paired within the immersive environment it genuinely feels like the world has its own culture and history. Another great element is that it does actually feel like a non stop action film. I personally found the endless action a bit monotonous but if you are a fan of action films this is certainly something you will enjoy. Once the characters hit the fury road, the violence and intensity just keeps hammering away right until the bitter end. I wouldn't say I didn't enjoy the film at all, but for me the endless action didn't allow for any character or story development at all and at times it felt completely exhausting personally. It's just not enough for me to consider it a great film, it is however action paced, immersive and fun. It's also visually stunning and has some incredible stunts and vehicle sequences that offer a unique experience. Mad max is a simple and streamlined action film that's genuinely fun and is complete non stop action. While it has an excellent and immersive world I did find the action became a bit exhausting and did at times wish they spent more time offering viewers any sort of depth or character development. A genuine action film but nothing you haven't seen before from the genre. 6 / 10 Dave Kaye (Bilbo Bagsy) 13/09/2026

texto: Malcolm X was a complex and controversial person but this film fails to engage with what he believed and why he was such a divisive figure. Despite the incredibly long run time, someone watching this film gets only a vague idea of what he actually believed in. The Civil Rights Movement is only mentioned in passing so a viewer wouldn't know that Malcolm X opposed Civil Rights, as he believed in segregation (though he changed his views somewhat before his death). His disillusionment with the Nation of Islam should be the climax of the movie, but there isn't any buildup or warning signs. Instead the sex scandal is dropped on the viewer out of nowhere and as a result has little emotional impact. The film is simply too long and suffers from poor pacing, as it takes an hour and a half before Malcolm even becomes Malcolm X. With a runtime of over 3 hours there should be enough time to examine his principles and he many extreme and bizarre beliefs of the Nation of Islam. But instead we got odd scenes like his visit to the pyramids that drag on too long and take time away from the interesting parts of his life.

texto: This movie was all over the place. It did a terrible job getting his political views across and failed to show how his upbringing shaped who he became. Malcolm X was a self-critic. He constantly challenged his own beliefs and was humble enough to admit when he was wrong. He was nicknamed Satan during one period of his life, before joining the Nation of Islam and later converting to Sunni Islam. He disagreed with many of Martin Luther King’s views and shared a well-known friendship with Muhammad Ali (then Cassius Clay). Before he entered the criminal world, he frequented music gigs and rubbed shoulders with some of the major blues musicians of the era. The film touches on none of this. It could have focused on one chapter of his life and explored it with real depth. Instead, it scatters across everything and lands on nothing. The film does show his Hajj, and to its credit, the pilgrimage sequence is depicted with some care. But it fails to follow through on what the Hajj meant. The transformation it triggered — his rejection of the Nation of Islam’s racial theology, his embrace of Sunni Islam, and his decision to challenge Elijah Muhammad — is barely explored. That’s the consequence that put a target on his back, and the film treats it as background noise rather than the pivotal turning point it was. The film also completely flattens his relationship with Martin Luther King. Malcolm was openly critical of the civil rights movement’s direction. He argued that political movements tend to get whitewashed, diluted, and commodified. The film makes it seem as though the two men were broadly aligned. They weren’t, and that tension matters. If you’re watching this to understand Malcolm X and his politics, skip it and read the autobiography instead. If you want to watch Denzel Washington play Malcolm X, this is your film because his performance is genuinely excellent. But as a portrait of the man? Three hours, and they left out almost everything that made him who he was.

tema: Falta de profundidade política e contexto histórico
exemplo: As críticas apontam que o filme não explora adequadamente as ideias políticas e religiosas de Malcolm X, deixando de lado suas contradições e o contexto do movimento pelos direitos civis.
texto: To be fair to Lee, and I think Baldwin vocalized this suspicion as well, a Malcolm movie is probably undoable: how can one conceivably imagine  Hollywood allowing a movie to do justice to Malcolm, as an individual life and a microcosm of black life and revolutionary politics in America, in an honest way? This movie is a perfectly fine drama if one wants to ignore the history or the political significance of its subject, but it’s bad history, and not even in a pedantic, fact-checking sort of way. It’s predicated on a book which itself failed to capture Malcolm’s politics or the changes he underwent toward the end of his life (see George Breitman’s excellent 1967 The Last Year of Malcolm X, or the excellent collection Malcolm X Speaks , as a corrective to the Haley autobiography which came out before the script for this movie was even finished). This script was itself famously lambasted by Baldwin as a terrible white Hollywood bastardization of his vision (the movie literally includes a scene Baldwin attacked as an egregious distortion of his vision in a co-writer’s “revision” of his work, instead of the scene Baldwin envisioned. Nell Irvin Painter and Gerald Horne have spilled enough ink on how the script and Lee distorts Malcolm’s historical legacy and political significance. While I won’t go so far as to fully endorse Kwame Ture’s harsh judgement that Lee is a “petit bourgeois who took the choice of selling out of his people for a fistful of dollars” by failing to show that “Malcolm X was a revolutionary”, I think it’s fair to say that Lee doesn’t capture what Baldwin saw in Malcolm, the revolutionary spirit, what he called “a virile impulse long since fled from the American way of life”, a virility which neither Lee’s skillful direction nor Denzel’s tremendous performance evoke. Aside from the formal skill in the movie’s direction, and the great acting, Lee is refreshingly bold in connecting Malcolm to ‘92 at the beginning of the movie, and it’s a shame the rest of thet movie isn’t animated by that same polarizing political charge: Malcolm was a political revolutionary, and by the end of the movie he ceased to be a calculating, political man and is elevated into a depoliticized symbol of Black cultural pride. He counts for color and attitude—for a temperament, much as King and Malcolm represent dueling temperaments at the end of Do the Right Thing— without the substantial content of his political trajectory (e.g. we could also take Karenga’s complaint of the lack of engagement of Malcolm with Africans in the movie, i.e. his internationalism, one of the vital elements of his later political evolution). You can’t capture everything in a life, but to capture someone truthfully , one must engage with the essential aspects of one’s life and work. Malcolm was too great a man, Lee too great a director and Denzel too great an actor for this movie to come together like this.

exemplo: Alguns espectadores sentem que o filme transforma Malcolm X em uma figura santificada, omitindo aspectos controversos e evitando um olhar crítico sobre sua trajetória.
texto: Entre une narration décousue, des longueurs réhibitoires et une version française particulièrement ratée pour Denzel Washington, le film peine à convaincre. Faute d'un traitement psychologique clair, le protagoniste demeure insaisissable et distant, interdisant toute empathie de la part du spectateur. Pour un réalisateur connu pour son audace (comme dans Do the Right Thing), ce film respecte de manière très scolaire les codes du biopic hollywoodien traditionnel. Le film bascule parfois dans l'hagiographie. Spike Lee manque de recul critique vis-à-vis de Malcolm X, en gommant ou en romantisant ses aspects les plus controversés ou ses revirements idéologiques extrêmes pour en faire une figure purement héroïque.

texto: Avec Malcolm X, Spike Lee signe un film qui se veut à la fois ambitieux et nécessaire. Il est évident que ce projet lui tient à cœur et que son importance pour la communauté afro-américaine ne fait aucun doute. Le film est complet, documenté, et témoigne d’un véritable engagement. On comprend pourquoi il a été réalisé et pourquoi il est considéré comme un jalon du cinéma engagé. Pourtant, malgré la force du sujet et l’évidence du travail fourni, le film peine à captiver. Trois heures de récit font parfois sentir le poids de la longueur, et le rythme manque de dynamisme. À certains moments, on a l’impression de parcourir une encyclopédie visuelle plutôt que de vivre une expérience cinématographique. Les séquences s’enchaînent avec fidélité aux événements historiques, mais sans toujours offrir de point de vue nouveau ou d’élan dramatique capable de captiver le spectateur non averti. Le problème n’est pas le sujet, qui est passionnant et chargé d’une intensité politique et humaine indéniable, mais la manière dont il est traité. Malcolm X ressemble parfois à un biopic « Wikipédia » : tout est là, rien n’est oublié, mais la narration peine à provoquer l’émotion ou à stimuler l’esprit. On ressent une impression de distance, comme si le film voulait tout raconter plutôt que raconter quelque chose. En résumé, Malcolm X est un film important, admirable dans son ambition et sa sincérité, mais qui, pour moi, échoue à captiver pleinement. La richesse du matériau historique ne suffit pas à transformer le film en une expérience cinématographique fascinante. Mon jugement repose moins sur le fond que sur la forme : malgré tout le respect que j’ai pour le sujet, je me suis ennuyé, et le film ne m’a pas accroché.

texto: Where to begin. First, I think I just hate Spike Lee. His use of sound, his use of music, the way he uses the camera, it's just so fucking annoying that this is probably the last of his films I will ever put myself through. I've just had it with him. First hour of this movie focuses on Malcolm being an insufferable piece of shit, until he goes to prison and converts to Islam. And despite this being three and a half hours long, Lee still doesn't manage to dive into any of his religious or political nuances, other than it's "us vs. them" Which is ironic, for a movie that's supposed to be anti racist, it sure does come off as pretty fucking racist a lot of the time. And yet despite its length, I managed to feel no empathy - or really anything at all - for not just Malcolm, but for his family, too. Perhaps that is just me - being void of empathy and compassion these days - but as a character study, it is just weak, hollow, and uninspired. Malcolm X deserved better. If you would really like to know more about the man and his views, just skip this and watch a few documentaries.

texto: I really wanted to like this more, especially given the subject and Denzel Washington’s presence, but honestly? This was a frustrating watch. Way too long and overexposed — it drags itself out for over three hours and somehow still feels like it’s just hammering you with information instead of guiding you through a story. It’s less of a movie and more like someone decided to do a Wikipedia reading session, page by page. There’s barely any emotional depth. It doesn’t feel like a character study or a lived experience — just a checklist of events with Denzel stepping in and out of different time periods while the editing makes sure you’re never quite sure where you are. The way it cuts between scenes, especially the flashbacks, is genuinely jarring. There were moments I didn’t even know if what I was watching was part of the present timeline or a narrated memory. It just throws you into transitions with no finesse, and it constantly undercuts any potential momentum. It’s like a photograph with the saturation maxed out — everything is pushed to the extreme without any room for nuance or subtlety. Just messy, loud, and overstuffed. There’s no breathing room. And that’s probably the biggest missed opportunity: with a figure as complex as Malcolm X, you expect depth. But this just overwhelms instead of connecting. Not even Denzel Washington could save this one for me. I’d give it a 2/10 — more exhausting than impactful.

texto: I get that the 202 minute length is a statement in itself, to go against the studio's wishes and make the biggest movie ever about African Americans by African Americans, with the help of additional funds from then A-List superstars like Oprah, Michael Jordan and Bill Cosby. When you've got a chance to make history, go for it! That being said, to sit and watch it is way too long for the intimate scope and simple arc it follows. So intensely focussed on Malcolm's personal life, public speaking, and evolution of beliefs, that it leads to the detriment of showing the results of his work. There's a whole montage summary at the end of the movie, to say how important Malcolm and his work was, and I'm left wondering where was this in the past three and a half hours? While it didn't work for me, I'm happy the movie exists and has its rightful place in history. Plus the production value is insanely good, and Denzel is giving the performance of a lifetime.

texto: I read bell hooks' critical essay about this film right after watching it, so I might be biased toward criticism here. But I think her points are important. She points out that key details of Malcolm's story have been changed, such as the role of his siblings in his conversion to Islam. She also points out that (Black) women in general are portrayed rather superficially, as "either virgins or whores, madonnas or prostitutes— and that’s Hollywood". And that Malcolm's criticisms of colonialism and capitalism are almost absent from the film – likely to make the film more palatable to white audiences. That said, it's still a powerful biopic. It's beautifully shot and powerfully acted. But it's also too Hollywood for its own sake.

texto: Дружба Малкольма Х и Мухаммада Али как показатель братства, и причем здесь "Нация Ислама". Нация Ислама и Малкольм Х Нацию Ислама создал Уоллесон Фардон Мухаммад в 1930. Данная религия продвигала измененный под афроамериканцев Ислам. Где они были божественным видом, а Аллах там считается черным. Малкольм Х - самый яркий бывший представитель "Нации Ислама". Он продвигал идеи религии и боролся за права афроамериканцев. Зарождение дружбы. Мухаммад Али тогда ещё Кэссиус Клей был восходящей звездой в боксе. С сильным характером и сильной агрессией к расизму. Малкольм ходил на бои Клэя, так они и начинали своё знакомство. Братство Кэссиус и Малкольм стали лучшими друзьями. Х помог Клэю обрести политический голос и найти Бога в "Нации Ислама". Элайджи Мухаммад дал имя Клэю - Мухаммад Али. Больше у него нет рабского имени. С того момента Мухаммад начал вести активную политическую жизнь с продвижением своих взглядов, взглядов "НИ" и борьбы с расизмом. Малкольм был наставником великого боксёра. Они были неразлучны. Уход Малкольма из Нации Ислама и единственное, а также главное сожаление Мухаммада Али. Посетив Мекку Малкольм понял, что Нация Ислама это обман и вышел из этой организации в истинную веру и стал настоящим мусульманином. Впредь Х выражал взгляды настоящего Ислама и осуждал "НИ". За это организация множество раз пыталась убить его, и у них это вышло. В тот момент Мухаммад перестал дружить с Малкольмом, он отрекся от него считая предателем. Вскоре после смерти Малкольма Мухаммад никак не отреагировал. Но когда умер лидер "Нации Ислама" Элайджи Мухаммад Али впал в депрессию и последовал за его сыном. Вскоре Мухаммад Али стал сунитом, тобишь проповедовал истинный Ислам. В одном из интервью Мухаммада Спросили, о чем он сожалеет. Он ответил, что только об одном: Он отвернулся от своего лучшего друга - Малкольма Х.

texto: For me this movie actually highlighted that kindness and righteousness are not borne from religion but from humanity. We see as Malcolm X distances himself from the Nation of Islam that it is his humanity that drives him rather than his blind faith. What I really enjoyed about this movie is that it doesn’t paint Malcolm X as a perfect man, not just prior to his prison years but even after. It maintains his humanness even after he joins the Nation of Islam. He struggles with his marriage, himself and his ever changing beliefs. The fact that the movie highlights how Malcolm’s stance on white people, Elijah Muhammad and the NOI was ever-changing over the years displays how he was not some shining and constant monolith of black Islam, but a man who only wanted justice for African-Americans and was malleable within himself to attain that goal. Incredible acting from Denzel Washington I haven’t seen many of his movies but I have a feeling this is one of his best. Fantastic biopic; many scenes gave me chills

texto: The second this 1992 biopic about one of the most important figures of the civil rights era opens with footage of Rodney King, I was fully on board for what Spike was doing. Maybe the greatest cradle to grave biopic I’ve ever seen, and the way how it handles Malcolm’s life as a child, adult pre conversion to Islam, and adult post conversion to Islam effortlessly lets you know you are in the hands of a master. And the whole story anchored by Denzel Washington’s magnum opus as an actor. This is one of those performances that could be described as one of the best of all time, as Denzel completely transforms into one of the most important minds and figure of our times. The filming techniques used to capture this story shows exactly why Spike Lee is one of the most talented directors of our time. Happy Blindspot Day!

texto: Truly one of the greatest, most committed lead performances maybe of all time. Yet, biopics — obviously! — are almost always so reverential and venerational, so totally mythologising in their vision of the biographic object, that I sometimes struggle with the form. I have previously had a very hard time finding some well-recognised, highly lauded biopics even worth finishing. I did not per se have that problem here; the life story is far too engaging, as are Malcolm X’s ideas and the stunning charisma with which Washington portrays him. Angela Bassett’s performance as Betty Shabazz also makes the film so gripping, as she insistently demands that his family life be taken as seriously as his public life, that the two combine to create the man. However, I also can’t say that this is my favourite kind of film, or that I could ever find a biopic a truly great Work Of Art. Perhaps a me-problem. (Obviously I recognise it’s completely deranged to watch a film this Big on a plane, but here we are)

texto: Once in a generation biopic? Once in a generation film? Once in a generation artistic achievement? I could hyperbolize about Malcolm X forever and I still would not be able to put into sufficient words just how monumental Spike Lee’s scrupulous account of this man is. No other visual rendition of a public figure can even approximate the effect of its testament to the significance of not just this individual life, but every individual life. It magnetizes with its ambition only to pull the viewer in further, further into its sweeping crevices that envelop the harrowing volatility of souls. Still so early in their illustrious careers, Denzel Washington and Spike Lee demonstrate a drive here that it’s difficult to say they ever had again (if anyone else has ever had it at all); their particular fortitude, courage, confidence, and determination as artists harmonize perfectly with their subject. From the first crackles of the smoldering Stars and Stripes, they reach for the limits of their capabilities and we are witnesses to an actor and his director refusing to deliver anything to the screen except undiluted inspiration. Just please watch this movie.

texto: The second this 1992 biopic about one of the most important figures of the civil rights era opens with footage of Rodney King, I was fully on board for what Spike was doing. Maybe the greatest cradle to grave biopic I’ve ever seen, and the way how it handles Malcolm’s life as a child, adult pre conversion to Islam, and adult post conversion to Islam effortlessly lets you know you are in the hands of a master. And the whole story anchored by Denzel Washington’s magnum opus as an actor. This is one of those performances that could be described as one of the best of all time, as Denzel completely transforms into one of the most important minds and figure of our times. The filming techniques used to capture this story shows exactly why Spike Lee is one of the most talented directors of our time. Happy Blindspot Day!

texto: Watched this for my spring of 2026 college course: cinema director: Spike Lee (think that was the course name). Theme/Subject: transformation Cinematic aspect: cinematography One expressive cinematography is the three different color pallets to paint the historical transformation Malcolm X had. Each color pallet reflects the three acts in the film. The first one (Act I) is shown to be warm and rich which represents his youth and his drug addiction since there was a crack epidemic ravaging  the black population. Then we move to Act II which contains one cool shade color that represents Malcolm X’s time in prison. When serving his time in prison Malcolm found his faith, Islam, and we get to Act III which is to be seen as more of the earthy type of color to represent him joining the National of Islam (NOI) and eventually Malcolm X left and went to Mecca he took the name of el-Hajj Malik el-Shabazz. Each color shows different stages of his life. I think the opening montage really sets the mood for the film. It was an interesting way of incorporating history of violence against the black population mixed with the audio of Malcolm X along with the American flag slowly burning up and turning into the letter X. Right there and then you get a sense of what the movie will be about. When reading the textbook (pg 203-207) it was important that Lee wanted to shoot the Middle Eastern scenes in Africa rather than New Jersey. “It was a life-changing experience for Spike” (pg 204). Lee felt an instant connection where he saw the pyramid and the sphinx for the first time and thought those were his ancestors who built them. Scientists to this day don’t know how it was built. That scene in the film was the turning point for Malcolm X where he wanted to express more of an internationalist and anti-racism perspective. And truly without one of Lee’s associate producers, Fernado Sulichin, that scene and Lee’s experience wouldn’t have happened. Sulichin did not take a no for an answer. Heck “he [even] went to the high Islamic court again and again, until they finally agreed to allow for the first time a 35mm motion picture camera in the city of Mecca during Hajj” (pg 204). Even though the film was long (which I did not expect) I thought it was put together beautifully. I mean Denzel Washington was phenomenal. Of all of Spike Lee’s films we were going to watch this semester, this film was the one I was most excited to watch because of Denzel’s performance and the man he delivered.

texto: MALCOLM X *SPOİLER* Önce kendisinin hayat hikayesini anlatmakla başlayalım. Malcolm'un babası daha Malcolm 6 yaşında iken öldürülür ve annesi ise yaşananlardan dolayı akıl hastanesine kaldırılır. Malcolm ise koruyucu ailede kalır. 20 yaşında hırsızlık ve diğer suçlardan hapishaneye girer ve orda "İslam Ümmeti" adlı harekata katılır ve Müslüman olup kendi yolunu çizmeye başlar. Malcolm harekata katılmadan önce de dünyanın nasıl işlediğinin farkındaydı ve kendisini film de siyahilerin ne durumda olduğunu en baştan söylüyordu. Harekata katıldıktan sonra ise en başta inandığı yoldan ilerledi ve hakkı yenen tüm siyahilere ses oldu. Ancak ilerde işler sarpa saracak ki kendisi idol aldığı *Elijah Muhammed* tarafından ihanete uğrar ve onlarla yollarını ayırır. Burada kendisinin söylediği şu sözü yazmak istiyorum; -"Ölümü anlarım ama ihaneti anlayamıyorum..." Malcolm çıktığı yerden dolayı ölümden korkmayan birisi olarak biliyoruz ancak kendisi bu yaşına kadar böyle sağlam bir ihanete uğramamıştı. Hem de dost dediği insanlardan gelen bu ihanetin sebebini kendisi o zaman bunu sorgulamış ve Allaha dua etmekten başka bir şey yapamamıştır. Peki neden Malcolm X? Kendisi bunu şöyle açıklıyor: -"Malcolm köle tacirlerinin verdiği bir isim X ise bilinmeyeni temsil ediyor aynı matematik de ki gibi. Kendi ana vatanımıza döndüğümüzde bu X anlamını kaybedecek ve bilinmeyen kalkacak." Malcolm kendi yolunda giderken aynı zamanda Hacca da gitmiştir ve gittikten sonra önemli bir bilinç kazanmıştır. **Irk eşitliği** bu bilinç ile amerikaya geri dönen Malcolm ırkçı olmadığını ve herkese kucak açtığını söyler. Her müslümanın yapması gerektiği gibi. Buradan sonra ise Malcolm artık diğer harekatçılar tarafından baskı görmeye başlar ve ölüm tehtitleri alır. Malcolm ise bunları umursamaz ve kendi davasından vazgeçmeyerek yoluna devam eder. En sonda ise yaptığı seminer konuşmasında suikaste uğrar ve orada can verir hem de kendi ailesinin yanında. Malcolm bu yola çıkar için başlamadı o sadece siyahilerin en doğal haklarından mahrum kalmasına karşı çıktı ve İslam'ın da buyurduğu gibi haksızlığa karşı çıktı. Bir Müslüman olarak ona Allah rahmet eylesin demek düşüyor bize, onun gibi insanlar bu dünya da çok az bulunuyor ve çoğumuz bize söyleneni yapıyoruz. Bunu yaparken de sorgulamıyor, internette ne dolaşırsa inanıyoruz. Bu biyografi eserine 10/10 puan veriyorum gerek anlatım olsun gerek duygu olsun her şekilde karşıladığını düşünüyorum özellikle *Denzel Washington* burada harika oynamış diyebilirim. *Spike Lee* ise muhteşem bir iş çıkarmış. Benden bu kadar bu tarz filmlere merakınız varsa izlemenizi kesinlikle öneriyorum bu tarz filmler size çok şey katar. Filmi izleyeceklere iyi seyirler diğerlerine de iyi günler dilerim.

texto: If Rocky was a narcissistic cipher or The Bear was centred on Mikey at his most selfish - you still wouldn't come close to this hot mess. Perhaps it shouldn't have been a surprise that a film that cast Kevin O'Leary thinks charm and emotional depths are unnecessary and that leaving bodies in your wake is acceptable if you consider yourself a 'visionary'. Maybe the message is you don't need to be wealthy to be a douche - but you do need to be rich to consider sexual humiliation and abuse as appropriate evening entertainment. There is one scene near the beginning where Chalamet is trying to hussle and threaten payment out of his employers. It's a brief moment where you think this film might give him space for the nuance he does so well and for the  character building needed to make everything work . . . But then it's gone. And Timmy is buried under over loud music and bewildering storytelling that lurches from vignette to vignette. The subplot with Paltrow could have been interesting but its squandered by the choice to end it with her in tears and Timmy being spanked by her husband - I wish I was joking. Chalamet, Paltrow and A'zion deserved better. So did the audience.

texto: ENGLISH Version below 🇩🇪 Fanatisch. Temporeich. Dramatisch. Marty Mauser (Timothée Chalamet) ist im Jahre 1952 zwar nur ein talentierter Schuhverkäufer, doch er strebt nach Höherem: er möchte unbedingt der erste US-amerikanische Tischtennis-Weltmeister werden, den Sport in den USA populär machen und durch den Verkauf spezieller Tischtennisbälle reich werden. Wären da nur nicht die japanische Konkurrenz und die dauernden Geldsorgen… Das größte Plus von „Marty Supreme“ ist zweifellos Timothée Chalamet, der seine Figur so ekstatisch spielt, dass man beinahe Angst um seine Gesundheit bekommt. Marty ist zwar ein narzisstisches Arschloch, allerdings nicht frei von Talent, beim Tischtennis und auch sonst. Dabei schlittert er von einer Katastrophe in die andere, windet sich immer wieder mit fragwürdigem Mitteleinsatz heraus aber bekommt irgendwie nie so ganz die Kurve. Die Handlung ist unfassbar temporeich, Kamera und Figuren scheinbar dauernd in Bewegung. Das kann man mögen, muss man aber nicht, ich fühlte nach einiger Zeit Kopfschmerzen aufkeimen, da half auch der - für mich - katastrophale und penetrante Soundtrack nicht. Das größte Problem jedoch: der Film ist viel zu lang geraten, das wirkt auch dramaturgisch unausgewogen, mindestens eine halbe Stunde hätte man streichen sollen. Ich finde „Marty Supreme“ nicht schlecht, aber das cineastische Meisterwerk, welches viele andere geschätzte Filmfreunde gesehen haben, vermochte ich leider nicht zu erkennen. 🇬🇧 Fanatical. Fast-paced. Dramatic. In 1952, Marty Mauser (Timothée Chalamet) may just be a talented shoe salesman, but he has his sights set on something greater: he’s determined to become the first American table tennis world champion, popularize the sport in the U.S., and get rich by selling special table tennis balls. If only it weren’t for the Japanese competition and his constant money troubles… The biggest highlight of “Marty Supreme” is undoubtedly Timothée Chalamet, who plays his character with such ecstasy that you almost start to worry about his health. Marty may be a narcissistic jerk, but he’s not without talent—in table tennis and in other areas as well. He slides from one disaster to the next, repeatedly wriggling his way out of trouble with questionable means, but somehow never quite gets his act together. The plot moves at an incredibly fast pace, with the camera and characters seemingly in constant motion. You might like that, but you don’t have to—after a while, I felt a headache coming on, and even the soundtrack—which I found disastrous and obtrusive—didn’t help. The biggest problem, however, is that the film is far too long; it also feels dramaturgically unbalanced—they should have cut at least half an hour. I don’t think “Marty Supreme” is bad, but unfortunately, I couldn’t see the cinematic masterpiece that many other esteemed film enthusiasts have seen in it.

texto: Inizio col dire che sono contento che Chalamet non abbia vinto l'oscar, per quanto valore abbia, con questo film. Perché? Perché sarebbe stata un'ingiustizia verso le altre GIGANTI performance che non sono state prese in considerazione tanto quanto Marty Supreme. Non fraintendete, qui è incredibile, ma probabilmente non si avvicina alla sua top 3. Sono dell'opinione che la pubblicità ed il marketing, abbiano reso iconico questo film, perché altrimenti non se ne sarebbe parlato così tanto. Safdie fa un lavoro sublime, il personaggio di Marty è scritto e messo in scena in un modo quasi unico. Mi è pesato particolarmente stargli dietro, più volte ho provato fastidio nel sentirlo parlare o anche solo respirare guardando le espressioni. E' proprio quel tipo di persona che non dovrebbe nascere, nemmeno per sbaglio. Narcisista, manipolatore, adulatore, ladro, bugiardo, truffatore, egoista. A livello tecnico con Diamanti Grezzi, che trovo superiore a Marty Supreme, ha già fatto vedere di cosa è capace. Qui ha comunque tenuto l'asticella alta, nonostante non abbia apprezzato alcune cose. Secondo me ci sono delle "problematiche" che sotto certi aspetti lo rendono debole: - il personaggio di Marty sovrasta completamente ogni altro personaggio all'interno del film. Sicuramente è una cosa voluta, ne sono certo, ma rende la visione troppo piatta in alcuni momenti. L'unico personaggio, che ha probabilmente un pò di risalto, è Kletzki. Ma solamente perché Safdie gli dedica 5 minuti di screenplay e gli da un'identità ben definita; - qual è il topic principale di questo film? è un (non)biopic, è un film sullo sport, è un film drammatico, è un film sull'ossessione. E' tutto, ma non è niente. Non è carne né pesce. Quindi cos'è? L'ho trovato senza identità. Trovo davvero ironico che alla fine della visione, l'unica cosa che mi abbia davvero colpito, è l'unica cosa che mi portava a non vedere Marty Supreme, Chalamet. La cosa che mi ricorderà di questo film è la pallina da ping pong, brandizzata ovviamente, che mi è stata regalata da mio nipote. Lo guarderò di nuovo però, questo è certo.

texto: Chalamet channels Woody Allen and Max Fisher from Wes Anderson's Rushmore. The film adds thumpy music here and there and a few inconsequential dramatic moments to make the movie feel more than the sports biopic it ultimately is. The film, to be sure, has some great writing and interplay between Chalamet's Marty and other characters he spars with in his quest to become the face of table tennis in the US. My ultimate feeling, though, is that this film didn't know what it wanted to say. And it tried to beef up its relative triviality with lots of scenes that felt quite meandering e.g. the Abel Ferrara's dog stuff. I can't say I enjoy the way either of the Safdie bros go about making movies. Nifty editing only goes so far as a tool to inject intrigue into familiar narratives.

texto: Egotistical asshole alert Marty’s a man who knows what he wants and will do anything to get it. Even if that means screwing over everyone he’s ever had any sort of relationship with. He believed he was worth everyone’s time and no one was worth his. Okay hotshot let’s get knocked down a peg. What a fast paced piece of art man. The talking over each other is a nice touch because it really paints through text that Marty always needed to be the loudest in the conversation; always the one that needed to be heard over everyone else. He didn’t give a shit about anyone else and truly talked them in circles over and over. He got it in the ass (literally) for it and perhaps he learned humility in those last moments of the match before rushing home but still . . lol man what a loser. But Rachel really loves him and I guess that’s all that matters. I mean she became a hell of a swindler also Nothing ever lasts forever, Everybody wants to rule the world, indeed Tears for Fears, you said it best.

texto: “Embarrass me? I am beyond embarrassment.” More like “ Marty Extreme .” The Safdies have perfected the art of portraying deeply flawed, anti-hero protagonists who are disruptive agents of chaos, spewing out hurricanes of entropy that derail the lives of everyone around them. Josh perfects it in this film, with a superb performance by Chalamet that shows in stark relief the cost of narcissism and the unbridled pursuit of greatness. I love the anachronistic score. To me it’s perfect. Forget about the era of the songs and just appreciate how perfectly they augment the emotional notes. So good. Unlike the other Safdie Brothers films, this one offers a hint of optimism. A sense that you can find a way to achieve a self-acknowledged win against the system, but still pull out (pun intended) before it’s too late, and spend a life focused on the aspects of existence that are less spotlighted, but infinitely more important. Just redefine the game.

texto: Why the fuck did I sleep on this when it was out in theaters? I would’ve been blown away seeing this there. I was still blown away just watching this home. Great soundtrack, GREAT performances and although it feels like another play on Safdies thing for manic protagonists scheming their way to satisfaction, it never feels overdone or tiresome. I think he just nailed the formula of just automatically understanding what this main character is and what he wants and rest of the film becomes a comedy of consequences.

texto: Yeah, Timothée was snubbed of that oscar. This might be his single best acting performance ever. (besides Dune ofc) Throughout the entire film he just embodies the feeling of overwhelming obsession. Every single scene with Chalamet is so strong just because of the acting and it’s remarkable. He didn’t get in the tournament, but he still got to achieve the feat of beating his rival head-to-head. I loved this movie and this is probably one of my favorite sports films ever.

texto: In a word, exhausting. The Safdies are masters at the sweaty nervous energy of the economically depressed, the abrasive, and the fast talking con-men of the world.  In Uncut Gems the propulsive nature of the constant wheeling and dealing, the sense of impending doom, and Adam Sandler's charisma kept the stress from becoming overwhelming and the character one you love to hate.  Wishing for his success despite loathing his actions. In Marty Supreme, the movie is more or less split into two separate and distinct tracks. One a fairly typical, but brilliantly shot, short sports movie.  The other, a scrabbling descent into layers and layers of cons, dodges, grifts, and hustles weaving in and out of one another for nearly two hours.  All of it wonderfully acted, with cameos galore, but utterly draining and seemingly endless. I find myself at a strange impasse as a result.  There can be no doubt that is an incredible and effective movie.  But I don't think I could ever deal with seeing it again. Highly recommended, but be prepared for a marathon of awful people being awful to one another for the bulk of the experience.

texto: والله يا ذا الفلم يا انه لمس فيني لين ما طفشت كل مشهد يصير اتذكر نفسي بشي مقارب سويته ( مب الزنا انتبه ) لين ما الله هدانا ( القصه والسيناريو )طيب القصه بسيطه السيناريو شفيقه سامج ؟ جات بخاطري المهم السيناريو كان مره جامد مره مره جامد ممتع لدرجة رغم تلغيم الاحداث إلا انه ما فقد جوهره الكتابي وظل متمسك فيه وزود انه يتكلم عن شاب مهووس بالرياضه إلا ان الفلم ما كان رياضي بل يتكلم عن رحلة شخص ممكن يضحي بأي شي لاجل الرياضه اللي هو يحبها او بالأصح مهووس فيها مبهر والله العناصر ( الصوتيه و البصريه ) عشان اكون صادق المؤثرات الصوتيه او الموسيقى ايًا كانت ما دخلتني جو الفلم ولا ركزت فيها حتى من كثر انها غير نافعه الا فالجزئيه الاخيره كانت متناسقه ( التمثيل والتطور ) تبون الصدق والله طولت عشان القى جمله توصف تيموثي بذا الفلم لانه شاله شيل بالأصح هو اساس نجاح ذا الفلم فــ لو اتكلم عن تمثليه بطول اما الشخصيات الجانبيه ثلاث او اربع أدّوها بنجاح البقيه ما تلومهم ولا تمدحهم ( الإخراج ) صراحة ما كانك بالقرن 19 يعني شي عادي إلا بعض الاوقات اما ككل مافيه تناسق مع القرن 19 يمكن هم مستقصدين الرتم مرههه قوي وممتع واعتقد ان المخرج قدر يتناغم مع أسلوب تيموثي وهذي النتيجه لان كيف كل مره تشوف تيموثي بإحساس تعرف وش يحس مب تطالع وتستغرب وش يحس وتقعد يومين تفكر ( الثيمات والقيمة الفنية )تبون الصدق والله ما عرفتها إلا لما بحثت يمكن الغلط مني لكن يوم قريت الثيمات كل شوي اقول والله صح والله صح صار كذا صار كذا صراحة تقدر تقول اكتسبت رؤية مختلفه لاشياء كانت تحصل لي وقتها يعني قيمته الفنيه متقنه الفلم فيه ضباب وانت لازم تستكشف الفلم مب واضح وانت لازم تبحث عنه الفلم كانك قدام منظر جميل لكن مب لابس نظارة هذا تخيلي الأقرب للي حصل لي

texto: Deux flics de province tellement dépassés par leur enquête qu'ils préfèrent frapper des suspects au hasard et consulter une voyante plutôt que suivre une vraie méthode scientifique, l'académie de police coréenne n'a visiblement jamais entendu parler de la scène de crime qu'on ne piétine pas à dix personnes. Bong Joon-ho enchaîne les scènes qui devraient installer une tension glaçante mais qui basculent sans prévenir dans un comique presque slapstick, comme cette poursuite ridicule dans les champs de riz où l'un des flics dégringole une pente en pleine filature. La scène de l'interrogatoire musclé, censée être un tournant dramatique fort, se retrouve elle aussi parasitée par ce ton étrange qui hésite entre le grave et le grotesque. Et le twist final, où l'enquêteur revient des années plus tard sur les lieux sans jamais avoir eu de réponse claire, tombe complètement à plat après tant de tergiversations tonales. Bref, ce mélange volontaire d'humour et d'enquête criminelle ne m'a jamais permis de rentrer dans le film, ni par la peur ni par la tension, le tout m'ayant laissé complètement indifférent du début à la fin, 1 étoile.

texto: was so excited to watch this and found it disappointing. i don’t understand what’s so special about it. it’s literally a detective movie, with unbelievably useless detectives. the mystery is left unresolved, so the film builds up to something that never comes together, which i understand was intentional but i just didn’t think it was that effective. i get that the film was exploring the nature of evil and how it can take the form of an 'ordinary' person, not a caricature-like obvious villain, and at times the mystery is really intriguing, but it feels like it never fully takes off. for the first hour especially, i was very bored and nearly gave up. i also understood the idea that the unsolved murders resulted in trauma for the detectives but i feel like the psychological impacts on them was never really explored in terms of things i did like, the setting was brilliant and worked well with the story. the confinement of the town, the enclosed, empty spaces like the train tunnel and the place the first body was found were all cleverly used. the ending shot was good and in places it's quite funny overall it wasn't bad but it wasn't great. not sure what all the fuss is about

texto: I found out after that this was based on a true story, of a then still unidentified murderer. This movie does make many statements. Among other things, I think it was meant to highlight the unethical ways police at the time operated, but also the bad conditions people lived in, the violence in the everyday, blame laid on disabled people because it was convenient, and unending other problems which seem to build the violence to the point of murder, and the inadequacy of the police in catching the culprit. And you do feel the helplessness, yet another murder happens and you’re still not any closer to the answers. There are criminals among us in society and they could be anyone. The way the movie ends could be interpreted in different ways, but it implies that society is part of the problem, which includes you. I liked the color grading and the vibe of the film, definitely felt like the time period it was supposed to have taken place in, but not my first pick because of how crude it was. The first half was worse.

texto: Pissed me off. I get it, I understand why it ends the way it ends but it was so immensely frustrating it ruined the movie for me. And I get that that is the point!!! Admittedly, I didn’t know that this movie was based on a true story and that it was a cold case in 2003 until it ended and my brother told me, so know that I know that, I get it even more. And so I don’t necessarily dislike the idea of a no-answer (the final shot is amazing, yeah) — especially if that was the ‘truth’ at the time — and of course I get that the cops are meant to be corrupt and that the desperation of an unsolvable crime drives people to the brink, but I had a very hard time caring about men with power abusing it while women were being brutally murdered, seemingly in the background. I like Bong Joon Ho, and I didn’t think that this was a hyper misogynistic movie, but the brutality of the crimes felt so commonplace. The victims were consistently treated as a narrative afterthought and I just couldn’t bring myself to care about it at all. The cops torture men to get a confession for their own sake. Of course they don’t care about the women being raped and murdered with their own clothes, why would they? All they want is a confession, which is what the movie makes us care about. The women are an afterthought to the corruption. They are victims twice over, once in ‘practice’ (for lack of a better term), and for a second time when they are effectively forgotten about during the course of the investigation. And I get that that is sadly the way it almost always seems to be in real life, and perhaps the movie does it so well, it portrays that calloused, misogynistic corruption that seeps into everything so well that I couldn’t stand it. I felt like this meme while attempting to laugh at the dropkicks. How can I care about anything in the face of such brutality, especially when that brutality seems to be barely relevant? I don’t think it’s a bad movie, but I rarely write searching for objectivity, so I can only say that I hated it. Not for me at all. Once again, I understand why it does all that it does, and I guess I understand why it’s hailed as a Great, but I couldn’t look past how cavalier it was towards women being consistently brutalized. And I understand that perhaps that’s the way it’s meant to be, I guess it is a critique on that very calloused misogynistic corruption, but it feels a bit like the idea of an anti war movie. How can a movie not be misogynistic when most of its female characters are shown with their limbs splayed out on the ground? I’ve been very angry lately and I just can’t bring myself to ignore misogyny more than any woman does every day.

texto: Let’s be honest: if you strip away all the pseudo-intellectual interpretations people have of this movie, it’s literally about nothing. It feels like everything that happens was made solely to build up to the ending. And yes, the ending is interesting in its own way, but it’s nowhere near as groundbreaking, revolutionary, or profound as people try to make it out to be. Movies like this existed before, were being made around the same time, and continued to be made afterward. There’s nothing particularly new here, other than the fact that this specific movie was made by Koreans. And if you take the ending away, there’s basically nothing left. The movie doesn’t stand out in any other way. There’s no particularly interesting detective element, no characters you actually want to follow, and no dialogue that’s especially engaging. Just exaggerated emotional reactions that start getting annoying after a while. It’s an incredibly boring movie. Yes, it has an idea, and yes, that idea is expressed reasonably well, but it’s hardly some extraordinary concept that magically makes up for everything else. It’s simply a mediocre movie about nothing that people seem to worship way too much — and, honestly, the only real reason I can see for that is that it was made in Korea. There just doesn’t seem to be any other explanation

texto: Je ne comprends pas trop en quoi memories of Murder est considéré comme un chef d'oeuvre. La seconde moitié du film était intéressante, l'enquête devient plus concrète, on a des jolis plans et j'ai trouvé ca cool mais on restait sur un scénario d'enquête assez classique selon moi. En fait j'ai pas trop compris où le film voulait vraiment nous emmener, j'étais vraiment hype de voir le dénouement, je me suis dit que ca débloquerait tout ça, mais non. Je trouve pas que la fin était si ouf, je la trouve meme frustrante, aucun réel dénouement. Je dis pas que c'est mauvais de ne pas avoir de coupable mais je trouve qu'après avoir eu autant de fausses pistes, finir sur une fausse piste était celle de trop.

texto: Terminei de assistir e fui procurar sobre o filme no Google, e simplesmente descobri que ele é superaclamado, considerado uma obra-prima do cinema sul-coreano. Mas, para mim, ficou longe disso. É aquilo: se a gente não gosta dos protagonistas, dificilmente consegue se envolver com a história. E aqui aconteceu justamente isso. A incompetência dos investigadores me dava agonia, principalmente por deixarem várias pistas passarem, como se não estivessem levando o caso a sério. Não é à toa que o caso não foi solucionado. Agora, uma coisa que gostei bastante foi a ambientação, mostrando a transição de um regime autoritário para uma democracia funcional e como esse contexto influencia a investigação. No final, senti como se o filme tivesse sido feito pensando justamente no serial killer. Quando o detetive quebra a quarta parede e olha diretamente para a câmera, dizendo que o assassino tem um rosto normal e que pode ser qualquer pessoa, parece quase um aviso à população: ele ainda está à solta e pode estar em qualquer lugar.

texto: I dont really get the hype. Its got the obvious Korean style of despite the seriousness of the subject matter will be quite silly or over exaggerated (i.e. the fella constantly drop kicking people), but beyond the style and obvious great direction from Bong Joon Ho, it was quite an unintresting story that lacked progression. Remins me somewhat of Zodiac or Summer of Sam in the sense that it shows how people react as these murders are going on rather than an exact detective who done it? thriller, but when your leads are intact detectives they just seem entirely incompetent. I dont know if their was some context that I missed but I dont get the hype and think its in the same bracket of Fight Club as one of the most overhyped films (not because their bad, just because their not as great as everyone says).

texto: Tratto da eventi storici realmente accaduti, ovvero gli omicidi seriali avvenuti a Hwaseong in una provincia rurale della Corea del Sud. "Memories of Murder" è stato uno dei maggior successi commerciali dell'apprezzato regista coreano Bong Joon-ho. Anche se l'incipit della narrazione e il modus operandi del serial killer vengono descritti in modo del tutto ordinario. Memories of Murder si discosta dal solito poliziesco per quel ricordo, un frammento di eventi autoctoni svaniti nel tempo che tornano alla mente solo nel finale, capace di trasportare lo spettatore occidentale in un mondo parzialmente estraneo. L'opera di Bong Joo-ho è dunque degna di interesse perchè porta alla superficie una concreta denuncia sociale, una pertinente e aspra critica alla società, nello specifico quella delle forze di Polizia, fondata sul concetto autartico dell'ego. Un ego smisurato che non si preoccupa minimamente del concetto di variabilità dell'ipotesi. Ciò che conta di più è portare a termine le indagini ad ogni costo, e insabbiare alla stampa certe pratiche ortodosse adottate a discapito dei sospettati. Tipiche pratiche fra l'altro molto diffuse nella cultura asiatica.. Il film cattura l'interesse già da subito grazie all'ottimo cast, Sang Kang-ho (Parasite), Park Ha-il, Kim Roi-ha, Kim Sang-Kyung, Jung In-sun etc, e all'ambientazione rurale piovosa e a una fotografia degna di nota. Aimé non mancano delle forzature per "incanalare" la sceneggiatura negli eventi voluti, e l'importante minutaggio evidenzia dei dettagli di trama superflui. Ma la soggettiva peculiarità della trama sta tutta racchiusa nel finale amaro quanto drammaticamente evocativo. La curiosità, e il rammarico di aver sbagliato scuotono i sensi del protagonista e dello spettatore.. Dove il cinismo del passato riemerge e si impadronisce di nuovo della ragione, ma quello che ne rimane e soltanto l'immaginazione di un volto comune. Troppo comune.. Visione consigliatissima. Voto: più che sufficiente.

texto: Gerade geguckt: „Memories of Murder“ ist ein Kriminal Thriller welcher 1986, in einer kleinen Provinz, im von der Militärdiktatur geprägten Südkorea spielt. Es geht um zwei ungleiche Kommissarre, die versuchen eine Reihe von Morden aufzuklären, welche immer an einem verregneten Tag und an rot gekleideten Frauen begangen werden. Allerdings ist der Film nicht nur ein einfacher Krimi sondern auch eine Nachricht an den echten Mörder, welcher erst 16 Jahre nach dem erscheinen des Films gefasst wurde. Abgesehen davon Thematisiert der Film die Inkompetenz der Polizei und den moralischen Verfall einer der Kommissare sowie Südkorea im Chaos des kurz bevorstehenden Umbruchs der Diktatur. Regisseur Bong Joon-ho zeichnet mit „Memorie of Murder“ ein atmosphärisches und immer düsterer werdendes Portrait einer traumatisierten Gesellschaft in wunderschönen aber dreckigen Bildern. Die letzte Szene ging mit einem einfachen aber tief gehenden Blick in die Kamera, nicht zu Unrecht in die Filmgeschichte ein. „Memories of Murder“ wird mir wahrscheinlich noch die nächsten Tage im Gedächtnis bleiben und motiviert mich weiter in Bong Joon-ho‘s Vita und das Koreanische Kino einzutauchen. Meiner Meinung nach einer der besten Filme seines Genres, die ich bis jetzt gesehen habe. Kann ich jedem empfehlen. (Btw noch nie so viele Dropkicks in einem ernsten Film gesehen)

texto: When first watching Memories of Murder: I had heard that it was a masterpiece of True Crime filmmaking. I had watched many Korean horror films but this was the first drama/true crime foreign film. I'll admit, I didn't really get it the first time. All the detectives are kind of inept and do some pretty bad things themselves. So who do we route for? And that ending .... What!? But for years it stuck with me. So I started looking into it and realized "Oh, this was based on an actual serial killing in South Korea." And not just a serial killing, but what many would consider to be the first modern serial killer in South Korea. The director, Bong Joon-ho, probably remembered and experienced some of this growing up.  The police were actually pretty inept did infact torture confessions from people and were in over their heads. While creative liberties were taken, timelines shortened and some people involved changes: the telling is quite accurate. Knowing that now, Memories of Murder becomes much more engaging, interesting and poignant. All of our characters are shades of grey because the detectives were in fact torturing confessions from people, were incredibly under resources and frequently went off of feelings or hunches because of a lack of evidence. While being culturallydifferent from traditional American detective stories (Zodiac and Seven come to mind) once you get used to the Korean style and culture, with some added understanding of the true events that inspire the story, Memories of Murder really is a master piece in true crime filmmaking. It is also an interesting look at a director's early work that would carry them into greater future success.

texto: For the first hour or so I assumed the film was building towards a scathing critique of the police, but that interpretation eventually falls flat. I think Memories of Murder is absent the social commentary I’m used to from Bong Joon Ho. Anyway, as one of the least subtle filmmakers operating at his level, I’d like to think if he were going for a big statement as with Parasite, Okja, Mickey 17, or Snowpiercer I would have picked up on it. Instead we get one of the best Fincher-lite neo-noir psychological studies.

texto: Logo de cara, uma coisa que me chamou atenção foi o filme ser dividido em partes. Normalmente, enquanto eu assisto, vou acumulando pensamentos — sobre fotografia, personagens, narrativa — até chegar no final com uma visão mais formada. Aqui, isso simplesmente não aconteceu. E eu fiquei me perguntando o tempo inteiro: eu não entendi… ou o filme não se sustenta? Porque, pra mim, nada funcionou. Eu não entendi a história. Não consegui me conectar com absolutamente nada do que estava sendo mostrado. As cenas são extremamente picotadas, desconexas, como se o filme nunca quisesse realmente construir algo — só sugerir, sugerir, sugerir… e nunca chegar em lugar nenhum. E isso, ao invés de me instigar, me afastou completamente. Tem 2 horas e 10 minutos de duração, e a sensação é que o tempo se arrasta. Em geral, mesmo quando um filme não é bom, eu ainda consigo me entreter minimamente, observar, pensar, me envolver de alguma forma. Aqui não. Foi um dos raros casos em que eu senti o tempo pesar de verdade. Essas 2 horas pareceram metade de um dia. Existe um momento — lá por mais de uma hora de filme — em que algo minimamente interessante acontece. E por um instante, parece que o filme finalmente vai se organizar, que vai dizer alguma coisa. Mas não. Ele volta pro mesmo estado de antes: arrastado, vazio, desconexo. Eu fui assistir por causa de uma cena específica — a da cachoeira ficando vermelha. E sim, é bonita. Mas é um detalhe tão rápido, tão pequeno dentro do todo, que não sustenta absolutamente nada do resto. E isso acaba resumindo muito da minha experiência. Nada ali me pegou. Não gostei da fotografia (tirando esse momento isolado). Não gostei dos personagens — não são cativantes, não me despertaram interesse. Não gostei da narrativa — não me disse nada, não me provocou nada. E talvez o que mais me incomoda é isso: eu tentei. Eu realmente me esforcei pra entrar no filme, pra pensar sobre ele, pra extrair alguma coisa. Mas não veio nada. Nenhuma sensação, nenhuma leitura, nenhum impacto. Só cansaço. Eu saí mais frustrado do que qualquer outra coisa. E até agora eu ainda fico me perguntando se perdi alguma coisa… ou se simplesmente não tinha nada ali pra mim. Mas, do jeito que foi: eu odiei.

texto: O Som ao Redor: Entre a Tensão Silenciosa e o TédioO longa de estreia de Kleber Mendonça Filho não é um filme de ação, mas um filme de atmosfera. Ele se passa em uma rua de classe média no Recife, onde a chegada de uma milícia de segurança particular altera a dinâmica dos moradores.Por que ele parece "lento e cansativo"?A sua sensação faz sentido porque o filme utiliza o tempo real e o cotidiano para construir uma sensação de mal-estar.Falta de um conflito central explosivo: Não há um grande crime a ser resolvido logo de cara. O filme foca em detalhes: o barulho do ar-condicionado, o latido do cachorro, a rotina de uma dona de casa entediada.Narrativa fragmentada: Ele acompanha vários personagens ao mesmo tempo, o que impede que a gente se apegue rapidamente a uma única jornada heróica.O que a crítica viu (e por que ele é tão premiado)Para a crítica, essa "lentidão" é proposital. O filme é visto como um suspense social.A "Casa-Grande" moderna: O filme sugere que, embora o Brasil tenha se modernizado, as relações de poder ainda são coloniais. O "coronel" (Seu Francisco) ainda manda na rua como se fosse sua fazenda.O som como personagem: O título não é por acaso. Kleber usa o desenho de som para criar paranoia. O medo não vem de um monstro, mas do vizinho, do porteiro ou do desconhecido que vigia seu carro.O final: Geralmente, quem acha o filme cansativo sente que a recompensa vem nos últimos minutos, quando as tensões acumuladas finalmente explodem em um desfecho que amarra o passado e o presente.Resumo da RecepçãoPúblicoCríticaDividido. Muitos acham monótono, sem ritmo e com cenas "aleatórias" (como a da televisão ou do fetiche nos carros).Aclamação quase unânime. Foi eleito pelo The New York Times como um dos dez melhores filmes do ano no mundo.Sensação: "Poderia ter 40 minutos a menos."Sensação: "Um retrato assustador e preciso da classe média brasileira."Veredito: Você não está "errado" por não ter gostado. O filme exige uma paciência que nem sempre estamos dispostos a entregar, especialmente se esperamos um suspense tradicional. Ele funciona mais como uma crônica de costumes com um toque de terror psicológico do que como uma história de entretenimento linear.

texto: Na minha review de Dazed and Confused eu falei que as vezes um filme sobre pessoas normais vivendo suas vidinhas normais as vezes dá muito certo, mas não é o caso quando a intenção é fazer uma crítica social. Depois de ler outras reviews, deu pra entender certas partes do filme e o que ele queria passar, mas pra uma crítica social ficou tudo só nas entrelinhas, não tem uma ênfase girando em torno de nada, não desperta nada. Sem exagero nenhum, o filme todo é literalmente como se tivessem colocado câmeras em algumas casas e em uma rua de um bairro classe média alta e deixado o pessoal viver suas vidas. Deu pra perceber (depois de pesquisar um pouquinho) como as nuances do filme trazem a crítica sobre a herança escravocrata e a manipulação da ideia de segurança na vida das classes média pra cima, mas ainda foi tudo muito sutil MESMO, fica difícil querer fazer uma crítica, gerar impacto, reflexão, conscientização no espectador em um filme que parece ser duas horas do cotidiano que esse espectador vê ou vive todo santo dia, pelo amor de deus, se eu quisesse um negócio desse eu sentava no sofá sem nem ligar a TV e olhava em volta por uma hora e saía bem ali na esquina pra ficar observando na outra hora. Crítica social, porque tem como objetivo alcançar o maior publico possível, todos os públicos, tem que ser direta e clara pra ser entendida, tem que causar alguma coisa, tem que ser algo com foco, com drama, que dê pra entender e sentir, filme parado assim não dá. O tempo todo parece que vai acontecer alguma coisa e não acontece porra nenhuma, e quando ameaça ter um plot o filme acaba, é uma broxada da porra sinceramente. Legalzinho mesmo a coisa dos sons cotidianos servirem pra gerar desconforto, que deu certo deu, mas não foi isso tudo, principalmente pelo fato de parecer antecipar um mal QUE NÃO ACONTECE EM HORA NENHUMA. E por mais amador que seja eu até gostei bastante do estilo da atuação.

texto: São duas horas de filme que parecem uma eternidade, e sinto que o longa tinha potencial para ser bem melhor. Os personagens são chatos e desnecessários, não acrescentando nada à trama, e a falta de profundidade sobre eles torna difícil se conectar. Embora o filme seja repleto de metáforas e tenha alguns personagens relevantes, ele permanece extremamente superficial, acredito que a intenção era criar um filme cult, com uma abordagem diferenciada. Além disso, o filme mantém um clima de mistério e suspense o tempo todo, mas quando entrega finalmente as revelações são decepcionantes e fracas. "O Som ao Redor" é um filme repleto de reflexões importantes  acerca da desigualdade social e das classes sociais, abordando a questão das pessoas privilegiadas de forma crítica. No entanto, para mim, esses temas poderiam ter sido explorados de maneira mais eficaz e focada.

texto: A análise hipotética, o filme se baseia em uma grande crítica sobre a classe média e sua relação com a sociedade através de uma emulação de um "realismo" da vida cotidiana dos personagens, a análise porém não tem um objetivo concreto, são apenas imagens sem significado real, no final o filme não contempla nem uma crítica a um objeto abstrato porém palpável e nem a realidade em si, se tornando imagens sem sentido real. A montagem tem momentos pavorosos que vão de desencontros de cenas intercaladas até mesmo a narrativa que está se apresentando, a direção de atores é algo que propositalmente é deixada no estado bisonho apresentado no filme, o desencaixe entre o "realismo" que é emulado e a condução de um personagem para contar uma história fazem com que todos os personagens ao final do filme sejam resumidos a caricaturas sem substância nenhuma.

texto: São duas horas de filme que parecem uma eternidade, e sinto que o longa tinha potencial para ser bem melhor. Os personagens são chatos e desnecessários, não acrescentando nada à trama, e a falta de profundidade sobre eles torna difícil se conectar. Embora o filme seja repleto de metáforas e tenha alguns personagens relevantes, ele permanece extremamente superficial, acredito que a intenção era criar um filme cult, com uma abordagem diferenciada. Além disso, o filme mantém um clima de mistério e suspense o tempo todo, mas quando entrega finalmente as revelações são decepcionantes e fracas. "O Som ao Redor" é um filme repleto de reflexões importantes  acerca da desigualdade social e das classes sociais, abordando a questão das pessoas privilegiadas de forma crítica. No entanto, para mim, esses temas poderiam ter sido explorados de maneira mais eficaz e focada.

texto: Eu assisti a O Som ao Redor, e essa é a minha opinião sobre o filme. A vida em uma rua de classe média da Zona Sul do Recife toma um rumo inesperado após a chegada de uma empresa de segurança particular. A presença do grupo traz tranquilidade para alguns moradores, mas provoca tensão e desconforto em outros. Paralelamente, Bia, casada e mãe de duas crianças, precisa encontrar uma maneira de lidar com os latidos constantes do cachorro de seu vizinho. É um bom filme e já apresenta diversos elementos que se tornariam marcas da filmografia de Kleber Mendonça Filho, como o ritmo mais lento e cadenciado. No entanto, acredito que, em O Som ao Redor, ele exagera um pouco nesse aspecto. Seus filmes, de modo geral, costumam ter um ritmo mais contemplativo, mas aqui essa cadência, em alguns momentos, me parece excessiva. Acho que Kleber conseguiu controlar melhor isso em seus filmes posteriores. O mesmo vale para o subtexto, outro elemento constantemente presente em sua obra. Neste filme, há tanto subtexto e tantas camadas implícitas que, para mim, a narrativa principal acaba se tornando menos interessante em determinados momentos. Ainda assim, O Som ao Redor deixa muito claro o quanto Kleber Mendonça Filho já era um cineasta autoral e genial. Mesmo com esses excessos, o filme já demonstra uma identidade própria, um domínio impressionante da atmosfera e uma capacidade muito particular de transformar o cotidiano em algo inquietante.

texto: O Som ao Redor capturou o exato segundo em que o pacto de conciliação do Lulismo começou a expor suas fraturas mais feias. Kleber Mendonça Filho colocou a câmera no coração de Boa Viagem para registrar o pânico moral de uma classe média confrontada pela ascensão do consumo popular no primeiro governo Dilma. ​O projeto político do PT sustentou a ilusão de que era possível incluir dezenas de milhões no mercado sem encostar em um único privilégio da classe dominante brasileira. O Som ao Redor desmascara essa contradição escancarando que o poder de compra da classe trabalhadora acirrou o ressentimento do andar de cima. A burguesia urbana tolera o pobre consumindo contanto que ele continue entrando pelo elevador de serviço e dormindo no quarto sem janela. ​Toda a construção estética do longa nasce da obsessão de Kleber pela arquitetura da paranoia urbana. O diretor acumulou essa percepção em curtas anteriores, observando a transformação do Recife, que trocava seus casarões por prédios de concreto blindados por grades, milícias privadas e câmeras de vigilância. Essa mutação na paisagem pernambucana revelava uma elite empenhada em se isolar do país real enquanto contratava a própria segurança para varrer o conflito social para debaixo do tapete. ​A narrativa vai muito bem ao expor que a estrutura do engenho colonial simplesmente se verticalizou. O latido do cachorro, o ruído do ar-condicionado e a presença constante dos seguranças na rua de Setúbal geram uma sufocante ilusão de controle. O filme opera como um suspense de invasão onde o acerto de contas já está contratado, revelando que a dita "paz social" da era petista foi apenas um intervalo entre a humilhação do passado e a desforra histórica que inevitavelmente cobra sua conta. ​O problema central reside no tom altamente esquemático. A direção aposta em uma cadência observacional que se pretende naturalista, mas que acaba soar engessada. Vemos um morador de classe média reclamar da empregada ou do barulho, a câmera recua para exibir a frieza dos edifícios de concreto, um diálogo pontua a distância entre as classes, e o ciclo se repete. Essa mecânica reiterativa desgasta a tensão ao longo das duas horas de projeção, resultando em um ritmo truncado e por vezes aborrecido.

texto: Independente de uma experiência agradável ou desagradável em assistir esse longa, é inegável a riqueza crítica e dramática da narrativa. Os diversos pontos de vistas insurgentes na observação superficial da vida na classe média brasileiro e, tão importante quanto, na escuta dos gritos e susurros dos cenários privados e comunitários suscitam em mim um deslocamento e, ao mesmo tempo, um interesse em relação à trama. Nesse sentido, julgo que a potência desse filme está na múltipla interpretação crítica que seu "incômodo" estilístico e sua estrutura narrativa "barulhenta" nos proporciona para pensar o privilégio irresponsável do tédio burguês brasileiro, o passado histórico latente nos cenários urbanos, a privatização dos afetos consigo e com o outro e o retorno da violência social a partir de sua criadora, a surda classe que se nega a ouvir a própria história de exploração e dominação e, com isso, decide tampar os próprios ouvidos com muros e vigílias.
