texto: Se7en is a film which attempts to wear many hats. On one hand you have attempts at a highly interesting and flashy serial murder case which operates as the major stopping points of the story. Each of the murders is extreme and profane, crafted with this kind of blunt detail that’s certainly entertaining, but ultimately surface level and less well thought out than they likely intended. On the other you have an extremely standard buddy cop framework between the two main characters which makes no real attempt at straying away from convention. Both of these central building blocks are joined together by this phenomenal, nearly noir, presentation which sets up the film as something which is both easily entertaining and contains more for those who are willing to seek it out. Unfortunately, I found Se7en ultimately ends up confused in this crossroad of seriousness and entertainment, ultimately ending up lingering at the surface level and only utilizing these bigger ideas as window dressing rather than something which builds towards something greater. Unfortunately the signs are there from the beginning. The characters in this film are prototypical to a degree which ends up being serviceable but lacking both in terms of story progression and intrapersonal drama. Brad Pitt plays a standard hotshot new detective, willing to prove himself and reeking in overconfidence by his supposed credentials. Rather than demonstrating his actual abilities, Pitt prefers to crack one liners and sneer at his partner’s persistence to do his job properly rather than quickly give up the moment he faces the first sign of abstraction. Likewise, his partner, Morgan Freeman, is his polar opposite. An old blood detective who just wants to retire out of the force because of the toxic apathy of society which has eroded his sense of goodwill. He’s ultimately pragmatic about his job and knows that their efforts are more likely than not to be pointless in the grand scheme of things. This is about as standard of a setup as you can get, but the film never really causes it to head in any sort of meaningful direction. Pitt and Freeman very rarely actually interact for the first quarter of the film, and due to the extremely short timeframe of the plot, their inevitable destination as uncommon allies mere days later is unnatural and unconvincing. The two of them lack chemistry, and their lack of substantial interaction makes the buddy cop presentation lose traction as a whole. Pitt’s more than willing to speak his mind, and the film is more than willing to utilize him as the main source of entertainment, but because Freeman isn’t willing to ever give him an inch these moments end up falling flatter than they had to. This is representative of how the film handles the crux of their characters as well. Pitt and Freeman represent opposite ends of the same coin. Being detectives and thoroughly entrenched in the toxicity of low society, Pitt’s optimism and Freeman’s pragmatism could represent some kind of clash of ideals. But instead, Se7en chooses to merely float these ideas rather than tackle them directly. This is most blatantly presented in a scene in a bar about halfway through the film. Freeman is telling Pitt about how he’s fed up with all of the apathy of society, how people are so willing to take the easy way out rather than work through their problems, which ultimately is the source of their misfortune. Society does not care about itself and so Freeman does not care about society. Pitt rejects this idea, not for any actual stated reason or counterargument, but merely because he cannot accept this line of thought. He states that Freeman himself is also taking the easy way out, which is true, but does little to shift his perspective in any meaningful way. This idea remains a loose thread rather than being properly explored, and this trend can be observed with much of the rest of what Se7en aims to accomplish. The other core principle of Se7en is, of course, the murders. This aspect is where the film really shines. Se7en is already a visually impressive film, perfectly capturing the kind of grime which makes up this low society by operating primarily with low blues and greys. This is a very dark film, but the main attribute I would give the visual quality is dirty. The murders primarily take place in these low income locations, even the apartment buildings are worn down and damaged. Despite the primary weather condition being rain this ends up reminding me of mud more so than dirt being washed away. This translates to the murders perfectly. Each of which are immensely brutal and highly creative, making use of the sin motif more as a suggestion for a gory creative artpiece than anything. My favorite ended up being the first of the murders, representing gluttony you have this obese man who was forced to eat himself to death, but not before cutting off an entire pound worth of meat off his body. This is far and away the most visually stimulating of any of the murders, and perfectly builds up the case as something which is equal parts sadistic and incredible. While grotesque, the visual quality makes it more entertaining than disgusting, and the absurdity of the murders themselves adds to this feeling. Of course, the problem lies with how these murders are presented. For the first half of the film, the duo is convinced that the murders are inspired by famous literary works such as The Divine Comedy and The Canterbury Tales due to them representing the titular seven sins. The film spends a significant amount of time showcasing them researching and discussing these ideas leading you to believe that these would be significant details to the case. Unfortunately, this ends up being nothing more than a wild goose chase, and these details are nothing more than window dressing than any kind of greater idea. Once you reach the halfway point, the film is more than willing to abandon this idea and pivot back towards the cops stumbling in the right direction rather than solving the murders from their own ideas. Of course, the books do end up being brought up again as a key plot point, but it’s only done so to a superficial degree rather than being an integral aspect of how the murders are conducted. This wouldn’t be so much of a problem had the film not spent as much time as it did during the set up period showcasing these works and explaining how they relate to the case. It makes their investigation seem even more like a wild goose chase rather than an intellectual process, a feeling which is only amplified as the film progresses as they never manage to make it off the back foot. Much like the murders, the person who’s leading them along is equally disappointing. John Doe’s reveal in the finale of the film is nothing short of abrupt, and what he actually manages to accomplish once he reveals himself is middling at best. While the ultimate climax, the psychological destruction of Pitt’s character, is certainly very entertaining (and brought forth one of the most iconic lines in modern cinema) John leaves a lot to be desired in terms of actually being a villain. He comes across as a caricature of Hannibal Lecture but without the raw intimidation or presence. He speaks in this very monotone and vague way as a way of demonstrating his control over the situation, only truly losing his temper when he begins to speak about his victims and their respective sins. Unfortunately, he offers little additional support to the foundation of the murders, only confirming that they were executed for superficial means rather than any kind of actual greater purpose or meaning. It’s easy to see that, yes, the people he murdered are representations of the seven sins in some way, but they aren’t carried out as a result of any sort of conviction or greater purpose, but rather just as a means of “higher punishment” administered through his own means. Pitt rightfully calls him out on this, but due to the shallow nature of his character he’s unable to capitalize on this point, mirroring his lack of ability to counter Freeman. My issues with Se7en are not due to a lack of entertainment. The movie excels when it comes to simply fun, the basic nature of its core elements, which are elevated due to the higher quality of its premise, is enough to make sitting through the film worthwhile. However, the film insists that it includes higher ideas in an attempt to nudge itself into something more without properly committing. Each of its greater elements: the character’s opposite personalities, the higher purpose of the murders/how the murders are actually solved are merely thrown out and left unresolved for the viewer to take at face value rather than leaving much room for thought. The ideas being unresolved isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but they end up feeling cheap because of how little foundation they’re given, rather than the lack of a concrete conclusion. Se7en seems to present itself as a movie which is more than your standard buddy cop serial murder mystery film, but while it’s certainly higher quality than your run of the mill flick it just can’t seem to escape its simplistic roots. In the end, it chose entertainment over truly committing to what it wants to say, it takes the easy way out, though I can’t blame them for it.

texto: “you know, lost souls are not that different from those in the zone. the zone is enjoyable, but when that joy becomes an obsession, one becomes disconnected from life.” you have to admit to dissect the nature of the afterlife and telling it through an older, childless, single, black man is awesome… but to tell a story about a dead black man who lives in black communities in america, reaching the pearly gates of the great beyond, and then doing all that while not mentioning jesus once is some backbreaking gymnastics that it’s almost impressive. and, despite that, it still feels like they kept their cards too close to their chest. it still feels like spirituality and heaven by committee. how do we include the least religion possible here? how do we make the movie about dying but keep our tail so far between our legs that you can’t see it? make every dead person on the travelator an old person who is ready to die, that rings true doesn’t it? how do we make the movie about jazz in black communities, have almost exactly half of it, and then ignore the rest of those spaces? how do we cover our arse by saying the great before and beyond is a hypothetical place, even though we’ve seen and made a more interesting cultural depiction of death before in ‘coco’? there also some funny nitpicks i have, things you only really realise once you think too hard. let me just go for the throat, there’s no point in wasting time: if this movie declares that people have personalities before they’re born, does this movie inadvertently say that life begins at conception? what are you doing? why would you put yourself in a position? i don’t hate this movie! if you watch it you’re gonna get a visually arresting and a beautifully animated film here, with specific touches like accuracy on musical instrument performance, some nice film grain, diversity, and mood lighting that will absolutely knock your socks off. ‘soul’ is a very impressive and slick piece of visual production. this movie is about adulthood careers as opposed to childhood dreaming which cuts to the heart of something honestly quite mature. this movie might not be the highlight of your week, but it would be a night well spent.

texto: I think the message they were trying to send was very true and powerful but I wasn’t a big fan of how they reached it, it was definitely contradictory which was the point of showing how one’s life’s purpose shouldn’t define their entire identity but Joe realizing that and then volunteering to give up his own life to let 22 live instead was noble I guess but a bit too noble to make sense. 22s spark which is something they really hammered in was never fully fleshed out as just explained by Joe as “your spark just means your ready to start living” kinda un explanatory and really contradictory to earlier. Kinda an interesting choice to have 22 realize it was ready to start living by living in someone’s else’s body and have that be its spark..? I don’t know if that really makes sense. Anyways the overall message was good but a lot of contradictions going on to get there which I didn’t like. Also I didn’t like the amount of liberties that were taken on a “before life” how  strong personality traits are assigned from birth. Bold, and I don’t personally agree with that. Fish story quote was super though

texto: Un film molto delicato, spirituale nel messaggio, come premesso dal titolo. Forse anche troppo per un bambino, perché il messaggio è sottile e complesso da cogliere anche per un adulto, e arriva nel finale, trasformando tutta la narrazione in un percorso dell’anima. Sarebbe bello far capire ai nostri figli, fin da piccoli, che la scelta migliore è trovare prima di ogni cosa serenità ed equilibrio dentro di noi, far la pace con noi stessi e godersi la vita come un grande dono, e non renderla bella o brutta a seconda se si raggiungano o meno i grandi obiettivi. Che ci aiutano a vivere una vita piena ma che non dovrebbero essere il senso unico dell’esistenza. Un messaggio delicato e difficile da trasmettere, e da rendere credibile, soprattutto dopo che le generazioni precedenti hanno costruito un mondo dove tutto ruota intorno al mantra capitalista “live your best life”… «Per che cosa vorresti essere ricordato al mondo?».

texto: I feel shortchanged. I didn’t want an inside out reskin, I wanted a journey to the soul of jazz, to the spirit of jazz (without Noel Fielding’s unfortunate portrayal). Children don’t need another film showing them the meaning of life, another film about finding yourself. They need a film to teach them about jazz. Who needs a personality or meaning in their life when Alice Coltrane and Pharoah Sanders exist? Be cool, don’t be happy. Anyway, the animation is certainly pretty but the visual language is occasionally cluttered. texto: Feels like one of those Pixar films that displays so much potential in the first 20 minutes in setting up some poignant message about grappling with our own sense of mortality, and Reznor and Ross' soundtrack accompanied with Jon Batiste is a worthy companion. But the movie stumbles over its own footing as it gets lost trying to narrow down and convey what exactly the underlying message of its story is. Is finding your "spark" supposed to be about realizing that your lifelong passion isn't actually lucrative and you should find something more sustainable if you can't make a living off it? Or is it about coming to terms with the idea that your lifelong ambition isn't always what it turns out to be and it's okay to just start anew? Or that your life still has purpose even if you feel like you haven't fulfilled what it is you thought you were meant to do? It becomes so convuluted by the end and these questions still go unanswered, so the emotional baggage you're left with doesn't feel nearly wrapped up as well as it could've been. Ultimately comes off as a visually and sonically captivating Pixar installment (still thought the "Great Beyond" looked and sounded cool af) but with a lot of unfulfilled potential in its central storyline and main character arc — coupled with an antagonist that's honestly not very memorable either. I liked it enough to stay entertained on my flight, but given the overall content and musical appreciation prevalent throughout its runtime, I do wish I ended up loving it more.

texto: Definitely had moments that touched my heart strings, but wish they expanded more of its themes. The similarities to being in ‘the zone’ and the lost souls searching to escape was so interesting, yet they barely touched over it. The character of #22 was an interesting choice. I get that she was an embodiment of a new soul searching for her spark, and was there to act as a reminder to enjoy the moments of life, but honestly, I didn’t really care all too much of that storyline. It felt like it was trying to be ‘inside out’. Like why did they make the type A counter evil? What I wanted more of was the grit, the tears, the pulling of the heart strings - a calling to why we are here in the first place. I wanted to leave this movie inspired to continue following my dreams but left muddled thinking that no one has a ‘spark’ - we just tell that to ourselves, and that we’re here to experience. I obviously agree to some of that and I get what they’re trying to say, but it comes across as ‘don't always follow your dreams because life gets in the way’. To play it safe. In the end, I thought the animation was unworldly. I thought the movie was good but I was hoping for more.

texto: Fuckass movie In all honesty, I've been going through a rough path for a couple of months now and I’ve been feeling a lot like 22 at the beginning of the movie. Everything about life is just « meh », I’ve slowly been loosing passion for my hobbies and passions, just kinda stopped caring overall about everything, becoming more cynical by the minute. I was just thinking about what I wanted to do in the future and how once I get to that point I’ll be fine and life will finally be great. When Joe stands on the sidewalk after the performance - the one he always wanted, the one that would change everything - he simply appears normal, or rather empty. His life isn’t changed like he always said it would be. It’s still pretty much the same overall, even if he achieved his dream. He achieved his « purpose », so what’s next? As he plays the piano all by himself in his dark apartment, he remembers the joyful moments of his life and yes music and jazz is there, but that’s not all there is. It’s the mundane things of everyday life. I also really liked the story of his barber friend, how he wanted to be veterinarian but bc he needed money for his daughter hospital bills, he took up barber lessons and he’s now the best there is. Becoming a barber wasn’t in his plans, as he said so himself, but he’s still happy being one bc isn’t that the whole point anyway? The message of the movie isn’t anything revolutionary per say, it isn’t the first time I’ve heard it, but I did need to hear it once again lately. Life is all about the small moments between the big events, that’s when you are truly living. My big events will come, but that doesn’t mean I have to sit here and do nothing in the mean time, I can live a little.

Belki de mesele bir purpose bulmak değil, o küçük spark’ların kendisini yaşayabilmek. Sonuçta hayat sadece tek bir şeyin peşinden gitmek ve bunu bir amaç haline getirmek için çok kısa :)

texto: Très bien, et vraiment beau. Joe Gardner est professeur de musique à New York et ne vit que pour le jazz. Le jour où il décroche enfin le concert de sa vie, il tombe dans une bouche d'égout et se retrouve dans l'au-delà. Il refuse d'y aller, et se retrouve associé à une âme qui, elle, refuse de naître. Ce qui rend le film remarquable, c'est son sujet. Pixar demande si une vie qui ne réalise pas sa vocation est une vie ratée, et répond non. Le film déplace la question de la passion vers celle de ce qui nous anime vraiment au quotidien, et c'est un propos rare pour un film familial. Docter matérialise des concepts abstraits avec une aisance hallucinante. Le Grand Avant, le Grand Bazar, l'océan des âmes égarées, et ces entités en charge de l'au-delà représentées par de simples traits en mouvement. On reproduit l'exploit de Vice-versa. La musique fait énormément, et le film a deux univers sonores : le jazz de Jon Batiste pour la Terre, ce sont ses mains qu'on voit jouer, rotoscopées  et les nappes éthérées de Trent Reznor et Atticus Ross pour le monde des âmes. Ma réserve : il y a quelques égarements scénaristiques au milieu, notamment le long passage dans un corps de chat. Premier Pixar avec un héros de couleur. texto: This top to toe banger’s Disney+ release the Christmas of Lockdown was the exact coming-of-age balm that fifteen-year-old me and so many viewers needed. Such a lovely film filled to the brim with wisdom, originality and spark (pun intended). Kemp Powers is the heart of this Soul, writing the intimacy of house and home into every scene. A love letter in part to the crown prince of jazz, Jon Batiste, Soul champions the everlasting joy of getting lost in ‘the zone’. Still one of the brightest jewels in the Pixar crown.

tema: Jazz como elemento temático e inspirador

texto: a gente passa tanto tempo procurando “o propósito”, esperando aquela grande coisa que finalmente vai fazer tudo ter sentido, que esquece que a vida também está nas coisas pequenas. numa música, numa conversa, no vento. incrível como a música tem esse poder quase inexplicável de mudar alguma coisa dentro da gente. às vezes ela não resolve nada, mas melhora o dia. acompanha uma tristeza, acalma, dá coragem, faz a gente sentir alguma coisa quando parecia que não estava sentindo nada.sinceramente, que filme lindo sobre estar vivo. 🤎 jazz is for ordinary people <3

texto: Joe Gardner lleva toda su vida soñando con convertirse en músico de jazz y justo cuando parece que por fin lo consigue termina en un lugar entre la vida y la muerte, ahí conoce a 22 y empieza un viaje que poco a poco le hace entender que vivir no se trata solamente de encontrar una gran pasión, Pixar aquí estaba cocinando durísimo porque detrás de toda la animación y el jazz hay una reflexión bien cabrona sobre el propósito, las pequeñas cosas y disfrutar estar vivo, visualmente preciosa y con una banda sonora que tiene una vibra increíble, “The spark isn’t your purpose” y esa idea me pegó durísimo, absolute cinema

texto: Fuckass movie In all honesty, I've been going through a rough path for a couple of months now and I’ve been feeling a lot like 22 at the beginning of the movie. Everything about life is just « meh », I’ve slowly been loosing passion for my hobbies and passions, just kinda stopped caring overall about everything, becoming more cynical by the minute. I was just thinking about what I wanted to do in the future and how once I get to that point I’ll be fine and life will finally be great. When Joe stands on the sidewalk after the performance - the one he always wanted, the one that would change everything - he simply appears normal, or rather empty. His life isn’t changed like he always said it would be. It’s still pretty much the same overall, even if he achieved his dream. He achieved his « purpose », so what’s next? As he plays the piano all by himself in his dark apartment, he remembers the joyful moments of his life and yes music and jazz is there, but that’s not all there is. It’s the mundane things of everyday life. I also really liked the story of his barber friend, how he wanted to be veterinarian but bc he needed money for his daughter hospital bills, he took up barber lessons and he’s now the best there is. Becoming a barber wasn’t in his plans, as he said so himself, but he’s still happy being one bc isn’t that the whole point anyway? The message of the movie isn’t anything revolutionary per say, it isn’t the first time I’ve heard it, but I did need to hear it once again lately. Life is all about the small moments between the big events, that’s when you are truly living. My big events will come, but that doesn’t mean I have to sit here and do nothing in the mean time, I can live a little.

exemplo: O desfecho é decepcionante, gratuito e tenta chocar sem construir um significado coerente, deixando uma sensação de vazio.
texto: Un horror che vuole sembrare qualcosa di grande o filosofico, ma fallisce miseramente proponendo un film che non ha senso. Il film, per quanto possa partire discretamente, è abbastanza blando. Tutto sembra essere costruito in funzione di uno scopo finale, ovvero la morte dei protagonisti. Quello che viene raccontato è abbastanza prevedibile e i personaggi compiono continuamente azioni che non hanno senso logico. Molte volte avrebbero potuto fare altre cose che li avrebbero eventualmente salvati, ma non l’hanno fatto. Il fatto che continuino a fidarsi non ha senso e il finale è qualcosa di insensato e che sembra essere dovuto, a causa delle loro continue decisioni. L’unica, forse, cosa positiva è la frase finale, quando viene detto “me l’avete lasciato fare”. Quella roba lì è vera, appunto, ci sta, però ha senso solo perché è stata una decisione della narrazione. Fanno costantemente azioni che non hanno senso, è ovvio che gliel’hanno lasciato fare. Avrebbero potuto scappare 1000 volte e nonostante questo non l’hanno fatto, hanno avuto 1000 occasioni, e c’è gente che cerca di trovarci un significato, manco fosse un film psicologico pieno di plot twist, quando è solo una porcheria, con una scrittura degna di un film dell’Asylum. Non riesco veramente a capire la gente che dice di essersi spaventata e di aver avuto una tensione assieme a un’ansia costante, non c’è un singolo momento di paura, arriva un pizzico di tensione forse verso la fine del film, ma anche lì era talmente prevedibile che a me veniva da ridere. Un altro problema che ho trovato è nella sceneggiatura, perché non è soltanto il comportamento dei personaggi a risultare poco convincente, ma proprio il modo in cui la storia viene costruita. Si percepisce troppo che determinati avvenimenti debbano necessariamente accadere per arrivare alla conclusione che il film si è prefissato, invece di sembrare una conseguenza naturale di quello che è successo prima. Questo rende anche difficile prendere sul serio quello che sta succedendo, perché più la storia va avanti e più sembra che siano le esigenze della sceneggiatura a guidare i personaggi. Anche il ritmo non mi ha convinto particolarmente. Il film cerca di creare tensione attraverso l’attesa e attraverso alcune situazioni ambigue, ma personalmente non ho trovato questa tensione particolarmente efficace. Alcune parti mi sono sembrate semplicemente dilatate, senza che questo aggiungesse davvero qualcosa alla storia o rendesse la situazione più inquietante. Forse ho apprezzato un po’ la fotografia, assieme ad alcune inquadrature, ma diciamo che più che apprezzabili, sono il minimo indispensabile. Alla fine, quindi, più che paura o inquietudine, mi è rimasta soprattutto una sensazione di vuoto. Il film vorrebbe arrivare a un finale scioccante e lasciare qualcosa allo spettatore, ma per me il percorso necessario per arrivarci è talmente poco convincente che, invece di rimanere colpito da quello che succede, finisco per distaccarmi completamente dalla storia.

texto: 1.75/5 Disgustingly nonsensical. I’ve never seen a horror film where the main characters act this fucking stupid. I get that’s supposed to be the point — that their inaction is where they go wrong. But I don’t care. There’s only so long I can suspend my disbelief when every character is this stupid. Not to mention that the point the film is trying to make is right-wing nonsense. It’s not just that I disagree with the themes and subtext.  It’s also incredibly hamfisted. No subtlety whatsoever. Also had some of the worst audio mixing for music consolidated in the first 30 minutes. My volume was only at 20 and the music blew out my eardrums. Then it went back to normal for a while before destroying my ears again. Well shot, but that’s about it. This movie sucked.

texto: Pretty well done, a good portrayal of how easy it is to socially coerce and subtlety violate boundaries until it’s not so subtle. Don’t be a push over or you will get pushed over (and stoned to death). I will say the protag couples ability to totally forgive and decide to stay after they returned for the stuffed animal stretched credulity to some extent. I thought the husband’s dissatisfaction with his life was sort of underdeveloped. In a kind of sick way it makes me think of that quote by Anais Nin ‘ life shrinks and expands according to one’s courage ‘ The family (especially the husband) is pushed exactly where the couple wants him because he doesn’t have the courage to assert his will, to object. The couple who exercise agency without any moral or societal restraint,  can push people exactly where they want them and socially lead, abusing customs of politeness, aware of just how much others will tolerate before speaking up.

texto: Tenía altas expectativas de esta película, porque escuché y leí bastante opiniones sobre que esta película tiene uno de los finales más brutales y crudos de el cine, y que el remake estadounidense de esta película no es nada comparada a esta (la original), pero siento que exageraban bastante. No estuve tan entretenido, no me tense ni me sorprendí mucho en todo el metraje y el final tampoco me sorprendió o convenció, pensé que vería algo crudo súper fuerte pero no fue la gran cosa realmente. El guion es mediocre, ya que no vemos un desarrollo sólido de los personajes ni de la historia, por eso es tan complicado conectar con algún personaje o llegar a tenerles lástima, cuando solo les tenemos casi rencor de lo pocos inteligentes que son los personajes. Las actuaciones son buenas y la cinematografía también es considerablemente buena, pero para mí la iluminación es el mayor logro técnico de la película, pero además de esos 3 detalles técnicos lo demás es mediocre o muy poco relevante quedando atrás. Esperaba más de esta película, no es tan traumática como dicen, tampoco la recomiendo, pero tengo que admitir que la trama es bastante original pero lamentablemente no cuenta con un desarrollo sólido. Gran potencial desperdiciado.

texto: As many have already noted, Speak No Evil is torture-porn cinema, but what struck the wrong note for me was the fact that it feels as though the creators thought they were cleverly and slyly subverting a Michael Haneke-like premise, while having absolutely nothing to say. I was occasionally engaged, mostly during the first half. Entering the second one, film started to ask for increasingly large suspensions of disbelief. And in the final act, film went down as fast as a speeding car goes off a cliff. And it ended in an explosion, too. The dialogue was bad for the most part, but I could have turned a blind eye to that if the characters hadn't been written as the world's ultimate idiots. On top of that, these "unexpected" villains had zero motivation for what they were doing, nor did they have anything interesting added to their backgrounds. Not to be a big bad wolf all of the time, I'll say that the film does have some merit; there are a few intriguing scenes and couple of note-worthy filmmaking choices... But, at the end, I tend to believe the filmmakers were a bit pretentious here in thinking that a muffled orchestral score could somehow turn a poorly written screenplay into an important picture, and that a controversial, shocking ending could serve as a good substitute for meaning.

texto: Thriller psychologique prometteur sur deux couples étrangers se rencontrant en vacances et finissent par se revoir le temps d'un weekend, amorçant une déconstruction progressive du couple Danois (rigide, poli et vertueux, d'ailleurs j'aime beaucoup leur présentation notamment visuelle comme le plan en plongée sur le service de table très carré dans leur appartement) par le couple Néerlandais (plus borderline) mais tel un soufflé dès qu'on apprend la véritable nature de ce dernier dans la cabane le film fini par balayer d'un revers de la main le thriller psychologique tombant dans le thriller plus conventionnel malgré ma compréhension du discours/parti-pris de son réalisateur/scénariste Christian Tafdrup, il y avait une promesse de déconstruction jusqu’au-boutiste ramenant la nature sauvage de l'être humain notamment via deux séquences (la scène de sexe du couple Danois dont la femme cherche le confort et exorciste sa frustration suite à une violation de son intimité dans la scène précédente de la salle de bain et celle du cri bestial entre les deux hommes dans la carrière) mais le film part sur autre chose. La dernière partie est difficilement crédible et tombe dans de gros sabots, même musicalement il surligne la tragédie qui se dessine sous nos yeux. Dommage parce-que le film arrivait à être malaisant jusqu'à son twist, on est bien en deçà d'un Seven par exemple.

texto: When I was younger I had no issue visiting my friends in different cities and countries and sleeping on a floor or if I’m lucky, a couch. As I’ve gotten older I still visit and stay over at friends houses but these days I get weirdly anxious about it, especially when trying to sleep. So much so that I’ll often just book a hotel instead. With that in mind it seems this film has been tailor made to torture me and twist the knife right where it hurts. So much so that I considered multiple times just switching it off. Glad I could see it through tho, this was fantastic; Psychological horror at its best. I don’t know what it is about Scandinavian films but they are so good at tapping into the minutia of social norms and what happens when you break them. Probably the area of the world with the highest ratio of bangers to flops- in fact I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a bad Scandi film. Add Christian Tafdrup to the list of Osterland, Trier, Vinterberg et al, cos this guy can cook.

texto: Speak No Evil mostra como, às vezes, seguir as convenções sociais apenas para evitar um constrangimento pode nos conduzir a um destino irreversível. Quantas vezes ignoramos os avisos da própria consciência e dizemos “sim” simplesmente para não contrariar alguém? É impossível não se identificar em algum nível. Concordamos com um motorista de Uber falando besteira apenas para não gastar energia discutindo, nos colocamos em situações desconfortáveis para não parecermos rígidos demais, flexibilizamos momentaneamente nossos próprios valores para não sermos vistos como chatos ou mal-educados. Speak No Evil pega algo absolutamente cotidiano e apenas o extrapola até transformá-lo em um terror desconfortável. Assistimos aos protagonistas caminharem lentamente em direção ao abismo. E o mais angustiante é perceber que não existe uma grande decisão responsável por levá-los até lá. São pequenas concessões, uma após a outra. Para não provocar desconforto, tornam-se progressivamente mais permissivos, até o momento em que aquilo que poderia ter sido evitado parece inevitável. No fim, Speak No Evil talvez seja um terror comportamental antes de qualquer outra coisa. Não precisa investir em jump scares, ameaças sobrenaturais ou grandes estímulos visuais. Seu terror está no comportamento humano e da facilidade com que reconhecemos aquelas pequenas concessões em nós mesmos. O filme apenas leva às últimas consequências uma armadilha na qual entramos todos os dias: o medo de contrariar o próximo.

texto: ¿VES LO QUE PASA? Es curioso lo que sucede con esta película. En gran parte es aburrida, y hasta pareciera no del todo bien llevada, poco clara incluso en lo que quisiera hacer hincapié, pero el tercer acto se lleva todos los premios. Hagamos el análisis que hagamos, deja una huella, te deja pensando y te marca con las imágenes que construye. Seguramente haya 2 o 3 imágenes que nunca voy a olvidar en mi vida. Y eso, la versión americana, aunque me encantó, no lo tiene. La remake es mucho más conceptual y guionada. Esta es más fuerte en sus imágenes. Creo que en definitiva son dos películas que funcionan bien a coro. Esta para marcarte a fuego sus imágenes, y la americana para brindarte la conceptualidad y la palabra que esta no tiene, sumado a mayor espesor dramático y de personajes. La crítica que ambas obras realizan, no es algo a pasar por alto. Un mal endémico de nuestros últimos tiempos: la cobardía encarnada.

texto: This whole movie is basically a masterclass in watching a grown ass man fail every survival check imaginable. The whole “Yes, yes… let’s turn around just to get some stupid stuffed animal” moment isn’t just bad decision making, it’s the thesis of the entire movie. This dad is so painfully clueless, so desperate to be polite, that he drags his entire family straight into hell with a smile and a nod. I wasn’t even frustrated with the bad guys. I was frustrated with him. Every red flag is practically screaming in his face, and he still chooses the most socially awkward, self destructive option possible. It’s like he’s allergic to self preservation. By the time things go bad, I wasn’t shocked I was exhausted. You can’t feel bad for people who refuse to help themselves… The movie is effective, sure. It’s tense, it’s uncomfortable, it’s bleak. But it’s also infuriating, because you’re stuck watching a dad who would rather die than be rude. And honestly? That’s the real horror…

texto: Eu achava que o remake de 2024 já era bizarro até ter assistido a esse que deu origem a ele. Esse é ainda mais cru e vai diretamente no âmago da questão da passividade e cordialidade excessiva. O final é totalmente revoltante — e, creio eu, ser pior ainda para nós homens. A sensaçao de impotencia, anulaçao e a falta de esforço para lutar ou se impor diante de situaçoes tirânicas e de pessoas aproveitadoras, tráz uma análise profunda e causa até reflexões de situações que já passamos em algum momento da vida. No geral é um filme excelente, coeso e bem estruturado, o elenco é muito bom, transmite exatamente a sensaçao de revolta e impotencia que causa até raiva ao assistir. Final mais condizente com a realidade que o de Speak No Evil (2024).

texto: This whole movie is basically a masterclass in watching a grown ass man fail every survival check imaginable. The whole “Yes, yes… let’s turn around just to get some stupid stuffed animal” moment isn’t just bad decision making, it’s the thesis of the entire movie. This dad is so painfully clueless, so desperate to be polite, that he drags his entire family straight into hell with a smile and a nod. I wasn’t even frustrated with the bad guys. I was frustrated with him. Every red flag is practically screaming in his face, and he still chooses the most socially awkward, self destructive option possible. It’s like he’s allergic to self preservation. By the time things go bad, I wasn’t shocked I was exhausted. You can’t feel bad for people who refuse to help themselves… The movie is effective, sure. It’s tense, it’s uncomfortable, it’s bleak. But it’s also infuriating, because you’re stuck watching a dad who would rather die than be rude. And honestly? That’s the real horror…

texto: Speak No Evil mostra como, às vezes, seguir as convenções sociais apenas para evitar um constrangimento pode nos conduzir a um destino irreversível. Quantas vezes ignoramos os avisos da própria consciência e dizemos “sim” simplesmente para não contrariar alguém? É impossível não se identificar em algum nível. Concordamos com um motorista de Uber falando besteira apenas para não gastar energia discutindo, nos colocamos em situações desconfortáveis para não parecermos rígidos demais, flexibilizamos momentaneamente nossos próprios valores para não sermos vistos como chatos ou mal-educados. Speak No Evil pega algo absolutamente cotidiano e apenas o extrapola até transformá-lo em um terror desconfortável. Assistimos aos protagonistas caminharem lentamente em direção ao abismo. E o mais angustiante é perceber que não existe uma grande decisão responsável por levá-los até lá. São pequenas concessões, uma após a outra. Para não provocar desconforto, tornam-se progressivamente mais permissivos, até o momento em que aquilo que poderia ter sido evitado parece inevitável. No fim, Speak No Evil talvez seja um terror comportamental antes de qualquer outra coisa. Não precisa investir em jump scares, ameaças sobrenaturais ou grandes estímulos visuais. Seu terror está no comportamento humano e da facilidade com que reconhecemos aquelas pequenas concessões em nós mesmos. O filme apenas leva às últimas consequências uma armadilha na qual entramos todos os dias: o medo de contrariar o próximo.

texto: When I was younger I had no issue visiting my friends in different cities and countries and sleeping on a floor or if I’m lucky, a couch. As I’ve gotten older I still visit and stay over at friends houses but these days I get weirdly anxious about it, especially when trying to sleep. So much so that I’ll often just book a hotel instead. With that in mind it seems this film has been tailor made to torture me and twist the knife right where it hurts. So much so that I considered multiple times just switching it off. Glad I could see it through tho, this was fantastic; Psychological horror at its best. I don’t know what it is about Scandinavian films but they are so good at tapping into the minutia of social norms and what happens when you break them. Probably the area of the world with the highest ratio of bangers to flops- in fact I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a bad Scandi film. Add Christian Tafdrup to the list of Osterland, Trier, Vinterberg et al, cos this guy can cook.

texto: Considerando sucessos recentes de terror e seus impactos verdadeiros no cinema, como Midsommar, Obsession e A Hora do Mal, três títulos que gosto e aprecio o trabalho de direção, Fale Comigo possuía um aspecto semelhante, talvez pela boa propaganda que sempre tive de alguns veículos da informação que sigo. Adolescentes burros se reúnem para brincar com o que não se deve, usando uma mão decepada como portal pro outro mundo. Aí acontece uma merda e a partir daí, o filme começa a andar em círculos e atirar para todos os lados, quase gritando "me escuta aqui! Eu tenho metáforas pra fazer!" Enquanto não aproveita pra desenvolver de verdade, nada. É uma visão criativa limitada, com uma direção que eu não achei nada demais, e que na minha opinião, precisava de outro segmento e uma interpretação mais simples (talvez até momentânea) para agradar. No entanto, é preciso salientar que esse filme seria sim muito funcional se seu texto fosse mais sincero consigo mesmo, e não uma máquina aleatória de escrever subtramas. O primeiro terço do filme é muito legal e promissor em apresentar uma história simples, no qual o terror adolescente iria valer o seu tempo, mas ao longo do meio e do final, após acontecer o acidente principal na trama, ele se perde em tantas mensagens e o desenvolvimento chato do passado da protagonista. Os personagens são rasos, alguns em atuações bem fraquinhas e em dilemas que você simplesmente não acredita que essa besteirada propõe a discutir. É muito chato acompanhar essa situação dos protagonistas onde nada acontece e eles são poucos punidos pelos problemas que causaram a partir de uma brincadeira errada. Os relacionamentos entre os personagens são somente tristes de acompanhar, e a "tensão romântica", numa tentativa de colocar mais um arco a se desenvolver, é falha e uma das piores coisas do filme A parte gráfica, do body horror, é bem executada, porém me parece jogada na trama apenas para causar impacto. No geral, eu simplesmente não gostei do filme e talvez eu só tenha achado bem bobo e desrespeitoso, pelo tamanho da discussão e mensagem que estavam ali retratando. Esquecível

texto: Achei um filme interessante, mas a princípio fiquei com a sensação de que ele era um pouco raso. Eu estava esperando que algumas coisas fossem mais aprofundadas e, quando terminou, ainda senti que faltava alguma coisa. Mas é um daqueles filmes que continuam na cabeça depois dos créditos. Quanto mais eu pensava, mais percebia as coisas que ele deixa nas entrelinhas. Me chamou atenção como a mão funciona quase como uma metáfora para o vicio. Depois que os personagens experimentam aquele contato, eles passam a querer repetir a experiência cada vez mais, ignorando as possíveis consequências. Não parece ser só um filme sobre espíritos, mas também sobre dependência, impulsividade e a dificuldade de parar quando algo já tomou conta de você. Mia acaba sendo a maior prova disso. Carregando o luto pela mãe, ela se agarra à ilusão de que ainda pode falar com ela, mesmo quando fica evidente que aquilo não é realmente sua mãe. Também achei interessante como o filme trabalha os personagens. Apesar de serem um grupo de amigos, cada um mantém sua individualidade. A Mia, por exemplo, demonstra um carinho pelo Riley durante parte da história, mas, quando surge a possibilidade de conseguir algo que ela queria, ela acaba deixando esse cuidado de lado. No geral, achei uma produção bem feita, com uma boa construção dos personagens e uma atmosfera que funciona muito bem. Não foi um filme que me conquistou de imediato, mas definitivamente me fez pensar depois que terminou.

texto: Que filme medíocre! Este filme é tão ruim que eu consegui prever o que os personagens iam fazer e dizer. Os personagens são completamente esquecíveis; você não consegue se importar com nenhum deles. Eles tentam fazer com que nos importemos com o Riley, mas ele é tão detestável que eu torci para que morresse. Mas o filme não é de todo ruim; há algumas coisas que eu realmente achei interessantes. Infelizmente, esses elementos minimamente interessantes são sufocados por várias piadas sem graça e gírias ultrapassadas. Parece que o roteirista passou cinco minutos na internet e pensou: "Ah, então é assim que os jovens se comunicam", e colocou isso no filme. Algumas cenas de diálogo são ridículas. Eles tentaram misturar comédia e terror, mas não funcionou. Resumindo, é um filme que tinha uma ótima ideia, mas não soube que direção tomar e acabou sendo apenas mais um entre tantos filmes de terror.

exemplo: Apesar de não ser considerado um filme muito assustador, muitos notaram que ele cria uma atmosfera perturbadora e desconfortável, com cenas de possessão e body horror bem executadas.
texto: Talk to Me propose un concept de possession particulièrement original grâce à cette mystérieuse main embaumée. J’ai aussi beaucoup aimé l’idée de voir des adolescents transformer une expérience aussi dangereuse en simple jeu, allant même jusqu’à se filmer. Honnêtement, j’ai trouvé cette idée très crédible : si un tel objet existait, il y a de fortes chances que ce soit exactement ce qui arriverait. Le film mise davantage sur le malaise que sur une accumulation de jump scares. Les scènes d’horreur sont brutales, dérangeantes et ponctuées d’un peu de body horror particulièrement efficace, même si elles ne sont finalement pas si nombreuses. Derrière son apparence de film d’épouvante, Talk to Me est avant tout un drame sur le deuil, la solitude et la dépendance. J’ai toutefois trouvé que la première moitié tournait un peu en rond. Le scénario tarde à véritablement décoller et le rythme manque d’équilibre avant que les enjeux prennent enfin de l’ampleur. Les personnages secondaires sont également peu développés, ce qui fait qu’on s’attache rarement à eux. Malgré ces défauts, Talk to Me demeure un film d’horreur original, moderne et efficace qui renouvelle intelligemment le cinéma de possession.

texto: Talk to Me tem uma premissa muito boa. A ideia de uma mão misteriosa que permite conversar com espíritos é criativa e encaixa muito bem no contexto de um grupo de adolescentes que transforma aquilo em uma brincadeira de festa. O filme também tenta construir um lado mais emocional ao explorar o trauma da Mia após a morte da mãe por suicídio e como isso influencia suas escolhas. O problema é que, para mim, essa parte da história simplesmente não funciona como deveria. Todo o conflito envolvendo o Riley, as consequências de ele usar a mão e a forma como a família passa a culpar a protagonista nunca conseguiu me envolver, então o peso dramático que o roteiro tenta criar acaba se perdendo. As atuações também não ajudam muito. A Sophie Wilde entrega uma boa performance como Mia e consegue carregar boa parte do filme nas costas, mas o restante do elenco passa uma sensação de ser apenas competente, sem interpretações que realmente se destaquem. Mesmo com algumas cenas de horror bem feitas e uma atmosfera desconfortável em certos momentos, fiquei com a impressão de que a execução ficou bem abaixo do potencial da ideia. Em compensação, a maquiagem merece muito destaque. Os ferimentos, as possessões e todo o visual dos espíritos são muito bem feitos e ajudam bastante na imersão, sendo facilmente um dos pontos altos do filme. Apesar disso, o final é, sem dúvida, a melhor parte. A conclusão amarra muito bem a trajetória da Mia e as regras da própria maldição. Ver a protagonista assumindo o lugar de um dos espíritos e sendo invocada por outras pessoas fecha o ciclo de uma forma muito inteligente e dá um novo significado a tudo o que aconteceu antes. É um desfecho forte e memorável, que quase faz o filme terminar melhor do que foi durante boa parte da sua duração. Ainda assim, no geral, Talk to Me acabou sendo uma experiência apenas mediana para mim.

texto: Talk to Me é um daqueles raros filmes de terror que compreende que o género não precisa de escolher entre a substância e o entretenimento. Pode ser profundamente alegórico sem deixar de ser genuinamente assustador. Pode falar sobre luto, dependência e autodestruição sem sacrificar a tensão em nome da mensagem. E é precisamente esse equilíbrio que faz do filme uma das obras mais marcantes do terror contemporâneo. À primeira vista, a sua premissa não parece particularmente inovadora. A possessão enquanto metáfora para o vício, a procura desesperada por uma fuga ao sofrimento e a sedução exercida por forças que prometem alívio imediato são temas que o cinema de terror tem explorado há décadas. No entanto, Talk to Me nunca depende da originalidade da ideia, depende da excelência da sua execução. Os irmãos Philippou demonstram uma confiança invulgar na realização, construindo uma atmosfera opressiva onde cada movimento de câmara, cada corte e cada silêncio contribuem para uma crescente sensação de inevitabilidade. O terror não nasce apenas daquilo que vemos, mas sobretudo da certeza de que a tragédia já começou muito antes de as personagens se aperceberem disso. O maior triunfo do filme reside na forma como recusa transformar a alegoria no seu principal espetáculo. Nos últimos anos, o chamado "elevated horror" tornou-se tão obcecado pelas suas leituras simbólicas que, muitas vezes, se esqueceu de provocar medo. Filmes excessivamente preocupados em explicar o trauma acabam frequentemente por neutralizar aquilo que torna o terror tão poderoso, a irracionalidade, a ansiedade e o desconhecido. Talk to Me faz exatamente o contrário. Primeiro assusta. Só depois convida à interpretação. A metáfora nunca sufoca a experiência, emerge naturalmente dela. A mão funciona como um objeto profundamente simbólico. Não representa apenas o contacto com os mortos, mas também a sedução de qualquer mecanismo de evasão que ofereça prazer imediato à custa da própria destruição. É impossível não estabelecer um paralelo com a dependência, a primeira experiência surge como uma curiosidade, transforma-se rapidamente num ritual coletivo e termina por consumir completamente quem já não consegue distinguir o controlo da ilusão de controlo. O filme evita qualquer moralismo simplista, preferindo mostrar como o sofrimento emocional cria terreno fértil para esse tipo de dependência. Grande parte da força dramática deve-se à extraordinária interpretação de Sophie Wilde. texto: Holy shit, so haunting and effortlessly scary, I loved the nature surrounding the hand and the mystery behind it. It was the right decision not including some kind of backstory or lore, it felt more sinister not knowing anything about the entity or this gateway to hell. The scene where Riley gets possessed gave me hella Hereditary vibes, which is a compliment btw. Both films tab into this feeling of dread and leaves you feeling unsettled beyond belief, to the point where I almost felt nauseating without being a gory mess. Something only a handful of horror movies is able to bring out in me, the sense of dread that lingers inside you throughout the film. The Philippou brother’s really made something special here, everything from the storytelling to the passing was incredible. And tremendous performance Sophie Wilde pulls in this simply can’t go unnoticed, easily the standout and lowkey carries the film acting wise! My one complaint though is with some of the characters being a little underbaked, where they feel a little pointless. Like the character of Max, who we only really see and spend time with ones, the scene where he gets stabbed, you can’t expect me to care after just two minutes of screentime! But other than that, the film feels extremely well passed, where every act and scene feels rewarding, just wished we could have seen a little more to Max… The Philippou brother’s is something else, I’ve already seen their latest film “Bring Her Back” and although I prefer this one, it’s already clear these guys mean business and I’m eagerly awaiting their next move, which I couldn’t help but notice could be a potential sequel to Talk to Me!!! O terror sempre foi uma linguagem privilegiada para falar do sofrimento humano. A diferença está na forma como cada filme escolhe fazê-lo. E Talk to Me escolhe fazê-lo através do medo. Medo genuíno. Daquele que não desaparece quando as luzes da sala se acendem. Daquele que permanece porque compreendemos que os verdadeiros demónios do filme nunca foram apenas os espíritos invocados, mas a facilidade com que o vazio emocional nos leva a abrir a porta a qualquer coisa que prometa preenchê-lo. Poucos filmes recentes conseguiram equilibrar de forma tão elegante o horror visceral, a tragédia íntima e a sofisticação formal. Sem reinventar completamente o género, Talk to Me demonstra que o terror continua a ser um dos meios mais poderosos para explorar aquilo que existe de mais frágil na condição humana. É um filme que assusta primeiro, pensa depois e permanece muito tempo connosco depois dos créditos terminarem.

texto: I can't remember having seen a movie with this many entirely unnecessary sex-scenes. "The Pianist" is one of my favorite movies of all times and Adrian Brody is a magnificent actor. Unfortunately, "The Brutalist" is a boring, sometimes confusing if not erratic movie that lost me when after a sudden timeskip of unknown time in the second half Laszlow's niece Zsofia, who we only saw as a young girl that was mute from the war trauma she had experienced, all of sudden was talking like it is the most normal thing. The movie never explains what happened, why the girl suddenly gained the ability to talk again, it's just something that happened. And that's true for the entire second half of the movie: Things happen. Are they exciting? Interesting? Fun? No. But they happen. And then the credits started running. I know this is from a different director (and a heartfelt "fuck you" to rapist Roman Polanski), but it's hard not to wish for a direct sequel to "The Pianist" when seeing Adrian Brody playing the role of a post-WW2 jew. There's a lot that could have been portrayed in such sequel. Instead, we're following Lazslow who flees from Europe to America to start a new life. And that is interesting. We see how he arrives, how he struggles, how cruel this unknown world is to him. We see how he rises up, gets chances and takes them. This is when this movie is at its best. This is the fantastic first half. And then his wife arrives and the movie gets worse and worse from there. Instead of focusing on the building of the ... building and the struggles that come with such work, we only ever get a surface-level look at his work. Instead, more and more time is spent on family issues, trauma and drug abuse. And sex. Lots of sex scenes. Those are important for reasons. The final 20 minutes or so would have been the moment where I would have walked out of the theater hadn't I watched the movie at  home. Without spoiling much, "The Brutalist" pulls a "Joker: Folie a Deux" and completely torpedos everything that came before. Absolute baffeling choice. Not a movie I want to watch again and not a movie that felt like it was telling an important story. The gimmicky use of loud sound effects during certain scenes felt desperate.

texto: Uma Bela Propaganda Ainda é Propaganda: A Perversidade do Cinema Pró-Genocídio 1. Propaganda Sionista Travestida de Cinema Uma peça de propaganda sionista travestida de cinema: assim podemos definir a experiência maçante de pouco mais de três horas que objetivam uma única mensagem: os judeus não são capazes de se assimilar a qualquer nação; portanto, sua única alternativa é a colonização da região Palestina. Essa mensagem perversa é incutida subliminarmente através de um voice-over nos primeiros 20 minutos de filme. O som que narra através das ondas do rádio a resolução que criou o Estado Genocida de Israel prepara o espectador para o inevitável caminho do povo judeu, e o filme irá trabalhar intensamente para justificar a aliá (migração dos judeus para colonizar a Palestina). 2. O Paralelo com Leni Riefenstahl Esse conteúdo já seria perverso em qualquer período histórico, mas, em tempos de um Holocausto promovido por Israel, ganha contornos semelhantes aos de O Triunfo da Vontade, de Leni Riefenstahl, com duas diferenças básicas: Leni era profundamente mais dominante em sua técnica e, naquele momento, o Holocausto judeu ainda não havia se consolidado, como o dos palestinos na atualidade. 3. A Fachada Progressista e a Supremacia Judaica O filme tenta levianamente travestir-se de progressista e anticapitalista para vender sua mensagem. Mas falha justamente em seu juízo moral e na evocação velada da supremacia judaica, afinal, como é citado pela personagem de Felicity Jones: "todos nesse país são podres". Deixando claro que não se trata de uma crítica ao sistema e sim aos gentios de modo geral. 4. Hollywood e a Tradição do Cinema Pró-Genocídio Não há novidades na relação entre o Estado de Israel e Hollywood. Aliás, isso sempre foi pauta em muitas discussões sobre a parcialidade do cinema estadunidense para com os diversos extermínios orquestrados pelo Estado Ilegítimo. Desde Exodus, de Otto Preminger, que desumaniza os árabes vítimas da Nakba, até produções mais recentes, como Setembro 5, Hollywood toma parte do opressor, assim como o cinema alemão o fez nos anos 30 e 40. 5. Méritos Técnicos e a Atuação de Adrien Brody Como pontos positivos do filme, podemos destacar a fotografia e a direção de arte, que tornam o filme um belo e ordinário exemplar de propaganda. Há também a grande atuação de Adrien Brody, vencedor do Oscar pelo longa, mas cuja extensão exagerada do filme acaba em alguns momentos saturando o espectador. 6. Conclusão: O Brilho Técnico Ofuscado pela Podridão Narrativa O Brutalista é uma perversidade envolta em erros e que tem poucos acertos em sua construção. Há o brilho técnico, porém ofuscado pela absorvente podridão narrativa e tentativa de ludibriar os olhos que veem a história ser escrita com lágrimas e sangue inocente.

texto: “The Brutalist”, de Brady Corbet, sigue a László Tóth, arquitecto húngaro y sobreviviente del Holocausto, cuando intenta reconstruir su vida en Estados Unidos. El sueño americano pronto se convierte en una incómoda relación entre arte, dinero y poder. Corbet construye un drama de época monumental, fotografiado por Lol Crawley con una textura áspera y elegante. La puesta en escena impresiona, aunque su extensa duración y cambios de género terminan dispersando el relato. La película habla de migración, pertenencia, explotación y del precio de perseguir una idea. Sin embargo, su discurso sobre el sionismo resulta problemático, especialmente por una mirada que presenta Israel como único refugio seguro para los judíos. A eso se suma una caracterización algo esquemática de sus posturas políticas y religiosas. Quiere ser película de época, drama familiar, relato de artista, thriller y tragedia, pero esa mezcla no siempre encuentra equilibrio. Adrien Brody y Guy Pearce sostienen buena parte del conjunto. Su relación mezcla dependencia, protección y amenaza con una química convincente. El apartado artístico es extraordinario, pero su irregular narrativa esta demasiado convencida de sus propias ideas.

The cinematography is among the most astonishing I have ever seen. Yet, even though you leave the film feeling like you’ve witnessed something monumental, I swear I was never bored while watching it, which is no small feat given its massive runtime. Adrien Brody is one of the best actors alive, so I wasn’t particularly surprised by his performance. It was a given that he’d knock it out of the park. But I have to heap praise on the great Guy Pearce. I know a 215 minute runtime might be off putting to many, but if you ask me, I’d watch this film another hundred times.

texto: Cinema and Architecture in a Single Film? Yes. The Brutalist definitely brings together my two greatest passions to present an extremely dense drama about pain, desire, obsession, and deep trauma, expressed through an art form as abstract as architectural design. The details and finishing touches, the straight lines, the play of light, and the raw concrete masterfully convey the pain of an artist destroyed by war, broken by a foreign country, and obsessed with a work that, in reality, belongs to someone else. I suppose The Brutalist is one of those extremely difficult films to watch. Nearly three and a half hours of runtime will scare many people away, and its slow, methodical, subtext-heavy plot will drive away whatever few have decided to stay. But if one has enough patience and openness to let themselves be absorbed by the generational drama presented by the film, The Brutalist will fly by and eventually become a masterful study, not only of a character, but of an entire generation forced to carry on with their lives in a postwar period almost as unreal as the war itself. People as privileged as László Tóth can express that uncertainty, that fear, that anger, and even their darkest desires through a building almost as monumental as it is exorbitant. Others, on the other hand, are forced to self-destruct through drugs, sexual violence, and a love relationship strong enough to survive a war, but incapable of enduring its aftermath. No. The Brutalist is not for everyone. And I will not say that it is perfect either. But it is precisely what it needs to be to become a cinematic landmark: living proof that many of us are willing to endure a slow and meditative story in order to reach a thesis that is powerful, devastating, and, above all, honest. By the way, Brutalism is an architectural movement hated by many because of its simplicity and, as its name suggests, its sordid brutality. To me, however, it is the most beautiful style in architecture. Even with its simplicity, the rawness of its materials, and its violent forms, it manages to achieve a pure kind of beauty without the need for ornamentation or retouching. Almost in the same way we humans are made. 4.5 out of 5

texto: “Is there a better description of a cube than that of its construction?” The Brutalist is an ambitious, visually stunning epic about art, ambition, trauma, and the complicated price of the American Dream. Brady Corbet creates a film that feels deliberately monumental, mirroring its main character’s obsession with architecture through its enormous scale and imposing visual language. Adrien Brody gives a remarkable performance as László Tóth , a Hungarian-Jewish architect rebuilding his life in post-war America. His character is deeply flawed, and often difficult to understand, but Brody gives him a quiet intensity that makes his struggles compelling. Felicity Jones and Guy Pearce are equally strong, adding layers to the film’s complicated relationships and power dynamics. The architecture is arguably the film’s greatest achievement. The brutalist structures are cold, imposing, and beautiful, functioning almost like another character. The cinematography and Daniel Blumberg’s haunting score give the film a weight that makes even its quieter moments feel significant. At nearly four hours, however, The Brutalist can feel a little prolonged. Some scenes linger longer than necessary, and its deliberately slow pace demands patience. The film also occasionally leans so heavily into its symbolism and grandeur that its emotional impact becomes slightly less immediate. Still, these aren’t huge criticisms. The Brutalist is the kind of film that feels increasingly rare now: visually bold, and genuinely interested in exploring difficult ideas rather than simply telling a straightforward story. texto: Esta segunda revisión que le hago me sorprendió un poco más. Puse más atención y pude apreciar mucho mejor la cinematografía, que me parece espectacular. Sobre la historia, sabemos que la película se separa en dos partes. La primera parte me sigue encantando, igual que la primera vez que la vi, y a la mitad, estaba casi 100% seguro de que se podía volver de mis favs. Siento que hace un mejor trabajo que la segunda parte y es donde más conectado me sentí con la historia. La segunda parte no me hizo sentir desconectado, solo que el desarrollo que tiene hacia el final es un poco apresurado. Aun así, esta vez pude apreciar mejor la historia y me gustó un poco más que la primera vez. Hay algo que todavía me saca un poco de la película: el final. Se siente demasiado apresurado, reitero. Hay una escena bastante tensa justo antes del final y, después de que termina, la película corta completamente ese momento y pasamos a la escena final, donde Laszlo ya es anciano y se habla de todo lo que logró. Creo entender lo que se quiere hacer con ese cambio de tono, pero no estoy seguro de si funciona para mí. Pasamos de una escena bastante tensa a una escena mucho más feliz, incluso con música que cambia completamente el tono de lo que acabamos de ver. Ese cambio ocurre rápido, me saca un poco del feeling en el momento. Aun con eso, esta segunda vez me gustó más. Pude apreciar mejor lo que la película quiere contar y, sobre todo, su cinematografía.

texto: “Is there a better description of a cube than that of its construction?” The Brutalist is an ambitious, visually stunning epic about art, ambition, trauma, and the complicated price of the American Dream. Brady Corbet creates a film that feels deliberately monumental, mirroring its main character’s obsession with architecture through its enormous scale and imposing visual language. Adrien Brody gives a remarkable performance as László Tóth , a Hungarian-Jewish architect rebuilding his life in post-war America. His character is deeply flawed, and often difficult to understand, but Brody gives him a quiet intensity that makes his struggles compelling. Felicity Jones and Guy Pearce are equally strong, adding layers to the film’s complicated relationships and power dynamics. The architecture is arguably the film’s greatest achievement. The brutalist structures are cold, imposing, and beautiful, functioning almost like another character. The cinematography and Daniel Blumberg’s haunting score give the film a weight that makes even its quieter moments feel significant. At nearly four hours, however, The Brutalist can feel a little prolonged. Some scenes linger longer than necessary, and its deliberately slow pace demands patience. The film also occasionally leans so heavily into its symbolism and grandeur that its emotional impact becomes slightly less immediate. Still, these aren’t huge criticisms. The Brutalist is the kind of film that feels increasingly rare now: visually bold, and genuinely interested in exploring difficult ideas rather than simply telling a straightforward story. It won’t work for everyone, but for viewers willing to surrender to its pace and scale, it is an unforgettable cinematic experience. Really didn’t expect to like this going in as I’d heard it’s both “Oscar bait” and AI fuled garbage. Where the hell did those rumours even come from? texto: Cinema and Architecture in a Single Film? Yes. The Brutalist definitely brings together my two greatest passions to present an extremely dense drama about pain, desire, obsession, and deep trauma, expressed through an art form as abstract as architectural design. The details and finishing touches, the straight lines, the play of light, and the raw concrete masterfully convey the pain of an artist destroyed by war, broken by a foreign country, and obsessed with a work that, in reality, belongs to someone else. I suppose The Brutalist is one of those extremely difficult films to watch. Nearly three and a half hours of runtime will scare many people away, and its slow, methodical, subtext-heavy plot will drive away whatever few have decided to stay. But if one has enough patience and openness to let themselves be absorbed by the generational drama presented by the film, The Brutalist will fly by and eventually become a masterful study, not only of a character, but of an entire generation forced to carry on with their lives in a postwar period almost as unreal as the war itself. People as privileged as László Tóth can express that uncertainty, that fear, that anger, and even their darkest desires through a building almost as monumental as it is exorbitant. Others, on the other hand, are forced to self-destruct through drugs, sexual violence, and a love relationship strong enough to survive a war, but incapable of enduring its aftermath. No. The Brutalist is not for everyone. And I will not say that it is perfect either. But it is precisely what it needs to be to become a cinematic landmark: living proof that many of us are willing to endure a slow and meditative story in order to reach a thesis that is powerful, devastating, and, above all, honest. By the way, Brutalism is an architectural movement hated by many because of its simplicity and, as its name suggests, its sordid brutality. To me, however, it is the most beautiful style in architecture. Even with its simplicity, the rawness of its materials, and its violent forms, it manages to achieve a pure kind of beauty without the need for ornamentation or retouching. Almost in the same way we humans are made. 4.5 out of 5

texto: This is one of those infuriating melodramas that spends two hours documenting the suffering experienced by a saintly young woman with a drab personality. She is surrounded by selfish monsters who don't bear any resemblance to actual human beings and the screenplay works overtime to make us feel pity for the idiotic masochist at the centre of the story. They presumably intended to craft this tale into a feminist parable about the horrors of a sexist society but it ends up falling prey to all sorts of misogynistic clichés. It's telling that every single female character who is presented is an unsympathetic light is willing to push back against social boundaries. The only woman that we are asked to admire is a pushover who actively chooses to become a martyr. I'm sick of watching supposedly tragic dramas that tell stories about characters who suffer from inertia.

texto: Family melodrama about a young woman who continually sacrifices everything for her ungrateful family and gets nothing in return, sort of like a reverse Tokyo Story , minus the subtlety and the dignity. Beautifully shot, to be sure (especially the first two shots, opening with Neeta, the protagonist, walking in front of an impossibly beautiful and massive tree followed by a split diopter shot of Neeta in the foreground, her singing brother in the middle ground and a moving train in the background, all in focus), but rather poorly edited and even more poorly acted. Gita Ghatak as Neeta's younger sister is especially bad and also looks too old to be playing her younger sister (I looked them up, and she was in fact four years older than Supriya Choudhury, who plays Neeta). The melodrama comes almost to the brink of self-parody, so that you pretty much know what 's going to happen beat for beat if you've ever seen any melodrama in your life ("This was expected," says the father when his youngest son has an accident at the factory where he works ... yes, it was). It also uses weird sound effects to denote Neeta's emotional state in case you couldn't tell by her overacting.

texto: Indian Neo-Realism mixed with melodrama. It's a combination of identifiers that sends shivers down my spine, and the film doesn't disappoint. It's a sluggish, 2-hour-long social drama (with some horrible musical influences) that never redeems itself, but only gets worse as it progresses. A relatively well-off family flees from their home and ends up in the slums of Calcutta. The daughter of the family does her very best to improve the situation for her family, even sacrificing her own life and happiness to do so. For all the sacrifices she makes though, her family doesn't seem very appreciative of her efforts. A film about self-sacrifice where things just get worse for the lead character. The performances aren't that great, the cinematography is very basic and the drama piles up endlessly. The music was pretty grating too, making the 2-hour runtime a real obstacle. Not my type of film, I really disliked this one.

texto: Upon my initial viewing of Ritwk Ghatak’s The Cloud-Capped Star last year, I wrote extensively about this film’s larger role in analyzing the socio-economic contexts in which the film emerged out of and how these factors, although never expressly called out in the film, convey a theme of industrialization and modernization as a method of disrupting the personal lives and social intimacies of those in society. While this is an analysis that I still stand by and continue to be proud of, I do want to highlight another aspect of the film that I neglected on my first watch; this being a review of the film itself. The Cloud-Capped Star is a difficult film to sit through both due to its themes and the structure of the film itself. This is a film that is poorly structured and paced causing it to be monotonous to watch given its over two hour runtime. Due to the language barrier I cannot attest to the quality of the performances, but there is an aura of over-exaggeration to the way characters move around their environments. This makes the performances feel very stilted and performative, which comes across as soap operatic rather than melodramatic. This is certainly a by-product of casting mostly non-actors however that doesn’t make it any less jarring to watch. In the end, The Cloud-Capped Star is a film which I appreciate for its narrative scope and underlying societal critiques more than I appreciate it as a film to watch and enjoy in its own right.

texto: I found it difficult to immerse myself in the film; I felt at a distance throughout my viewing. While the characterizations feel true to the film’s setting, the exaggerated or caricature-ized performances kept me at arm’s length. This feeling is also due to key moments feeling compressed, the same way a novel condenses something significant moments into a single sentence. That can work in instances, but here it comes across as underdeveloped (I hesitate to call it “lazy” given the clear care behind the film). It’s unfortunate, because I was genuinely interested in its exploration of the New Woman in Bengal.

texto: Family melodrama about a young woman who continually sacrifices everything for her ungrateful family and gets nothing in return, sort of like a reverse Tokyo Story , minus the subtlety and the dignity. Beautifully shot, to be sure (especially the first two shots, opening with Neeta, the protagonist, walking in front of an impossibly beautiful and massive tree followed by a split diopter shot of Neeta in the foreground, her singing brother in the middle ground and a moving train in the background, all in focus), but rather poorly edited and even more poorly acted. Gita Ghatak as Neeta's younger sister is especially bad and also looks too old to be playing her younger sister (I looked them up, and she was in fact four years older than Supriya Choudhury, who plays Neeta). The melodrama comes almost to the brink of self-parody, so that you pretty much know what 's going to happen beat for beat if you've ever seen any melodrama in your life ("This was expected," says the father when his youngest son has an accident at the factory where he works ... yes, it was). It also uses weird sound effects to denote Neeta's emotional state in case you couldn't tell by her overacting.

texto: This is one of those infuriating melodramas that spends two hours documenting the suffering experienced by a saintly young woman with a drab personality. She is surrounded by selfish monsters who don't bear any resemblance to actual human beings and the screenplay works overtime to make us feel pity for the idiotic masochist at the centre of the story. They presumably intended to craft this tale into a feminist parable about the horrors of a sexist society but it ends up falling prey to all sorts of misogynistic clichés. It's telling that every single female character who is presented is an unsympathetic light is willing to push back against social boundaries. The only woman that we are asked to admire is a pushover who actively chooses to become a martyr. I'm sick of watching supposedly tragic dramas that tell stories about characters who suffer from inertia.

In 1960, or now. We're all inherently selfish people. We need encouragement to be less selfish, not more.

texto: Indian Neo-Realism mixed with melodrama. It's a combination of identifiers that sends shivers down my spine, and the film doesn't disappoint. It's a sluggish, 2-hour-long social drama (with some horrible musical influences) that never redeems itself, but only gets worse as it progresses. A relatively well-off family flees from their home and ends up in the slums of Calcutta. The daughter of the family does her very best to improve the situation for her family, even sacrificing her own life and happiness to do so. For all the sacrifices she makes though, her family doesn't seem very appreciative of her efforts. A film about self-sacrifice where things just get worse for the lead character. The performances aren't that great, the cinematography is very basic and the drama piles up endlessly. The music was pretty grating too, making the 2-hour runtime a real obstacle. Not my type of film, I really disliked this one.
