texto: I tried watching The Turin Horse , and I didn't get anything out of it. So I then listened to Jonathan Rosenbaum's audio commentary. hoping it might offer something I had missed. Rosenbaum talks about many things. He talks about his own relationship with Tarr, whom he calls a friend. About anecdotes from when they were in a jury together at a film festival, and they couldn't decide on a winner because Tarr hated all the films (he describes Tarr as an anti-cinephile). He describes Tarr’s shift from socio-political concerns toward something more "metaphysical" and "philosophical" from Sátántangó onward. He discusses Tarr’s collaboration with Ágnes Hranitzky, his wife and co-director, and with László Krasznahorkai, his closest collaborator, and the writer of The Turin Horse and several of Tarr's other films. Notably, what he doesn't talk about is the content of the film itself. Which is fitting, as the film offers nothing to talk about. That may be why I, too, am talking about Rosenbaum’s commentary instead of the film. --- One of the problems with films like these is that difficulty and tedium become their primary — and often only — defining characteristics. Questioning the work is then treated, by the cult of the initiated, as evidence of insufficient patience, seriousness, or artistic literacy. But art and cinema do not — and should not — earn significance merely by exhausting the viewer. Because the film itself offers remarkably little by way of internal articulation, even Rosenbaum has no choice but to turn outward: toward the director’s supposed philosophical inclinations, his biography, and Rosenbaum’s own authority as a friend of the director. If a work is so sparse that even its defenders cannot meaningfully discuss what happens within it, then the problem is not with the audience.

texto: I dip into slow cinema once every six months to challenge myself by going out of my comfort zone but this is my last detour in my journey to watch all of film canon. A father and daughter survive a storm which could be interesting if it was an hour shorter. There are only so many ways you could show a man peeling a potato before you send the audience running back to their phones. More than the slow pace I am bothered by the lack of narrative. I have mentioned in other reviews – The decision to let the visuals do the heavy lifting does not work for me in spite of some beautiful, painterly images. Cinema is not just a visual medium it is a visual storytelling medium. That is not a difference in semantics but in function. The slow pace is an invitation to think but the movie does not give me much food for thought. Arthouse films peaked in the 60s with the likes of Fellini, Bergman, Antonioni and Rohmer. All of them are on the slower side but they ask incisive questions about sex, religion and creativity. They reward thinking you have to ponder about the character motivation to get most out of them. On the other hand slow cinema from directors like Tarr, Claire Denis or Abbas Kiarostami has one-note characters who never give the impression of having rich inner lives so thinking about them adds nothing to the experience. They are just badly paced, thematically empty and unabashedly self-indulgent. I am not fond of either extremes – I hate both Fast and Furious and its ilk, and slow cinema. Neither has any semblance of story and to enjoy them one has to either stop thinking or give into overthinking.

texto: Patates sahnesinde aklıma direkt Van Gogh'un Patates Yiyenler tablosu geldi. Doğayla kurulan ilişki en ilkel haline inmiş. Tat yok, keyif yok, sadece hayatta kalma refleksi. Film boyunca kurulan düzen de işlevsel olduğu sürece değerli olan bir dünya. O kadar sene yaşadığı toprağı bir kova su için kimseyle paylaşmayan adam kuyu kurur kurmaz evi bir saniye düşünmeden terk ediyor. Dün “benim" dediği yer bugün hiçbir şey. Kızına bakışı bile sevgi yerine hala iş görüyor mu diye kontrol eder gibi. Her gün aynı döngü uyan, giydir, içki, at, patates ye, camdan bak. At yürümüyor hayat ilerlemiyor ve hem açlar hem de patatesi yemiyorlar yani yaşamak için fiziksel sebep olsada anlam yok. Filmde bu noktaya kadar sahiplik, değer ve anlam tamamen işlev üzerinden kurulmuş. Buraya kadar güzel ama takıldığım yer de tam bu. Film sürekli “her şey değersizleşti, insan içten içe öldü” diyor ama baştan gösterdiği canlı bir değer, tutunulacak bir anlam hiç yok ki yıkımını hissedelim. Karakterlerle bağ kurmak zaten mümkün değil çünkü ortada karakter yok sadece hareket eden bedenler var. Ne hissediyorlar, neyin yasını tutuyorlar, neden yaşıyorla. hiçbir şey açılmıyor. Çöküşü izliyoruz ama çöken bir hayat görmediğimiz için etkisi de olmuyor. Başından beri bitmiş bir dünyayı altı kez tekrar izlemek gibi. At yemiyor, kuyu kuruyor, ışık gidiyor. Bunlar büyük metaforlar gibi girip bırakiyor. Sadece “bak her şey sönüyor” diyor. Eee tamam sönüyor da bu bana ne düşündürüyor? İzleyiciye alan açmakla hiçbir şey kurmamak arasında fark var, bunda ikincisi var. Zaten en başından beri hayat mekanik bir tekrar. Dolayısıyla yok oluş bir çöküş gibi değil uzatılmış bir hiçlik gibi. Tempo meselesine gelirsem evet uzun planlar düşünmek için alan açıyor ama bir noktadan sonra aynı şeyi defalarca izlemek derinlikten çok durağanlık hissi yaratmış. Hareketsizlik de bilinçli bir tercih evet ama bu kadar da amaçsızlık izleyiciyle kurulan bağı zorlamış. Tanrı meselesi de çok kararsız. Eğer mutlak bir hiçlik anlatılıyorsa kuyunun taşla dolması ve ışığın sönmesi ilahi bir cezalandırma değil mi? Tanrınının yok olduğu bir evren yerine terk edilmiş ama hala bir düzen tarafından kapatılan bir dünya hissi var. Bir diğer aklımda kalan soru da zaten başından beri ölü doğmuş bir hayatı izliyorsak bunun çöküşünü neden bu kadar uzun izliyoruz? Unutulmaz mı? Evet. Ama benim için etkileyici olduğu kadar karakter, anlam ve dönüşüm kurmaktan tembellik edilip yok oluşu sadece biçimsel bir tekrar olarak izletmesi yüzünden çok itici. Görüntü güzel, atmosfer güçlü ama bir yerden sonra bu da yetmiyor çünkü zihinsel temas kuramıyorsun.O yüzden finalde tamamen karanlığa gömüldüğümüzde bir şey hissetmek yerine şükür sonunda bitti dedirtiyor. Bu filmi izlemek sinirlerimi çok bozdu. Bir de mal insanlar çıkıp “abi slow sinema, sanat sineması” falan deyince daha da çileden çıkıyorsun. Yavaşlık amaç değil araç olmalı. O kadar açık fırsat, o kadar detay ve potansiyel varken filmin yaptığı şey ise dümdüz tekrar ve sadece yavaşlık. texto: I dip into slow cinema once every six months to challenge myself by going out of my comfort zone but this is my last detour in my journey to watch all of film canon. A father and daughter survive a storm which could be interesting if it was an hour shorter. There are only so many ways you could show a man peeling a potato before you send the audience running back to their phones. More than the slow pace I am bothered by the lack of narrative. I have mentioned in other reviews – The decision to let the visuals do the heavy lifting does not work for me in spite of some beautiful, painterly images. Cinema is not just a visual medium it is a visual storytelling medium. That is not a difference in semantics but in function. The slow pace is an invitation to think but the movie does not give me much food for thought. Arthouse films peaked in the 60s with the likes of Fellini, Bergman, Antonioni and Rohmer. All of them are on the slower side but they ask incisive questions about sex, religion and creativity. They reward thinking you have to ponder about the character motivation to get most out of them. On the other hand slow cinema from directors like Tarr, Claire Denis or Abbas Kiarostami has one-note characters who never give the impression of having rich inner lives so thinking about them adds nothing to the experience. They are just badly paced, thematically empty and unabashedly self-indulgent. I am not fond of either extremes – I hate both Fast and Furious and its ilk, and slow cinema. Neither has any semblance of story and to enjoy them one has to either stop thinking or give into overthinking.

exemplo: Este grupo critica o que considera uma postura pretensiosa do diretor e de seus admiradores, sugerindo que a obra valoriza a dificuldade e o tédio como se fossem virtudes artísticas. Alguns expressam frustração com a ideia de que apenas uma audiência específica, supostamente mais culta, seria capaz de apreciar o filme, tratando a incompreensão como falha do espectador.
texto: I tried watching The Turin Horse , and I didn't get anything out of it. So I then listened to Jonathan Rosenbaum's audio commentary. hoping it might offer something I had missed. Rosenbaum talks about many things. He talks about his own relationship with Tarr, whom he calls a friend. About anecdotes from when they were in a jury together at a film festival, and they couldn't decide on a winner because Tarr hated all the films (he describes Tarr as an anti-cinephile). He describes Tarr’s shift from socio-political concerns toward something more "metaphysical" and "philosophical" from Sátántangó onward. He discusses Tarr’s collaboration with Ágnes Hranitzky, his wife and co-director, and with László Krasznahorkai, his closest collaborator, and the writer of The Turin Horse and several of Tarr's other films. Notably, what he doesn't talk about is the content of the film itself. Which is fitting, as the film offers nothing to talk about. That may be why I, too, am talking about Rosenbaum’s commentary instead of the film. --- One of the problems with films like these is that difficulty and tedium become their primary — and often only — defining characteristics. Questioning the work is then treated, by the cult of the initiated, as evidence of insufficient patience, seriousness, or artistic literacy. But art and cinema do not — and should not — earn significance merely by exhausting the viewer. Because the film itself offers remarkably little by way of internal articulation, even Rosenbaum has no choice but to turn outward: toward the director’s supposed philosophical inclinations, his biography, and Rosenbaum’s own authority as a friend of the director. If a work is so sparse that even its defenders cannot meaningfully discuss what happens within it, then the problem is not with the audience.

texto: Derzsi János szavaival élve: Fuhbazdmeg Borzasztóan szikár és rideg film a Torinói ló. Olyan, ami szánt szándékkal antagonizálja a nézőjét annak érdekében, hogy ne csak átadja, de fizikailag éreztesse is üzenetét. Amit itt kapunk, az nem a végnek a kezdete, hamem már a végnek is a legvége, a teljes nihil. Mindezt Tarr Béla azzal éri el, hogy gyakorlatilag egy végtelen, kilátástalan loopba helyez minket. Öltözés, krumpli, pálinka, öltözés, krumpli, pálinka, öltözés, krumpli, pálinka. Az első óra után már könyörögtem a szereplők feje fölött lógó apokalipszisért, hogy végre kikerüljünk a körforgásból. Szándékos ez a rendező részéről? Persze, kibaszottul. Kétségtelen, hogy rommá trollkod minket az öreg és amikor már hatodszorra nézeti végig, hogy az apát felöltöztetik, szinte látom a lelki szemeim előtt, ahogy a markában röhög, hogy "na, elég volt már a létzésből, vagy még hetedszerre is felöltöztessük". Adom! Mindez dícséretes, de ez nyílván magában hordozza, hogy nem egy "fun watch", hanem inkább kínkeserves hosszútávfutás. Nem viccelek, amikor azt mondom, hogy antagonizáló. Olyan a Torinói ló, mint amilyennek szerintem a laikusok elképzelik, hogy milyen lehet egy Tarrbéla film. Csak éppen nem ilyen szokott lenni általában, de most tényleg olyan! Épp ezért ez nyolcórásabbnak érződik, mint a Sátántangó. Kicsit olyan érzés, mint amikor a Dark Souls híres lett arról, hogy kurva nehéz, ezért a Dark Souls 2-ben unfair és élvezhetetlen szintekre tekerték a nehézséget.  Senkinek nem ajánlom első Tarr Béla filmjeként, ahogy a Dark Souls 2-t se ajánlanán első Dark Souls játéknak.

texto: Just to avoid any misunderstanding: I’ve watched thousands of films in my life, and I consider myself capable of sensing any kind of idea or philosophy even in simple actions and stillness. I  get that this is Béla Tarr’s style, but if you still find a film heavy even after watching most of it at 2x speed, if nothing pulls you in, then something isn’t working. I watched an old man eat a potato for three minutes in the most “interesting” way possible. The entire film probably has less than 30 lines of dialogue. I knew the story about Nietzsche and the horse, so I expected a different pattern, a different flow. Honestly, if Nietzsche rose from his grave and watched this, he’d probably break down all over again. I just don’t understand how this has a 7.7 on IMDb. I can’t help thinking that the artsy crowd didn’t genuinely enjoy it but rather enjoyed saying they enjoyed it.

tema: Uso repetitivo da trilha sonora e som
exemplo: A trilha sonora, caracterizada por um refrão de cordas que se repete incessantemente, é mencionada como um elemento que intensifica a sensação de monotonia e desgaste. O som do vento, onipresente, também é citado como fator que contribui para a atmosfera opressiva, mas que se torna cansativo ao longo do tempo.
texto: Oh boy. There is perhaps an argument that Béla Tarr is one of the most predictable filmmakers in contemporary cinema. The film is going to be in black and white. It’s going to feature extremely long takes. Seconds will turn into hours. Characters’ speech will sometimes sound as if they’re reading straight from an intimidating philosophical treatise or hard-line manifesto. And it’s going to be one of the grimmest things you’ve ever seen in your sorry little life. With this movie, Tarr and Hranitzky amply follow through on all of these predictive suppositions, and just to add even more spice to proceedings, there is no dialogue for the first 30 minutes. There’s a short introductory voiceover, and then…no one speaks. At all. For half an hour. Meanwhile, a string refrain that sounds like Phillip Glass’s Koyaanisqatsi score under the influence of heavy sedatives repeats over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over again. The story? A father and daughter live in a dilapidated hovel in the middle of nowhere. That’s it. That’s the whole film. I just saved you 154 minutes. Oh yeah- and it’s the windiest place in the world. This is a film that is about wind as much as it is about anything else. The wind howls. The wind whistles. It howls. It whistles. It tugs at the windows and the doors. The hovel creaks. The string refrain scrapes its way through another tortuous, hopelessly despairing iteration. The daughter helps the father get dressed in an unbroken take- there’s 10 minutes. The daughter goes to the well- let’s follow her all the way there and all the way back again as she fights her way through the ridiculous wind. There’s another 10 minutes. Even by Béla Tarr’s standards, this was extreme. It was simply one of the most challenging films I have ever watched to completion. Imagine Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse with 95% of the dialogue taken out and being played at 20% speed. Was it an allegory? Most certainly. Do I care? No. Will I be watching it again, ever? Only after death, if I find myself in hell. For more of my reviews, why not visit www.wilfullyobtuse.com.

texto: Revendo 14 anos depois, com uma concepção formada sobre o que acredito ser a vocação do cinema, gostei bem menos deste trabalho final de Béla Tarr. Compreendo perfeitamente as intenções contra-hegemônicas do diretor. De modo geral, ele propunha o reverso do cinema de storytelling, em que tudo se resume a "contar uma boa história", conferindo-se ao enredo uma centralidade absoluta. E, de fato, o cinema de storytelling é a décima primeira praga do Egito. Mas Tarr, embora operando no regime do cinema narrativo, suprime consideravelmente o plot, com seu arco dramático, reviravoltas, surpresas etc. É quase um retorno aos Lumière. Em uma entrevista, o húngaro disse recusar-se ao esquema de montagem corriqueiro, baseado em "informação-corte-informação-corte". Às vezes não há informação alguma, e outras vezes a informação está algures na mise-en-scène. Mas até aqui tudo bem, já que há bons exemplos de mise-en-scène rica e naturalismo ajustado ao teor da narrativa. O problema de "O Cavalo de Turim" é que ele não é apenas anti-storytelling; é anti-cinematográfico. Para além do ascetismo à Bresson, com personagens cujos pensamentos e emoções são inescrutáveis, já que tudo que vemos são exterioridades distanciadas e economia expressiva, aplica-se a lógica documental ao material ficcional: longos planos-cena e raríssimos cortes, profundidade de campo e reprodução fotográfica do visível ao invés de sua transfiguração. Até existe uma narratividade mínima, onde pouco a pouco, em meio ao marasmo cotidiano, vemos algumas mudanças. Mas elas não são inseridas para catalisar a narrativa, voltá-la noutra direção, alterar objetivos de personagens, nada disso. Se assim fosse, poderíamos tentar examinar se a forma "documental" se justificaria em face delas. Entretanto, o que parece interessar ao diretor é simplesmente o contraste entre o vazio existencial da gente simples de Turim no fim do séc. XIX com a agudeza intelectual de Nietzsche, que passou naquele lugar seus últimos anos. Mas note o seguinte: não temos nenhum vislumbre deste na obra. É para o camponês, sua filha e o cavalo que Tarr direciona as câmeras, Ora, a encenação de um único incidente – aquele em que o filósofo alemão defende o cavalo do impiedoso açoite do camponês – até acentuaria tal contraste e justificaria o roteiro. Mas este não é um filme de "incidentes".

There are only so many ways you could show a man peeling a potato before you send the audience running back to their phones. More than the slow pace I am bothered by the lack of narrative. I have mentioned in other reviews – The decision to let the visuals do the heavy lifting does not work for me in spite of some beautiful, painterly images. Cinema is not just a visual medium it is a visual storytelling medium. That is not a difference in semantics but in function. The slow pace is an invitation to think but the movie does not give me much food for thought. Arthouse films peaked in the 60s with the likes of Fellini, Bergman, Antonioni and Rohmer. All of them are on the slower side but they ask incisive questions about sex, religion and creativity. They reward thinking you have to ponder about the character motivation to get most out of them. On the other hand slow cinema from directors like Tarr, Claire Denis or Abbas Kiarostami has one-note characters who never give the impression of having rich inner lives so thinking about them adds nothing to the experience. They are just badly paced, thematically empty and unabashedly self-indulgent. I am not fond of either extremes – I hate both Fast and Furious and its ilk, and slow cinema. Neither has any semblance of story and to enjoy them one has to either stop thinking or give into overthinking.

tema: Comparações desfavoráveis com outras obras ou diretores
exemplo: Algumas críticas comparam o filme a trabalhos anteriores do próprio diretor ou a cineastas como Tarkovski, Fellini e Bergman, considerando-o inferior em termos de narrativa e profundidade. A obra é por vezes descrita como uma versão menos eficaz de outras produções que também exploram o cotidiano ou o pessimismo, mas conseguem manter o interesse.
texto: Revendo 14 anos depois, com uma concepção formada sobre o que acredito ser a vocação do cinema, gostei bem menos deste trabalho final de Béla Tarr. Compreendo perfeitamente as intenções contra-hegemônicas do diretor. De modo geral, ele propunha o reverso do cinema de storytelling, em que tudo se resume a "contar uma boa história", conferindo-se ao enredo uma centralidade absoluta. E, de fato, o cinema de storytelling é a décima primeira praga do Egito. Mas Tarr, embora operando no regime do cinema narrativo, suprime consideravelmente o plot, com seu arco dramático, reviravoltas, surpresas etc. É quase um retorno aos Lumière. Em uma entrevista, o húngaro disse recusar-se ao esquema de montagem corriqueiro, baseado em "informação-corte-informação-corte". Às vezes não há informação alguma, e outras vezes a informação está algures na mise-en-scène. Mas até aqui tudo bem, já que há bons exemplos de mise-en-scène rica e naturalismo ajustado ao teor da narrativa. O problema de "O Cavalo de Turim" é que ele não é apenas anti-storytelling; é anti-cinematográfico. Para além do ascetismo à Bresson, com personagens cujos pensamentos e emoções são inescrutáveis, já que tudo que vemos são exterioridades distanciadas e economia expressiva, aplica-se a lógica documental ao material ficcional: longos planos-cena e raríssimos cortes, profundidade de campo e reprodução fotográfica do visível ao invés de sua transfiguração. Até existe uma narratividade mínima, onde pouco a pouco, em meio ao marasmo cotidiano, vemos algumas mudanças. Mas elas não são inseridas para catalisar a narrativa, voltá-la noutra direção, alterar objetivos de personagens, nada disso. Se assim fosse, poderíamos tentar examinar se a forma "documental" se justificaria em face delas. Entretanto, o que parece interessar ao diretor é simplesmente o contraste entre o vazio existencial da gente simples de Turim no fim do séc. XIX com a agudeza intelectual de Nietzsche, que passou naquele lugar seus últimos anos. Mas note o seguinte: não temos nenhum vislumbre deste na obra. É para o camponês, sua filha e o cavalo que Tarr direciona as câmeras, Ora, a encenação de um único incidente – aquele em que o filósofo alemão defende o cavalo do impiedoso açoite do camponês – até acentuaria tal contraste e justificaria o roteiro. Mas este não é um filme de "incidentes".

texto: Olha… The Turin Horse é aquele tipo de filme que você respeita mais do que gosta. Dirigido por Béla Tarr, ele tem uma proposta claramente artística e até fascinante em teoria, mas na prática, pode ser extremamente cansativo. A rotina repetitiva do pai e da filha, comendo batata e encarando o vento infinito, até funciona como metáfora no começo. Você entende a ideia: o esgotamento da vida, o peso da existência, o mundo “apagando”. Só que chega um ponto em que o filme parece preso nessa mesma repetição e não evolui o suficiente pra sustentar o interesse. Visualmente, o filme é lindo. O preto e branco, os planos longos, a atmosfera pesada… tudo muito bem construído. Mas ao mesmo tempo, o ritmo é tão arrastado que acaba afastando mais do que envolvendo. Em vez de te puxar pra experiência, ele pode simplesmente te cansar. E aí fica aquela sensação: você entende o que o filme quer dizer, mas não necessariamente sente vontade de continuar ali. No fim, é um filme com intenção, estética e conceito fortes, mas que sacrifica demais o envolvimento em nome da proposta. Pra alguns vai ser uma obra-prima contemplativa; pra outros (como no meu caso), uma experiência interessante… só que arrastada demais pra realmente marcar. Bonito, simbólico e cheio de significado mas também excessivamente lento e pouco envolvente. Um daqueles que você admira mais do que gosta!!

texto: Le Cheval de Turin est un film qui semble d’abord réduit à une sensation : le vent. Un vent incessant, presque agressif, qui empêche toute respiration et finit par envahir tout le film. À part cette force naturelle, il ne se passe presque rien, et c’est précisément ce “rien” qui déroute. Le quotidien se répète, les gestes s’épuisent, le monde paraît se vider de son sens. Béla Tarr ne cherche pas à raconter une histoire mais à faire ressentir une fin, une extinction lente, silencieuse, sans explication. C’est un film difficile à commenter parce qu’il refuse le discours : on ne le comprend pas vraiment, on le subit.

texto: ''Werckmeister harmonies aura été d'une incroyable incroyable accessibilité en comparaison de ceci'' J'apprécie beaucoup le cinéma contemplatif, lent ou sans beaucoup de réels dialogues. Si ce n'est que l'expérience dans ces cas là passe souvent en priorité par la mise en scène. Si on place par exemple Terrence Malick à ce niveau sur une extrémité de ce spectre avec une mise en scène extrêmement dense et foisonnante, je pense que l'on peut placer Bela Tarr à son autre extrémité. C'est L'austérité pure. Une maisonnette isolée durant une tempête et de la répétition à tout les niveaux : Des plans fixes interminables, un thème musical unique rejoué en boucle une douzaine de fois, un vent qui souffle pendant deux heures trente, de la gestuelle répétée. Cela n'a même pas le sens que cela peut prendre chez Jeanne Dielmann. Bela ne nous donne rien et on doit faire avec. Qu'est ce qui fait que je ne ressens rien, que ça été une expérience extrêmement sensorielle agressive et éprouvante pour moi par rapport à tant de personnes qui ont aimé. Ça me semble plus intéressant comme réflexion que de trouver un sens au film en lui même.

texto: The Turin Horse is immaculately composed, weighing with apocalyptic finality in every shot from its austere opening horse ride to its final scenes of mundanity amid despair. The film isn't desperate so much as it is purely hopeless, offering no solace or commiseration for its protagonists but rather luxuriating in their suffering. While I found the films interiors and landscapes alike to be stunning in their obsessive emptiness and despair, I struggled to find much substance in this commitment to a single, uncompromised evocation of pain; even if The Turin Horse feels like the work of a great artist, its lack of particularly mixed feelings is not very interesting or thought-provoking.

texto: I always love Béla Tarr movies for about 20 minutes. Then I realize that I'm not getting much more than a fairly immersive mood-piece. Absolutely gorgeous to look at, with interesting symbolism, but everything there is to be gained from it is already apparent from the get go. The longer it runs, the more you notice all the small issues. Acting isn't great and all the repetition wears out even the aspects that I was initially really into. The music itself has a very nice tone, but it's repeated to such an extent, it's completely ruined after some point. I like a lot of what it's going for and there is a lot to analyze thematically. Béla Tarr is damn good at capturing the feeling of human suffering, but the experience of watching it is often frustrating in ways that don't seem intentional.

Partiendo de aquel episodio que, según parece, llevó a Nietzsche a la demencia, la película nos enfrenta a la deprimente monotonía de una pareja (padre e hija) de granjeros. texto: Je découvre ce cinéaste hongrois à titre posthume, avec ce film complètement fou qui repousse les limites du réalisable grâce à des plans séquences contemplatifs d’une lisibilité et d’une poésie épatantes comme personne n’en avait encore vus, la cohabitation des personnages avec les spectateurs dans leur minable et interminable quotidien est plus efficace que n’importe quel scénario. Les scènes d’ouvertures comptent parmis les plus époustouflantes jamais faites, avec des références évidentes aux premières décennies du 7e Art, des volets naturels pour retrouver l’historique format carré de Chaplin où y déambule la mystique Charette fantôme de Sjoström contre des bourrasques aveuglantes. L’histoire évolue non pas par une narration développée mais par l’action à travers la mise en scène, qui, elle, convoque l’équivalent de l’image-temps pour capturer chaque instant sans en perdre une miette. L’époque dépeinte est d’une obscurité sans égal, et le grain de cette pellicule noir et blanc le rend si bien qu’il nous ferait oublier qu’il tourne au steadycam bien après notre naissance à tous, le talent de l’équipe image est indéniable je veux faire un film en noir et blanc ptn!! L’élément clé reste le vent, sans citer une populaire unpopular opinion: sans le vent le film serait lent et assez ennuyant, mais cet élément vient donner vie à la moindre feuille, et au son aucune seconde de silence n’a de répit, le film souffle et vacille. Extrêmement plaisant de pouvoir voir de l’audace dans chaque choix et de voir qu’un film de 2h30 peut t’attraper sans te lâcher avec seulement 100 mots et 25 plans, gg

texto: hmmm gingembre je pense que c’est le film avec le plus bas ratio nombre de dialogues/temps, ce qui peut être une bonne chose si réussie déjà les premières paroles prennent 30min à arriver et c’est « va te coucher » et « à table » et puis il n’y a réellement qu’une intervention intéressante, qui n’est même pas un dialogue et qui est absolument incompréhensible le cerveau a pas assez chauffé avant je pense qu’il faut relire le script de ce passage pour comprendre des éléments philosophiques du film en tout cas ce que j’ai adoré: -le bruit du vent en continu qui « parle » beaucoup plus que les personnages, c’est marquant cet environnement hyper hostile et sec -la même musique qui pop toutes les 5minutes, à la fin c’était limite un jeu de deviner quand est-ce qu’elle allait apparaître ça entretient très bien cette monotonie illustrée à l’écran -justement le culot de nous montrer 2h30 des mêmes scènes exactement similaires, le quotidien qui se répète infiniment et ce décompte des jours pour qu’on puisse se situer et remarquer que en réalité rien ne change, et qu’ils sont bloqués, condamnés à répéter cette tâche infiniment c’est un peu des sisyphes -les prises très longues, je pense que la plupart des scènes duraient 15 20min. C’est très beau, à partir d’un unique point de vue, de montrer un départ en voyage sans bouger la caméra de même la prise à la steadycam de la première scène est exécutée avec génie, et ceci ajouté aux prises sons qui altèrent entre la musique et le vent c’était une magnifique scène d’ouverture

texto: When the very last meaning of survival is stripped away, that raw silence becomes unbearable to endure. As you watch, something inside just hollows out. No dramatic tears, no final farewells only a creeping, silent darkness accumulating piece by piece. A numbing silence washes over you before you even realize it. This film forces you to feel what happens when the final urge to live completely flickers out.

exemplo: Muitas reviews associam o filme a uma profunda reflexão sobre o nihilismo, a falta de sentido e a dureza da vida, descrevendo-o como uma obra que transmite desesperança e vazio existencial.
texto: On January 3rd 1889, renowned German philosopher Fredrich Nietzsche acted in opposition to the very philosophy he had spent the entireity of his adult life preaching. Upon witnessing the brutal whipping of a horse in Turin by a carriage driver, overwhlmed by empathy and sadness, he rushed over to the aforementioned horse and hugged it, preventing it being beat any longer. He sobbed greatly and was eventually removed by a friend of his, and transported back to his quarters, where he would remain in a delirious sleep-state for 2 days. This marked his profound mental breakdown, under which he would remain for the next 10 years of his life, cared for by his mother and his family before his eventual passing. Tarr begins The Turin Horse with a narration that essentially summarises these events. Yet, Tarr's introduction also ends with the line "yet no one knows what happened to the horse." That is the story that Tarr wants to tell, the story of the horse after this infamous incident. Bela Tarr's The Turin Horse is an apocalyptic tale of death. Not just the death of human or animal life, but the death of life itself, in a profoundly existential way, life as a force itself. We follow this family of two, a father and a daughter, as they carry out their monotonous daily routines, repeated over 6 days. Their lives are spent mostly in silence, the two hardly involve themselves in many conversations with each other, and they carry on with a deep resignation. A resignation of life, of meaning and an eventual submission to suffering and death. It is one of the bleakest narratives I have seen; a completely painful experience as the inevitability of death and meaninglessnes takes over, a complete dissolution of the human spirit. I will not claim to know or have read much of Nietzche's works, but it's clear Tarr employs Nietzsche as more than just a narrative prologue to the begin his story. He turns Nietzsche's concepts of nihilism and stasis into a daily routine for these protagonists, mirroring the empty hopelessness of their lives. The repetitive sequences mirror his idea of eternal reccurrence. I'm sure there's even more meaning that I may not have picked up in relation to Nietzsche's philosophy because of my lack of having read his work, but what all I could pick up is extremely alluring and brilliant. Furthermore, there is the elemental nature of this film that embodies its own spirit. The howls and the shrieks of the wind act as tertiary characters in the scenes between the daughter and her father, further contributing to the despair echoed by the screenplay. The wind, to me, acts as nature's own response to its exploitation and mistreatment by humans. Just like the titular horse's own decision to stop working on the second day, the wind's aggression is in a way its own revolution, its own protest to humanity's exploitation, a theme that is echoed by a very brilliant metaphorical monologue by a neighbour later on in the film. The film de-centers the man from the collapse of the world, here Tarr is less interested in the suffering of humanity, but the suffering of the environment itself. The Turin Horse is apocalyptic not because it depicts some radically terrifying future, but because of its profound vision of environmental collapse, leading to humanitarian collapse. Any anthropological sympathy is lost; this is the destruction we caused, and we must pay the price for it. There is hardly a filmmaker who can capture so much meaning within a single shot like Bela Tarr. His movies can be seen as boring, pretentious, over-wrought with metaphors and a grueling, monotonous exercise in patience testing. This may be true, after all all art is subjective, yet I find Bela Tarr and his long-winding and patience testing narratives to be incredibly heavy and rewarding. Thematically rich and still somehow, incredibly relevant to this day. I have only seen one other film of his (Werckmeister Harmonies), but I am already confident his filmography will be something I will adore. Loved nearly every second of this.

texto: in a lot of ways it feels almost pointless to ascribe a rating to this. because how do you properly rate a quasi-arthouse installation that's nigh-hyper focused on testing your time. making you feel the same kind of dreary hopelessness in a world devoid of love and hope i guess in that way, this movie should be a perfect 10/10 because it absolutely achieves the kind of mood it sought out to capture. the heaviness of human existence, the perspectives of man where one sees barbaric cruelty and another sees the only way he can afford to continue surviving in a world that has given him no rope. but i guess when it comes down to it, this simply didn't connect with me on an emotional level the way damnation did that film similarly feels entirely committed to its vision of a world devoid of god, where hell is the dreary rain and aching pain with which all of our hollow bones are constructed. but damnation gripped me by the soul and never let go, every torrential downpour, muddy flailing limb, glowing neon light; it depicted a world i could vividly and tangibly connect with. the turin horse, while having no less an enrapturing world, ultimately felt like i was watching it from the outside in. that there was a lens, a window, between the harrowing, grueling experience it captured and the emotions i wished to feel from witnessing such an event still a very worthwhile experience, one that again informs the nihilistic viewpoint tarr captures through his apocalyptic visions of man's own barbarism and the aimlessness of such a life. rife with moments not just of harrow but moments of fervor and almost beauty; moments that trick you into thinking this world is worth salvaging. but ultimately, i found my connection to it much more fleeting than i would have liked

exemplo: Algumas reviews mencionam a conexão com a filosofia de Nietzsche e a história do colapso mental do filósofo, interpretando o filme como uma exploração de conceitos como o eterno retorno e a decadência.
texto: In Turin, on January 3rd, 1889, Friedrich Nietzsche steps out of the door of number six Via Carlo Alberto, perhaps to take a stroll, perhaps to go by the post office to collect his mail. Not far from him, or indeed very far removed from him, a cabman is having trouble with his stubborn horse. Despite all his urging, t he horse refuses to move, whereupon the cabman... Giuseppe? Carlo? Ettore? ...loses his patience and takes his whip to it. Nietzsche comes up to the throng and puts an end to the brutal scene of the cabman, who by this time is foaming with rage. The solidly built and full-mustached Nietzsche suddenly jumps up to the cab and throws his arms around the horse's neck, sobbing. His neighbor takes him home, where he lies still and silent for two days on a divan until he mutters the obligatory last words, "Mutter, ich bin dumm," and lives for another ten years, gentle and demented, in the care of his mother and sisters. Of the horse, we know nothing. Cut to horse. If that premise moves you, watch The Turin Horse . Whatever you think about Nietzsche, the idea that one of the most preeminent (prominent, at least) thinkers of our time had his brain melted into infancy for ten years by this singular, relatively normal event, is so thought-provoking that I still can’t stop thinking about it. To then execute on the concepts of divinity, humanity, and suffering over the course of the film is an artistic miracle. Gorgeous score, and some of the best photography ever put to screen; made possible by masterful camera operation. Sparse, meaningful, efficient dialogue highlights the nuance of our understated, weary characters. The ONLY problem I have is the chewing, but the chewing is the point, so I’m scratching that one. Thank you Bela Tarr, and rest in peace.

texto: There are many reasons why I particularly avoid Korean films, yet I do not detest them entirely. One of the biggest factors is their tendency toward exaggerated theatricality at the expense of a tighter logical structure in the plots they follow. Park-Chan Wook is the most classic example of this phenomenon of Korean cinema with his films such as Oldboy where he tries to tie out a similar moral tragedy like the Danish film Jagten (2012) through a stylistically elaborate revenge spiral, but the plot eventually moves beyond the boundaries of grounded internal logic. Devices such as hypnosis can feel like one-time narrative bandages, introduced primarily to connect pieces that otherwise resist being connected. My problem isn't simply that Oldboy is unrealistic, it's that, for me, certain revelations and mechanisms feel retroactively installed to preserve a plot that has already stretched beyond its own credibility. The Handmaiden is also a victim of a massive twisted theatrical presentation with an underwhelming logical ground for plot. So are many many films such as I Saw The Devil, A Bittersweet Life, Forgotten etc... Decision To Leave is what I consider the most perfect Park-Chan Wook film and what I consider the film where he establishes a perfect route between a top-notch presentation, poetic moral complexity and an established ground of logic that complements the plot. The Wailing is no stranger to this victimisation but deliberately worse. Here we follow the story of a dad, who is a police in a remote town, where the guilty, the misdeeds, the victims and even the apparent solutions reveal themselves so early, yet the plot repeatedly demands that its characters descend further into its catacombs of uncertainty, not necessarily because the logic requires it, but because the theatrical experience does with its top-of-the-class cinematography, set design and the quote-unquote "thriller" ride of Korean cinema which is deemed to be so extraordinarily unique. Even the 2 hour 40 minutes runtime serves the furthest from being a momentum of an intrigued continuity. Instead, the film repeatedly pauses, expands, and obscures itself in pursuit of an exhilarating theatrical experience, backed by extraordinary cinematography and production design, but without enough narrative momentum to justify the journey. It could be a brilliant concept film, if only it was told with a better expression of plot in mind, better attachment of all the fragmentations of the elements since they were so obviously present. Yet none clicks except until the final reveal becomes the most emphasized point of the film. In short, my utmost frustration is specifically with the film's prolonged withholding of decisive movement. Underwhelming is an understatement for The Wailing. Bong Joon Ho is the only Korean director to ever do Korean cinema the justice of the trio- cinematic experience, established complementary logic and an unique narrative statement of being a Korean foreign cinema. Lee Chang Dong also comes to mind. Burning is my most favorite Korean cinema of all time. I just want to say this phenomenon is of course not exclusive to Korean cinema only. Any film can become a victim of its own grandiosity when cinematic spectacle begins demanding sacrifices from the internal logic that is supposed to sustain it. I'm looking right at you Amadeus .

texto: Shapeless, meandering, directionless, turgid, and centered on a mystery with an incomprehensible resolution, The Wailing (an awkward translation; the Hanja means "crying sound," but the Hanja-to-English fails to capture the pun) does involve a lot of screaming and crying and suffering and dying over the course of its extremely overlong two and a half-hour runtime. The time is used to fill the plot with so many reversals (he is a ghost; he isn't; he is; he isn't; he is) that whatever the resolution is, and that is not even clear, it no longer matters by the time that we get to it because we have spent so much time getting jerked back and forth that we just want this to end already. One star for some nice cinematography and fine acting, although in service of nought.

texto: 2026 Spooky szn bracket 7/26: Man I really wanted to love this one, sadly I was left quite disappointed 😔 The good: 1) great acting, especially from the actress who played Hyo-Jin! 2)  Gorgeous cinematography, with some stunning shots of the Korean countryside 3) That exorcism scene! That’s about where my praises end The bad:  There’s a couple of good moments in this film, but overall it’s a mess, both tonally and narratively. This movie can’t decide what it wants to be: comedy? Drama? Horror? Zombies? Pandemic? Ghosts? Demons? Instead of choosing one or two of these, this film feels like all 7 were just thrown into a blender and mixed together. This also has some of the dumbest characters I’ve ever seen in any horror movie, and that’s really saying something…The ending left me with more questions than answers. This film feels a lot like “subversion of expectations” at the expense of good storytelling, and as if that wasn’t bad enough, it’s also way too long 😑🥱 I really hope this bracket starts getting better soon 😂

texto: "O Lamento" é um suspense com potencial que se estende além do necessário. Esse é mais um longa sul-coreano de Na Hong-jin que mistura elementos do terror e suspense em torno de Jong-Goo, um policial de uma pequena cidade que investiga mortes misteriosas em seu vilarejo. O que parecia epidemia ganha contornos sobrenaturais e religiosos conforme sua filha apresenta sintomas estranhos. A premissa é sólida e o diretor faz questão de marcar presença, mas o filme carrega consigo um problema estrutural que o compromete: é longo demais para a ideia que sustenta. O filme possui um bom clima de suspense, porém a duração não ajuda, poderia ter sido mais enxuto, e se perde às vezes no roteiro deixando o espectador impaciente. Há momentos onde a câmera trabalha com precisão, onde o diretor demonstra sensibilidade visual genuína ao filmar os rituais e a tensão entre personagens. A estrutura religiosa do filme oferece camadas interessantes, mas Na Hong-jin não consegue contê-las adequadamente dentro de 156 minutos. O roteiro flerta com devaneio total em seus segmentos intermediários, explorando filosofia religiosa quando deveria intensificar a narrativa principal. Algumas atuações carecem de sutileza, especialmente em momentos que exigem nuance emocional, o que prejudica a credulidade de cenas críticas. O melhor que o filme oferece existe em seu final. A última meia hora confunde o espectador e o deixa cheio de dúvidas, com reviravoltas e um final surpreendente. É quando Na Hong-jin finalmente alinha visão e execução, permitindo que a ambiguidade moral do desfecho respire adequadamente. Nesse segmento, o diretor comprova que possui potencial genuíno para manipular emocões e conceitos complexos. Porém, tudo o que precede essa conclusão deveria ter sido trabalhado com maior economia narrativa. Certamente é um filme de ideias contidas demais numa estrutura que não sabe dizer não, logo, não entendo o alvoroço em torno dele.

texto: I'm disappointed. My expectations were incredibly high for this film, given its high ratings and how intrigued I was by the synopsis. However, what could have been a well-crafted epic horror felt more like a long Frankenstein's monster of a movie, that couldn't decide on a direction, so it tried to go everywhere. While it features some genuinely good moments of horror and dread, a great atmosphere and nice makeup, it lost me elsewhere with ineffective comedy, confusing dialogue, forgettable characters, and a messy storyline. I really wanted to like it more. Still, I'm willing to check out the director's other films and see what happens.

texto: Злодеем оказался Дьяво Ляо При могучем хронометраже в два с половиной часа и достаточно интересной завязке о чумной деревне кино не втягивает меня в по-настоящему неоднозначное расследование. Кино, казалось бы, говорит: «Оно!», а ты такой: «Оно!», а оно такое: «Точно оно?», чтоб по итогу оказалось: «Оно». Интересный мув, когда верное подозрение ещё не означает верного знания, а надёжного способа отличить веру от заблуждения нет. Но проблема в том, что здешние намёки слишком жирные, а попытки переобуться слишком неубедительны. Из-за этого наблюдать за происходящим попросту скучно. Хорошо поставленных, жутких сцен и эффектных задумок хватает, но чем глубже пытаешься во всём этом разобраться, тем более шаткой кажется конструкция. Ведь ключ к пониманию происходящего то ли в религиозных подтекстах, то ли в южнокорейской внутрянке, то ли в широкотрактовных метафорах. Сложно из-за этого проникнуться, хотя вайб, безусловно, присутствует.

texto: In Asia il coesistere di giallo e paranormale nella stessa storia ha un carattere diverso da quello che possiamo trovare in Sherlock o altri racconti occidentali. Lo spiritismo spesso si assimila alle indagini come un dato plausibile e popolarmente creduto, almeno nei villaggi più rurali. Goksung parte molto bene, la prima parte è un crime a tinte mostruose, inspiegabili, che sono proprio l'aspetto più avvincente, perché spingono a voler sapere cosa ci può essere dietro gli efferati omicidi. Per tutta la durata del film, nel totale un po' troppo prolungata, la fotografia va migliorando, diventando pian piano più fredda, come se un'occulta entità diabolica si stesse impossessando della stessa atmosfera, mentre per quanto riguarda la storia la seconda parte vede incrinarsi  la componente misteriosa per schiaffarti in volto la verità. In questa parte prende vigore la parte religiosa del film, tra esorcisti, citazioni bibliche al canto del gallo e altro che giustifica la citazione evangelica a Luca all'inizio del film, ma con ciò si assiste anche all'indiscreto farsi protagonista del gore, all'indebolimento del ritmo investigativo, alla banalizzazione della storia, che di originale ha solo ciò che riguarda la tradizione coreana a noi sconosciuta, e a scene che non hanno l'impatto desiderato, come il rituale sciamanico per liberare la figlia, un costante battere di percussioni e grida senza climax ascendente. Il buon regista tiene in piedi l'impianto fino al termine, ma lo script a mio parere non fa altrettanto, non per difetti oggettivi ma per scelte talvolta imperfette.

texto: Maybe it's because only "the best of the best" makes it over here to America, but it feels like Korean filmmakers really know how to make incredible detective stories (Memories of Murder) and horror movies (Train to Busan and Exhuma). The Wailing combines both and makes an incredible film noir, meets folk horror film. The wailing exceeds at making you feel uncomfortable, there are certainly movies that are more intense, more unrelenting and/or more brutal, but few movies make my skin crawl in the way The Wailing does. It's fast and intense when it needs to be and it lets you sit long and slowly with the disturbing material it's presenting you. Its folk horror aspects also take parts of Korean spiritualism and culture and makes them digestible to those of us who are unfamiliar. The police procedural and detective parts are engaging and keep you guessing throughout. The characters are handled very well, especially as we watch the family of our main protagonist struggle and then have to face suppernatural forces. The Wailing really balances things incredibly well when you consider it's a family drama, police procedural, folk horror. That's a lot for one movie to take on, but it does it phenominally well and parts of it will stick with you for years to come.

texto: And Ari wept Quite the wild romp upon an initial viewing, even now I still remember how distributed Jong-goo finding those photos made me feel. Regretfully though this wound up being less riveting  conceptually after a much delayed rewatch. Now in saying that I’m not claiming it's entirely void of any non-cinematic merit. With a much better understanding of Korea’s antipathy towards Japan due to their colonialist occupation during the early 20th century helps illuminate Gokseong’s central subtext ( or just text now ) in a very appreciated manner. This makes a lotta the “clues,” “hints” or actions of Kunimura Jun’s character, aptly named Japanese Man , click for me. Our character's treatment of him, however “justified” in the context of the film's spiritual battle between light and dark, is painted in a far more tragic light by the end. Jong-goo , the village, and by extension us are given divine punishment for blind discrimination. This helps make the ending, one which I found quite frustrating on a first watch, ring rather potent. What we see and what is actually there are two different things and believing that isn’t true is a dangerous belief to hold. The wider issue for myself is the film doesn’t always compel and thus my mind occasionally tends to wander here or there. Could this’ve been remedied by trimming it down a tad? Yea maybe but even then it’s so clearly a fully realized vision that I can’t help but still admire the ambition. Certain leaps in logic might be perplexing if not for the fact the film actively acknowledges them in a manner less irksome and more cheeky fudging of plausibility. I will say it helps that this film still looks euphoric. Splendid mountainscapes made of croaked bark and rough rock all doused in a healthy hue of blue and orange make their harboring of poisonous beasts feel all the more enticing. Again, not an all timer for me but far from being a foul film.

texto: I've finally found it. My favorite horror movie ever made. This was not only stunning, it was deeply political and cultural. How they managed to so tastefully weave in criticism of religion, post-war trauma, and absolutely insane Biblical references together alongside cultural shamanism, black magic, and its unbreakable hold over generations was absolutely mindblowing. The terror went hand in hand with the tragedy. The atmosphere draws you in in the way so many horror movies have tried to do and failed. Just goes to show you don't need jumpscares in order to suffer from series upon series of mind-numbing chills for the duration of two and half hours. At some point the plot did begin to confuse me, but honestly? I didn't even care, the sinister beauty and the depth behind this piece surpassed everything else it might have lacked. I've seen my fair share of horror movies, but this one had something different about it, something very special that I will most definitely come back to time and time again.

texto: Maybe it's because only "the best of the best" makes it over here to America, but it feels like Korean filmmakers really know how to make incredible detective stories (Memories of Murder) and horror movies (Train to Busan and Exhuma). The Wailing combines both and makes an incredible film noir, meets folk horror film. The wailing exceeds at making you feel uncomfortable, there are certainly movies that are more intense, more unrelenting and/or more brutal, but few movies make my skin crawl in the way The Wailing does. It's fast and intense when it needs to be and it lets you sit long and slowly with the disturbing material it's presenting you. Its folk horror aspects also take parts of Korean spiritualism and culture and makes them digestible to those of us who are unfamiliar. The police procedural and detective parts are engaging and keep you guessing throughout. The characters are handled very well, especially as we watch the family of our main protagonist struggle and then have to face suppernatural forces. The Wailing really balances things incredibly well when you consider it's a family drama, police procedural, folk horror. That's a lot for one movie to take on, but it does it phenominally well and parts of it will stick with you for years to come.

texto: I know I’m probably in the minority with this one, but The Wolf of Wall Street just didn’t work for me. On paper, it has everything going for it: Martin Scorsese behind the camera, an incredible cast and a larger-than-life true story about greed, excess and corruption. Unfortunately, I never really connected with the film’s central character, and that made the whole experience feel like a very long slog. Leonardo DiCaprio is exceptional as Jordan Belfort, completely throwing himself into the outrageousness of the character. Jonah Hill is equally memorable, while Margot Robbie makes a huge impression in one of her breakthrough roles. The performances across the board are strong, and there’s no denying that everyone is giving it their all. My problem is that I simply didn’t care about Belfort or his journey. The constant partying, drugs, money and excess become repetitive rather than entertaining, and with a runtime of nearly three hours, that repetition really starts to drag. There are some genuinely funny and memorable moments, but they were never enough to keep me invested in the story. I can appreciate what Scorsese was trying to do, and I can absolutely see why this film has such a huge following. The performances are outstanding and the filmmaking is undeniably impressive. But for me, it’s a case of admiring the film more than actually enjoying it. Perhaps the biggest problem is simply that The Wolf of Wall Street never grabbed me. When a film is this long, you need to be invested in its characters or story, and unfortunately I was neither. A technically brilliant film with some fantastic performances, but one that just wasn’t for me.

tema: Glorificação do protagonista em vez de crítica
exemplo: Diversos espectadores sentem que o filme retrata a vida luxuosa e criminosa do protagonista de forma atraente, falhando em condenar seus atos e acabando por romantizar o comportamento que deveria satirizar.
texto: “The wolf of wall street” is a movie that doesn’t take its subject matter seriously . It is rather insensitive, pretentious and empty . The fact that this movie is told from Jordan Belfort’s POV logically explains why some of the scenes are depicted the way they are, I wasn’t expecting this to be a moral awakening or a repentance type of movie, but I sure as hell did not expect this to glorify Jordan Belfort’s hedonistic lifestyle & crimes. I fail to see the so called “satire” in this film when the criminal & asshole himself makes a cameo in the film . The “wolf of wall street” is a film in which a criminal who managed to steal and send more than 1500+ working class/middle class people into financial hardship and debt can proudly boast and promote the film discussing his crimes as if it was a movie discussing the life of some scientist or humanitarian. The tone of the film mishandles the severity of the subject, which is probably the main reason why Jordan Belfort felt so comfortable endorsing this film and promoting it. This movie doesn’t depict Jordan for the flawed opportunistic greedy character he is , and even when it does attempt to show that, it is plainly “comedic” and it is not something to be criticized, it is something to be endorsed, it is just being “ambitious”, it is just being “smart”, it is just “wanting the best for yourself”. Being greedy, self-serving and opportunistic is alright and even good because then you get to have endless sex, do endless drugs, and afford everything from lavish parties to lavish trips . This film showed all “the good and the beautiful”, the beautiful women, the parties, the drugs, the trips, but when it came to the consequences of Belfort’s actions, we are shown practically nothing of use . In a way, watching this film you might even get the impression that even if you ended up doing everything that Jordan did you would manage to get away with a slap on the wrist, basically unscathed . We saw no real serious effects or consequences of his drug and sex addiction, no real or serious consequences of his crimes, we only see him playing tennis at jail . In this glorified romanticized piece of media, everything is lavish and extravagant, even jail time is portrayed as something that is not far away from pleasurable or hedonistic . This film intends to criticize hedonism while ironically taking a part of that same hedonistic lens that it is trying to argue against .

texto: Zacznijmy od tego że to fiilm mistrzowski w sensie pomysłu. Nie wiedziałem że jest on tak dobry, niestety mam z nim spory problem. Załamało mnie to gdy zrozumiałem jak płytko filmy są oceniane. 90% ludzi którzy dali dobre opinie nie zrozumieli w ogóle filmu. Widzicie znane nazwisko i już kochacie film? Myślicie że daciw wysoko bo fajnie się oglądało? Na prawdę nie widizcie jakiejkolwiek głębi? Bo nie rozumiem dlaczego godzinami można debatować nad zakończeniem wyspy tajemnic ale po wilku z wall street słyszę że to był fajny do oglądania płytki film. Ale to się działo na prawdę! Film ma rzekomo demaskować Jordana Belforta - oszusta, który dorobił się fortuny dzięki manipulowaniu ludźmi i rynkiem. Tylko że przez większość seansu dostajemy przede wszystkim najbardziej atrakcyjną możliwą wersję jego historii: pieniądze, jachty, luksus, seks, narkotyki, imprezy, władzę i tłumy ludzi zachwyconych jego charyzmą. I większość ludzi została uwiedziona przez belforta. Szkoda tylko że najważniejszy element - to że jest to oszust zostaje w tle. Belfort nie odkrył wspaniałego pomysłu na biznes, pump and dump to bardzo znana, jednak nielegalna zagrywka. Zamiast jednak na ofiarach jego manipulacji, ludzi którzy stracili oszczędnośi życia a ich sytuacja finansowa została zruinowana oglądamy imprezy, narkotyki i popisy belforta. To tak jakby pokazać że przestępca napasa na bank i powiedzieć "tak nie wolno" a za chwilę pokazać tego przestępcę na luksusowym jachcie. Tylko że problem nie polega wyłącznie na tym, co film mówi, ale na tym, jak sprawia, że widz się czuje. Można przez trzy godziny powiedzieć widzowi: „Ten człowiek jest zły”, a jednocześnie pokazać mu jego życie w taki sposób, że widz pomyśli: „Chciałbym mieć takie życie”. Kochamy belforta a to oszust. Tyle że to nie jest problem. Problemem jest to że dla wielu ludzi po czasie nie przychodzi myśl "dałem się zmanipulować belfortowi tak jak ci ludzie" bo tak, daliście się! To jest film na podstawie jego książki! Ale ta myśl nie przychodzi i dalej kochacie belforta i chcecie być jak on. Mieliście okazje zorientować się że ulegliście incepcji, ale to się nie wydarzyło. Ale to nie wasza wina! Film po prostu ostatecznie za bardzo pokazuje nam dostatek belforta i zapomina o ofiarach. Dlaczego po trzech godzinach filmu o oszuście tak dobrze pamiętamy jego jacht, pieniądze, narkotyki i imprezy, a tak słabo pamiętamy ludzi, których oszukał?” jest tak dobry w sprzedawaniu legendy Jordana Belforta, że chwilami sam zaczyna robić dokładnie to, co Belfort robił swoim klientom - sprzedawać atrakcyjną historię, w której niewygodne elementy schodzą na dalszy plan. Co więcej, dzisiaj ta kwestia jest jeszcze bardziej interesująca. Prawdziwy Jordan Belfort nie zniknął po wyroku. Zbudował wokół swojej historii markę i obecnie sprzedaje między innymi kursy dotyczące sprzedaży, perswazji i negocjacji. Można więc odnieść wrażenie, że człowiek, który kiedyś zarabiał na manipulowaniu ludźmi, ostatecznie dostał coś bardzo cennego: własną legendę. I tutaj film staje się wręcz paradoksalny. Historia miała być opowieścią o chciwym oszuście. Tymczasem Belfort wyszedł z niej jako popkulturowa postać, którą wiele osób podziwia za bezczelność, pewność siebie i umiejętność sprzedawania. „Wilk z Wall Street” stał się częścią jego marki. Pomysł miał potencjał - zostaliśmy zmanipulowani. Tylko niestety gloryfikacji belforta nie było końca i nie nadeszło otrząśnięcie się z fascynacji.

texto: I won’t say it’s amazing or outstanding but it’s a good watch. It reminded me of Uncut gems, which was similar to this (just remove the 100 sex scenes). Since the story and stuff happening in the film are real I can’t critic the film as I would have but I must say they could’ve chopped out 45 mins of the film easily. And there was no use of adding so many 18+ scenes. It felt like every 20 mins we were getting a nudity scene, adding no value to the story. The film when it works on an overall story level is actually really good. It’s like such a good take. But the problem is what’s surrounding that story. The film is so hilarious at times and actually really fun to watch. Especially the whole lemon drug pill incident is probably my personal favourite scene. Coming to the performances, Leo is outstanding you can give him any role and he’ll do justice to it. Margot is good but she’s honestly just there for you know what. All of the team with Leo acted amazingly but I feel like they deserved more time, we just got more of Donnie’s character over everyone. Overall the wolf of Wall Street is an enjoyable movie when it works only. Otherwise it’s a just a routine film.

texto: The Wolf of Wall Street is basically three hours of watching terrible people make increasingly terrible decisions while Martin Scorsese somehow makes it impossible to look away. DiCaprio is ridiculously good here. Jordan Belfort is charismatic, disgusting, hilarious and exhausting all at once, which is probably exactly why the film works. Jonah Hill is also completely unhinged in the best way. There are loads of brilliant scenes, and the comedy is much sharper than I remembered, but at three hours it definitely starts to feel repetitive. After a while it becomes another party, another drug binge, another speech, another financial crime, repeat. I can see why people love it, and it is incredibly well made, but I probably admire the performances and filmmaking more than I actually enjoy spending three hours with these people.

texto: Buena pelicula de Martin Scorsese protagonizada por Di caprio como Jordan Belfort, nos cuenta la historia de un corredor de bolsa ambicioso y motivado por el sueño de hacerse millonario. La pelicula nos muestra como una ambición desmedida unida a las drogas y otras adicciones nos pueden llevar a la ruina y haciendo que seamos la sombra de lo que alguna vez fuimos, en general es una pelicula sumamente divertida, con momentos de risa y en ningún rato la pelicula se siente pesada o sobrecargada. Destaco que las actuaciones de todos los personajes son muy buenas y el guion es increíble

texto: I won’t say it’s amazing or outstanding but it’s a good watch. It reminded me of Uncut gems, which was similar to this (just remove the 100 sex scenes). Since the story and stuff happening in the film are real I can’t critic the film as I would have but I must say they could’ve chopped out 45 mins of the film easily. And there was no use of adding so many 18+ scenes. It felt like every 20 mins we were getting a nudity scene, adding no value to the story. The film when it works on an overall story level is actually really good. It’s like such a good take. But the problem is what’s surrounding that story. The film is so hilarious at times and actually really fun to watch. Especially the whole lemon drug pill incident is probably my personal favourite scene. Coming to the performances, Leo is outstanding you can give him any role and he’ll do justice to it. Margot is good but she’s honestly just there for you know what. All of the team with Leo acted amazingly but I feel like they deserved more time, we just got more of Donnie’s character over everyone. Overall the wolf of Wall Street is an enjoyable movie when it works only. Otherwise it’s a just a routine film.

texto: Vu sur la plateforme CANAL + TITRE FRANÇAIS : LE LOUP DE WALL STREET Un film de Martin SCORSESE 2013, USA 🇺🇸 J’avais déjà essayé de regarder ce film auparavant. Mais non ça ne prend pas avec moi. Je peux pas mettre + que 3 étoiles. Ok ok la satire du milieu, blah blah blah, c’est issu d’une histoire vraie, blah blah blah... mais franchement écouter tous ces cons gueuler sans arrêt, superficiels, cupides, drogués et misogynes pendant 2 h c’est au-dessus de mes forces. Je m’ennuie très vite. Trop vide pour moi. Aucun sens, même sous couvert de satire. Et puis, je ne peux pas m’empêcher de penser que quand on réalise un film dans cette veine un peu comme American psycho ou Fight club, on voue une fascination larvée pour la violence et la dépravation en réalité... on trouve ça rock n’roll je pense... tout au fond dans un petit espace de son for intérieur. SCORCESE je te vois 🤣 Et c’est pas pour rien que t’as choisi DI CARPACCIO pour alter ego... Bref, clairement pas le genre de film qui risque de soigner ma misandrie... 😂😂😂

texto: The Wolf of Wall Street is a phenomenal film. Watching it again after a few years makes you remember just how good it is. Despite its length, the plot and almost every scene feel necessary and actually add something to the film. It is ridiculously over the top, and some scenes almost feel unrealistic, but there is so much conviction in the performances that even the absurdity somehow remains grounded. It’s excessive in almost every way, but that is also exactly what makes it work so well.

exemplo: A direção de Scorsese é frequentemente elogiada por manter o ritmo acelerado e transformar uma história excessiva em uma experiência cinematográfica marcante.
texto: Three hours of money, drugs, sex, screaming, terrible decisions, and somehow one of the most entertaining movies ever made. Leonardo DiCaprio is absolutely unhinged here, and Martin Scorsese turns Jordan Belfort’s outrageous rise and fall into a chaotic roller coaster that somehow never loses momentum. It’s hilarious, excessive, disgusting, and incredibly well-made all at the same time. Jonah Hill is also fantastic, and that Quaalude scene alone deserves its own five stars. I know I’m supposed to be horrified by these people… but Scorsese made it way too damn entertaining.

texto: the wolf of wall street was INSANE 😭 i knew it was supposed to be chaotic, but actually watching this was a whole different experience. the entire movie is just one ridiculous thing after another, and somehow Martin Scorsese makes nearly three hours of absolute insanity fly by. Leonardo DiCaprio was incredible as Jordan Belfort. he’s so charismatic and entertaining that you almost forget how awful this guy actually is, which i think is exactly what the movie is playing with. Margot Robbie was great too, and i especially liked how Naomi isn’t just treated like another part of Jordan’s lifestyle. she actually pushes back against him and has her own presence. the comedy worked for me way more than i expected. there were so many moments where i was genuinely laughing, especially because the characters are behaving in completely ridiculous ways while the movie plays everything with such confidence. the whole Quaalude sequence was probably the point where i was just sitting there like WHAT IS HAPPENING 😭 my only real issue is the length. i enjoyed myself, but there were definitely moments where i felt the runtime. and because the movie is intentionally so excessive, sometimes it felt like it was repeating the same cycle of partying, money, drugs and chaos over and over. still, the performances and energy carried it.

texto: the wolf of wall street was INSANE 😭 i knew it was supposed to be chaotic, but actually watching this was a whole different experience. the entire movie is just one ridiculous thing after another, and somehow Martin Scorsese makes nearly three hours of absolute insanity fly by. Leonardo DiCaprio was incredible as Jordan Belfort. he’s so charismatic and entertaining that you almost forget how awful this guy actually is, which i think is exactly what the movie is playing with. Margot Robbie was great too, and i especially liked how Naomi isn’t just treated like another part of Jordan’s lifestyle. she actually pushes back against him and has her own presence. the comedy worked for me way more than i expected. there were so many moments where i was genuinely laughing, especially because the characters are behaving in completely ridiculous ways while the movie plays everything with such confidence. the whole Quaalude sequence was probably the point where i was just sitting there like WHAT IS HAPPENING 😭 my only real issue is the length. i enjoyed myself, but there were definitely moments where i felt the runtime. and because the movie is intentionally so excessive, sometimes it felt like it was repeating the same cycle of partying, money, drugs and chaos over and over. still, the performances and energy carried it.

texto: A movie that only gets more disappointing the more you watch it. Maverick completely lacks the nuance and beauty of the original film. All the love has been drained out in favor of vague foreign threats and fancam fodder. Every time the story is presented with the opportunity to do something interesting, it decides instead to go in the most bland direction possible. In Maverick grief is smoothed over and easily forgotten. In the first film, our heroes were fallible - grief forced them into their own personal reckonings. Not even the US government can save men from their feelings, and that creates a compelling and relatable narrative. In Maverick, the heroes exist only to kill faceless bad guys and always make it out alive. Freedom fighters can never die. There is no questioning the protagonists and no sympathizing with the antagonists. When nothing bad can happen, the franchise cannot be anything more than a spineless advertisement with facist undertones, and I truly believe it has the capacity to be more than that. The more friends ask me to watch this movie with them, the more I find it hard to ignore its glaring faults. I’d just rather be watching the original. I love Tom Cruise and I love action movies; I know that they are capable of more.

exemplo: O filme se apoia demais em referências e recriações do primeiro filme, soando como uma sequência preguiçosa que não consegue se sustentar sozinha.
texto: A big dumb movie like Top Gun deserves a big dumb sequel,  otherwise the entire endeavor doesn't seem worthwhile. Maverick doesn't go far enough in that direction. I'm of the mind that most of this is fine, if uninspired. However, Kelly McGillis not returning, and rather slotting Jennifer Connely into a new character role, is a terrible choice that feels retrofitted around the absence of the romance from the first movie. Like many late career Tom Cruise romances on film, it feels perfunctory at best and carries no weight. Similarly, Miles Teller unfortunately lacks the charisma of his onscreen deceased father,  Anthony Edwards/Goose. Disappointed in the young recruits' call signs: Playback; Hangman; Rooster; boring.I wish they'd have gotten weirder with it: Doghat; Flip-Flop; Groundswell; etc There's nothing as interesting as Iceman, here. All of the new recruits mostly feel like hollow proxys of characters from the original, most glaringly Glen Powell. It's bad criticism to say what you'd prefer the movie to be about rather than what it is,  and I'm anti-deaging effects in onscreen generally, because they seldom look good, but the opening of this movie,  Tom Cruise flying mach 10+ in a fancy future jet,  made me think that a plot where he accidentally flies into the past, back to the 80s, and saves a de-aged Anthony Edwards from death, maybe even bringing him back to the 2020s, would rule. Overall lacking the blissed out stupidity of the original.  Disappointing it doesn't lean harder into some legacy aspects, namely musically. Kind of insane not to do a Danger Zone needledrop. Possibly just in need of a Tony Scott infusion that is sadly no longer possible. Jets are very cinematic.

texto: É um ótimo exercício de marketing, com cenas de caça que tiram o fôlego. E só! A sessão nostalgia tem agradado muito ao público nos últimos anos. Filmes que fizeram sucesso nos anos 80, 90 e até no início dos anos 2000 estão ganhando cada vez mais remakes, reboots ou, como neste caso, continuações. Há muitos críticos dizendo que Top Gun: Maverick é “maravilhoso”, uma “correção do passado”. No caso das cenas de voo, eu até concordo. São impressionantes e, sem dúvida, o grande destaque do filme. Mas todo o restante acaba sendo prejudicado pela repetição de trilha sonora — com exceção da música-tema, que continua linda —, de cenas e até de um contexto muito semelhante ao primeiro filme, tudo cuidadosamente pensado para manter os saudosistas encantados. Assim como no primeiro Top Gun , não temos um roteiro muito elaborado. Em alguns momentos, a história se mostra confusa, enquanto os personagens são explorados de maneira superficial. O próprio nome Maverick faz jus ao filme: tudo gira em torno dele. O maior destaque é, mais uma vez, Tom Cruise. Parece que o filme foi concebido também para mostrar que, mais de 30 anos depois, ele ainda consegue tirar o fôlego do público com suas performances — seja na moto, no caça ou simplesmente demonstrando um vigor e uma energia que continuam sendo sua marca registrada. Top Gun: Maverick entrega um espetáculo visual impressionante e cumpre muito bem a missão de despertar a nostalgia. Mas, quando retiramos todo esse aparato, sobra pouco além de uma continuação que se apoia demais no passado para funcionar no presente.

texto: I get why people love this more than I do. The flying scenes are incredible, it looks fantastic, and you can actually feel that so much of it was done for real rather than just throwing actors in front of a green screen. The final mission is especially class and probably the strongest part of the film. Tom Cruise is exactly what you expect, Miles Teller is good, and the whole thing does a solid job of bringing the original Top Gun back without feeling completely pointless. But for me, outside of the flying, a lot of the story is fairly predictable. You can see most of the emotional beats coming a mile away, and I never got as invested in it as everyone else seems to. Very well made, very entertaining, and definitely a proper cinema film.Just not one I’d be rushing to call a masterpiece.

texto: É um ótimo exercício de marketing, com cenas de caça que tiram o fôlego. E só! A sessão nostalgia tem agradado muito ao público nos últimos anos. Filmes que fizeram sucesso nos anos 80, 90 e até no início dos anos 2000 estão ganhando cada vez mais remakes, reboots ou, como neste caso, continuações. Há muitos críticos dizendo que Top Gun: Maverick é “maravilhoso”, uma “correção do passado”. No caso das cenas de voo, eu até concordo. São impressionantes e, sem dúvida, o grande destaque do filme. Mas todo o restante acaba sendo prejudicado pela repetição de trilha sonora — com exceção da música-tema, que continua linda —, de cenas e até de um contexto muito semelhante ao primeiro filme, tudo cuidadosamente pensado para manter os saudosistas encantados. Assim como no primeiro Top Gun , não temos um roteiro muito elaborado. Em alguns momentos, a história se mostra confusa, enquanto os personagens são explorados de maneira superficial. O próprio nome Maverick faz jus ao filme: tudo gira em torno dele. O maior destaque é, mais uma vez, Tom Cruise. Parece que o filme foi concebido também para mostrar que, mais de 30 anos depois, ele ainda consegue tirar o fôlego do público com suas performances — seja na moto, no caça ou simplesmente demonstrando um vigor e uma energia que continuam sendo sua marca registrada. Top Gun: Maverick entrega um espetáculo visual impressionante e cumpre muito bem a missão de despertar a nostalgia. Mas, quando retiramos todo esse aparato, sobra pouco além de uma continuação que se apoia demais no passado para funcionar no presente.

texto: Assorted moments that stood out to me while watching: - Actually having a flashback to Goose dying in a fiery explosion during 'Goodness Gracious Great Balls of Fire' was awesome. - Maverick literally throwing the rule book into the trashcan on his first day as a teacher. And in that opening shot in the hangar, he does the Riker Maneuver on his chair! He's not like a regular teacher, he's a cool teacher. - The enemy is never named or specified, they just have old planes and a red bird symbol. I could write a whole essay about this (which usually means I like something?). - Big Military Propaganda, huh? Sort of just a Navy recruitment ad, pretty weird to watch while I was abroad in New Zealand. I felt like I should have to stand at attention while the national anthem plays over the credits or something. - Wet denim football < short shorts volleyball - Miles Teller was delightful in the secret third act when he got to do something other than resent his dad stand-in. Just yelling "holy shit" at every crazy fucking thing Cruise did was very fun. - None of the dialogue/advice in the secret third act could be anything other than stuff we've already heard before (don't think, just act; it's not the plane, it's the pilot; etc.) which I think is smart screenwriting, but it was funny to notice because whenever a character needed a pep talk, it was like you had a word bank and could just slot in whatever motif fit the best at the time. - I think there was a throwaway line about Bob not being short for Robert but being an acronym. But there was no payoff!! I wanted him to be Big Ol' Balls. He always will be in my mind. - I begged for a Hangman redemption, and we got it. - Seriously this movie feels like a script you'd pull out for a screenwriting class, very neat and by-the-book, which is brilliantly conservative for a sequel 20 years later which I expected to be a mediocre cashgrab. - A very straightforward, very sincere nostalgia trip to a place and time I have no nostalgia for. Pairs well with popcorn.
