texto: This is the last one. The last Tom Cruise movie I had never seen. I still have to watch the final two Mission: Impossible films to complete my goal, but I have now seen all of Cruise’s movies. texto: I get why people love this more than I do. The flying scenes are incredible, it looks fantastic, and you can actually feel that so much of it was done for real rather than just throwing actors in front of a green screen. The final mission is especially class and probably the strongest part of the film. Tom Cruise is exactly what you expect, Miles Teller is good, and the whole thing does a solid job of bringing the original Top Gun back without feeling completely pointless. But for me, outside of the flying, a lot of the story is fairly predictable. You can see most of the emotional beats coming a mile away, and I never got as invested in it as everyone else seems to. Very well made, very entertaining, and definitely a proper cinema film.Just not one I’d be rushing to call a masterpiece.

texto: Mini-collab with Dan (who also convinced me to watch the OG, kudos to Dan) Watched literally right after rewatching Top Gun , and I know I'm in the minority here, but I did not like this as much. The magic of Top Gun is gone. What made the OG special was its coming of age story. The focus was on Maverick. Of course the sequel's title is Maverick , but the thing is, Maverick got his arc in the first film. Instead of passing the torch on to the young generation, the film doesn't dare do so, instead rewinding and resetting Maverick's major arc beats. This is as per course of a series, but it still makes it no less lazy, especially when Cruise is pushing 60. Maverick's very much an outsider and he needs a new romance which adds even less to the sum than the original (while absolutely trashing McGillis's Charlie by not even giving her a passing mention from anyone , I'm not even going to pretend Maverick is in any way hung up on her after so many years, so they could've had anyone mention her). Sure, there's new blood, Rooster and Hangman (Glen Powell was a mix of Iceman and Maverick somehow for me), but the spotlight's still on Maverick. Glen Powell didn't have enough screentime, but then again, he wasn't the most important of the recruits, but even Miles Teller's Rooster felt side-lined. It's telling that the focus of training was Maverick. Can the recruits outmanoeuvre him, can he simulate bombing (Iran-- ahem-- I mean--) an unnamed nuclear enrichment site under the deadline? The visuals match the OG at the beginning, but gradually slip into ugly modern lensing. The music is nostalgia bait and not as strong. Even the greater focus on the mission with its target specifics lent a darker tone. At a point earlier on, Maverick makes a comment to Jon Hamm's character that he's going to train the kids to return only to be met with an incredulous stare. The connotation was clear. They're training pilots for suicide missions. Meeting the objective is the most important and only goal. The original film was an entirely different vibe. Maverick felt modern in the worst ways for me, including sacrificing character and connection for plot beats and seriousness. Basically, I don't think the sequel brought anything fresh or better; it was entirely of its 2020s generation. I suppose I got to watch Glen Powell in another film. Yay?

texto: Wow, easily better than the original Top Gun for me. That was great as well, but man I haven’t been this emotional watching a movie in a while. The acting in Top Gun: Maverick wipes the originals with the additions of Miles Teller, Glen Powell, and Jon Hamm. Hearing that score drives chills down your spine. I love how they use the perfect amount of nostalgia from the first one and mix it with a great story in the sequel. The effects and action scenes are genuinely insane. Tom Cruise is Maverick, one of, if not the best legacy sequel of all time.

texto: Top Gun: Maverick genuinely surprised me. I wasn’t expecting a sequel decades later to feel this fresh while still respecting and building on the original story. The callbacks actually felt meaningful instead of forced, and the relationship between Maverick and Rooster gave the whole movie some emotional weight. And of course, those real flight sequences are absolutely insane. A rare legacy sequel that understands exactly why people loved the original in the first place.

texto: Nou de bsm filmafdeling sloeg weer toe, dit keer op de mooie zondagavond bij gastheer Jelmer (& thijme). Na er achter te zijn gekomen dat het rad wel eens bijgewerkt mag worden is uncut gems eruit gekomen als winnaar! Deze film had maar liefst een rating van 4,0 vele prijzen gewonnen en is in mijn ogen waarschijnlijk een van de weinige goeie en serieuze films van Adam sandler( als we voice acting niet meetellen tenminste, love hotel transylvania). Zoals u aan de rating kan zien heeft de waarschijnlijkheid zich niet geopenbaard en was adam zoals vanoids weer een teleurstelling. De hele film is een soort marathon van een persoon die een bepaalde eindtijd wil halen maar die helaas niet getraind heeft, laten we die persoon voor het gemak even het compleet fictieve personage jesse noemen en die persoon heeft een bijzonder matige conditie, een peuk- en gokverslaving, en een bijzondere woordenschat en manier van debken zal ik maar zeggen maar tegelijkertijd is het een zeer amicale en gemakkelijk lullende gozer. Er zit constant spanning( en daarbij behorende zeer spannende en epische muziek onder) op en er is constant chaos en wat aan de hand en soms moet er even aangezet worden om vervolgens even de vuilnisbak te legen en dan vervolgens denkt de film weer van oh het is een marathon en hij heeft geld nodig, gooi er maar weer wat doms tegenaan. Tempo zit er wel in maar er gebuert telkens wel heel veel, onnodig veel. En net zoals bij marahtons moet het tempo hier wat beter gedoseerd worden. Aan het begin moet je nooit te veel rennen en dat is orecies wat hier wel gebeurt het was nog wel begrijpelijk maar gewoon onnodig. Daarna js de hele film eigebkijk wat ik al zei. Een soort jesse die een marathon onvoorbereid gaat lopen. Hij denkt telkens oomh ik kan wat aanzetten maar dat ging toch niet, dan loopt hij weer tegen een van eerdere benoemde problemen aan en en ziet ie na wat creatieve,idiote en wat bizarre problemsolving  later weer een gokkast( of gaat ie dus weee sneller lopen, of hij heefr nieuwe schoenen gekocht en maakt verkoopt er 1 hlaverwege) en creëert ie weer een nieiw probleem of het oude komt bovendrijven. Ondertussen een heleboel fucks maar het is gewokn debiel dat je zo een marathon gaat rennen, ik heb ooit een filmpje van streetLabs gezien en daaruit concludeer ik dat dat geen aanbeveler is, zo ziet u ook hier in dit metafoor! De oplossingen, logica, voorspelbaarheid en de hele situatie zijn idioot en na een paar keer bijna omvallen komt jesse er zelf achter dat ie het helemaal neot leuk vind en vervolgens gaat hier toch weer verder waar ie mee bezig was. De toeschouwer aan de zijkant gaat hete chter vervelen en haakt helaas af bij deze absurde poging tot een goede prestatie. Het vermaak is weg de prestatie zelf qas al niet goed en zijn avond was ( deels ) geruïneerd! Jesse zelf is als een mongool doorgegaan tot de finishlijn en js over ds lijn gekropen na heel veel moeite met een zelfvoldsne uitdrukking op zijn gezicht loopt hij naar de medaillestand om er daar achter te komen dat de goede prestatie voor niks is geweest. Zijn zendertje met de bijbehorende tijd is per ongeluk verwisseld met die van iemand die te laat over de finishlijn is gekomen en die dus niet gefinisht is waardoor zijn euforie verdwijnt als sneeuw vork de zon. Tot overmaat van ramp heefr fit slechte nieuws geleidt tot een hartaanval ( al kan dit ook beïnvloed zijn door de levensstijl) en moest jesse het leven laten. Wat is nu de moraal van het verhaal? Nou simpelweg dat ik het een kutfilm vond. Film was dus niet best einde was nog enigzins verassend eb moest lachen daardoor maar dat kwam ook omdat het weer heel slecht was. Voor het overige verwijs ik naar de metafoor. Maar goed dat ik het rad zelf ga bijwerken, buiten hele hoge ratings vanwege benieuwdgeid ben ik blij dat ik normaliter niks van deze man kijk want dit beviel okk weer niet en dus zal zijn bijdrage aan het rad minimaal zijn. Tja zelf vind ik vooral de ratinf van 4 sterren en de goede reviews et cetera bizar, wat zien mensen in deze film? Ik snap het niet kevin naast me ook niet als ik hem zo zag maar misschien was dit niet mijn padje of ben ik te kritisch. Qua ratinf zat ik echt tussen een 2 en een 2,5. Onmogelijke keize voor mijn gevoel. 2,5 is te hoog plus te vermakelijk, 2 is eigenlijk wel te laag want de storyline zelf is wel oke, allen de onderliggende keizes soms niet. Ga toch maar voor een 2 omdat dit me qia krtikek en stijl doet denken aan what happend to monday en die had ik 2 gegevens,maar 2,5 is eigenkijk ook prima. De avond zelf was uiteraard zeer gezellig en de hamburgers qaren heerlijk. Beetje jammer dat ik ik vervolgens en een kut wedstrijd en een kutuitslag en een kutfilm en kevin ook nog eens op de een of andere manier preckes hetzeldd aantal punten als mij heeft gehaald op de fantasy( hij heeft op een of andere manier ook 115 punten gehaald🤯) waardoor ik niks op hem inloop. Ach ja je kan niet altijd zes gooien he!

texto: A movie of self-inflicted wounds. It was hard for me to feel the suspense and the pull into the plot because everything howie did was his own creating. It was stupid decision after stupid decision. I didn't root for him. I didn't want to root for him and that's probably not the point, but it didn't draw me in. I also felt that the acting fell a little bit flat. There was a lot of yelling, a lot of shouting and not a lot of nuance and a lot of small moments to make a great performance. I think it was relied on to scream and act scared. Music was good cinematography was good but overall the story didn't draw me in and I didn't love the performances.

texto: Uncut Gems suit Howard, un bijoutier new-yorkais constamment à la recherche du prochain coup qui pourrait enfin tout arranger, alors même que chacune de ses décisions ne fait qu’aggraver sa situation. Le film réussit parfaitement à installer une tension quasi permanente. La mise en scène des frères Safdie est nerveuse, étouffante, presque agressive, et Adam Sandler est excellent dans ce personnage incapable de s’arrêter, même quand tout lui échappe. Le problème, c’est que le début est tellement chaotique qu’on a parfois du mal à réellement s’attacher à Howard. On observe surtout sa chute comme une suite de mauvaises décisions plutôt que comme quelque chose qui nous touche. Et pourtant, la fin fonctionne justement parce qu’elle donne enfin tout son sens à cette fuite en avant : Howard semble incapable de vivre autrement que dans le risque, comme si gagner importait finalement moins que le besoin de continuer à jouer. Une fin réussie, qui rend le personnage plus tragique qu’il n’en avait l’air.

texto: A 135 minute anxiety-inducing sensory onslaught directed by the Safdies, who have mastered the art of creating stressful cinema. It follows the decisions of Howard - a jewelry dealer and gambling addict -  constantly betting in the hopes of achieving more , sending him on a path into self-destruction. Watching the chaos of his life unravel is agonising, as we witness his euphoric highs and godawful lows. Adam Sandler’s characteristic trashiness and dickheadery aligns perfectly with Howard, making for a captivating, immersive performance. There are no breaks, no pauses - there’s no time for stopping; Uncut Gems is a relentless, claustrophobic masterpiece.

texto: This film helped me understand the Safdie brothers’ directing style a lot better, as it feels quite similar to Marty Supreme. The movie starts abruptly and keeps you in constant tension until the very end, with barely any moments to breathe. One thing that especially stands out is the overlapping dialogue in many scenes. That was probably my main issue with it, though i needed the pace to slow down a little at some point. The third act is easily the best part, showing how well the Safdies can handle a three-act structure. They also manage to bring out Adam Sandler’s talent beyond comedy. The way he talks and moves makes you forget that he is primarily a comedic actor and pulls you deeply into his character.

texto: A 135 minute anxiety-inducing sensory onslaught directed by the Safdies, who have mastered the art of creating stressful cinema. It follows the decisions of Howard - a jewelry dealer and gambling addict -  constantly betting in the hopes of achieving more , sending him on a path into self-destruction. Watching the chaos of his life unravel is agonising, as we witness his euphoric highs and godawful lows. Adam Sandler’s characteristic trashiness and dickheadery aligns perfectly with Howard, making for a captivating, immersive performance. There are no breaks, no pauses - there’s no time for stopping; Uncut Gems is a relentless, claustrophobic masterpiece.

texto: • I really enjoyed this one. It had a very independent-movie feel, with an edgy introduction and immersive (but disorienting) sound editing which tries to get you in the city and in the jewelry store. • Adam Sandler is excellent as an eccentric Jewish NY jeweller with patterns of erratic behaviour. Kevin Garnett was a surprising strong point in the movie too; he acted well. • I enjoyed living with Adam Sandler’s character in his hectic life and his bad decision-making. • The movie surprises you at times, and the ending is not gratuitous. • Initially I gave this 4/4 stars. Upon a rewatch in 2026, I’m downgrading it because I simply don’t appreciate this kind of movie as much anymore. I can see why it really appealed to me as a younger man. It has a frantic pace and a claustrophobic atmosphere that sets it apart from other Hollywood productions that you would see Sandler in. It’s funny, often at Sandler’s expense, because he puts himself in these catastrophic situations over and over. There is an element of fantasy to his affair with Julia Fox, the very attractive younger woman who is seemingly head-over-heels for our old, funny-looking, ambitious protagonist. And yes, the gag at the beginning is very good and the ending is punchy. But as a 30 year-old, I didn’t enjoy being in this world quite as much, with sleazy jewellers, bookies, groupies, and the like. Also, having seen a lot more independent cinema by now, it wasn’t as interesting or groundbreaking as before. However I can still appreciate that it’s well-crafted and does incredibly well at what it sets out to do.

tema: Romantização do abuso e da toxicidade
exemplo: Várias reviews criticam a forma como o filme retrata a relação entre professor e aluno como uma apologia à violência psicológica e física, normalizando o sadismo e a humilhação em nome da excelência artística.
texto: Whiplash em sua recepção crítica divide opiniões profundas entre aqueles que enxergam uma obra-prima sobre obsessão artística e espectadores que, assim como relatado, encontram na narrativa uma apologia incômoda ao abuso psicológico e físico. Logo nos primeiros minutos, o filme de fato incomoda pela forte estilização visual, adotando uma paleta de cores fria e esverdeada nos interiores dos conservatórios e ensaios, remetendo a uma atmosfera quase sufocante que afasta o espectador mais desatento. No entanto, o maior obstáculo da experiência reside na premissa das relações apresentadas. É revoltante e rapidamente beira o insustentável testemunhar a facilidade com que o protagonista aceita a violência física e as humilhações verbais de seu mentor, transformando a suposta busca pela excelência musical em um exercício contínuo de sadismo normalizado. Em vez de uma crítica aos métodos abusivos, a trama parece flertar com a ideia de que a genialidade só pode ser alcançada através da destruição humana, culminando em um final problemático onde a vítima, após ser mentalmente dilacerada, ainda busca a validação e o sorriso de aprovação de seu agressor. Financiado de maneira independente com um orçamento enxuto de aproximadamente 3,3 milhões de dólares, o filme surpreendeu o mercado cinematográfico ao arrecadar cerca de 50 milhões de dólares mundialmente nas bilheterias, impulsionado pela força do boca a boca após sua passagem de sucesso por festivais como Sundance. Na temporada de premiações, o longa alcançou grande destaque, culminando em cinco indicações ao Oscar na octogésima sétima edição da premiação da Academia, realizada em 2015. Na categoria de melhor ator coadjuvante, J.K. Simmons saiu vitorioso interpretando o implacável professor, concorrendo contra Robert Duvall por O Juiz, Ethan Hawke por Boyhood, Edward Norton por Birdman e Mark Ruffalo por Foxcatcher. Na categoria de melhor montagem, Tom Cross garantiu a estatueta para o filme, superando os concorrentes de American Sniper, Boyhood, O Grande Hotel Budapeste e O Jogo da Imitação. O filme também venceu o Oscar de melhor mixagem de som, desbancando os indicados de American Sniper, Birdman, Interstellar e Invencível. Por outro lado, nas categorias em que concorreu e não levou os prêmios principais, o filme registrou derrotas expressivas. Na categoria de melhor roteiro adaptado (classificado surpreendentemente nessa categoria pela Academia), escrito por Damien Chazelle, o vencedor da noite foi O Jogo da Imitação, adaptado por Graham Moore, com os demais indicados sendo Sniper Americano, Vício Inerente e A Teoria de Tudo. Na categoria principal de melhor filme, o grande vencedor foi Birdman ou (A Inesperada Virtude da Ignorância), que superou Whiplash ao lado de outros indicados de peso como Sniper Americano, Boyhood, O Grande Hotel Budapeste, O Jogo da Imitação, Selma e A Teoria de Tudo.

texto: I cant get over how unrealistic and toxic this movie’s view of jazz is. Real jazz training is about deep listening and collaboration, not a brutal boot camp where you practice until your hands literally bleed. It turns someone’s creative passion into a painful, agonizing humiliation ritual for the amusement of a sadistic teacher who belongs in jail, not a classroom. This level of physical destruction would make way more sense in a movie about a heavy metal band. As a film about jazz, it’s just ridiculous. With that said, the last concert scene did give me a profound satisfaction right up until andrew started doing too much

exemplo: Várias reviews criticam a forma como o filme retrata a relação entre professor e aluno como uma apologia à violência psicológica e física, normalizando o sadismo e a humilhação em nome da excelência artística.
texto: 12 ans pour me décider à voir Whiplash. D'abord à sa sortie, puis après celle de La La Land, mais la relation toxique entre un professeur et son élève ne m'inspirait pas forcément plus que ça. Cela n'a pas manqué. La relation entre les deux personnages est tellement poussée à l'extrême qu'elle en devient presque risible. Une surenchère du début à la fin, sans que le film ne monte vraiment en intensité. Les prestations de Miles Teller et J. K. Simmons sont d'ailleurs loin d'être exceptionnelles, alors même qu'elles sont portées par le scénario. Et pourtant, Black Swan, qui aborde lui aussi la quête de perfection et l'emprise psychologique, me laisse un bien meilleur souvenir. Whiplash parvient malgré tout à susciter des réactions : on déteste ce professeur, on éprouve de l'empathie pour son élève et les nombreux retournements de situation maintiennent la tension jusqu'à une scène finale particulièrement réussie. Mais cela ne suffit pas à en faire un bon film, encore moins un chef-d'œuvre.

exemplo: As reviews apontam que o filme reforça tropos como o artista sofredor e a ideia de que a grandeza justifica o abuso, sem oferecer uma crítica ou reflexão mais profunda.
texto: Whiplash em sua recepção crítica divide opiniões profundas entre aqueles que enxergam uma obra-prima sobre obsessão artística e espectadores que, assim como relatado, encontram na narrativa uma apologia incômoda ao abuso psicológico e físico. Logo nos primeiros minutos, o filme de fato incomoda pela forte estilização visual, adotando uma paleta de cores fria e esverdeada nos interiores dos conservatórios e ensaios, remetendo a uma atmosfera quase sufocante que afasta o espectador mais desatento. No entanto, o maior obstáculo da experiência reside na premissa das relações apresentadas. É revoltante e rapidamente beira o insustentável testemunhar a facilidade com que o protagonista aceita a violência física e as humilhações verbais de seu mentor, transformando a suposta busca pela excelência musical em um exercício contínuo de sadismo normalizado. Em vez de uma crítica aos métodos abusivos, a trama parece flertar com a ideia de que a genialidade só pode ser alcançada através da destruição humana, culminando em um final problemático onde a vítima, após ser mentalmente dilacerada, ainda busca a validação e o sorriso de aprovação de seu agressor. Financiado de maneira independente com um orçamento enxuto de aproximadamente 3,3 milhões de dólares, o filme surpreendeu o mercado cinematográfico ao arrecadar cerca de 50 milhões de dólares mundialmente nas bilheterias, impulsionado pela força do boca a boca após sua passagem de sucesso por festivais como Sundance. Na temporada de premiações, o longa alcançou grande destaque, culminando em cinco indicações ao Oscar na octogésima sétima edição da premiação da Academia, realizada em 2015. Na categoria de melhor ator coadjuvante, J.K. Simmons saiu vitorioso interpretando o implacável professor, concorrendo contra Robert Duvall por O Juiz, Ethan Hawke por Boyhood, Edward Norton por Birdman e Mark Ruffalo por Foxcatcher. Na categoria de melhor montagem, Tom Cross garantiu a estatueta para o filme, superando os concorrentes de American Sniper, Boyhood, O Grande Hotel Budapeste e O Jogo da Imitação. O filme também venceu o Oscar de melhor mixagem de som, desbancando os indicados de American Sniper, Birdman, Interstellar e Invencível. Por outro lado, nas categorias em que concorreu e não levou os prêmios principais, o filme registrou derrotas expressivas. Na categoria de melhor roteiro adaptado (classificado surpreendentemente nessa categoria pela Academia), escrito por Damien Chazelle, o vencedor da noite foi O Jogo da Imitação, adaptado por Graham Moore, com os demais indicados sendo Sniper Americano, Vício Inerente e A Teoria de Tudo. Na categoria principal de melhor filme, o grande vencedor foi Birdman ou (A Inesperada Virtude da Ignorância), que superou Whiplash ao lado de outros indicados de peso como Sniper Americano, Boyhood, O Grande Hotel Budapeste, O Jogo da Imitação, Selma e A Teoria de Tudo.

texto: I cant get over how unrealistic and toxic this movie’s view of jazz is. Real jazz training is about deep listening and collaboration, not a brutal boot camp where you practice until your hands literally bleed. It turns someone’s creative passion into a painful, agonizing humiliation ritual for the amusement of a sadistic teacher who belongs in jail, not a classroom. This level of physical destruction would make way more sense in a movie about a heavy metal band. As a film about jazz, it’s just ridiculous. With that said, the last concert scene did give me a profound satisfaction right up until andrew started doing too much

texto: I like character stories. I like comically evil villains. JK Simmons is the lightning in a bottle, basically how session musicians talked about Zappa. And since this movie tries to be about pursuing a vague notion of success and Andrew is never anything but successful, Fletcher’s assholery makes him a fantastic foil for a story where the biggest hurdle is just having to try harder. This movie flows buttery smooth, but the music here isn’t all that inspired. Hard work sounds really cool? Like isn’t music cool because it’s hedonistic? I don’t really get that from miles teller, since anything andrew does outside of drum practice is guy being dude. There’s a lot of sugarcoating and weird things too: the girlfriend, the trumpet player who kills himself. Teller is smug all the time and feels very good will hunting. They made a movie for people to go “yup, that’s jazz.” And yeah man sure there’s definitely jazz here, elite viewers will hear them name drop charlie parker and buddy rich. tldr it should’ve ended with the drummer alternatives in a throuple and the weeping trombone guy showing up jaded and coked up at the jazz bar with jo jone’s cymbal in hand to bludgeon fletcher to death

texto: Whiplash genuinely shook me. Watching Neiman push himself like that while Fletcher keeps shouting, swearing and humiliating him… hard to watch. If you’re easily affected by that kind of thing, prepare yourself. Fletcher is terrible, but seeing how genuinely he believes this is what it takes to make someone great really got to me. The film pushes it so far, it left me wondering where discipline ends and psychological harm begins with this kind of teaching. Is it really okay to accept cruelty just because it produces something extraordinary?

texto: Whiplash has a strong premise centered around ambition, obsession, and the pursuit of perfection, but I found the execution quite uneven. The story follows a young drummer who becomes consumed by his desire to become one of the best, while facing constant pressure from an extremely demanding instructor. The strongest part of the film is its intensity. The rehearsal scenes create a lot of tension, and the editing makes the performances feel fast and energetic. The drumming itself is also presented in an exciting way, with the camera focusing closely on the physical effort and exhaustion involved. However, the characters and writing didn't work particularly well for me. The relationship between the student and teacher becomes repetitive, with the same cycle of pressure, humiliation, and confrontation happening again and again. The dialogue can also feel overly dramatic, and some of the character decisions seem designed primarily to push the story toward another intense scene. The film clearly has something to say about talent, sacrifice, and whether greatness can justify extreme behavior, but I felt these ideas were handled too simplistically. The final sequence is effective on a technical level, but it wasn't enough to completely change my overall impression.

texto: Eli yüzü düzgün bir film ama beklentimi karşılamadı. Yani belki bana hitap etmemiştir bilemiyorum. Ama bir tatsızlık var filmde. Anlatılan o süreç gelişim değişim bana maalesef geçmedi. Bir de sürekli aynı planlar aynı açılar baydı yani. Alt açıdan bateristi çek, terlesin, tuhaf mimikler yapsın, hocası bağırsın...cidden filmde 20-30 kez bu sahneyi görüyoruz. Bunun yerine koysana karakter değişimi dönüşümü hırsını anlatacak hayattan sahneler. Anladım zaten bateri sahnesinin mizansenini derdini, 30 kez göstermek niye? Bak mesela ne güzel ayrıldı kızdan, kaza yaptı devam etti, ebeveynlerine çevresine meydan okudu..bu tarz sahneler filmi zenginleştirir meselesini anlatır. Aynı bateri sahnesini aynı açıyla yüz kez çekerek değil be.

exemplo: Críticas apontam que a trama se torna repetitiva, com ciclos previsíveis de pressão e humilhação, e que os personagens carecem de profundidade.
texto: Whiplash genuinely shook me. Watching Neiman push himself like that while Fletcher keeps shouting, swearing and humiliating him… hard to watch. If you’re easily affected by that kind of thing, prepare yourself. Fletcher is terrible, but seeing how genuinely he believes this is what it takes to make someone great really got to me. The film pushes it so far, it left me wondering where discipline ends and psychological harm begins with this kind of teaching. Is it really okay to accept cruelty just because it produces something extraordinary?

texto: Very solid movie. It shows, beautifully, the inside world of jazz business in New York City. For that, immediate three stars from me. It also shows a young man that starts of his adult life, trying to pursue his passion. It shows his life in a beautiful and vulnerable way, similar to "Good Will Hunting". Another star for that. This movie gained fame because of the depiction of the super intense jazz music teacher. Both his and the boy's performance are excellent. In the second part, the movie takes off to Black Swan territory. That was also very, very cool to watch. For weaker points: I thought the whole story should have been stitched together more smoothly.

It’s so bad that I was genuinely wondering at times if some of the effects were AI generated. Amidst all the bad greenscreen and CGI is the occasional physical prop or set, which look so cheap you’d think these specialized props were purchased at Spirit Halloween. And as if that’s not bad enough, the whole movie has this gross filter that takes all the color out and makes it look gray and dull and terrible. I hate it I hate it I hate it, not one fucking frame of this movie looks even somewhat okay to the point that it made me actually angry while watching. I could genuinely complain about it so much more, I would rate this at least a full star higher if it wasn’t one of the ugliest movies I’ve ever seen in my entire life. The plot of this movie is real basic and predictable but not bad. The cast is all pretty good, I was not really expecting to like Timothee Chalamet as Wonka but I honestly did. There’s some good music but some of the songs are kinda boring and go on longer than they need to. The humor is mixed with some genuinely funny jokes and some really obnoxious bad comedy. As dumb and nostalgia bait-y as he was, I also kinda liked the Oompa Loompa. Real shame about the entire look of every single thing tho.

texto: Le film de Paul King sur le biopic de Wonka est une oeuvre orienté jeunesse. On sens une très grande inspiration cartoon de NOS jeunes années. Les chansons et danses omniprésentes parlent d'eux même mais ne sont pas les seuls points caractérisant ce coté cartoons. Les cadrages et décors colorés rappellent des prises de vue non habituelle du cinéma et une autre facon de retourner dans notre enfance. Le scénario va de paire avec cette idée, pas très elaboré ni très originale, cependant efficace. Le seul point noir de ce film est sa pâte graphique. Quelques manques de qualité de 3D se font ressentir. Surtout lors de deux scenes, les bonbons volants et la scène final de la fabrique. Malgré tout la girafe CGI fait très bien son effet. C'est avec plaisir que j'ai vu ce film de Paul King qui m'a encore renvoyé en enfance après ma découverte de ce réalisateur avec les deux films Paddington qui m'ont émerveillé.

texto: ❝ we are the music makers, and we are the dreamers of dreams. ❞ wonka felt like walking through a sweet shop at christmas — warm lights, colourful wrappers, and the smell of chocolate drifting through the air before you’ve even stepped inside. i went into it expecting something whimsical, and it certainly has that storybook charm. the film moves with a kind of cheerful optimism that feels very disney-coded, as though the world might become kinder if everyone sang at the right moment and shared a piece of chocolate. timothée chalamet brings a gentle sweetness to wonka that makes him easy to root for. this version of the character feels less eccentric genius and more hopeful dreamer, which gives the film a softer, more fairy-tale quality. what i enjoyed most was the atmosphere. there are moments that genuinely feel magical — little bursts of colour and wonder that reminded me of opening a childhood book and finding illustrations tucked between the pages. at the same time, i found myself wanting a little more of the strange edge that makes willy wonka such a fascinating character. the film is so determined to be charming that it occasionally feels a bit too safe, and some of the magic slips through my fingers before it can fully settle. still, there’s something comforting about it. it feels like a rainy-afternoon film: cosy, sugary, and easy to spend time with, even if it didn’t completely enchant me. a sweet, whimsical adventure that made me smile, even if it never quite became the golden-ticket experience i hoped for.

texto: ‘Tis the season for a sweet treat and, whilst not anything to do with Christmas, Wonka hits quite a lot of the festive buttons: fun, light-hearted, colourful and one for all the family. With much of the Paddington team behind this, it delivers that quintessentially English, quirky family film that its forebear (pun intended) achieved but sprinkled with a little bit of Cruella in its prequel backstory to a familiar character. It doesn’t present the titular chocolatier as a villain though, and rubs maybe just a little too much mystery off of the character, but does still feel very much a Roald Dahl tale. Wonka’s dream is to open a chocolate shop and he arrives in an alt-Paris (I think it’s meant to be Paris) to compete against the most famous chocolate makers of the time. From there, frolics, mishaps and big musical numbers ensue. Yes, this is a full musical like the OG Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory. Taking a couple of the songs but throwing in some excellent originals, this could well be destined for a stage run itself in the future. It’s cut through with a particularly English sense of humour and a brilliant ‘spot the famous person’ cast with a, hopefully intended, hat tip to Peep Show and yet another turn from Hugh Grant’s new comedy persona as an Oompa-Loompa. It’s just an utter delight, against all the odds, much like the aforementioned Cruella. A brisk and breezy one-for-all-the-family movie to smack a smile on your face. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

texto: Chinatown is a beautifully made and highly respected neo-noir mystery, but personally, it didn't work for me. The film follows private detective J.J. “Jake” Gittes as he investigates what initially appears to be a simple case involving a wealthy Los Angeles family. The mystery gradually becomes much darker and more complicated. There is no doubt that the filmmaking is excellent. Roman Polanski creates a fantastic noir atmosphere, the cinematography is beautiful, and Robert Towne's screenplay is considered one of the great screenplays of American cinema. Jack Nicholson is also excellent as Jake Gittes. His performance has plenty of charm and personality, and he fits the private-detective role perfectly. Faye Dunaway is also strong, particularly as the mystery surrounding Evelyn Mulwray becomes increasingly complicated. But despite all that... I was bored. 😭 The pacing is simply too slow for my taste. The investigation takes a long time to develop, and many of the conversations and discoveries didn't keep me interested enough. The mystery itself is complicated, but for me, complicated didn't necessarily mean engaging. There were moments where I was more interested in seeing the movie finish than finding out what happened. The film's atmosphere is impressive, but atmosphere alone isn't enough to make me enjoy a movie. The story also becomes increasingly dark and disturbing, especially towards the end. I can appreciate what the filmmakers were trying to achieve, but emotionally I never connected with it. The ending is undeniably powerful and tragic, and I understand why it is so highly regarded. But again, respecting a film and enjoying a film are two different things. Chinatown clearly has enormous influence and technical quality. It simply isn't my kind of movie. Overall, Chinatown is a technically brilliant and historically important neo-noir, elevated by Jack Nicholson, Faye Dunaway and an excellent screenplay, but its slow pacing and style made it a boring and unenjoyable experience for me. A great film for many people — just absolutely not my cup of tea. 🖤🎬

texto: Oh boy where do I begin. Until the last 10 minutes of this film this was going to be at least 4 stars as the screenplay until then was brilliant, the acting first rate, the script sharp ,cinematography wonderful and the direction I admit begrudgingly was great. I sometimes have difficulty separating the art from the creator and knowing Polanski’s crimes made it hard for me to admit that this was one of those times I was going to have to as I really thought this was terrific. THEN that ending came and it is rancid. For an abuser to be “let off “ and even excused is bad enough but added with the knowledge of the director behind it felt like at best he was pardoning himself and at worst sticking two fingers up to the audience reminding them what he personally got away with. I felt cheated ,sickened and grubby and there is no way I can like this . Few films have changed my opinion and repulsed me as quick as this one, maybe that’s the point but I still hate that ending. Frustrated and fuming with this film.

texto: Chinatown is a beautifully made and highly respected neo-noir mystery, but personally, it didn't work for me. The film follows private detective J.J. “Jake” Gittes as he investigates what initially appears to be a simple case involving a wealthy Los Angeles family. The mystery gradually becomes much darker and more complicated. There is no doubt that the filmmaking is excellent. Roman Polanski creates a fantastic noir atmosphere, the cinematography is beautiful, and Robert Towne's screenplay is considered one of the great screenplays of American cinema. Jack Nicholson is also excellent as Jake Gittes. His performance has plenty of charm and personality, and he fits the private-detective role perfectly. Faye Dunaway is also strong, particularly as the mystery surrounding Evelyn Mulwray becomes increasingly complicated. But despite all that... I was bored. 😭 The pacing is simply too slow for my taste. The investigation takes a long time to develop, and many of the conversations and discoveries didn't keep me interested enough. The mystery itself is complicated, but for me, complicated didn't necessarily mean engaging. There were moments where I was more interested in seeing the movie finish than finding out what happened. The film's atmosphere is impressive, but atmosphere alone isn't enough to make me enjoy a movie. The story also becomes increasingly dark and disturbing, especially towards the end. I can appreciate what the filmmakers were trying to achieve, but emotionally I never connected with it. The ending is undeniably powerful and tragic, and I understand why it is so highly regarded. But again, respecting a film and enjoying a film are two different things. Chinatown clearly has enormous influence and technical quality. It simply isn't my kind of movie. Overall, Chinatown is a technically brilliant and historically important neo-noir, elevated by Jack Nicholson, Faye Dunaway and an excellent screenplay, but its slow pacing and style made it a boring and unenjoyable experience for me. A great film for many people — just absolutely not my cup of tea. 🖤🎬

texto: Chinatown is one of those movies where I can absolutely see why it's considered a classic... but it just didn't work for me. The acting is good, the cinematography is strong, and the mystery is clearly crafted with a lot of care. There’s a reason people still talk about this film fifty years later. But personally, I struggled to stay invested. The story felt slower than I expected, and while the mystery gradually becomes more complex, I never reached the point where I was completely hooked. I spent most of the movie appreciating what it was doing rather than actually being engaged by it. Jack Nicholson is excellent, and there are some memorable scenes throughout. But for whatever reason, the emotional connection just never happened for me. By the time the ending arrived, I admired it more than I felt impacted by it. I understand why it's a classic. I just don't think it's my classic.

texto: A ideia do roteiro é legal, filme de detetive padrão, com aquele plot twist mais chocante em alguma medida... Mas muitos detalhes me incomodaram muito, por exemplo o problema da direção em "não dar o drama suficiente nas cenas que deveriam ser dramáticas". O filme em momento algum transmite a ideia de tensão REAL, e a atuação da Faye me pareceu BEM fraca, dada a importância que a personagem dela tem no contexto geral. O que dá um lampejo ao filme é a individualidade do Jack Nicholson, principalmente na primeira metade do filme, na qual ele ainda parece ter licença poética pra dar nuances pessoais ao personagem, sendo que mais próximo à conclusão do filme volta-se para um encaixe mais "genérico" de detetive.

texto: "Esqueça, Jake, é Chinatown." Essa frase, apesar de aparecer no último momento, é, para mim, a forma como o filme se desculpa por tanta enrolação. Jake, que até então vive na crença de que, por vir de onde veio, entende que qualquer caso possa ser resolvido, se esvai ao perceber sua inocência. Ele consegue resolver o caso principal; contudo, sua expressão ao final revela que permeia uma complexidade e uma estruturação política que não podem ser alteradas. Essa fragilidade de tentar mudar algo muito maior que você é o ápice de Chinatown. Aquela região em que nunca se espera algo pior, e quando o pior chega, você já entra em conformidade, é o jeito como Jake e todos lidam com a impotência. texto: Good noir: Intellectually great, emotionally distant This was my first time watching Chinatown, and honestly, the thing that pulled me in the most wasn't the mystery, it was the vibe. The world-building is incredible: the clothes, the cars, the quiet jazz, the heat of 1930s Los Angeles, the backyard scenes, the hats, all of it. Jack Nicholson has this classy, effortless presence, and the film's whole aesthetic feels timeless. Great performance by Faye Dunaway too. But the movie itself is emotionally cold. It's a slow burn, and for most of the runtime, I felt like the film kept a distance from me. The message and themes are definitely strong, but for me, they don't fully hit until the final scene, and that's where I had a mixed reaction. It almost feels like the entire movie was built for that final moment, where everything becomes very obviously "noir" and you see the system's corruption laid out. But the thing is: even without that last scene, I already sensed the corruption throughout the film. It's implicit. It's in the world, the tone, the dialogue. So the movie didn't need to rely so heavily on that final punch for me to understand what it was doing. And maybe that's because we watch the film from a third-person perspective. We see signs of the system's rot throughout the story, long before the main character truly realizes it. If I were in the detective's shoes -if I were seeing things only through his head- it would probably feel more engaging and shocking step by step. But as viewers, we catch the overall darkness earlier, which made the ending feel powerful but also slightly predictable in feeling, even if not in plot. So overall, I loved the atmosphere and the classic detective tone, but emotionally it didn't grip me the same way other classics do. Chinatown doesn't grip emotionally at all. It's more observational. More philosophical. You're meant to watch the world and its corruption, not get pulled into the characters' inner lives.

texto: Era uno de los grandes clásicos del cine negro que todavía tenía pendiente de ver, y la verdad es que no me ha decepcionado. Roman Polanski hace un trabajazo en la dirección. Me gusta mucho cómo va construyendo la historia poco a poco, haciendo que el misterio vaya creciendo a medida que avanza la película. Además, los planos y la puesta en escena ayudan muchísimo a crear esa sensación de tensión e incomodidad que está presente durante prácticamente toda la película. La ambientación de Los Ángeles de los años 30 también me parece increíble y le da a la película una personalidad enorme. La interpretación de Jack Nicholson es sobresaliente. Su personaje, Jake. J. Gittes, tiene muchísimo carisma, pero también es bastante cínico y arrogante, y creo que Nicholson consigue transmitir muy bien todas esas facetas. Si no me equivoco, este fue uno de sus primeros papeles realmente importantes en Hollywood, y demostró que podía llevar perfectamente el peso de una película. Y ese final... Uff. Creo que es casi lo mejor de la película. Me parece un cierre brutal, tanto por lo que ocurre como por la forma en la que está planteado. Es de esos finales que hacen que, cuando terminan los créditos, te quedes unos minutos pensando en lo que acabas de ver. Lo dicho, creo que Chinatown es una de las mejores películas policíacas y de cine negro que he visto. Tiene una historia muy bien construida, una atmósfera increíble y un final difícil de olvidar. Una auténtica joya que recomiendo muchísimo. 👌

texto: On my recent movie arc, a natural fulcrum point that you reach is whether the classics are worth visiting. Are you watching them because you'll think you'll like them or because movie buffs say you should like them so you HAVE to watch them? I've never been a huge fan of classical acting, a bane that plagues me with movies from the 40s all the way to the 80s. The style is very different and while understandable and appeals to some, I usually find it to date movies too much, it's dramatic in a more theatrical way. As ironic as it sounds I prefer movies that are a little less theatrical with their character portrayals. I prefer more realistic/grounded performances you find in modern acting or performances that are less like caricatures and more like the person they're supposed to be. But times were different, in bygone times of film-making people weren't looking for relatable they were looking for better versions of themselves. A detective that always has the perfect quip, a damsel in distress that is beautiful but sassy but also mysterious!? While I say all of that, I can't help but notice the bright spots in older movies that shine through every time I watch them. Old movies are time capsules of the past that allow you to see the origins of where the modern films you love came from; their humble beginnings. With little experience with Noir films of the 40s, 50s and 60s its easy for me to overlook just exactly HOW revolutionary this movie was for the genre at the time of its release. How purposefully theatrical the acting was and how much it used plot devices from these films and then subverted them or expanded upon them. Looking at it through that lens, everything started to click for me, and the biggest thing I noticed is that Jake Gittes isn't the typical noir detective he's actually a flawed man that fails to see the dark corners of the world and our "femme fatale" is actually a traumatized woman and a victim of those same dark corners. This movie is THE quintessential Noir film for me. It wears the influences of its predecessors on its sleeve while also influencing decades of films to follow. While carrying out the tropes you typically see in these movies, it, at least at the time, had an ending that made stomachs churn in defeat at the hopelessness that it leaves you with.  I can confirm that never having been spoiled, for me it had the same effect. It follows an intriguing mystery, that at parts is cliche but also provides nuance in strange places. The acting is great, despite my biases towards modern acting (it took me some getting used to). The shots were innovative for the time and its layered with thick metaphors to the corrupt vs life on the surface throughout. AND nearly every scene has a double-meaning or a callback for later. I was thoroughly engaged and it accomplished what I hope to see in any watching of a classic movie according to critics. It MADE SENSE why this movie was influential and considered a classic. Has the formula been improved upon since this film? Probably. Is it dated and completely different from a Noir film that would be made today? Yes.... I mean, noir as a genre itself is dated. BUT! Did I enjoy myself with this film? HELL YEAH! That's all I can ask for, and in my surprise of how much I enjoyed this movie I sometimes caught myself stopping to appreciate what it did at the time it came out. The fact that i'm a big Jack Nicholson fan also helped a tremendous amount.

tema: Personagens sem carisma ou pouco desenvolvidos
exemplo: Muitos espectadores afirmam não ter conseguido se importar com os personagens, considerando-os rasos, previsíveis ou simplesmente antipáticos.
texto: Le casting est excellent et la mise en scène irréprochable. J'interprète ce film comme une réflexion sur l'immoralité. Contrairement à de nombreux films de gangsters, il ne cherche pas véritablement à glorifier ses personnages en leur attribuant des qualités chevaleresques, comme la solidarité ou l'honneur, qui viendraient en quelque sorte compenser leurs actes infâmes. Le film semble au contraire nous dire : regardez donc ce que vous, spectateurs, admirez tant. Pourtant, ce que je reproche à Martin Scorsese, c'est d'avoir choisi une approche extrêmement centrée sur les hommes. Comment peut-on représenter un tel univers en effaçant presque totalement une partie de la population ? Où est l'écosystème social qui entoure cette mafia ? Les femmes sont bien présentes, mais leurs personnages ne sont ni développés ni dotés d'une véritable personnalité, alors même qu'elles semblent constituer l'arrière-plan indispensable de cette structure. Certes, il n'était pas nécessaire de faire d'elles le sujet principal du film (ce n’est semble il pas l’objectif d’origine). Cependant, il aurait été intéressant de leur donner davantage de profondeur : quel regard portent-elles sur ce monde mafieux ? Comment vivent-elles cette proximité avec la violence, le pouvoir et la criminalité ? Ici, elles apparaissent essentiellement comme des objets de désir lorsqu'elles sont jeunes, comme des gardiennes du foyer lorsqu'elles deviennent épouses et mères, ou encore comme des mères âgées et aveugles aux agissements de leurs fils. Toutes, qu'elles soient jeunes femmes ou femmes mariées, semblent n'avoir qu'un seul désir : intégrer l'univers de l'homme mafieux, dangereux mais irrésistiblement fascinant. Nous sommes en plein dans les clichés. Je ne souhaite pas ici condamner de représenter le banditisme, l'immoralité et certaines formes de masculinité toxique (qui malgré cette intention critique, une forme de fascination ou de glorification peut transparaître aux yeux du spectateur dont l’ambiguïté fait la richesse du film, mais aussi sa limite) mais de déplorer avant tout l'absence d'un autre point de vue, qui aurait permis d'enrichir la réflexion. Au final, il appartient à chacun d'interpréter l'œuvre soit comme une représentation de la masculinité, soit comme une critique du masculinisme ; soit comme la mise en scène d'un idéal fantasmé, soit comme une satire destructrice.

texto: Iconic movies that I've put off watching because there is no way they could live up to the hype usually end up impressing me...unfortunately, Goodfellas was an exception to this. While it does a good job immersing you in the world of a mafia movie, and has some memorable characters, I found that it did a surprisingly poor job building consistent relationships between the characters and making the most of its runtime. While the relentless narration and freeze frames got old quick, where the movie lost me is the large time skips, where relationships or situations get better or worse arbitrarily, which lessens the time that we get to see with the characters. I get that the characters are supposed to be despicable, but they're not likable or unlikable enough to be properly invested in. They're consistently shown to be rolling in money, but take unnecessary risks to try to get more...I know the main character has a fifth grade education and isn't meant to be the best or brightest, but he's got nothing going for him. The way his life falls apart isn't in a "train wreck you can't look away from", but instead something I couldn't wait to get over with, given the day it all falls apart for him is the first time in ten years we've checked in with him, and he's making stupid decisions for no reason. The acting was pretty average in my opinion, Pesci and Deniro were the standouts but don't do anything they haven't done in other roles, and the plot beats were fairly predictable, and nothing too shocking. It was just a really long time to spend with characters that I didn't really have any interest or attachment to, due to the lack of depth, nuance, or originality in any of them. There was nothing particularly bad about this movie, and it wasn't actively unenjoyable. There are some really good long shots, and the setting and atmosphere are really solid, there is clearly care and thought put into the filming of this movie. There just wasn't a single moment I can think of that kept me glued to the screen, surprised me, or made me feel anything at all, other than indifference.

texto: GoodFellas 1990 Directed By: Martin Scorsese Rewatch🔁: 4 قررت أن أعيد مشاهدة جميع الأفلام التي سبق أن قيمتها تقييم 5/5 لأني أفضل أن تكون أفلامي قابلة لإعادة المشاهدة، وهذه المرة ستكون إعادة المشاهدة مختلفة، إذ تأتي بعد سنوات من المشاهدة والنضج وتراكم التجارب لأرى كيف ستبدو هذه الأفلام الآن بإعادة أكثر نضجًا ومن ضمنها هذا الفيلم. ➤ أدري أن أول ما يلح على المتلقي في معظم أعمال المافيا الحماسية التي تمتلئ بالبوم والطخ والزنا، الذي لاحظت أنه طغى على جوانب أخرى كانت أحق وأجدر بالالتفات له. فالقطيع استحبوا الإزعاج والإنفجار والمسدسات، وأبرز ما اتضح لي بعد هذه الإعادة هي مفارقة سعة العالم وضحالة المساحة النفسية التي منحها سكورسيزي للبطل المحوري. فعرض العمل بناء اجتماعي ممتد للجريمة المنظمة. وعدد كبير من الشخصيات والعلاقات والتفاصيل اليومية ويهم المتلقي ببناء اجتماعي كثيف، مع العلم بأن أساس السرد [هنري] ظل محجوب عن الدواخل التي تبرر أفعاله، فرأيت حركاته وردود فعله والتعليق الخلفي، فالعيب الأوضح من ذلك هو سرد قدم تاريخ سلوكيات وأفعال أكثر من ما يقدم جوانب نفسيا أكثر تعقيدًا [ليست بجوانب سيئة، لكن إن صح القول؛ تم إهمالها]، ولاحظت هذا بشكل واضح بعد الإعادة، تقديم اتساع أكثر من تقديم عمق. واعتراضي قابل للتأسيس على نص الفيلم ذاته، لأن تم طرح التجربة الإنسانية [سواء لهنري أو غيره] وظلت بعيدة عن فحواها ومن المتفق عليه إن الصورة تبتكر وسائل تعبير عن الدواخل النفسية لأي عمل مع أن التصوير هنا تعامل مع الظاهر. من بناء المواقف الدرامية ومن التمثيل، ومن الصمت، وبين التناقض بين أقوال وأفعال. [وكل هذه الوسائل كانت متاحة لسكورسيزي] لكنه آثر في توسيع الدائرة الاجتماعية على حساب أي فعل نفساني، فقياس على ذلك ظل الجانب النفسي في العمل أدنى من اتساع العالم الذي يعيش فيه [حتى لا، يأتيني شخص سطحي في التعليقات ويتقوَّل علي بـ"لا تنتظر من العمل شيء هو لم يضيفه"] وبناء على الذي ذكرته [هنري] ظل شخص ثابت في نظرته إلى العالم، فبدأ وهو مذهول بالعصابات ورأى أنها مجال يعطي الاحترام والسلطة. وينتهي من ذلك تحت التهديد من ضغط العالم بالقتل بعد رحلة الصعود العظيمة الأبسلوت سينما [طبعًا هذا كان متوقع لكن لن ألتفت له الآن] بمعنى آخر، خروجه من عالم الجريمة جاء اضطرار وحفاظ منه على حياته، والقناعة الأخلاقية بقيت في توب تو، وهذا يعني أن التغير الدرامي للشخصية متحول خارجيًا [من تأثير البيئة المحيطة التي هنري كان يتعامل معها] أكثر من داخليًا [الجانب النفسي الذي ذكرته]، فما تغير هو ظروف هنري الخارجية ومكانته الاجتماعية ويبقى وعيه بذاته وإدراكة لحقيقة ما كان يعيشه في مرتبة ثانية. ومن يطلب بأن يكون التحول الداخلي شرط من شروط العظمة التراجيدية فحريٌ به أن يجد في مراجعتي ما يسوغ تردده في منح الفيلم توب ون. أما كارين، ففتح السيناريو رؤية منظور سردي ثاني حين اعطاها مساحة روائية من خلال صوتها لكنه عاد ليجعل هنري هو الراوي والمتحكم في استمرار السرد مع إن منظور كارين في الكتاب كان أكثر قوة وحضور، والمعالجة السينمائية اختزلته. وهذا يعتبر مهم لأنه يتعلق بالبناء السردي الداخلي للعمل ففتح الفيلم أفق من منظور مختلف ثم أهملها، يتصنع توقع لدى المشاهد ثم يخيب ذلك التوقع وهذا شأنه أن يضعف تماسك العمل ولو أن السيناريو منح كارين مساحة أوسع للتعبير عن رؤيتها الخاصة لذلك العالم، لا سيّما أن منظور المرأة في عالم ذكوري عنيف يحمل إمكانات درامية ونقدية هائلة لكان حقق توازن سردي أعمق عدا أن ما تم طرحه فعلًا هو أن كارين ظلت في مكان تثبت وجودها وتنسحب. المضمون المشكلة الثانية أو الثالثة هي في علاقة الأسلوب والمضمون الخاص بالعمل وبالتحديد الطريقة التي يصور بها العالم الإجرامي فمن جهة يريد سكورسيزي أن يقدم نقد ضمنيًا لذلك العالم وأن يظهر انهياره ويفضحه والقيم التي يقوم عليها، ومن جهة أخرى يستخدم كل أدواته، من حركة، لقطات، تعليق صوتي، مونتاج، ليقدم ذلك العالم في أبهى صوره وأكثرها جاذبية. ➤ فالديناميكية البصرية ذاتها التي تفضح رجولة المافيا الزائفة في الوقت ذاته تعطيها جاذبية جميلة تجعل المشاهد منجذب لها على الرغم من إدراكه لانحلالها الأخلاقي وهذا المتضح بين مقالات الجماهير وفانز التيكتوك وغيره. وهذا يعني أن المسافة النقدية [التي أراد سكورسيزي تقديمها] بين المتلقي والعالم الإجرامي تضيق بدل أن تتسع وأن هذا التنظيف والتجميل يطغى على الإدانة الأخلاقية لعالم المافيا [وهذا يعد نقد من مباني فكر سكورسيزي نفسه وليس فكر شخصي لدي] فهو ناقض الذي يريد تقديمه بنفسه، وكل من يتابعني على علم بأنني لا أنشغل عادةً بالجوانب الأخلاقية لكل الأعمال أنا فقط أنتقدها من منظور فني بحت، فهذا الطرح صنع حدود قدرة بين الأسلوب على حساب خدمة المضمون [الذي سكورسيزي ادّعى أنه ينتقده ضمنيًا] وإذا كان بعض المحنكين قد ذهبوا لأبعد من ذلك، وقالوا إن عملية صناعة عمل نفسها تصبح موضوع الفيلم بمعنى أن الاستعراض الشكلي المبالغ به يتحول من وسيلة إلى غاية وهذا يحتاج إلى تفصيل ذلك أن الأسلوب في الفيلم مرتبط بهنري بتجربة هنري ذاتها مع عالم المافيا [أي أن أساليب عناصر الفن قد تؤثر على حيثية طرح شخصياته] فالرتم السريع، والكاميرا المتحركة، والمونتاج، كلها عوامل تعكس حالة الوعي لشخصية مأخوذة بسطوع العالم الذي تعيش فيه، وأرى أن الشكل نفسه يصنع التحول النفسي —والموضوعي— وألف سطر تحت كلمة موضوعي، وأن الفصل بين الأسلوب والمضمون في هذه الحالة بالذات فصل مصطنع بعيد عن حقيقة التجربة فمن العدل أن نميز بين الاعتراض على العمق النفسي للعمل، وبين الشكليات —وهذا التمييز من أساسيات الحكم على العمل—. ومن الأفكار الأخرى التي يطرحها العمل هي الانتماء للجماعة، شبكة من الولاءات والالتزامات والعلاقات فالانتماء إلى هذه الجماعة يعطي الفرد إحساسه بالمكانة وكلما توغل الفرد في العالم ازدادت مطالب الجماعة عليه وثمن الخروج منها فبهذا الشكل طُرح التناقض بين حرية كل فرد منهم وانضباطها مع الجماعة لأنه يريد أن يحقق نفسه والجماعة سلطتها، من ثم ينشأ التوتر الذي يسري على كل العمل وهذا التوتر هو ما يعطي العمل قوته من حيث الدراما حتى مع غيب العمق النفسي وهذه نقطة في صالحة، وأيضًا فكرة العنف اليومي الذي يظهر صورة روتينية يمارسه الناس في نسق حياتهم العادية في المطاعم والبيوت والطرق وهذا العنف يصبح جزء من الجماعة ويصنع اعتياد المتلقي عليه. فالعنف يظهر بصورة عادية وروتينية [وهذا عكس ما كان ينتقده سكورسيزي بشكل ضمني كما ذكرت]. المال والمكانة والقتل والسلطة كأهداف مشروعة في نظر الشخصيات وهذا ما جعل الصراع الأخلاقي معقد فكانوا يعيشون في قيم مختلطة فنجاحهم مرتبط بولاء الجماعة. وشيء اخر في صالح العمل هو [البارانويا] التي تنتشر في نهاية العمل فكلّما اقترب الفرد من قمة العالم الإجرامي زاد خوفه من الخيانة ويبدأ يشك في من حوله وانهيار الثقة بين الجماعة وانهيارهم هو الثمن الذي تدفعه الشخصيات مقابل انتمائها لعالم عنيف ➤ وإذا أردت تحرير حديثي على أقوى نقاط ممكنة يمكن ذكر أن أقواها من توجّه ضد العمل بشكل —موضوعي— قوي، أولها العمق لشخصية هنري أدنى من العالم الذي يعيش فيه ومن تعدد الشخصيات [ليس سوء منه] والفكر الداخلي للشخصية أضعف من قوة الحدث الدرامي وقوة الأسلوب الإخراجي وأن كارين في مكانة المنظور المتناقض لم تبلغ المدى الذب كان السيناريو ذاته يفتحه له [بناء على الكتاب] ➤ مع ذلك جودفلس يظل ذا شأن، يتعذر على مشتغل النقد المجنون أن يتجاهله وعلى أي كاجول أن يفوته لكن المكانة التي يتبوأها في الأعمال الفنية تظل في تفاوت بالنسبة لي [مع العلم بأني حاولت أن أكون موضوعي بقدر الإمكان] تبعًا لاختلاف المعايير في تقدير التفاوت بين الأسلوب والمضمون [وهذه أقوى نقطة في حديثي] ومن اعاد مشاهدته بعد اول انبهار بالبوم والطخ والمطاردات وتبين ما فيه من مواضع قوة فنية ومن حدود سيئة فهو شخص أحترمه وأوجه له تحية لأنه حاور العمل من داخل إطاره فضلًا عن الشخصنة ويزن ما أعطاه بحيادية بغية الإنصاف والأمانة جدير من ذكر التقنيات فيه بشكل مستقل عن العمق النفسي. طبعًا مقصدي من هذا الكلام ينأى على التشنيع على أعمال سكورسيزي فهو مخرج له مكانة عظيمة [حسب ما يزعم الأغلب] لكني شرحت شعوري له بعد الإعادة الرابعة للعمل [تقريبًا] وهذا موضع تقييمي له 6.0/10

texto: Iconic movies that I've put off watching because there is no way they could live up to the hype usually end up impressing me...unfortunately, Goodfellas was an exception to this. While it does a good job immersing you in the world of a mafia movie, and has some memorable characters, I found that it did a surprisingly poor job building consistent relationships between the characters and making the most of its runtime. While the relentless narration and freeze frames got old quick, where the movie lost me is the large time skips, where relationships or situations get better or worse arbitrarily, which lessens the time that we get to see with the characters. I get that the characters are supposed to be despicable, but they're not likable or unlikable enough to be properly invested in. They're consistently shown to be rolling in money, but take unnecessary risks to try to get more...I know the main character has a fifth grade education and isn't meant to be the best or brightest, but he's got nothing going for him. The way his life falls apart isn't in a "train wreck you can't look away from", but instead something I couldn't wait to get over with, given the day it all falls apart for him is the first time in ten years we've checked in with him, and he's making stupid decisions for no reason. The acting was pretty average in my opinion, Pesci and Deniro were the standouts but don't do anything they haven't done in other roles, and the plot beats were fairly predictable, and nothing too shocking. It was just a really long time to spend with characters that I didn't really have any interest or attachment to, due to the lack of depth, nuance, or originality in any of them. There was nothing particularly bad about this movie, and it wasn't actively unenjoyable. There are some really good long shots, and the setting and atmosphere are really solid, there is clearly care and thought put into the filming of this movie. There just wasn't a single moment I can think of that kept me glued to the screen, surprised me, or made me feel anything at all, other than indifference.

texto: Film particulier. Visuellement que ce soit dans la beauté des plans, des couleurs, ou des mouvements de caméra c'est  vraiment très beau. Dans l'ambiance, notamment au début de son intégration c'est pas mal parce que tu vois un peu le fonctionnement des mafieux, sympatoche. Le choix de la musique intéressant aussi. Après j'ai eu beaucoup de mal à me plonger dans l'histoire. La voix off qui raconte tout déjà, même si elle est justifié du coup avec la fin du film, j'aime vraiment pas c'est grave pas immersif je trouve. Les personnages sont tous des énormes fdp à différentes échelles, donc impossible de ressentir quoique ce soit tellement ils sont déshumanisés. L'ultra violence très terre à terre c'est pas trop ma came non plus. Le rythme est correct en soit c'est pas si ennuyant, mais juste les histoires de mafieux sont vites répétitives, sexe drogue violence argent, toujours les mêmes thématiques pendant 2h30 et ce sans forcément un fil rouge d'un truc précis, ce qui fait que même la fin donne pas l'impression d'une conclusion d'une affaire spécifique. Bref en vrai je peux capter le buzz du film et c'était pas non plus de la merde, mais pas forcément fait pour moi.

texto: Martin Scorsese’s Goodfellas is the antithesis to Coppola’s romanticized mob opera—a hyper-kinetic, visceral descent into the intoxicating high and inevitable paranoia of organized crime. Driven by Thelma Schoonmaker’s relentless editing and Scorsese’s signature tracking shots, the film eschews tragic dignity in favor of an unvarnished, manic realism. Ray Liotta’s voiceover functions as a darkly intoxicating tour guide through a world where loyalty is a transactional facade and violence is merely an occupational hazard. It is a masterpiece of kinetic energy, soundtrack integration, and moral decay.

texto: There’s not much that can be said about this film that hasn’t been said a million times already. It’s one of the few films out there that 100% deserves all the praise and hype it gets and is one that always gets a little bit better every time I see it. At this point, it’s more of a comfort movie for me than anything. Everyone here is at the top of their game, like I could gush on and on about how much I love Ray Liotta, Robert De Niro, Lorraine Bracco, and so on but we’d be here for hours. With that said, the clear standout from the cast is Joe Pesci, who is absolutely fucking electric in this. Every line spoken from this man’s mouth is pure comedy gold, yet he’s such a loose cannon that he can turn you from laughing to terrified in a matter of seconds. That Oscar was completely deserved. The structure of this film is also something that I can’t really get enough of, and to some extent, the same could be said for Scorsese (Wolf of Wall Street, The Irishman, etc.). I just love how much it builds up the mobster life in the first act, showing all the excesses that drew Henry into it in the first place. Then, the second act comes, you start seeing the cracks show, and you really get a bleak picture of how psychotic, deranged, and destructive these people are. As the third act arrives, everything falls apart in a chaotic way that puts you on edge until the very end. I think this structure is not only a great feat in writing but also editing, which can be attributed to Thelma Schoonmaker’s genius work. The entire sequence with the helicopter still gives me so much anxiety, and almost all of that is because of the frantic way it’s edited. From a director with such an iconic filmography, this film really stands out as a timeless classic that I think I could watch endlessly for the rest of my life.

texto: I always wanted to be a gangster. In this masterpiece, you get Scorsese’s absolute best direction—yes, even better than Raging Bull, alongside the single greatest performances of both Joe Pesci and Ray Liotta’s careers. Goodfellas translates the original story of a kid growing up in a neighborhood overrun by mobsters, captivated by the seductive pull of their lifestyle: the sharp suits, the endless cash, and the street justice that commanded everyone's respect. I’m a huge sucker for scripts that capture natural conversation between characters, and the specific scene where Scorsese’s own mother plays Tommy's mom is pure genius; I felt like I was right there in that era, sitting at that dinner table with that family. The dialogue between Tommy Devito and Henry Hill when Henry laughs at him "Funny how?" is one of the greatest displays of screen presence I have ever witnessed in my life. The whole context is spectacular a masterclass in camera angles, lighting, and contrast. Lorraine Bracco is flawless as well. While she shines even brighter in The Sopranos, she anchors crucial moments here, like that iconic tracking shot with Ray Liotta that provides an unreal level of immersion. You feel completely present every second of the runtime. After watching so many mob films, you realize that every interaction between these guys matters whether they're talking about food or planning a hit and Scorsese delivered that authenticity to the world better than anyone. I love you, Scorsese!

texto: I feel like I’ve stepped into an alternate reality of the Sopranoverse. Scorsese brings the heat with a great (based on a) true story and incredible leading cast. We follow Henry Hill’s climb into the mob world with besties Jimmy & Tommy. Joe Pesci sure is one crazy banana. Overall, there were some pretty good twists and you’re continuously left wondering who’s the next to get pinched or whacked. Moral of the story: do NOT drugs and DO call from an outside line.

texto: (Started (slight majority of it) Sep. 4, finished Sep. 5) “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster.” Still an absolutely phenomenal movie. Probably Scorsese’s magnum opus , even if I would put Shutter Island over it. I get why this is considered one of the best movies of all time, & is one of the “everyone’s seen it” movies. Karen’s perspective, especially the scene with the other mob-wives, IMO adds something that many others (including Scorsese’s other mob flicks) lack. It’s such a shame that a lot of the actors herein (Ray Liotta, Lorraine Bracco, Paul Sorvino, &c.) never worked on another Scorsese film again.

texto: An absolute nothing burger of a horror film. The characters are one dimensional, the story is full of horror and mystery cliches that are just chucked into the plot but aren’t effective, and worst of all it actually had potential. Theres multiple interesting sequences that had potential to be great but they all fell flat due to a lack of depth. This film felt like a 10 minute horror short film that was forced to have a runtime of nearly 2 hours, except the writers decided to not add to the story and instead drag it out.

texto: plot aside, but this is a pure aesthetic masterclass. Even if you find the narrative a bit mid, you cannot deny that Longlegs is an absolute art object. Osgood Perkins and DP Andrés Arochi crafted a visual nightmare that feels less like a standard horror movie and more like a meticulously curated, deeply unsettling painting. The way they weaponize the image composition is insane. Switching from those grainy, claustrophobic 4:3 35mm flashbacks to the ultra-wide 2.39:1 digital present creates this massive, yawning negative space. Arochi uses extreme wide-angle lenses even for close-ups, which slightly distorts the world and leaves so much empty air around Maika Monroe. The dread doesn't come from jumpscares but rather lives right there in the empty corners of the frame, waiting. I also loved the color palette. You're constantly trapped between the freezing, desaturated blues of the Oregon winters and the sickly, feverish ochre/orange tones leaking through the windows of the interior scenes. Then, the sudden, sharp slashes of devilish red just cut right through the monochrome sadness. It's visually rigid, perfectly symmetrical and deeply atmospheric. Even if the script didn't fully work for many, the sheer craftsmanship on display here is undeniable.

texto: J'aime beaucoup le jeu d'acteur de Maika Monroe (Lee) dans ce film. Elle campe à merveille ce personnage d'introvertie, constamment mal dans sa peau et épuisée par l'affaire. Dès les premières scènes on voit qu'elle ne se sent pas bien, et plus ça avance, plus ça empire. Le film ne lui donne jamais de vraie catharsis, ce que j'aurais bien aimé voir, mais je suppose que c'est par choix. (Bon, il y a eu le cri dans la voiture vers la fin, mais pas assez cathartique à mon goût vu tout ce que la pauvre a vécu !) Le meilleur acte reste selon moi le premier : mention spéciale à toute la scène où Lee rentre chez elle, particulièrement réussie, exemplaire en terme de tension. On a, de plus, le droit à une photo hyper léchée (la palette de couleurs du film, les ombres et les cadrages avec ces plans larges, vraiment un plaisir pour les yeux), une bande son qui fait bien le taf (même si peu mémorable), et une belle atmosphère. Le film ne cache pas ses influences, notamment du côté de Fincher, avec Seven et Zodiac , néanmoins ça ne le dessert pas à mon sens. Mais Cage cabotine . Et ça m'emmerde que ce soit le cas. Je sais pas, c'est peut-être moi, mais je ne trouve pas les scènes avec lui particulièrement intéressantes, la faute à des répliques peu inspirées et au manque d'idées de mise en scène lorsqu'il apparaît à l'écran. Pourtant, il y avait quelque chose à faire avec un Cage qui en fait des caisses, mais là y a aucune aura, le personnage ne dit rien ou ne fait rien qui n'ait été fait ailleurs en mieux, même le maquillage est assez bof. Sa performance est clairement plombée par l'incapacité du film à lui donner des répliques et des motivations qui soient suffisamment marquées (à part le "UNMAKE MEEE!" qui était chouette) et faisant un minimum froid dans le dos. C'est là où le film pêche à mon sens le plus : il peine à faire du personnage de Cage l'entité glauque et malsaine que le mystère mérite.

I feel like there were some really cool ideocracies in this movie, the way the main character was characterised, the light world building, the way the horrors are conveyed, the other worldly threat of longlegs. This movie is really cool but I don't think it's narrative did a good job at hooking me as much as I wanted it to. On further contemplation there's some commentary on stranger danger (ie "the threat is not from the outside but the inside" that line of thinking.) and that was a HAUNTING way to end the movie but still it was kinda... Yeah.

texto: The beginning was so captivating and it created an expectation for the rest of the movie to follow. The premise was promising, a serial killer who was merely doing the devil’s bidding, but the question of why the murders were committed still remains. Why were the daughter’s birthdays so important? Why dolls? Why couldn’t Harker remember? These are some other questions that remain unanswered by the end of the movie. To say the least, the ending was unsatisfying for the mind and for the eyes.  Still worth a watch, the acting was incredible and so was the ambience.

texto: take this from someone who RARELY gets scared, longlegs spooked the hell out of me !! his mannerisms, speech, and appearance made me gag so many times because i was watching the latter part of this movie while eating (bad decision i know)… i literally had to pause during that interrogation scene because i felt an immense creepiness when he started doing that dancy thing and MOST ESPECIALLY when he started banging his head out of nowhere … 😭 huge shoutout to the actor for nailing his character!! the cinematography and editing of this movie was also 🤌 it was superr good, the angles really know how to build up tension and i don’t think i can recall a movie i’ve watched that has camera positions like this! i think this was one of the main reasons why i was super scared—  the way they hid longleg’s face at the beginning, the way they captured the massacres, and the ominous feeling following mc, it was all so exhilarating and terrifying at the same time 🫨 although -1 star because of the mc’s stupidity … i couldn’t watch it in one sitting because i felt sooo frustrated at her!! WDYM SHE’S AN FBI AGENT BUT SHE MADE THE DUMBEST DECISION TO GET OUT OF HER HOUSE AND LOOK FOR THE “INTRUDER” WITH ONLY A PISTOL WHEN SHE LIVES ALONE IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FREAKING WOODS ?! NOT ONLY THAT, SHE SEES A LETTER INSIDE OF HER HOUSE AND YET SHE SITS AND INVESTIGATES IT WITHOUT MAKING SURE THE INTRUDER’S ALREADY LEFT 😫 like c’mon girl… you’re smarter than this … didn’t they teach you awareness before you became an fbi? also another -1 star because i have mixed feelings about that ending.., i never could’ve predicted it would end with satanism because i thought it was purely psychological horror … personally, i would’ve preferred it if there was no satanic occult added because longlegs was literally the most perfect horror character for me 💔 lost the scare factor when he died legit

texto: The beginning was so captivating and it created an expectation for the rest of the movie to follow. The premise was promising, a serial killer who was merely doing the devil’s bidding, but the question of why the murders were committed still remains. Why were the daughter’s birthdays so important? Why dolls? Why couldn’t Harker remember? These are some other questions that remain unanswered by the end of the movie. To say the least, the ending was unsatisfying for the mind and for the eyes.  Still worth a watch, the acting was incredible and so was the ambience.

exemplo: Os elogios se concentram nas atuações de Maika Monroe e Nicolas Cage, que são descritas como assustadoras, cativantes e capazes de sustentar o clima tenso do filme.
texto: Maika Monroe played Agent Lee Harker with a look in her eyes that the viewer isn’t able to see through  from the beginning of the film. We can tell something haunts her, something we’re yet to see including her. Throughout the performance her character is being portrayed as “highly intuitive” but even with her intuition she never expects to keep finding herself in front of the gun. With a a new sense of terror waiting for her at each turn, or perhaps the same one that haunts her just getting louder and louder. With that being said Maika Monroe has done this role justice. Alice Witt and Nicholas Cage gave me the horror I wanted, turning this movie into something I told myself I’d be watching again without a doubt. The plot strings itself together with beautiful maddening detail, as Oz Perkins directs the hell out of it . The lack of on screen kills turns our focus to Maika and the horror she experiences throughout the film, but I’ll say the last act makes for a gruesome, satisfying, and emotional experience to make us clench our teeth for our beloved protagonist. Which includes my favorite shot in the film by far where the figure appears in the reflection as Carter closes the the door behind Harker. This made me say woah, it honestly shook me since I felt like there was a tension for something to pop up in unexpected places throughout just for this singular shot to relive that. I really liked this movie and it’s deserving ending

exemplo: Os elogios se concentram nas atuações de Maika Monroe e Nicolas Cage, que são descritas como assustadoras, cativantes e capazes de sustentar o clima tenso do filme.
texto: Longlegs is still terrifying to me on a rewatch. The opening feels like some fever-dream nightmare I somehow never had as a kid: hazy, surreal, and deeply unsettling in a way that immediately gets under your skin. Maika Monroe devours every scene, completely disappearing into an emotionally exhausting performance that feels both vulnerable and haunted. She’s phenomenal here, and the role firmly cements her as one of modern horror’s great scream queens. And Nicolas Cage is simply unmatched. There’s something so grotesque and unnerving about his performance that even his presence alone feels like a threat. Longlegs’ mostly grounded and disturbingly plausible storytelling fills nearly the entire film. It unfolds like a grim procedural wrapped in a tightening nightmare, constantly feeding you fragments of a mystery without letting you see the full bloody picture. Every frame feels ominous. Every silence feels loaded. There’s this persistent sense that you’re witnessing something you were never meant to see. Then, when those final pieces finally click into place, the mystery reveals itself with a horrifying inevitability. It’s entirely engrossing, relentlessly foreboding, and tensely scary in a way that lingers, leaving me second glancing shadows in the corner. Even knowing exactly where it’s going, Longlegs still manages to make me feel like I’m watching something I shouldn’t be. And that’s a helluva feat. 🩸
